Outside local mode, `requireLocalMode` answers 404 `{ error: "not_available" }` (no message) for every sessions route and every recordings route. The sessions WebSocket checks `isLocalMode()` itself in `checkUpgradeRequest` (S9), and outside local mode it is refused like every other failed upgrade: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` and a destroyed socket (spec Security 1).

### Server modules

#### `server/runtime/process-tree.js` (S1)

- `trackPid(pid, onExit?)`: registers a process this module did not start; ignores anything that is not a positive integer. `onExit` is an optional subscribe function `(listener: () => void) => unknown` that trackPid calls once, so the pid untracks itself when the process ends. pty-host passes the handle's own `onExit`.
- `untrackPid(pid)`; `listTrackedPids()` → `number[]` (a copy).
- `listDescendants(pid)` → `Promise<number[]>`: one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` (argv only, 2 s limit), every pid below `pid` at any depth. On Linux without `ps` it reads `/proc/<n>/stat` for every numeric entry of `/proc`. `[]` on Windows, for a bad pid, or when neither can be read.
- `descendantsFromPsOutput(text, pid)` → `number[]` (the pure walk); `parseProcStat(text)` → `{ pid, ppid } | null` (fields counted from the last `)`).
- `killProcessTree(pid, { graceMs = 1500 } = {})` → `Promise<void>` (never rejects). POSIX: lists descendants first, sends SIGTERM to the group led by `pid` and to each descendant, polls every 50 ms, sends SIGKILL to every target still alive after `graceMs`, then waits at most 1 s more. Windows: `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`.
- `killAllTracked({ graceMs = 1500 } = {})`: every tracked child and tracked pid in parallel, then forgets them. `killAllTrackedSync()`: one `ps` snapshot (500 ms limit; the `/proc` read on Linux when `ps` fails), then SIGKILL to every tracked group and descendant (Windows: `child.kill()` for children, `taskkill /T /F` for tracked pids). `spawnTracked` keeps its signature.

#### `server/runtime/shutdown.js` (S1)

- `HARD_EXIT_MS = 8000`, `SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS = 7000`, `STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN"`.
- `registerShutdownTask(name, fn)` → an unregister function; a second registration under the same name replaces the first; an empty name or a non-function throws `TypeError`.
- `shutdown({ server, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: stops the scheduler; runs the runs' `stopAll()` and every registered task in parallel, each task cut off at `taskLimitMs` (errors logged, never thrown); awaits them BEFORE `killAllTracked()`; then the live-chat children; then `server.close` (500 ms fallback).
- `installShutdownHandlers(server, { hardExitMs = HARD_EXIT_MS, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: SIGTERM, SIGINT (and SIGBREAK on Windows) start the shutdown with the hard exit timer (exit code 0). When `process.env.AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN === "1"` it reads stdin lines; the line `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN` (compared after trimming spaces and a trailing carriage return) or the end of stdin starts the same shutdown. Without that variable stdin is never read.
- Budget: sessions quit ≤ 7 s (`SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS`, S7) < server hard exit 8 s < desktop `QUIT_GRACE` 10 s (D1).

#### `server/runtime/store.js` (S2)

- `runtimePaths()` gains `sessions: <root>/sessions` and `worktrees: <root>/worktrees`.
- `ensureRuntimeStore()` makes `root`, `sessions` and `worktrees` 0700 as under "Files on disk".
- `export async function ensurePrivateDir(dir)` → `dir` (mkdir -p with 0700, then chmod 0700; Windows only makes it).

#### `shell-env.js` (S2)

- `LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`; `NESTED_MARKERS = ["CLAUDECODE", "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT"]` (spikes S3 and S6 add the Codex and Cursor markers); `FALLBACK_NOTICE = "Agent OS could not read your login shell's settings, so sessions use a basic environment."`.
- `resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell, timeoutMs = 10000, nodePath = process.execPath, platform = process.platform } = {})` → `{ env, source: "login-shell" | "fallback" | "process", notice: string | null }`; never throws.
  - `shell` defaults to `process.env.SHELL`, else `os.userInfo().shell`. Runs `<shell> -i -l -c '<node> -e <script>'` (`-ic` for csh and tcsh), detached, stdin ignored, `cwd` HOME. The script prints `process.env` as JSON between two random markers; only the text between them is read.
  - The shell's environment is the server's minus `AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` and every excluded name, plus `AGENT_OS_RESOLVING_ENVIRONMENT=1`. Its `PATH` is `process.env.AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` when that is a non-empty string (the `PATH` the desktop app was started with, before `server_path_env()` adds its folders; Task D1). Otherwise it is the server's own `PATH` (`npm start`, the tests). `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` is an `AGENT_OS_*` name, so it never reaches the shell or a session. The fallback and the Windows environment keep the server's own `PATH` (H2). The parsed result leaves out `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and that flag; a result without `PATH` is a failure.
  - Timeout or failure: `source: "fallback"`, the server's environment without the excluded names, plus `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `~/.local/bin` appended to PATH when missing, and `notice: FALLBACK_NOTICE`. Windows: `source: "process"`, the process environment without the excluded names, `notice: null`.
- `excludeFromSessionEnv(keys)`: adds each string to the module's set of excluded names (Q11a; compared without letter case on Windows). `resetExcludedForTests()` empties it. Excluded names are left out of what goes INTO the login shell, the fallback and the Windows environment, never out of what the login shell gives back.
- `getLoginShellEnv()` → the same promise on every call (resolved once per server); `resetLoginShellEnvForTests()`.
- `sessionEnv(baseEnv, { sessionId, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION, claudeFullscreen = false, agentId, platform = process.platform } = {})` → a new object:
  - without every `AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` and `NESTED_MARKERS` key (names compared without case on Windows);
  - with `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `TERM_PROGRAM=AgentOS`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=<agentOsVersion>`, `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID=<sessionId>`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` only when `agentId === "claude" && claudeFullscreen === true`;
  - never setting or changing `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, any `OPENCLAW_*` variable or `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`, and never `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`.

#### `folders.js` (S2)

- `checkSessionFolder(input, { home = os.homedir(), agentOsHome = runtimePaths().root, managedRoot = managedNodeRoot(), platform = process.platform } = {})` → `{ ok: true, path, name }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }`.
  - Input is trimmed. `path` is `fs.realpath.native` of the input; `home`, `agentOsHome` and `managedRoot` are compared as real paths too, ignoring letter case on `darwin` and `win32`.
  - `<agentOsHome>/worktrees` and below pass the Agent OS rule but must still be inside HOME. The managed Node folder is refused like AGENT_OS_HOME (Q12).

  | code | message |
  |---|---|
  | `not_absolute` | "Type the full path, starting with / (or a drive letter on Windows)." |
  | `missing` | "That folder doesn't exist." (exists but can't be opened: "Agent OS can't open that folder.") |
  | `not_a_directory` | "That is a file, not a folder." |
  | `is_home` | "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it." |
  | `inside_agent_os` | "Agent OS's own folder can't be used." |
  | `outside_home` | "Pick a folder inside your home folder." |

- `recentSessionFolders({ limit = 8 } = {})` → `[{ path, name, lastUsedAt }]`, newest first, one row per real folder, from meta.json `kind`, `folder`, `folderShown`, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `lastUsedAt` (a row's `lastUsedAt` is the latest of `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `lastUsedAt`, so an older meta.json without `lastUsedAt` still sorts). Rows with `kind: "update"` or `folderShown: false` are left out; each folder is re-checked with `checkSessionFolder` and dropped when it fails.

#### `settings.js` (S3)

- `readSessionSettings()` → `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` (false when the file is missing, broken, or holds anything but `true`).
- `writeSessionSettings(patch)` → the new settings. Only `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` is accepted; anything else throws `invalid_settings` and writes nothing.

#### `profiles.js` (S3), plus two exports elsewhere

- `server/runtime/builders/brain-launch.js`: `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession = false } = {})`; with `forSession: true` the settings `env` has no `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`. Headless callers (two arguments) are unchanged.
- `server/runtime/runs/run-manager.js`: `export function hasCursorForceFlag(plan)` (body unchanged).
- `SESSION_AGENTS = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"]`.
- `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED = false` (until spike S5).
- `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL = { claude: "Claude Code", codex: "Codex", cursor: "Cursor", hermes: "Hermes", openclaw: "OpenClaw" }`: the short names every session message, tab and dialog uses. `manager.js` imports it and re-exports it; nothing defines a second map.
- `buildSessionProfile({ agentId, folder, sessionId, kind = "agent", resume = null, settings, detected, brain = null, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION } = {})` → `{ command, args, cwd, env, agentSessionId, settingsFile, softStop, resumeMode, folderShown, notes }`:
  - `resume` is `null` (a fresh start) or `{ agentSessionId: string | null }` (the value in meta.json). `settings` undefined reads `readSessionSettings()`; `detected` undefined calls `getAdapter(agentId).detect()`.
  - `command`: `detected.path`; when detection found nothing, the first match on the login shell's `PATH` through a private `findOnPath` (`agent` before `cursor-agent`; Q8). argv only, never a shell.
  - `args`:

    | Agent | Start | Resume |
    |---|---|---|
    | claude | `--session-id <new uuid>` (+ `--settings <file>` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `--resume <agentSessionId>` (+ the same `--settings` rule) |
    | codex | `-C <folder> -c tui.notification_method=osc9 -c tui.notifications=["agent-turn-complete","approval-requested"] -c tui.notification_condition=always` (+ `codexBrainArgs` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `resume --last` + the same `-c` options and brain options, in the same folder |
    | cursor | `--workspace <folder>` | `--resume --workspace <folder>` |
    | hermes | `--in <folder>` (kind `update`: exactly `update`) | `--resume latest --in <folder>` |
    | openclaw | `tui --session agentos-<sessionId>` | the same |

  - `cwd`: the real path from `checkSessionFolder(folder)`; OpenClaw uses `os.homedir()` while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false, with `folderShown: false`.
  - `env`: `sessionEnv((await getLoginShellEnv()).env, { sessionId, agentOsVersion, claudeFullscreen, agentId })`; for a node-shebang CLI inside the managed Node folder, `withSiblingNodePath` puts its own folder first on `PATH` (Q7); then `PWD` is set to `cwd` (Q7a).
  - `agentSessionId`: Claude a new `crypto.randomUUID()` (or the resumed one); OpenClaw `agentos-<sessionId>`; Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the update kind `null`.
  - `settingsFile`: `<root>/sessions/<sessionId>/claude-settings.json` (0600) for Claude with an OpenRouter or Local brain, written from `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession: true })` after `assertSafeClaudeSettings`; otherwise `null` and no `--settings`. Sessions never add `--model` (Q9).
  - `softStop`: `"claude-bg"` (Claude), `"openclaw-abort"` (OpenClaw), otherwise `null`. `resumeMode`: `"id"` (Claude, OpenClaw), `"fallback"` (Codex, Cursor, Hermes), `null` (update). `notes`: `[FALLBACK_NOTICE]` when the login shell could not be read, else `[]`.
- `assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args)`: throws `unsafe_argv` unless `args` is exactly one of the shapes above and no option name is on the blocked list (`containsBlockedFlag`), `--bare`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--mcp-config`, `--accept-hooks`, `--yolo`, `--trust`, `--no-alt-screen`, a token containing `dangerously`, `bypass`, `full-access` or `skip-permission`, `--tui` for Hermes, or Cursor's `-f` / `--force` (`hasCursorForceFlag({ command: "agent", args })`). Codex `-c` values must be the exact notification options or `codexBrainArgs` keys. Values (folders, ids, models) are checked by shape. Every per-agent lookup uses `Object.hasOwn` or a `Map`, so `"constructor"` and other prototype names are refused.

#### `pty-host.js` (S4)

- `PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer."`
- `ptyAvailable()` → `Promise<{ ok: true, reason: null } | { ok: false, reason: string }>`. Loads node-pty once and runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY once; a missing module is final, a failed probe is retried after 30 s.
- `spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker })` → `PtyHandle` `{ pid, write(data), resize(cols, rows), kill(signal = "SIGTERM"), pause(), resume(), onData(cb) → unsubscribe, onExit(cb) → unsubscribe }`.
  - `command` and `cwd` absolute, `args` a string array, `env` an explicit object; otherwise `TypeError`. Errors carry `code: "pty_unavailable"` (S6 answers 503) or `code: "spawn_failed"`.
  - `onExit` delivers `{ exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null }`: the signal as a name (`"SIGTERM"`), and `exitCode: null` when a signal ended it. A listener added after the end is still called once.
  - Output before the first `onData` listener is kept (up to 1 MB) and handed to it.
  - `trackPid(pid, handle.onExit)` right after the spawn; `untrackPid(pid)` on exit. `tracker` and `setPtyLoaderForTests(fn | null)` are for tests only.

#### `mirror.js` (S4)

- `createMirror({ cols, rows, onQueryReply, onAlert, now = Date.now })` → `Mirror`:
  - `write(chunk)`; `resize(cols, rows)` (cols 2-500, rows 1-200, else ignored); `dispose()`;
  - `snapshot()` → `Promise<{ data, cols, rows, modes }>`, covering exactly the chunks written before the call. `modes = { altScreen: boolean, bracketedPaste: boolean, mouseTracking: "none" | "x10" | "vt200" | "drag" | "any", mouseEncoding: "default" | "sgr" | "sgr-pixels", focusReporting: boolean, cursorKeysApp: boolean, kittyFlags: number }`. `data` already restores the alternate screen, bracketed paste, focus reporting, cursor keys and mouse tracking; the client applies only `mouseEncoding` and `kittyFlags` after writing it;
  - `setWriterAttached(boolean)`: while false, DA1 (`ESC[?1;2c`), cursor position (`ESC[<row>;<col>R`) and kitty (`ESC[?<flags>u`) replies go to `onQueryReply(reply)`; every other reply is dropped, and nothing is sent while a writer is attached;
  - `onCountedOutput(cb)` → unsubscribe: at most every 250 ms, when the text above the bottom 6 rows changed or the screen scrolled.
  - `onAlert(raw)`: `"bel"` or `"<osc number>;<payload>"` (for example `"9;Approval requested"`, `"777;notify;Codex;Waiting"`), capped at 4096 characters.
  - Uses `@xterm/addon-unicode11` with `allowProposedApi: true`, so wide characters measure as in the browser terminal.
- `isUserInput(data)` → `false` for a frame made only of terminal replies (DA, cursor position, status, kitty flags, mode reports, XTVERSION, DECRQSS, OSC colour replies), focus reports (`ESC[I`, `ESC[O`) or mouse-motion reports; `true` for keys, paste, clicks and the wheel; `false` for an empty frame.
- `COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS = 6`, `COUNTED_CHECK_MS = 250`, `MIRROR_SCROLLBACK = 1000`, `ALERT_RAW_LIMIT = 4096`.

#### `recorder.js` (S5)

- `CAST_FILE = "screen.cast"`, `PREV_CAST_FILE = "screen.prev.cast"`, `SEGMENT_BYTES = 26214400`, `RECORDING_CAP_BYTES = 1073741824`, `ROTATION_MARKER = "[earlier output removed]"`, `RESUME_MARKER = "--- resumed ---"`.
- `createRecorder({ dir, cols, rows, segmentBytes = 26214400, append = false, now = Date.now, onError })` → `{ output(chunk), marker(text), resize(cols, rows), close() }`.
  - asciicast v2, output events only, never input; writes in order in the background; event times never go backwards.
  - `marker(text)` writes an `"m"` event; `resize(cols, rows)` an `"r"` event `"<cols>x<rows>"`; `close()` returns the same Promise every time and resolves when everything is on disk.
  - Rotation at `segmentBytes`: `screen.cast` becomes `screen.prev.cast`, and the new segment starts with the rotation marker.
  - `append: true` (resume) writes the `"m"` event `"--- resumed ---"` and an `"r"` event itself (a new header when no recording is left); the manager never writes this marker.
  - A recording that cannot be written calls `onError(error)` once (default one `console.warn`) and ignores further output; it never throws into the session.
- `listRecordings({ isLive } = {})` → `[{ sessionId, kind, agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown, startedAt, endedAt, bytes, live }]`, newest `startedAt` first; only sessions with a valid id folder, a readable meta.json and at least one cast file.
- `enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes = 1073741824, isLive } = {})` → `Promise<{ deleted: string[] }>`: while over the cap, deletes the cast files of the ended recording with the oldest `endedAt` (else `startedAt`); never a live one; keeps meta.json (the ended tab and Resume stay); one run at a time.
- `recordingsRemovedByCap()` → how many recordings the cap removed since the server started.
- `deleteRecording(sessionId, { isLive } = {})` → `{ ok: true }`; removes only the two cast files; throws `unknown_session`, `recording_live` or `recording_missing`.
- `openRecording(sessionId)` → `{ lines: AsyncGenerator<string> }`: one header line (the older segment's when it exists), the older segment's events, then the newer segment's events without its header and leading rotation marker; each line ends with `"\n"`; a last line still being written is left out; throws `unknown_session` or `recording_missing` before anything is streamed.
- `isLive(id)` lets the caller say which sessions run right now: the manager passes `(id) => live.has(id)` (a session still flushing its recording counts as live); the routes pass the manager's own `isLive` (`(id) => manager.isLive(id)`, ruling R8). Without it, meta.json decides.

#### `manager.js` (S6, S7)

- Constants: `IDLE_AFTER_MS = 20000`, `PAUSE_LAG_BYTES = 524288`, `PAUSED_DROP_MS = 10000`, `CLOSE_LAG_BYTES = 4194304`, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES = 65536` (S6); `STOP_GRACE_MS = 3000`, `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS = 7000` (S7).
- Re-exports: `SESSION_ID_RE`, `isSessionId`, `sessionError` (from `errors.js`) and `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL` (from `profiles.js`). Also `readGitBranch(folder)` → `string | null`.
- `createSessionManager({ now, spawn = spawnPty, buildProfile = buildSessionProfile, recorderFactory = createRecorder, mirrorFactory = createMirror, maxLive = 8, isExecutionAllowed = isExecutionEnabled, checkFolder = checkSessionFolder, ptyCheck = ptyAvailable, detect, resolveBrain, readSettings = readSessionSettings, enforceCap = enforceRecordingCap, killTree = killProcessTree, softStop = runSoftStop } = {})` (all optional; `detect` defaults to `(agentId) => getAdapter(agentId).detect()`, `resolveBrain` to `(agentId) => resolveBrainForRun(agentId, undefined, { prepare: true })`). `getSessionManager()` returns one manager per server and registers `registerShutdownTask("sessions", () => manager.shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" }))`. Session ids are `crypto.randomUUID()` (Q39).
- `SessionSummary` (every item of `GET /api/sessions`, and the answer of `create`, `get`, `resume`, `dismiss`):
  `{ id, kind: "agent" | "update", agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown: boolean, branch: string | null, status: SessionStatus, stateSince: string, startedAt: string, endedAt: string | null, exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null, endedBy: "stop" | "quit" | null, dismissed: boolean, brain: { kind: "plan" | "openrouter" | "local", label: string } | null, resume: { available: boolean, reason: string | null, fallback: boolean }, alerts: "basic", recordingBytes: number }`
  - `SessionStatus = "starting" | "live" | "waiting" | "idle" | "held" | "exited"`; `waiting` and `held` are never produced in SP3 (SP4).
  - `stateSince` is when the current status began (ISO). `exitCode` is `null` when a signal ended the process; `signal` is a name. `recordingBytes` is 0 when the recording was removed.
- Methods:

  | Method | Answer |
  |---|---|
  | `create({ agentId, folder })` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; `folder` is `null` for OpenClaw while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false. Checks the agent, Look only, the terminal module and the folder policy in that order (a Look only refusal comes before a folder refusal), and the live limit |
  | `createUpdateSession({ agentId, folder })` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; Hermes only (400 `update_not_available` otherwise; an agent outside `SESSION_AGENTS` is `unknown_agent`); the folder passes the folder policy; not gated by Safety; not counted toward 8; at most one at a time (`update_running`); `brain: null` |
  | `list({ includeUpdate = false } = {})` | `Promise<SessionSummary[]>`, sorted by `createdAt`, dismissed sessions included (the UI filters) |
  | `get(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; `unknown_session` |
  | `resume(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; only an ended `agent` session; same id and tab, new process, `status` back to `starting`, `dismissed: false`, the recorder in `append: true` |
  | `dismiss(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; only an ended session (`session_live` otherwise); stored in meta.json |
  | `attach(id, { id, send(frame), close(reason) })` | `Promise<{ snapshot, detach() }>`; see the WebSocket protocol; throws `session_ended` for an ended session |
  | `focus(id, attachmentId)`, `write(id, attachmentId, data)`, `resize(id, attachmentId, cols, rows)`, `ack(id, attachmentId, seq)` | `boolean`, synchronous (false = dropped: not the writer, out of bounds, `data` over 64 KB in UTF-8 bytes, unknown session or window) |
  | `stop(id, { by = "stop" } = {})` | `Promise<SessionSummary & { note: string \| null }>`; stopping an ended session answers its unchanged summary; two Stops of one session share one sequence |
  | `quitCheck()` | `Promise<{ live: [{ id, title, kind }] }>`, every live session of both kinds; an update's title is "<agent> update" |
  | `isLive(id)` | `boolean`, synchronous: `live.has(id)`, true from the spawn until the session's recording is closed and its meta.json written (a session still closing its recording counts as live, ruling R8); S8 hands it to `listRecordings` and `deleteRecording` |
  | `shutdownAll({ reason = "quit" } = {})` | `Promise<{ stopped: number }>` |
  | `recoverStaleSessions()` | `Promise<{ recovered: number }>`: every meta.json still `"starting"` becomes `"exited"` with `endedBy: "quit"` ("Ended when Agent OS quit."), Resume available |

- Activity (every SP3 session is "basic"): `starting` → `live` on the first output of any kind or user input (`isUserInput`); `live` → `idle` after 20 s without counted output; `idle` → `live` on counted output or user input; any → `exited` when the process ends. Counted output in the 1 s after an applied resize is not activity.
- After each exit the manager closes the recording, writes meta.json, then calls `enforceCap({ isLive: (id) => live.has(id) })`; a session leaves the `live` map only after its recording is closed. An applied writer resize also calls `recorder.resize(cols, rows)`.

#### Stop and quit (S7): `soft-stop.js` and `manager.js`

- `soft-stop.js`: `SOFT_STOP_LIMIT_MS = 2000`; `OPENCLAW_STOP_NOTE = "Stopped the terminal. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step."`; `findBackgroundAgent(text, { agentSessionId, pid })` → `string | null` (accepts an array, `{ agents }` or `{ sessions }`, entries with `kind` or `type` `"background"`, matched by `id` / `sessionId` / `session_id` or `pid`; never an id starting with `-`); `runCli(command, args, { env, cwd, signal, onSpawn })` → `Promise<{ ok, code, aborted, stdout }>` (never rejects); `runSoftStop({ softStop, command, env, cwd, agentSessionId, pid, limitMs = 2000, run = runCli, onSpawn })` → `{ outcome: "none" | "terminal-only" | "stopped-background" | "failed" | "timeout", note: string | null }`.
- Stop sequence (never writes into the PTY): the soft stop with a hard 2 s limit for the whole step (Claude: `claude agents --json`, then `claude stop <id>` when this session is a background session; OpenClaw: no CLI call until spike S5, `note: OPENCLAW_STOP_NOTE`; others and `update` sessions: none), then `killTree(pid, { graceMs: STOP_GRACE_MS })`. Soft-stop CLI calls use the session's own `profile.env` and `profile.cwd` (Q11) and are `spawnTracked` children.
- `shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" })` writes `endedBy: "quit"` and `status: "exited"` into every live session's meta.json BEFORE any kill, then stops all sessions in parallel, capped at `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS`.

#### `routes.js`, `local-session.js`, `server/index.js` (S8)

- `server/runtime/local-session.js`: `export function isLocalMode()` (not the public demo, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH=1`, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE=1`) and `export function requireLocalMode(req, res, next)` → 404 `{ error: "not_available" }` outside local mode. Every sessions route and recordings route use it; the WebSocket (S9) cannot use Express middleware, so it calls `isLocalMode()` in its own upgrade check and answers 403.
- `createSessionsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {})` at `/api/sessions` and `createRecordingsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {})` at `/api/recordings`; fixed paths before `/:id`. Any `:id` failing `SESSION_ID_RE` is 404 `unknown_session` before anything else runs.

  | Method and path | Answer |
  |---|---|
  | `GET /api/sessions[?kind=all]` | 200 `{ sessions: SessionSummary[], environmentNotice: string \| null, pty: { ok: boolean, reason: string \| null }, maxLive: 8 }`; agent kind only unless `kind=all` (Q24); `environmentNotice` is `(await getLoginShellEnv()).notice`, `null` until the login shell has been read |
  | `POST /api/sessions` `{ agentId, folder }` | 201 `SessionSummary`; the manager's refusals with their own status |
  | `GET /api/sessions/folders` | 200 `{ folders: [{ path, name, lastUsedAt }] }` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/settings` | 200 `{ claudeFullscreen }` |
  | `PUT /api/sessions/settings` `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` | 200 the new settings; 400 `invalid_settings` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/quit-check` | 200 `{ live: [{ id, title, kind }] }` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/:id` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 404 `unknown_session` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/stop` | 200 `SessionSummary & { note: string \| null }`, bare (no wrapper object); an ended session answers its unchanged summary |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/resume` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 409 `not_resumable`, `session_live`, `execution_gate_off` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/dismiss` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 409 `session_live` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/:id/recording` | 200 `Content-Type: application/x-asciicast`, the lines of `openRecording(id)` (Q26); 404 `unknown_session`, `recording_missing` |
  | `DELETE /api/sessions/:id/recording` | 200 `{ ok: true }`; 409 `recording_live`; 404 `unknown_session`, `recording_missing` |
  | `GET /api/recordings` | 200 `{ recordings: RecordingSummary[], removedByCap: number }` |

  An unexpected error is 500 `internal_error`. The recordings routes pass the manager's `isLive` (`(id) => manager.isLive(id)`, ruling R8) to the recorder.
- `server/index.js`: a module-scope `const sessionManager = getSessionManager();`; the port is `parsePort(process.env.AGENT_OS_PORT ?? process.env.PORT)` (Q11a); right after `const envFile = loadLocalEnv({ root });` it calls `excludeFromSessionEnv(envFile.applied)`. Before `app.listen`: `sessionManager.recoverStaleSessions()` and `enforceRecordingCap()`, each in its own try/catch (a failure is logged, the server still starts; Q13). After `AGENT_OS_READY`, in local mode only, `getLoginShellEnv()` starts resolving and never delays READY (Q23).

#### `ws.js` and the WebSocket protocol (S9)

- `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES = 65536`.
- `CLOSE_CODES = { too_far_behind: 4000, session_ended: 4001, attach_failed: 4004 }`; the close reason text is the same word, and clients decide by the reason word, never the number (U1's `sessionCloseAdvice`). ws itself closes with 1009 when a message is over 1 MB.
- `allowedOrigins(port, env = process.env)`; `checkUpgradeRequest(req, { port })` → `{ ok: true, sessionId } | { ok: false, reason }` (pure; `reason` is for tests only, never sent or logged); `parseClientFrame(data, isBinary)` → `{ t: "focus" } | { t: "in", d } | { t: "resize", cols, rows } | { t: "ack", seq } | null`; `attachSessionsUpgrade(server, { getPort, manager })` installs the one `upgrade` listener.
- `scripts/dev-server.mjs` sets `process.env.AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN = "1"` and imports `server/index.js`; `npm run dev` = `concurrently "node --watch scripts/dev-server.mjs" "vite --host 127.0.0.1"`. `vite.config.ts`: the `/api` proxy gains `ws: true`.
- Upgrade (Security 1): path `/api/sessions/<id>/attach` checked lower-cased, no query string, Host allowlisted with the real bound port, Origin exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://localhost:<port>` (the Vite dev origin on 5173 only with `AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1`, ignored when `NODE_ENV=production` or `AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1`; `AGENT_OS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` never widens the Origin list), the session cookie compared with `timingSafeEqual`, local mode. An unknown id, an ended session (`manager.get(id)` says `exited`) and any other upgrade address are refused the same way: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`, socket destroyed.
- Frames (JSON text, one message per frame). Client → server: `{t:"focus"}` (makes this attachment the writer; the client sends `{t:"resize"}` right after), `{t:"in", d}` (writer only; the whole raw frame at most 64 KB), `{t:"resize", cols, rows}` (writer only, debounced 50 ms, cols 2-500, rows 1-200), `{t:"ack", seq}` (at least every 64 KB received and processed). A frame over 64 KB, a binary frame, non-JSON or an unknown frame is dropped without an answer; the socket stays open.
- Server → client, in this order on attach (the manager sends them; `ws.js` never sends a snapshot): `{t:"snapshot", data, cols, rows, modes}`, then `{t:"state", status, exitCode, signal, endedBy, resetAt}` (`exitCode`, `signal`, `endedBy` only with `exited`, `resetAt` only with `held` in SP4; the client reads a missing field as `null`), then the output and alerts that arrived while the snapshot was taken, then live `{t:"out", seq, d}` and `{t:"alert", raw}`. `seq` is the cumulative UTF-8 byte count of all `d` sent to this attachment, from 0 after its snapshot.
- Terminal queries: while a writer is attached only its browser terminal answers (viewers' replies are dropped); while none is attached the mirror answers DA1, DSR cursor position and kitty `CSI ? u`.
- Back-pressure, per attachment `lag = bytes sent - last acked seq`: pause the PTY only when every open attachment lags more than `PAUSE_LAG_BYTES`; resume when any one catches up; never pause with zero attachments; a closed attachment leaves the count at once; an attachment more than `CLOSE_LAG_BYTES` behind is closed with `too_far_behind`; a PTY paused for more than `PAUSED_DROP_MS` closes every attachment still over 512 KB behind with `too_far_behind`, so the PTY resumes. That timer is not cleared just because one attachment closes; it stops when the PTY resumes or the process exits.
- When `attach` fails after the upgrade, the socket closes with 4001 `session_ended` for a `session_ended` error and 4004 `attach_failed` otherwise. Stopping a session closes its attachments with `session_ended`. No shutdown task closes sockets.

#### Hold to stop all (S10, `src/ui/stopAllShared.ts` and `src/ui/stopAll.ts`)

- `interface StoppableSession { id: string; status: string; kind?: string; agentId?: string; agentLabel?: string; folderName?: string; folderShown?: boolean }` (a `SessionSummary` fits it).
- `StopAllDeps` gains `listSessions(): Promise<{ sessions: StoppableSession[] }>` (`GET /api/sessions?kind=all`) and `stopSession(id): Promise<unknown>` (`POST /api/sessions/:id/stop`), both kinds of session. `StopLook` gains `sessions` and `sessionsChecked`. `StopAllResult` gains `sessions`, `sessionsStopped`, `sessionsFailed`, `sessionsTimedOut`, `sessionsAlreadyEnded`, `sessionsChecked: boolean` and `openClawStopped`.
- `SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED = "session_already_ended"`; `withSessionAnswers(deps)` (a `not_available` list is empty; `unknown_session`, or a stop answer `{ status: "exited" }` with `endedBy !== "stop"`, is `SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED`); `thingsWord(runs, rooms, sessions = 0)`; `sessionStopTitle(session)` (the same words as `sessionTitle`).
- Sessions and rooms start together; runs follow the rooms and never wait for sessions. Never calls a service control (`adapter.service`, `POST /api/agents/:id/service/:action`).
- The palette item `stop-all` reads "Stop all agent work" and its dialog "Stop all agent work?"; the hold control keeps "Hold to stop all".

### Desktop shell (D1, `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`)

- Events: shell → page `"agentos://quit-requested"` (payload `null`); page → shell `"agentos://quit-shown"` (any payload) and `"agentos://quit-answer"` with `{ "quit": true | false }` (anything else ignored). `listen` and `emit` are in `core:default`; no custom command.
- The shell shows, unminimizes and focuses the main window before it emits `quit-requested`. No `quit-shown` within 2 s (`QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT`) means no window can ask: it quits. After `quit-shown` it waits for the answer with no time limit; another quit request while the question is open does nothing; a page load (`Builder::on_page_load`) drops an open question, so the next quit request asks again.
- Routes that ask: the "Quit Agent OS" item and ⌘Q, `RunEvent::ExitRequested` (last window destroyed, `app.exit()`), and closing the window on Windows and Linux. Routes that cannot ask (Q5a, Q5b): a termination signal to the app, the Dock's Quit, the app switcher's Quit, logout and the updater's restart; they run the graceful stdin stop without the question.
- macOS: `CloseRequested` → `prevent_close()` + `hide()`; `RunEvent::Reopen` → show + focus; the app menu item "Show Agent OS" (`agentos-show`, no accelerator) does the same.
- Menu ids: `"agentos-quit"` ("Quit Agent OS"; accelerator `CmdOrCtrl+Q` on macOS only), `"agentos-show"`; `"reload"` stays. Windows and Linux: Reload has no accelerator, and the predefined Edit, Window and Hide items are left out (their Ctrl accelerators cannot be removed).
- Server: `spawn_server` sets `AGENT_OS_PORT=0` (never `PORT`), `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1` and `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` (the app's own `PATH`, `env::var_os("PATH").unwrap_or_default()`, empty when it had none; S2's login-shell read starts the shell with it, H2, Q11a). The server's own `PATH` stays `server_path_env()`. Its stdin is piped and kept open for the app's whole life. On quit it writes `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n`, waits up to `QUIT_GRACE` (10 s), then forces the server at once (SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows); if the line cannot be written, unix sends SIGTERM at once.
- `tauri_plugin_dialog::init()` is registered; `"dialog:allow-open"` is last in the pinned permissions of `capabilities/default.json` and `test/release-config.test.js`; the capability description names quit and the folder picker. The opener scope stays as the owner approved (commit `8264b2b`).
- Rust unit tests: `cargo test --locked` in `desktop/src-tauri` (18 tests; 15 on Windows).

- `scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs`: `parseTargetArgs(argv, { platform = process.platform, arch = process.arch } = {})` → `{ platform, arch }`; `binaryArches(buffer)` → `("x64" | "arm64")[]` (reads the Mach-O, ELF or PE header); `copyNodePty({ from, to, platform, arch })` → `{ prebuild: "<platform>-<arch>", files: string[], bytes: number }`.

#### `src/sessionsApi.ts` (U1)

- `SESSION_LIMITS_MS` (every call has its own time limit; a time limit rejects with `new Error("Agent OS did not answer in time.")`). Refusals are the existing `ApiError` (`message` = the server's code, `detail` = its sentence).
- `listSessions(): Promise<SessionListResponse>`, `createSession({ agentId, folder }: { agentId: string; folder: string | null }): Promise<SessionSummary>` (no `confirm`), `stopSession(id): Promise<StopSessionResult>`, `resumeSession(id)`, `dismissSession(id): Promise<SessionSummary>`, `getSessionSettings()`, `putSessionSettings(patch: Partial<SessionSettings>): Promise<SessionSettings>`, `listSessionFolders(): Promise<SessionFolderList>`, `quitCheck(): Promise<QuitCheckResponse>`, `listRecordings(): Promise<RecordingListResponse>`, `deleteRecording(id): Promise<{ ok: true }>`; `sessionProblem(error)`, `sessionGotNoAnswer(error)`, `sessionSocketUrl(id)`.
- `openSessionSocket(id, { onSnapshot, onOut, onState, onAlert, onClose })` → `{ focus(), input(data), resize(cols, rows), close() }`. A promise returned by `onSnapshot` holds later frames; a promise returned by `onOut` counts its bytes as processed when it settles; `input` splits data into frames of at most 64 KB (JSON and all) without breaking a character; `ack` at least every 64 KB processed. `onClose({ code, reason, hadSnapshot, advice })`, `advice: "reattach" | "ended" | "wait"` (`too_far_behind` → reattach; `session_ended` → ended; `attach_failed` or 1009 → wait; anything else → reattach).

### Tests and fakes (W1, and every task)

- `npm test` = `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`: with no arguments it runs `test/*.test.js` (never `test/helpers/` or `test/fakes/`); arguments starting with `-` go to `node --test` (`--flag=value` form), others replace the file list. It removes `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV`, `BASH_ENV` and `HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS` (detection's extra folders, searched before `PATH`) and sets `SHELL` to `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` for the whole run (not on Windows). A clean run ends `no-real-agents watcher: no real agent started (<n> checks)`; on Windows it prints `no-real-agents watcher: not available on Windows`.
- `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js`: `AGENT_NAMES`, `REAL_AGENT_PATHS`, `defaultAllowedRoots()`, `parsePsRows(text)`, `readPsRows()`, `isAllowedBinary(token, allowedRoots?)`, `findViolations(rows, { baseline, rootPid, seenDescendants, allowedRoots, names })` → `[{ pid, ppid, name, binary, command, testFile }]`, `startWatcher({ rootPid, intervalMs = 200, onViolation, allowedRoots, names, kill = true })` → `Promise<{ stop() }>`.
- `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`: `FAKE_AGENT_NAMES` (`claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw`), `FAKE_AGENT_MODES` (`tui`, `setsid-grandchild`, `ignore-term`, `agents-hang`, `updater`), `FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT`, `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, mode = "tui" } = {})` → `Promise<{ dir, script, paths }>` (POSIX `#!/bin/sh` shims that exec this Node on `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`; `FAKE_AGENT_MODE` in the environment wins over `mode`), `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` (the absolute path of `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`).
- `test/fakes/login-shell.sh` (0755): started as `<it> -i -l -c <command>`, runs the command with `/bin/sh -c`, reads no startup file and keeps PATH exactly as given.
- `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`:
  - one-shot answers (no terminal): `--version`, `--help`, `auth status`, `login status`, `status`, `doctor`, `config get`, `gateway status`; `gateway start|stop|restart` logged as `{ event: "gateway", args }`; `claude agents …` prints `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON` or `[]` (never answers in mode `agents-hang`); `claude stop <id>` prints `stopped <id>`;
  - a headless run (`-p`, `--print` or `exec` anywhere in argv; no session argv has these) prints nothing, is logged as `{ event: "run", args }` and keeps running until it is stopped (at most 5 minutes);
  - any other argv starts the terminal program: the line `FAKE_ARGV <json>` (`{ name, mode, argv, cwd, isTTY, env, agentOsKeys, secretKeys }`), then the prompt `> `;
  - typed commands: `alt on|off`, `paste on|off`, `mouse on|off`, `focus on|off`, `keys app|normal`, `kitty on|off`, `bell`, `osc9`, `osc9st`, `osc99`, `osc777`, `title`, `ask`, `ask after <ms>`, `ask kitty`, `ask color`, `lines <n>`, `flood <KiB>`, `bottom <text>`, `ticker <ms> <count>`, `exit <code>`; anything else prints `you said: <text>`. Replies and focus reports print `REPLY <json>`, a bracketed paste prints `PASTE <json>` (the pasted text), other escape sequences `KEY <json>`; Ctrl+C exits 130; the end of stdin exits 0;
  - environment: `FAKE_AGENT_MODE`, `FAKE_AGENT_LOG` (one JSON line per event, each with `name`, `pid`, `at`: `start`, `line` (each typed line, with `text`), `paste` with `text`, `reply`, `key`, `grandchild`, `agents`, `stop`, `gateway`, `run`, `sigterm` with `snapshot` (or `snapshotError`)), `FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE` (mode `setsid-grandchild` writes the grandchild's pid there and prints `GRANDCHILD:<pid>`), `FAKE_AGENT_GRANDCHILD_IGNORE_TERM`, `FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM` (the literal `{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}` in it is replaced with the fake's own `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID`), `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON`;
  - modes: `setsid-grandchild`, `ignore-term` (survives SIGTERM), `agents-hang`, `updater` (asks `Update now? [y/N] `, prints `ANSWER <text>`, exits 0 for y and 1 otherwise).
- `SHELL` in tests (Q1c): `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` is the only `SHELL` any test uses, including every test that starts `server/index.js` (it sets `SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` explicitly, so a single file run with `node --test` is safe) and the environment handed to a fake agent in a PTY. Never `SHELL=/bin/sh`. The only exceptions are the S2 and S8 tests whose subject is a slow, noisy or failing login shell (they pass their own fake shell), and S3's profile tests, which use a wrapper that only exports variables and puts a PATH folder first before it execs `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` (plus a missing shell for its fallback test).
- `PATH` in a test that can start a session (Q1c): the fake bin folder (all six names) plus `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, nothing else, and `HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS` unset in that test's environment (S8's and S9's `CLEARED_KEYS`, S10's end-to-end test, E1's smoke).
- Temp `HOME`, `USERPROFILE` and `AGENT_OS_HOME` in tests only (real paths: on macOS `os.tmpdir()` sits behind a symlink, so tests use its realpath).
- UI audit harness (`.superpowers/ui-audit/`, git-ignored): `audit.mjs` starts its throwaway server on :8791 with `SHELL` = `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`, a real-path temp HOME passed to probes, and `fake-bin/` holding the six `makeFakeAgentBin` shims, so sessions in probes behave like TUIs (U1 sets this up with the first session probe; U3 and U4 reuse it). `fake-bin/` is an allowed root of the watcher.

## Plan brains: shared names, constraints and review focus (Tasks B1a to E3)

Every plan-brains task uses these names, paths, signatures and shapes exactly. A task's Interfaces quote from this file; where a task's text and this file differ, this file is right and the task is fixed before it is dispatched. The binding spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-plan-brains-design.md` (owner-approved 2026-10-15; the owner kept the risk tick, the two Hermes warning lines and the Fable usage-credits note); "§n" below means its section n. Everything named in `00-contract.md` (for example `sessionError`, `errorBody`, `requireLocalMode`, `SessionSummary`, `SESSION_LIMITS_MS`, `withTimeout`, `SessionTerminal`, `makeFakeAgentBin`, `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`) keeps its name and shape; this file adds to it and renames nothing. Line numbers are HEAD `a6c9f4a`; U3 and U4 move some UI lines, so tasks anchor UI edits on quoted text.

### Shared names and shapes (plan brains)

#### Files on disk

| none for a `setup` session: no `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/sessions/<id>/`, no `meta.json`, no `screen.cast` | | B1a (never written) |
| `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/setup/terminal/<name>-<8 hex>.command`, content exactly the command line plus `"\n"`; `<name>` is `<agentId>-login` (sign-in, unchanged) or `hermes-model` (Hermes picker); swept after one hour as today | 0700 | B1c (`openCommandInTerminal`) |
| `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/setup/jobs/<id>.json` for a plan job (every field of the job object below) | as today | B1b |
| receipt entries (existing `appendReceiptEntry`) with `provider: "claude-plan" \| "chatgpt-plan"`, `action: "configure"` | as today | B1b |

| 409 | `{ error: "setup_running", message: "A ChatGPT sign-in is already open in Agent OS.", sessionId: "<uuid>", setupAction: "openclaw-chatgpt-signin" }` | `POST signin-terminal` | B1a |

- B1a answers its session refusals with `res.status(err.status).json(errorBody(err))` (`server/runtime/sessions/errors.js`), never through `mapJobError`, which drops extra fields.
- B1b adds `plan_not_ready: 409` to `mapJobError`'s table and `plan_not_ready` to `MESSAGE_CODES` (`invalid_model_id` is already in both).

#### The `setup` session kind (B1a; consumed by B2, E1)

`server/runtime/sessions/profiles.js`:
- `export const OPENCLAW_SIGNIN_ACTION = "openclaw-chatgpt-signin";`
- `export const SETUP_ACTIONS = Object.freeze({ "openclaw-chatgpt-signin": Object.freeze({ agentId: "openclaw", args: Object.freeze(["models", "auth", "login", "--provider", "openai", "--method", "siwc"]) }) });` Every per-action lookup uses `Object.hasOwn`.
- `buildSessionProfile({ agentId, folder, sessionId, kind = "agent", resume = null, settings, detected, brain = null, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION, setupAction = null } = {})`. Kind `"setup"`: `setupAction` must be an own key of `SETUP_ACTIONS` whose `agentId` equals `agentId`, else 400 `unknown_kind` ("Agent OS can't start that kind of session."); no folder check; `cwd = os.homedir()`; `folderShown: false`; `args` a fresh copy of the action's args; `agentSessionId: null`, `settingsFile: null`, `softStop: null` (never `"openclaw-abort"`), `resumeMode: null`; `env` exactly as every kind (`sessionEnv(...)`, then `PWD = cwd`); `resume` is ignored. Any other kind name still answers `unknown_kind`.
- `assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args, { kind = "agent", setupAction = null } = {})`: for `kind: "setup"` the only accepted argv is exactly the action's args, item by item; every other kind keeps today's `SHAPES`. `SHAPES.openclaw` is unchanged, so an `agent` session can never run the sign-in argv. Two-argument callers are unchanged.

`server/runtime/sessions/manager.js`:
- `createSetupSession({ action, detected } = {})` → `Promise<SessionSummary>`. Its own start path (`startNew` is unchanged and still makes only `agent` and `update`). In order: `action` must be an own key of `SETUP_ACTIONS` (else 400 `unknown_kind`); the session id (`crypto.randomUUID()`) is made first; the setup slot is reserved under that id (409 `setup_running` with `{ sessionId, setupAction }` of the live or reserved setup session); `requirePty()` (503); `detected` defaults to `detect(agentId)`; `buildProfile({ agentId: "openclaw", folder: null, sessionId: id, kind: "setup", setupAction: action, settings: { claudeFullscreen: false }, detected })`; no Safety gate, no folder policy, no brain, no `ensurePrivateDir`, no `readGitBranch`, no `saveStarted` or `persist`; `recorderFactory` is never called (a private no-op recorder stands in); then the process starts and the summary is returned.
- `liveSetupSession()` → `Promise<SessionSummary | null>`: the setup session in `live` whose status is not `"exited"`, else `null` (a start still between reservation and spawn is `null`).
- The setup slot never touches `reservedAgents` or `liveCount("agent")`, so a setup session is never counted toward `maxLive`.
- `onProcessExit` for a setup session: `mirror.dispose()` as today, then it leaves `live` at once; no `recorder.close()`, no `persist`, no `enforceCap`.
- `write(id, attachmentId, data)` for a setup session writes the bytes to the PTY and runs no `isUserInput` scan and no `markActive` (input is never parsed; activity comes from output only). `resize` never reaches a recorder for it.
- `quitCheck()` leaves out `kind: "setup"`. `shutdownAll()` writes no meta for a setup session but still stops it inside the 7 s guard. `stop`, `list`, `get`, `resume`, `dismiss`, `recoverStaleSessions` and `ws.js` need no change: `GET /api/sessions?kind=all` (and `&live=1`) lists a live setup session; after it ends, `GET /api/sessions/:id`, stop, resume and dismiss answer 404 `unknown_session`, and the WebSocket upgrade is a bare 403.
- `SETUP_RUNNING_MESSAGE = "A ChatGPT sign-in is already open in Agent OS."` (private constant; the sentence is contract).

A setup session's `SessionSummary` (the same 20 keys, no new key; `setupAction` is only on the 409 body):
`{ id, kind: "setup", agentId: "openclaw", agentLabel: "OpenClaw", folder: <os.homedir()>, folderName: <basename of HOME>, folderShown: false, branch: null, status, stateSince, startedAt, endedAt, exitCode, signal, endedBy, dismissed: false, brain: null, resume: { available: false, reason: null, fallback: false }, alerts: "basic", recordingBytes: 0 }`

#### The OpenClaw version gate (B1a; consumed by B1b, B2)

- `server/runtime/builders/resolve.js`: `export function parseVersion(text)` → `[major, minor, patch] | null` and `export function versionAtLeast(have, need)` (both take arrays), bodies unchanged.
- New `server/runtime/setup/openclaw-version.js`:
  - `export const OPENCLAW_SIGNIN_MIN_VERSION = "2026.9.7";`
  - `export const OPENCLAW_TOO_OLD_MESSAGE = "Update OpenClaw first: its ChatGPT sign-in needs version 2026.9.7 or newer.";`
  - `export const OPENCLAW_VERSION_UNKNOWN_MESSAGE = "Agent OS couldn't read OpenClaw's version.";`
  - `export function openclawVersionInfo(detected)` → `{ have: string | null, need: "2026.9.7", newEnough: boolean | null }`. `have` is the three parsed numbers joined with "." (`"OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac)"` gives `"2026.9.6"`), `null` when OpenClaw is not installed or `parseVersion(detected.version)` is null; `newEnough` is `null` exactly when `have` is.
- Every caller reads `ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true })` (never the 30 s detect cache or the 60 s system check), so an update installed a moment ago is seen.

| `POST /api/setup/openclaw/signin-terminal` `{ confirm: true }` | 201 `{ session: SessionSummary }`. Order: local mode, confirm, detect (refresh), not installed 409 `agent_not_installed`, version unreadable 409 `openclaw_version_unknown`, too old 409 `openclaw_too_old`, then `createSetupSession({ action: "openclaw-chatgpt-signin", detected })` (409 `setup_running`, 503 `pty_unavailable`, other `sessionError`s with their own status) | B1a |

| `POST /api/setup/openclaw/plan` `{ plan, model, confirm: true, acceptOpenClawRisk }` | 200 the `SetupJob` (status `"running"`), like `POST /api/setup/configure`. Order: local mode, confirm, plan value, then `startOpenclawPlanJob` | B1b |
| `POST /api/setup/hermes/model-terminal` `{ confirm: true }` | 200 `{ opened: boolean, command: string, reason?: "copy" \| "spawn_failed" }` | B1c |

`POST /api/setup/configure` keeps refusing `claude-plan` and `chatgpt-plan` (`parseConfigureBody` and `normalizeTarget` unchanged); B1b tests it.

Spec §7 shapes, verbatim in shape:
- `OpenclawPlansAnswer = { version: { have: string | null, need: "2026.9.7", newEnough: boolean | null }, claude: { installed: boolean, status: "signed_in" | "not_signed_in" | "unknown", method: string | null, note: string }, chatgpt: { signedIn: boolean | null, sharing: boolean | null, readiness: "ready" | "expiring" | "not_ready" | null } }`. `claude` comes from `signInStatus("claude")`; `readiness` is non-null only while OpenClaw is on the ChatGPT plan (`planOfPrimary(...) === "chatgpt"`); OpenClaw not installed gives `version.have: null` and every `chatgpt` field `null`.
- `PlanModelsAnswer = { models: [{ id: string, name: string, note: string | null, available: boolean }], source: "account" | "fallback", asOf: "2026-10-15" | null }`. `id` has no provider prefix; `note` is `FABLE_NOTE` for a `claude-fable-` id, else `null`; `available` is false only for a Claude plan model the runtime check would reject once any `claude-cli` pin exists; `asOf` is `"2026-10-15"` with the fallback and `null` with the account list.

#### OpenClaw plans on the server (B1b; consumed by B2)

New `server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plan-rules.js` (pure: no imports, no I/O; parsers take values already parsed by `parseJsonOutput`):
- `OPENCLAW_PLANS = ["claude", "chatgpt"]`; `PLAN_PROVIDER = { claude: "anthropic", chatgpt: "openai" }`; `PLAN_MODE = { claude: "claude-plan", chatgpt: "chatgpt-plan" }`; `PLAN_MODELS_AS_OF = "2026-10-15"`; `PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000` (`models list`, `models auth list`, `models status`; `config get` keeps `CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- `PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS = { claude: ["claude-opus-5-5", "claude-sonnet-5-5", "claude-haiku-5-5", "claude-fable-5-1"], chatgpt: ["gpt-6.1-sol", "gpt-6-sol", "gpt-6-luna"] }`.
- `PLAN_MODEL_NAMES = { "claude-opus-5-5": "Opus 5.5", "claude-sonnet-5-5": "Sonnet 5.5", "claude-haiku-5-5": "Haiku 5.5", "claude-fable-5-1": "Fable 5.1", "gpt-6.1-sol": "GPT-6.1 Sol", "gpt-6-sol": "GPT-6 Sol", "gpt-6-luna": "GPT-6 Luna" }`.
- `TYPED_MODEL_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._:-]{0,99}$/`.
- `FABLE_NOTE = "Uses usage credits: on Pro from the first request, on Max after half your weekly limit."`; `isFableModel(id)` → `/^claude-fable-/i`.
- `CLAUDE_PLAN_METHODS = ["claude.ai", "oauth_token"]`; `CLAUDE_API_METHODS = ["api_key", "api_key_helper", "third_party"]`.
- `planModelRows(value, plan)` → `Array<{ id, name }> | null`: an array or `{ models: [...] }`; id from `key`, else `id` (strings only); a leading `<PLAN_PROVIDER[plan]>/` is stripped; a row whose id still holds a `/` (another provider) is dropped; rows deduped by id ignoring letter case (first wins); name from the row's `name`, else `PLAN_MODEL_NAMES[id]`, else the id; unknown fields ignored; any other shape or an empty result is `null` ("cannot be read").
- `hasClaudeCliPin(modelsConfig)` → boolean (any entry with `agentRuntime.id === "claude-cli"`); `claudeCliPinned(modelsConfig, id)` → boolean: `anthropic/<id>`'s entry has `agentRuntime.id === "claude-cli"`, or that entry has no `agentRuntime` of its own (or is absent) and `anthropic/*` has `agentRuntime.id === "claude-cli"`.
- `claudePlanReadiness({ installed, status, method })` → `"ready" | "not_installed" | "not_signed_in" | "api_billing" | "unknown_method"`: not installed; status `"not_signed_in"`; method in `CLAUDE_API_METHODS`; method `null` (or status `"unknown"` while installed); else ready.
- `parseAuthRows(value)` → `Array<{ method: string | null, sharing: boolean | null }> | null`: an array or `{ profiles: [...] }`; `method` from `method`, else `type`; `sharing` from a boolean `tokenSharing`, else `null`; rows with a `provider` other than `"openai"` dropped; every other field dropped (provisional names until S-B3).
- `chatgptSignIn(rows)` → `{ signedIn: boolean | null, sharing: boolean | null }`: `rows === null` gives both `null`; a row with method `"siwc"` gives `signedIn: true` and `sharing` true if any siwc row is true, false if any is false, else `null`; otherwise `{ signedIn: false, sharing: null }`.
- `readinessOf(result)` → `"ready" | "expiring" | "not_ready"` from a `runCommand` answer: `ok === true` is ready; `!ok && code === 2 && !signal` is expiring; anything else (a timeout is `{ ok: false, code: 0, signal: "SIGTERM" }`) is not ready.
- `planOfPrimary(primary, modelsConfig, signedInWithChatgpt)` → `"claude" | "chatgpt" | null`: a primary containing `@` is never a plan; `anthropic/<id>` with `claudeCliPinned` is `"claude"`; `openai/<id>` with `signedInWithChatgpt === true` is `"chatgpt"`.
- `openclawProviderLabel(provider, plan)` → `"Claude plan" | "Anthropic API key" | "ChatGPT plan" | "OpenAI" | null` (`null` for other providers, which keep today's labels).
- `PLAN_NOT_READY_MESSAGE = { openclaw_missing: "Install OpenClaw first.", not_installed: "Install Claude Code first.", not_signed_in: "Sign in to Claude Code first, then try again.", api_billing: "Claude Code uses an API key or a cloud account, not your Claude plan, so OpenClaw would bill that instead.", unknown_method: "Agent OS couldn't tell how Claude Code is signed in. Update Claude Code, then check again.", chatgpt_signed_out: "Sign in with ChatGPT first, then try again." }`.
- `RUNTIME_CHECK_FAILED = "OpenClaw would use an Anthropic API key for this model, not your Claude plan."`; `CHATGPT_EXPIRING = "Your ChatGPT sign-in expires soon. Sign in again."`; `CHATGPT_NOT_READY = "OpenClaw can't use your ChatGPT plan yet. Sign in again, and allow token sharing when ChatGPT asks."`; `INVALID_PLAN_MODEL = "That doesn't look like a model name."`; `PLAN_JOB_INTERRUPTED = "Agent OS quit before this finished. Apply the plan again."`; `noEarlierPrimary(ref)` → `` `OpenClaw had no model set before, so it keeps ${ref}.` ``.

New `server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plans.js` (async readers; imports `models.js`, `signin.js`, `openclaw-version.js`, the rules and `runCommand`; never imported by `models.js`, so there is no cycle):
- `readOpenclawModelsConfig(detected)` → `Promise<object | null>` (`config get agents.defaults.models --json`; a plain object or `null`).
- `readChatgptAuth(detected)` → `Promise<{ signedIn, sharing }>` (`models auth list --provider openai --json` through `runCommand`; output kept only as `parseAuthRows` rows).
- `readChatgptReadiness(detected)` → `Promise<"ready" | "expiring" | "not_ready">` (`models status --check --plain` through `runCommand`; exit code only, output discarded).
- `readOpenclawPlans()` → `Promise<OpenclawPlansAnswer>` (Claude and OpenClaw reads in parallel).
- `readPlanModels(plan, { detected } = {})` → `Promise<PlanModelsAnswer>` (`models list --provider <anthropic|openai> --json`; for `claude` also `readOpenclawModelsConfig` for `available`).
- `resolvePlanModel(plan, model, { detected } = {})` → `Promise<string>` (the id to apply): the list is read again; a name equal to a listed id ignoring letter case gives the list's own id; otherwise a leading `<provider>/` matching the plan is stripped and the rest must match `TYPED_MODEL_RE`, and is accepted only while the list is the fallback; else throws `invalid_model_id` with `INVALID_PLAN_MODEL`.

`server/runtime/setup/signin.js` (B1b): `signInStatus(agentId)` → today's object plus `method: string | null` on every answer: for `claude`, the parsed `authMethod` when it is a key of `CLAUDE_METHOD_NOTE`, else `null`; always `null` for `codex`, `cursor` and when not installed. `interpretStatus` keeps returning only `{ status, note }`.

`server/runtime/setup/models.js` (B1b): `readAgentModel("openclaw", detected)` → today's object plus `plan: "claude" | "chatgpt" | null` on every OpenClaw answer (installed or not, known or not), and `providerLabel` from `openclawProviderLabel` for `anthropic` and `openai` primaries. It reads `config get agents.defaults.models --json` for an `anthropic/` primary and `models auth list --provider openai --json` for an `openai/` primary, through `runCommand`, using the pure rules (it never imports `openclaw-plans.js`). Hermes's answer is unchanged (no `plan` key).

`server/runtime/setup/jobs.js` (B1b):
- `export async function startOpenclawPlanJob({ plan, model, acceptOpenClawRisk })` → `Promise<SetupJob>`. First line: `acceptOpenClawRisk !== true` throws `openclaw_risk_not_accepted` before anything runs. Then inside `withJobLock`: detect OpenClaw (not installed: `plan_not_ready`, `openclaw_missing`); readiness read again here, never trusted from the card (`claude`: `claudePlanReadiness(signInStatus("claude"))` must be `"ready"`; `chatgpt`: `readChatgptAuth(...).signedIn === true`), else 409 `plan_not_ready` with the matching `PLAN_NOT_READY_MESSAGE`; `resolvePlanModel`; then the job starts. Any plan value other than `"claude"` or `"chatgpt"` throws a `TypeError` (the route refuses it first).
- `export const PLAN_JOB_STEPS = { claude: ["openclaw-plan-onboard", "openclaw-safe-defaults", "openclaw-plan-runtime-check", "openclaw-plan-model", "services", "health"], chatgpt: ["openclaw-plan-model", "openclaw-safe-defaults", "openclaw-plan-readiness", "health"] }` (all with `agentId: "openclaw"` except `services` and `health`, which keep `null`).
  - `openclaw-plan-onboard`: `onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice anthropic-cli` plus today's optional flags, all checked against `onboard --help` as today; through `runConfigureCommand`.
  - `openclaw-plan-runtime-check`: `readOpenclawModelsConfig` then `claudeCliPinned(config, model)`; false fails the step and the job with `RUNTIME_CHECK_FAILED`.
  - `openclaw-plan-model`: `models set anthropic/<id>` or `models set openai/<id>` through `runConfigureCommand`; for `chatgpt` it first reads the current primary (`config get agents.defaults.model.primary`, `parseConfigText`) into `job.previousPrimary`.
  - `openclaw-plan-readiness`: `readChatgptReadiness`; `"expiring"` pushes `CHATGPT_EXPIRING` onto `step.warnings` and goes on; `"not_ready"` runs `models set <job.previousPrimary>` when there was one (logged on the step), or pushes `noEarlierPrimary("openai/<id>")` onto `step.warnings` when there was none, then fails the step and the job with `CHATGPT_NOT_READY`.
  - `openclaw-safe-defaults`, `services` and `health` are today's steps. `health` treats a plan job like a `kind: "model"` job: a fresh OpenClaw conversation and the 90 s cap (`MODEL_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- The plan job object (persisted and returned): `{ id, kind: "configure", status, plan: "claude" | "chatgpt", mode: "claude-plan" | "chatgpt-plan", model: <id>, targets: { hermes: null, openclaw: { mode, model: <id> } }, scope: ["openclaw"], steps, currentStepIndex, startedAt, endedAt, acceptOpenClawRisk: true, acceptOpenClawRiskAt, previousPrimary: string | null, readiness: "ready" | "expiring" | "not_ready" | null, execModeChanged?, servicesStarted?, health? }`. It never holds command output, an e-mail or anything from `auth list` or `models status` beyond `readiness`.
- Receipt on success: `{ agentId: "openclaw", action: "configure", version, provider: "claude-plan" | "chatgpt-plan", model: <id>, changes: ["Set the model provider to <mode>", "Set the model to <id>", ...today's exec-mode and gateway lines] }`.
- `getSetupJob(id)`: a stored plan job (`plan` set) whose status is `"running"` but which is not in `activeJobs` (Agent OS quit while it ran) is answered, and saved, as `status: "failed"` with its current step failed and `PLAN_JOB_INTERRUPTED` as that step's `error`. `activeJobs` is set before the job's first `persistJob`.
- `retrySetupJob` keeps refusing every configure job (plan jobs included); the card's way back is Apply again.
- `export function healthFixLine(output, target, timedOut)` (now exported, same signature). For `target.mode` `claude-plan` and `chatgpt-plan`, in this order: `/usage limit|limit reached|rate.?limit|\b429\b|quota/i` gives "Your plan's usage limit is used up. Try again after it resets."; `/not (logged|signed) in|\/login|\b401\b|unauthori[sz]ed|expired/i` gives "OpenClaw isn't signed in to your plan anymore. Sign in again."; today's network pattern gives "Couldn't reach Anthropic." (`claude-plan`) or "Couldn't reach OpenAI." (`chatgpt-plan`); `timedOut` gives "The agent didn't answer within a minute. Try again."; anything else gives today's last sentence. `openrouter` and `ollama` keep today's order and words.

#### Terminal.app launches (B1c; consumed by B2)

`server/runtime/setup/signin.js`:
- `export async function openCommandInTerminal(binPath, args, { name, platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {})` → `{ opened: true, command } | { opened: false, reason: "spawn_failed", command } | { opened: false, reason: "copy", command }`. `command = loginCommandLine(binPath, args, platform)`; any `platform !== "darwin"` answers `"copy"` with no file and no spawn; on macOS it sweeps old files, writes `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/setup/terminal/<name>-<8 hex>.command` (content `command + "\n"`, mode 0o700) and calls exactly `spawnFn("open", ["-a", "Terminal", file], { stdio: "ignore", detached: true, shell: false })`. `name` must match `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$/`, else `TypeError`. No `readFile`, `createReadStream`, `openSync` or quoted agent-folder piece (the existing source scan).
- `openSignInInTerminal(agentId, { platform, spawnFn })` keeps its signature and answers, and calls `openCommandInTerminal(detected.path, def.loginArgs, { name: `${agentId}-login`, platform, spawnFn })`.

New `server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js`:
- `export const HERMES_MODEL_ARGS = Object.freeze(["model"]);` `export const HERMES_TERMINAL_NAME = "hermes-model";`
- `export async function openHermesModelTerminal({ platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {})` → the same three shapes. Hermes's path comes from `ADAPTERS.hermes.detect({ refresh: true })`; not installed throws an error with `code: "agent_not_installed"` (the route answers 400). Nothing from the request reaches the file or the argv. It never calls the session manager.

#### Fakes and knobs

- **Knob rule (every fake):** a knob `FAKE_X` is read from `process.env.FAKE_X`; when that is unset, from the trimmed text of `$HOME/.fake-knobs/FAKE_X` when that file exists. The file form is needed because `childEnv` (used by `signInStatus` and the run manager) passes only an allow list and drops `FAKE_*` variables.
- **State file:** `$HOME/.fake-agent-state.json` = `{ primary: string | null, models: object | null, authRows: object[] }` (the spec's `FAKE_AGENT_STATE`). `tools.exec.mode` stays in today's `$HOME/.fake-openclaw-exec-mode` (missing means `full`, empty means unset) so the earlier tests stay unchanged.
- `test/helpers/fake-knobs.js` (B1a): `FAKE_KNOBS_DIR = ".fake-knobs"`, `FAKE_AGENT_STATE_FILE = ".fake-agent-state.json"`, `setFakeKnob(home, name, value: string | null)` (null removes it), `readFakeAgentState(home)`, `writeFakeAgentState(home, state)`.
- `FAKE_AGENT_VERSION`: the whole first line `--version` prints, verbatim (tests use `OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac)`, `OpenClaw 2026.9.7`, `OpenClaw 2026.10.1` and `OpenClaw unknown`). Unset keeps today's lines. W1's TUI fake applies it only under the name `openclaw` (B1a); the setup-brain OpenClaw fake applies it too (B1b).
- W1's TUI fake, `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs` (B1a): the argv `models auth login --provider openai --method siwc` (chosen by argv; no new `FAKE_AGENT_MODE`) runs the sign-in program: without a TTY it prints `This command needs a terminal.` and exits 1; otherwise it logs the usual `start` record and prints `Sign in with ChatGPT: https://auth.openai.com/fake-signin?state=agentos-test`, `Code: FAKE-1234` and `Press Enter after you approve in your browser.`; on a typed line it appends `{ provider: "openai", method: "siwc", tokenSharing: true, email: "someone@example.com" }` to the state file's `authRows`, prints `Signed in.` and exits 0; Ctrl+C exits 130. Its env record (`SHOWN_ENV`) gains `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR`, and the record gains `openclawKeys` (the names of every `OPENCLAW_*` variable present).
- W1's TUI fake also logs a `probe` record (B1a; added by the controller on 2026-10-16 from B1a's Interfaces): under the name `openclaw` only, `answer()` first logs `{ event: "probe", ...the start record's fields }` (`name`, `mode`, `argv`, `cwd`, `isTTY`, `env`, `agentOsKeys`, `openclawKeys`, `secretKeys`), so every quick answer (`--version`, `--help`, the status questions, the sign-in's no-terminal refusal) is in `FAKE_AGENT_LOG`; no other name logs one. Safety 3 and 4 checks in B1a, B1b, B1c and E1 run over every `start` and `probe` record.
- `test/helpers/fake-openclaw.js` (B1b): `FAKE_OPENCLAW_CLI_SOURCE` and `installFakeOpenclawShim(home)` moved from `test/setup-brain.test.js` (same signature), plus `FAKE_CLAUDE_CLI_PINS = ["claude-opus-5-5", "claude-fable-5-1"]` and `FAKE_SECRET = "SECRET-fake-0000"`. New answers: `config get agents.defaults.model.primary` prints `primary`; `config get agents.defaults.models --json` prints `JSON.stringify(models)` (empty line when null); `models set <ref>` saves `primary`; `onboard ... --auth-choice anthropic-cli` adds `{ "anthropic/<id>": { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } } }` for each `FAKE_CLAUDE_CLI_PINS` id and no `anthropic/*` entry; `models list --provider <p> --json` prints `FAKE_OPENCLAW_MODELS_JSON` verbatim (`fail` = a stderr line and exit 1), else the default list (anthropic: opus-5-5, sonnet-5-5, fable-5-1 as `{ models: [{ key: "anthropic/<id>", name }] }`; openai: gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-luna); `models auth list --provider openai --json` prints `FAKE_OPENCLAW_AUTH_JSON` verbatim (`fail` = exit 1), else `JSON.stringify(authRows)`; `models status --check --plain` prints a line holding `FAKE_SECRET` and exits `FAKE_OPENCLAW_STATUS_EXIT` (0, 1 or 2; unset 0). Its record line gains `home` (the `HOME` it saw) and `setVars` (which of `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME` and any `OPENCLAW_*` reached it).
- `test/helpers/fake-builder-clis.js` (B1b): `FAKE_AGENT_CLI_SOURCE`, `shimText(jsPath, kind)` moved from `test/setup-builders.test.js`, plus `writeFakeAgentCli(dir)` → `Promise<string>` (the `.mjs` path) and `installFakeAgent(home, kind, jsPath)`. `claude auth status` prints `FAKE_CLAUDE_AUTH_JSON` verbatim when set and exits 0 when it parses with `loggedIn: true`, else 1; unset keeps today's markers. Every call also appends `{ kind, args, home, setVars }` to `$HOME/.fake-agent-env.jsonl`.
- Test rows the knobs carry: auth rows with `email: "someone@example.com"` and `accessToken: FAKE_SECRET`, so tests prove both are dropped; 2026.9.6-style rows carry only `type`.
