```js
test("SIGTERM is logged with a snapshot of the session's file, then ends the fake by that signal; mode ignore-term survives it", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  await withBin({}, async (bin, dir) => {
    const log = path.join(dir, "fake.log");
    // Task S8's quit test learns the session id only after the session starts,
    // so it names the file with a placeholder that the fake fills in from its
    // own AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID.
    const sessionId = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555";
    await mkdir(path.join(dir, "sessions", sessionId), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(path.join(dir, "sessions", sessionId, "meta.json"), JSON.stringify({ status: "exited", endedBy: "quit" }));
    const snapshotOnTerm = path.join(dir, "sessions", "{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}", "meta.json");

    const plain = startInPty(
      bin.paths.claude,
      [],
      baseEnv(dir, { FAKE_AGENT_LOG: log, FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM: snapshotOnTerm, AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID: sessionId })
    );
    try {
      await plain.waitFor("> ", "the prompt");
      const before = Date.now();
      process.kill(plain.term.pid, "SIGTERM");
      assert.equal((await plain.exited).signal, os.constants.signals.SIGTERM);
      const entries = await readLog(log);
      const entry = entries.find((item) => item.event === "sigterm" && item.pid === plain.term.pid);
      assert.equal(entry.snapshotError, undefined);
      assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(entry.snapshot), { status: "exited", endedBy: "quit" });
      assert.equal(entry.name, "claude");
      assert.ok(entry.at >= before, "every entry carries its time, so a test can put events in order");
      assert.ok(entries.some((item) => item.event === "start" && item.pid === plain.term.pid), "the start is logged too");
    } finally {
      plain.stop();
    }

    const stubborn = startInPty(
      bin.paths.claude,
      [],
      baseEnv(dir, { FAKE_AGENT_LOG: log, FAKE_AGENT_MODE: "ignore-term", FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM: path.join(dir, "missing.json") })
    );
    try {
      await stubborn.waitFor("> ", "the prompt");
      process.kill(stubborn.term.pid, "SIGTERM");
      await delay(500);
      assert.equal(stubborn.exitInfo, null, "ignore-term must survive SIGTERM");
      const entry = (await readLog(log)).find((item) => item.event === "sigterm" && item.pid === stubborn.term.pid);
      assert.equal(entry.snapshotError, "ENOENT", "a file that cannot be read is named by its error code");
      process.kill(stubborn.term.pid, "SIGKILL");
      assert.equal((await stubborn.exited).signal, os.constants.signals.SIGKILL);
    } finally {
      stubborn.stop();
    }
  });
});

test("the stand-in login shell runs the command with the PATH it was given and reads no startup file", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  assert.ok(FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL.endsWith(path.join("test", "fakes", "login-shell.sh")));
  assert.equal((await stat(FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL)).mode & 0o777, 0o755, "it is executable");
  const dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-login-shell-"));
  try {
    // Startup files that would change PATH and leave a mark if any shell read them.
    const mark = path.join(dir, "startup-ran");
    const startup = `touch ${shQuote(mark)}\nPATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH\nexport PATH\n`;
    for (const file of [".profile", ".zshenv", ".zprofile", ".zshrc", ".bash_profile", ".bashrc", "env.sh"]) {
      await writeFile(path.join(dir, file), startup);
    }
    const given = [path.join(dir, "bin"), SYSTEM_PATH].join(path.delimiter);
    // shell-env.js's form (Task S2): -i -l -c '<node> -e <script>'.
    const command = `${shQuote(process.execPath)} -e ${shQuote("process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ PATH: process.env.PATH }))")}`;
    const stdout = execFileSync(FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, ["-i", "-l", "-c", command], {
      env: { PATH: given, HOME: dir, ZDOTDIR: dir, ENV: path.join(dir, "env.sh"), BASH_ENV: path.join(dir, "env.sh") },
      encoding: "utf8"
    });
    assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(stdout), { PATH: given });
    assert.equal(existsSync(mark), false, "no startup file ran");
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});
```

(node-pty notes: `onExit` reports `{ exitCode, signal }`, where `signal` is the number from `WTERMSIG` in node-pty's `src/unix/pty.cc`; on macOS the PTY child starts with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID`, so `term.pid` leads its own session and process group. A terminal turns each `\n` into `\r\n`, so the fake's `\r\n` arrives as `\r\r\n`; the tests match substrings or `\r+\n`.)

- [ ] **Step 6: Run it to make sure it fails.**

Run: `env -u HERMES_HOME node --test test/fake-agents.test.js 2>&1 | grep -E '^# (tests|pass|fail)|Cannot find'`
Expected: `Cannot find module '…/test/helpers/fake-agents.js'`, `# tests 1`, `# fail 1`.

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the fake agent, its shim writer and the stand-in login shell.** Create `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`:

```js
// A fake agent CLI that behaves like a terminal program (a TUI), for the SP3
// session tests (planning decision Q2). It is not a test file: `npm test`
// (scripts/run-tests.mjs) runs only test/*.test.js. Start it through the
// shims that makeFakeAgentBin() in test/helpers/fake-agents.js writes; each
// shim sets FAKE_AGENT_NAME to the agent it stands in for.
//
// Modes (FAKE_AGENT_MODE; the shim's mode unless the environment sets one):
//   tui                FAKE_ARGV line, then a "> " prompt; echoes typing; runs typed commands
//   setsid-grandchild  tui, plus a grandchild in its own session (spawn with
//                      detached: true, so libuv calls setsid; macOS has no setsid command)
//   ignore-term        tui, but SIGTERM is ignored (SIGKILL still ends it)
//   agents-hang        `claude agents --json` never answers
//   updater            asks "Update now? [y/N] ", prints "ANSWER <text>", exits 0 for y, 1 otherwise
//
// Quick answers (no terminal needed): --version, --help, auth status, login
// status, status, doctor, config get (approvals.mode prints "manual"),
// gateway ..., claude agents ..., claude stop <id>. A headless run (-p,
// --print or exec anywhere in argv, as the Runs page starts one; never a
// session argv) prints nothing and keeps running until it is stopped, like
// the UI audit harness's earlier fake-agent, whose probes stop live runs.
//
// Typed commands (each ends with Enter):
//   alt on|off   paste on|off   mouse on|off   focus on|off   keys app|normal   kitty on|off
//   bell   osc9 <text>   osc9st <text>   osc99 <text>   osc777 <text>   title <text>
//   ask (DA1 and DSR)   ask after <ms>   ask kitty   ask color
//   lines <n>   flood <KiB>   bottom <text>   ticker <ms> <count>   exit <code>
//   anything else prints "you said: <text>"
// Replies to its questions (DA1, DSR, kitty flags, OSC 10/11 colour) and
// focus reports print "REPLY <json>"; a bracketed paste prints
// "PASTE <json>"; other escape sequences (arrows, mouse reports) print
// "KEY <json>". Ctrl+C exits with code 130. SIGTERM is logged, then ends the
// fake (mode ignore-term only logs it). SIGHUP is never handled, so the fake
// leaves when its terminal closes (the server tests rely on this).
//
// Environment:
//   FAKE_AGENT_LOG                       append one JSON line per event to this file
//                                        ({ name, pid, at, event, ... }; at is Date.now())
//   FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE                   setsid-grandchild: write the grandchild's pid here
//   FAKE_AGENT_GRANDCHILD_IGNORE_TERM=1  the grandchild ignores SIGTERM
//   FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM          on SIGTERM, copy this file's text into the log entry;
//                                        a literal {AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID} in it becomes this
//                                        process's AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID (the quit test knows
//                                        the id only after the session starts)
//   FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON              what `claude agents --json` prints (default "[]")
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const name = process.env.FAKE_AGENT_NAME || "";
const mode = process.env.FAKE_AGENT_MODE || "tui";
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const ESC = "\x1b";
const BEL = "\x07";
// Never outlive a forgotten test by more than ten minutes.
const MAX_LIFETIME_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;
// A headless run ends by itself after five minutes, as the earlier audit fake's did.
const HEADLESS_RUN_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

if (!name) {
  process.stdout.write(
    "tui-agent.mjs is a fake agent for tests. Start it through makeFakeAgentBin() in test/helpers/fake-agents.js.\n"
  );
  process.exit(0);
}

function out(text) {
  process.stdout.write(text);
}

function line(text) {
  out(`${text}\r\n`);
}

function log(entry) {
  const file = process.env.FAKE_AGENT_LOG;
  if (!file) return;
  try {
    appendFileSync(file, `${JSON.stringify({ name, pid: process.pid, at: Date.now(), ...entry })}\n`);
  } catch {
    // the test reads what it can
  }
}

function answer(text, code = 0) {
  process.stdout.write(`${text}\n`, () => process.exit(code));
  return true;
}

function clampInt(text, min, max, fallback) {
  const value = Number.parseInt(String(text), 10);
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, value));
}

// Names only for anything secret-looking: values never reach the screen,
// the recording or the log.
const SECRET_KEY = /TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|_KEY$/i;
const SHOWN_ENV = [
  "TERM",
  "COLORTERM",
  "TERM_PROGRAM",
  "TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION",
  "AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB",
  "CLAUDECODE",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT",
  "HOME",
  "USERPROFILE",
  "SHELL",
  "EDITOR",
  "VISUAL",
  "SSH_AUTH_SOCK",
  "LANG",
  "LC_ALL",
  "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR",
  "CODEX_HOME",
  "XDG_CONFIG_HOME",
  "HERMES_HOME",
  "FAKE_AGENT_MODE"
];

function argvRecord() {
  const env = {};
  for (const key of SHOWN_ENV) {
    if (process.env[key] !== undefined) env[key] = process.env[key];
  }
  const keys = Object.keys(process.env).sort();
  return {
    name,
    mode,
    argv: args,
    cwd: process.cwd(),
    isTTY: Boolean(process.stdin.isTTY && process.stdout.isTTY),
    env,
    agentOsKeys: keys.filter((key) => key.startsWith("AGENT_OS_") || key.startsWith("HERMES_AGENT_OS_")),
    secretKeys: keys.filter((key) => SECRET_KEY.test(key))
  };
}

// The quick, non-interactive questions that agent detection and the Stop
// sequence ask. Each answers at once and exits, so nothing waits on a TUI.
// Returns true when it handled the command line.
function oneShot() {
  const joined = args.join(" ");
  if (args.includes("--version") || joined === "-v") return answer(`${name} 9.9.9-fake`);
  if (args.includes("--help") || joined === "-h") {
    return answer(`Usage: ${name} [options]\n  --help     Show help\n  --version  Show version`);
  }
  if (joined === "auth status") return answer(JSON.stringify({ loggedIn: true }));
  if (joined === "login status") return answer("Logged in using ChatGPT");
  if (args[0] === "status") return answer(JSON.stringify({ status: "authenticated" }));
  if (args[0] === "doctor") return answer(args.includes("--json") ? "{}" : "ok");
  // Hermes's approvals setting reads as on ("manual"), as the earlier audit fake answered.
  if (args[0] === "config" && args[1] === "get") return answer(args[2] === "approvals.mode" ? "manual" : "");
  if (args[0] === "gateway") {
    if (args[1] === "status") {
      return answer(args.includes("--json") ? JSON.stringify({ running: false }) : "gateway is not running");
    }
    // Service controls: the Hold to stop all tests check that nothing calls these.
    log({ event: "gateway", args });
    return answer(`gateway ${args[1] || ""} done`);
  }
  if (name === "claude" && args[0] === "agents") {
    log({ event: "agents", args });
    if (mode === "agents-hang") {
      // Never answers; the Stop sequence's 2 s limit kills it. It still ends
      // itself after the lifetime cap, so a failed test cannot leave it behind.
      setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), MAX_LIFETIME_MS);
      return true;
    }
    return answer(process.env.FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON || "[]");
  }
  if (name === "claude" && args[0] === "stop") {
    log({ event: "stop", id: args[1] || null });
    return answer(`stopped ${args[1] || ""}`);
  }
  if (args.some((arg) => arg === "-p" || arg === "--print" || arg === "exec")) {
    // A headless run (never a session argv): no output, and it keeps running
    // until it is stopped (SIGTERM ends it at once).
    log({ event: "run", args });
    setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), HEADLESS_RUN_MS);
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// --- the terminal program ---------------------------------------------------

const REPLY_PATTERNS = [
  /^\x1b\[\?[\d;]*c/, // DA1 reply
  /^\x1b\[\d+;\d+R/, // DSR cursor position report
  /^\x1b\[\?\d*u/, // kitty keyboard flags reply
  /^\x1b\](?:10|11);[^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)/, // OSC 10/11 colour reply
  /^\x1b\[[IO]/ // focus in / out report
];
const PASTE_START = `${ESC}[200~`;
const PASTE_END = `${ESC}[201~`;

let pending = "";
let typed = "";
let updaterWaiting = false;

function prompt() {
  out(`> ${typed}`);
}

function notice(text) {
  out(`\r\n${text}\r\n`);
  prompt();
}

// The length of one complete escape sequence at the start of s, or 0 when
// more bytes are needed.
function escapeLength(s) {
  if (s.length < 2) return 0;
  if (s[1] === "[") {
    for (let i = 2; i < s.length; i += 1) {
      const code = s.charCodeAt(i);
      if (code >= 0x40 && code <= 0x7e) return i + 1;
    }
    return 0;
  }
  if (s[1] === "]") {
    for (let i = 2; i < s.length; i += 1) {
      if (s[i] === BEL) return i + 1;
      if (s[i] === ESC && s[i + 1] === "\\") return i + 2;
    }
    return 0;
  }
  if (s[1] === "O") return s.length >= 3 ? 3 : 0;
  return 2;
}

function onInput(chunk) {
  pending += chunk;
  while (pending.length) {
    if (pending.startsWith(PASTE_START)) {
      const end = pending.indexOf(PASTE_END);
      if (end === -1) return;
      const text = pending.slice(PASTE_START.length, end);
      pending = pending.slice(end + PASTE_END.length);
      log({ event: "paste", text });
      notice(`PASTE ${JSON.stringify(text)}`);
      continue;
    }
    if (pending[0] === ESC) {
      const reply = REPLY_PATTERNS.map((pattern) => pending.match(pattern)).find(Boolean);
      if (reply) {
        pending = pending.slice(reply[0].length);
        log({ event: "reply", seq: reply[0] });
        notice(`REPLY ${JSON.stringify(reply[0])}`);
        continue;
      }
      const length = escapeLength(pending);
      if (!length) return;
      const key = pending.slice(0, length);
      pending = pending.slice(length);
      log({ event: "key", seq: key });
      notice(`KEY ${JSON.stringify(key)}`);
      continue;
    }
    const ch = pending[0];
    pending = pending.slice(1);
    if (ch === "\r" || ch === "\n") {
      const text = typed;
      typed = "";
      out("\r\n");
      handleLine(text);
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "\x7f" || ch === "\b") {
      if (typed) {
        typed = typed.slice(0, -1);
        out("\b \b");
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "\x03") {
      out("^C\r\n");
      process.exit(130);
    }
    typed += ch;
    out(ch);
  }
}

function handleLine(text) {
  log({ event: "line", text });
  if (updaterWaiting) {
    updaterWaiting = false;
    line(`ANSWER ${text}`);
    const yes = /^y(es)?$/i.test(text.trim());
    process.stdout.write("", () => process.exit(yes ? 0 : 1));
    return;
  }
  const [command = "", ...rest] = text.trim().split(/\s+/);
  const value = rest.join(" ");
  switch (command) {
    case "alt":
      out(value === "off" ? `${ESC}[?1049l` : `${ESC}[?1049h`);
      break;
    case "paste":
      out(value === "off" ? `${ESC}[?2004l` : `${ESC}[?2004h`);
      break;
    case "mouse":
      out(value === "off" ? `${ESC}[?1006l${ESC}[?1000l` : `${ESC}[?1000h${ESC}[?1006h`);
      break;
    case "focus":
      out(value === "off" ? `${ESC}[?1004l` : `${ESC}[?1004h`);
      break;
    case "keys":
      out(value === "normal" ? `${ESC}[?1l` : `${ESC}[?1h`);
      break;
    case "kitty":
      out(value === "off" ? `${ESC}[<u` : `${ESC}[>1u`);
      break;
    case "bell":
      out(BEL);
      break;
    case "osc9":
      out(`${ESC}]9;${value}${BEL}`);
      break;
    case "osc9st":
      out(`${ESC}]9;${value}${ESC}\\`);
      break;
    case "osc99":
      out(`${ESC}]99;;${value}${ESC}\\`);
      break;
    case "osc777":
      out(`${ESC}]777;notify;Fake agent;${value}${BEL}`);
      break;
    case "title":
      out(`${ESC}]0;${value}${BEL}`);
      break;
    case "ask":
      if (value === "kitty") out(`${ESC}[?u`);
      else if (value === "color") out(`${ESC}]11;?${BEL}`);
      else if (value.startsWith("after ")) {
        // DA1 and DSR later, so a test can close the writer's window first (S9: the mirror answers).
        setTimeout(() => out(`${ESC}[c${ESC}[6n`), clampInt(value.slice(6), 10, 60000, 1000));
      } else out(`${ESC}[c${ESC}[6n`);
      break;
    case "lines": {
      const count = clampInt(value, 1, 100000, 10);
      for (let i = 1; i <= count; i += 1) line(`line ${i}`);
      break;
    }
    case "flood": {
      // 16 rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB.
      const kib = clampInt(value, 1, 65536, 64);
      const row = `${"x".repeat(62)}\r\n`;
      for (let i = 0; i < kib * 16; i += 1) out(row);
      line(`FLOOD DONE ${kib}`);
      break;
    }
    case "bottom": {
      // Redraw only the last row (a status line) and put the cursor back.
      const rows = process.stdout.rows || 24;
      out(`${ESC}7${ESC}[${rows};1H${ESC}[2K${value}${ESC}8`);
      return; // no new prompt: nothing above the bottom row changes
    }
    case "ticker": {
      const [every, times] = rest;
      const intervalMs = clampInt(every, 10, 60000, 100);
      const count = clampInt(times, 1, 100000, 10);
      let tick = 0;
      const timer = setInterval(() => {
        tick += 1;
        const rows = process.stdout.rows || 24;
        out(`${ESC}7${ESC}[${rows};1H${ESC}[2Ktick ${tick}${ESC}8`);
        if (tick >= count) clearInterval(timer);
      }, intervalMs);
      return;
    }
    case "exit": {
      const code = clampInt(value, 0, 255, 0);
      process.stdout.write("", () => process.exit(code));
      return;
    }
    case "":
      break;
    default:
      line(`you said: ${text}`);
  }
  prompt();
}

function startGrandchild() {
  const source = [
    'if (process.env.FAKE_AGENT_GRANDCHILD_IGNORE_TERM === "1") process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});',
    "setInterval(() => {}, 1000);",
    `setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), ${MAX_LIFETIME_MS});`
  ].join("\n");
  const grandchild = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", source], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" });
  grandchild.unref();
  const pidFile = process.env.FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE;
  if (pidFile) writeFileSync(pidFile, String(grandchild.pid));
  log({ event: "grandchild", pid: grandchild.pid });
  line(`GRANDCHILD:${grandchild.pid}`);
}

function onTerm() {
  const entry = { event: "sigterm" };
  const snapshotFile = (process.env.FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM || "").replaceAll(
    "{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}",
    process.env.AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID || ""
  );
  if (snapshotFile) {
    try {
      entry.snapshot = readFileSync(snapshotFile, "utf8");
    } catch (error) {
      entry.snapshotError = error?.code || String(error);
    }
  }
  log(entry);
  if (mode === "ignore-term") return;
  // Die from the signal itself, so the parent sees "killed by SIGTERM".
  process.removeListener("SIGTERM", onTerm);
  process.kill(process.pid, "SIGTERM");
}

function startTui() {
  process.on("SIGTERM", onTerm);
  // No SIGHUP handler on purpose: when the terminal closes (for example the
  // server was killed with SIGKILL), Node's default action ends the fake.
  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), MAX_LIFETIME_MS).unref();
  if (process.stdin.isTTY) process.stdin.setRawMode(true);
  process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
  const record = argvRecord();
  log({ event: "start", ...record });
  line(`FAKE_ARGV ${JSON.stringify(record)}`);
  if (mode === "setsid-grandchild") startGrandchild();
  if (mode === "updater") {
    updaterWaiting = true;
    out("Update now? [y/N] ");
  } else {
    prompt();
  }
  process.stdin.on("data", onInput);
  process.stdin.on("end", () => process.exit(0));
  process.stdin.on("error", () => process.exit(0));
}

if (!oneShot()) startTui();
```

Then create `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`:

```js
// Fake agent CLIs for the SP3 session tests (planning decision Q2). Each
// shim is a tiny POSIX shell script named like a real agent CLI that runs
// test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs with this Node, so node need not be on PATH.
// Put the folder first on a test's PATH, or pass a shim's path directly.
// This is a helper, not a test file: the runner only runs test/*.test.js.
// Importing it has no side effects (scripts/run-tests.mjs imports it too).
import { chmod, mkdir, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const fakesDir = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "fakes");

export const FAKE_AGENT_NAMES = Object.freeze(["claude", "codex", "agent", "cursor-agent", "hermes", "openclaw"]);
export const FAKE_AGENT_MODES = Object.freeze(["tui", "setsid-grandchild", "ignore-term", "agents-hang", "updater"]);
export const FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT = path.join(fakesDir, "tui-agent.mjs");
// The stand-in login shell (planning decision Q1c): `<it> -i -l -c <command>`
// runs the command with /bin/sh, reads no startup file and keeps the
// environment as given. It is the only SHELL any test uses: the runner sets
// it for the whole run, and every test that starts server/index.js sets
// SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL itself. Never /bin/sh: a real login sh runs macOS's
// path_helper, which puts /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin first on PATH.
export const FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL = path.join(fakesDir, "login-shell.sh");

function shQuote(value) {
  return `'${String(value).replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'`;
}

// Writes one executable shim per name into dir (created if missing).
// mode is the default FAKE_AGENT_MODE; a FAKE_AGENT_MODE in the environment
// the shim runs with wins. Resolves { dir, script, paths: { <name>: <file> } }.
// A file or link already at a shim's path is removed first: writing through a
// link (the UI audit harness's fake-bin/ links every name to one fake-agent
// file) would change the file it points at instead.
export async function makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, mode = "tui" } = {}) {
  if (process.platform === "win32") {
    throw new Error("makeFakeAgentBin: the fake agents are POSIX shell shims; skip this test on Windows");
  }
  if (!FAKE_AGENT_MODES.includes(mode)) throw new Error(`makeFakeAgentBin: unknown fake agent mode "${mode}"`);
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  const paths = {};
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(name)) throw new Error(`makeFakeAgentBin: bad agent name "${name}"`);
    const file = path.join(dir, name);
    const shim = [
      "#!/bin/sh",
      `FAKE_AGENT_NAME=${shQuote(name)}`,
      "export FAKE_AGENT_NAME",
      `: "\${FAKE_AGENT_MODE:=${mode}}"`,
      "export FAKE_AGENT_MODE",
      `exec ${shQuote(process.execPath)} ${shQuote(FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT)} "$@"`,
      ""
    ].join("\n");
    await rm(file, { force: true });
    await writeFile(file, shim);
    await chmod(file, 0o755);
    paths[name] = file;
  }
  return { dir, script: FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT, paths };
}
```

(A shim for `claude` reads: `#!/bin/sh`, `FAKE_AGENT_NAME='claude'`, `export FAKE_AGENT_NAME`, `: "${FAKE_AGENT_MODE:=tui}"`, `export FAKE_AGENT_MODE`, `exec '/path/to/node' '/repo/test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs' "$@"`. Before the `exec`, `ps` shows `/bin/sh <temp>/claude …`, which lives in the temp folder; after it, `node …/test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs …`, which is not named like an agent. Either way the watcher lets it through.)

Then create `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Stand-in login shell for tests (planning decision Q1c): runs Agent OS's
# command (the last argument, after -i -l -c) with /bin/sh, reads no startup
# file and keeps the environment, PATH included, as given. scripts/run-tests.mjs
# sets SHELL to this file, and every test that starts server/index.js sets it
# too, so a server a test starts never reads the owner's shell setup, and a
# real login sh never puts /usr/local/bin or /opt/homebrew/bin ahead of a
# test's fake folder.
for last; do :; done
exec /bin/sh -c "$last"
```

and make it executable, so git records it as mode 100755:

Run: `chmod 755 test/fakes/login-shell.sh`

(In plain English: `chmod 755` lets anyone run the file, the same as the fake shims; the test checks this. `/bin/sh -c` with no `-i` or `-l` reads no startup file, and the runner also removes `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV` and `BASH_ENV`, the variables that point shells at startup files.)

- [ ] **Step 9: Write the runner and switch `npm test` to it.** Create `scripts/run-tests.mjs`:

```js
// `npm test`: runs every test/*.test.js file with `node --test` under the
// no-real-agents watcher (spec SP3; planning decisions Q1, Q1a). Arguments
// are passed on: flags (anything starting with "-") go before the files,
// and file paths replace the default list. For example:
//   npm test -- test/portable.test.js
//   npm test -- --test-name-pattern="shutdown" test/portable.test.js
// The run fails (exit 1) when a real agent CLI started during it, even if
// every test passed. Windows has no `ps`, so there the tests run unwatched.
// The tests never read the owner's shell setup: SHELL is the stand-in login
// shell, and ZDOTDIR, ENV and BASH_ENV are removed (planning decision Q1c).
// HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS is removed too, so detection never finds
// the owner's real agents ahead of a test's fake folder.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL } from "../test/helpers/fake-agents.js";
import { startWatcher } from "../test/helpers/no-real-agents.js";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const extra = process.argv.slice(2);
const flags = extra.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith("-"));
const named = extra.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith("-")).map((file) => path.resolve(file));
const files = named.length
  ? named
  : readdirSync(path.join(root, "test"))
      .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".test.js"))
      .sort()
      .map((name) => path.join(root, "test", name));

function shownPath(file) {
  if (!file) return "an unknown test file";
  const relative = path.relative(root, file);
  return relative.startsWith("..") || path.isAbsolute(relative) ? file : relative;
}

function violationLine(violation) {
  const where = shownPath(violation.testFile);
  return (
    `no-real-agents watcher: a real "${violation.name}" started during the tests ` +
    `(pid ${violation.pid}, ${violation.binary}, from ${where}). Sent it SIGTERM.`
  );
}

let watcher = null;
if (process.platform === "win32") {
  console.log("no-real-agents watcher: not available on Windows");
} else {
  try {
    watcher = await startWatcher({ rootPid: process.pid, onViolation: (violation) => console.error(violationLine(violation)) });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`${error.message}. The tests did not run.`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

// From Task S8 on, every server a test starts in local mode reads its login
// shell ($SHELL -i -l -c). The owner's real shell would run their startup
// files, and a real login sh (macOS path_helper) puts /usr/local/bin and
// /opt/homebrew/bin ahead of a test's fake folder. Tests that start
// server/index.js also set SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL themselves, so a single
// file run with node --test is safe too. The variables that point shells at
// startup files go, and so does detection's extra folders
// (HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS), which are searched before PATH: set to
// the owner's real agent folders, they would put a real agent ahead of a
// test's fake folder (server/runtime/safety.js executableSearchDirs).
const testEnv = { ...process.env };
for (const key of ["ZDOTDIR", "ENV", "BASH_ENV", "HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS"]) delete testEnv[key];
if (process.platform !== "win32") testEnv.SHELL = FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL;

const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["--test", "--test-timeout=180000", ...flags, ...files], {
  cwd: root,
  env: testEnv,
  stdio: "inherit"
});
for (const signal of ["SIGINT", "SIGTERM"]) {
  process.on(signal, () => child.kill(signal));
}
child.once("error", (error) => {
  console.error(`Could not start node --test: ${error.message}`);
  process.exit(1);
});
child.once("exit", async (code, signal) => {
  let exitCode = signal ? 1 : (code ?? 1);
  if (watcher) {
    const { checks, violations } = await watcher.stop();
    if (violations.length) {
      console.error(
        `no-real-agents watcher: ${violations.length} real agent process(es) started during the tests, so the run fails.`
      );
      exitCode = 1;
    } else {
      console.log(`no-real-agents watcher: no real agent started (${checks} checks)`);
    }
  }
  process.exit(exitCode);
});
```

In `package.json`, change line 20 from

to

(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` already runs `env -u HERMES_HOME npm test` on Linux and macOS and `npm test` on Windows, so CI needs no change: the watcher runs on the first two and prints the "not available" line on Windows, planning decision Q22.)

#### Notes

1. **Watcher rules beyond planning decision Q1a (deliberate).**
   - A command word with no folder (a bare `claude`) is a violation: it was found on a PATH the watcher cannot see, so it cannot be proved to be a fake. Every fake shim shows up in `ps` with its full path, because the kernel passes the script's path to `/bin/sh`.
   - A remembered descendant whose pid now runs a different command under a parent that is not watched is treated as a reused pid and ignored. This is what keeps the owner's own `claude` from ever being flagged or sent SIGTERM. A process that replaces itself (`exec`) under a watched parent is still checked.
   - Stricter than Q1a: a new descendant that runs from a real agent's own install folder (`REAL_AGENT_PATHS`) is a violation even inside an allowed root. The temp folder is an allowed root, and on macOS it also holds every temp HOME the tests create, so a real agent installed under one (an npx cache, Setup's managed Node, a copied Claude `versions` folder) would otherwise pass. No existing test and no SP3 task runs anything from those folders; the fake npm in `test/setup-builders.test.js` writes only `<prefix>/bin/codex`, a shim to a fake script.
2. **Known limit: the watcher samples.** It polls every 200 ms, so a real agent that starts and exits in under 200 ms (a bare `claude --version`) can be missed. The spec's polling design accepts this; every session the tests start lives far longer.
3. **Runner flags.** Besides test files (Q1), arguments that start with `-` go to `node --test` before the files, so `npm test -- --test-name-pattern=… test/x.test.js` works. Flags must use the `--flag=value` form.
4. **The fake does more than Q2 lists, because later tasks use it** (S4, S6 to S10, D2, the UI probes): mode `ignore-term`, the extra typed commands, the `REPLY`/`PASTE`/`KEY`/`GRANDCHILD:` markers, the log events and the environment variables under Interfaces, and one-shot answers to every detection probe, so `detect()` finds a fake without starting its terminal program. Whoever changes the fake later keeps two things the code comments also state: no SIGHUP handler (Task S8's recovery test relies on the fake leaving when its terminal closes) and the `{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}` placeholder in `FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM` (Task S8's end-to-end quit test; its Step 0 checks for it).
5. **`claude agents --json` is a guess.** What the real command prints is not known yet (Task S7 and spike S0 decide), so the fake prints `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON` verbatim and S7's tests choose the shape.
6. **The UI audit harness is not touched here.** `.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin/` (git-ignored) still links every name to one `fake-agent` script that exits at once on a session argv. Task U1, which adds the first session probe, writes `makeFakeAgentBin` shims (all six names) into that folder and later UI tasks reuse them. The folder is already an allowed root, and `makeFakeAgentBin` removes each link before it writes, so the old `fake-agent` file is left as it was. The fake keeps the two behaviours of the old one that SP2's probes rely on: `hermes config get approvals.mode` prints `manual`, and a headless run (`-p`, `--print`, `exec`) keeps running until it is stopped (the `keys` mode of `audit.mjs` holds to stop live runs). Other answers differ from the old fake, which printed nothing for them: `--version` prints `<name> 9.9.9-fake` instead of `9.9.9-fake`, `claude auth status` prints `{"loggedIn":true}`, and `codex login status` and `cursor status` say signed in, so a probe that reads the Agents or Setup page's sign-in state may see a different line after the swap.
7. **The terminal tests have not run through node-pty yet.** node-pty arrives with W0, so while drafting, this file's code was run in a throwaway copy of the repo with a scratch-only stand-in for node-pty (a Python `pty` bridge, never part of the plan): all 15 fake-agent tests passed; the link, placeholder, headless-run and approvals checks each failed with their code line removed; the fake left within 1 s of its terminal's owner being killed with SIGKILL (SIGHUP); the watcher tests gave `# tests 12`, `# pass 11`, `# skipped 1`; Steps 8, 10 and 11 printed what they show; and the whole suite under the runner gave `# fail 0` and `no-real-agents watcher: no real agent started`. Step 8 is the first run of the terminal tests through the real node-pty.
8. **For the hand-off (owner).** `npm test` now ends with a watcher line and fails a run in which a real agent CLI started, even when every test passed. The tests no longer read the person's own shell settings: `SHELL` is the stand-in login shell and `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV` and `BASH_ENV` are removed for the run. `HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS` (extra folders Agent OS searches for agents before `PATH`) is removed for the run too, so a person who set it to their real agent folders never has a test find, or start, a real agent ahead of the fakes.

### Task S1: process-tree (trackPid, descendant walk, setsid-proof kill); shutdown 8 s and shutdown tasks; stdin shutdown line

Sessions put agents in real terminals, and three things in today's cleanup code do not fit that (map-server-engine 1, 2 and 11; map-tests-harness 6):
- `server/runtime/process-tree.js` only tracks children it started itself with `spawnTracked`. node-pty starts session processes, so there is no `ChildProcess` to track. This task adds `trackPid(pid, onExit)` / `untrackPid(pid)`, so `killAllTracked` and the exit sweep include sessions.
- `killProcessTree` signals the process group only. A tool an agent starts that calls `setsid` (or `setpgid`) leaves the group and survives both SIGTERM and SIGKILL. This task makes it list every descendant with one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` walk BEFORE it sends any signal, signal the group and every descendant, and SIGKILL survivors after the grace period (planning decision Q3). On Linux without `ps` (the Docker image `node:20-bookworm-slim` has no `procps`), the same walk reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` instead, so Stop still reaches a setsid grandchild there. Windows keeps `taskkill /T /F`.
- `server/runtime/shutdown.js` gives a quit 3 s, and nothing else can join the shutdown. The spec raises the hard exit to 8 s and puts sessions in the shutdown path. This task adds `registerShutdownTask(name, fn)` (S7 registers the sessions' quit through it): tasks run in parallel with the runs' own stop and before the kill sweep, each with its own time limit. It also adds the graceful quit that works on every OS (planning decision Q4): when `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1`, the server reads stdin, and the exact line `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN` (or the end of input) runs the same shutdown as SIGTERM. On Windows the desktop shell has no other graceful way to stop the server (map-desktop-packaging 6).

`test/portable.test.js` still names the old 3 s budget; its wording and limits move to the 8 s hard exit, while it still checks that an idle server exits quickly.

Every test here that starts `server/index.js` gives it W1's stand-in login shell (`SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`, ruling R15) and a `PATH` of the six fake agents plus `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` only (R16). From Task S8 on, a server in local mode reads its login shell right after READY, and agent detection always searches `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` after `PATH` (`executableSearchDirs` in `server/runtime/safety.js`), so the fakes must come first and no real login shell may rebuild `PATH`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `server/runtime/process-tree.js`: the whole file (lines 1-114) is replaced by the version in Step 3. `spawnTracked`, `killProcessTree`, `killAllTracked` and `killAllTrackedSync` keep their names and signatures.
- Modify: `server/runtime/shutdown.js`: the whole file (lines 1-74) is replaced by the version in Step 7. `shutdown({ server })` and `installShutdownHandlers(server)` keep working as called today (`server/index.js:1858` needs no change).
- Modify: `test/portable.test.js`: one new import line after line 13 (`import { shutdown } from "../server/runtime/shutdown.js";`), and lines 258-292 (the test `"SIGTERM to the real server exits within 3 seconds"`), both in Step 9.
- Test: `test/process-tree.test.js` (new), `test/shutdown.test.js` (new), `test/portable.test.js`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - W0: `node-pty` (`require("node-pty").spawn(file, args, { name, cols, rows, cwd, env })` → `IPty` with `pid`, `onExit(listener)` giving `{ exitCode, signal? }`, `kill(signal?)`). On macOS the PTY child starts with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID` (node-pty `src/unix/pty.cc`), so `pty.pid` leads its own session and process group.
  - W1: `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, mode = "tui" } = {})` from `test/helpers/fake-agents.js` → `Promise<{ dir, script, paths }>`, one POSIX shim per name (all six by default: `claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw`) that runs the fake with this Node, so node need not be on `PATH`; it throws on Windows. Mode `"setsid-grandchild"`: the fake writes its grandchild's pid to `FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE`; the grandchild was started with `detached: true` (setsid); the fake dies from SIGTERM.
  - W1: `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` from `test/helpers/fake-agents.js` (the absolute path of `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`): run as `<it> -i -l -c <command>`, it runs the command with `/bin/sh -c`, reads no startup file and keeps `PATH` as given. The only `SHELL` any test uses (R15).
  - W1: `npm test` runs under the no-real-agents watcher.
- Produces (`server/runtime/process-tree.js`):
  - `trackPid(pid, onExit?)`: registers a process this module did not start. Ignores anything that is not a positive integer. `onExit`, when given, is a subscribe function `(listener) => unsubscribe`; trackPid calls it once with a listener that ignores its arguments (so S4's handle `onExit`, whose listener receives `{ exitCode, signal }`, fits as it is) and ignores what it returns, so the pid untracks itself when the process ends. With node-pty directly: `trackPid(pty.pid, (listener) => pty.onExit(() => listener()))`. The owner may also call `untrackPid(pid)` on exit; doing both is harmless.
  - `untrackPid(pid)`.
  - `listTrackedPids()` → `number[]` (a copy; for tests and diagnostics).
  - `listDescendants(pid)` → `Promise<number[]>`: one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` (argv only, 2 s limit); every pid below `pid` at any depth, not `pid` itself. When `ps` cannot run on Linux, it reads `/proc/<n>/stat` for every numeric entry in `/proc` (one file at a time) and walks the same `pid ppid` lines. `[]` on Windows, for a bad pid, or when neither `ps` nor `/proc` can be read (macOS always has `ps`).
  - `descendantsFromPsOutput(text, pid)` → `number[]` (the pure walk behind it).
  - `parseProcStat(text)` → `{ pid, ppid } | null`: one `/proc/<n>/stat` line. The command name (2nd field) is in parentheses and may hold spaces and `)`, so the fields are counted from the LAST `)`: the state, then the ppid.
  - `killProcessTree(pid, { graceMs = 1500 } = {})` → `Promise<void>` (never rejects). POSIX: lists descendants first, sends SIGTERM to the group led by `pid` and to each descendant (to its own group when it leads one), polls every 50 ms, after `graceMs` sends SIGKILL to every target still alive, then waits at most 1 s more. Windows: `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`.
  - `killAllTracked({ graceMs = 1500 } = {})`: every tracked child and every tracked pid, in parallel; then forgets them.
  - `killAllTrackedSync()`: one `ps` snapshot (500 ms limit; on Linux, when `ps` fails, the same `/proc` snapshot read with `readdirSync`/`readFileSync`), then SIGKILL to every tracked group and every descendant (Windows: `child.kill()` for children, `taskkill /T /F` for tracked pids).
- Produces (`server/runtime/shutdown.js`):
  - `HARD_EXIT_MS = 8000`, `SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS = 7000` (the sessions task S7 registers caps itself at 7 s too), `STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN"`.
  - `registerShutdownTask(name, fn)` → an unregister function. Throws `TypeError` for an empty name or a non-function. A second registration under the same name replaces the first (so S7 can register once per manager without duplicates). At shutdown every task runs in parallel with the runs' `stopAll()` and with the other tasks, BEFORE `killAllTracked()`; each is cut off after `taskLimitMs`, and its errors are logged, never thrown. S7 registers `registerShutdownTask("sessions", () => manager.shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" }))`.
  - `shutdown({ server, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: scheduler stop; the runs' `stopAll()` and the registered tasks in parallel; `killAllTracked()`; the live-chat children; `server.close` (500 ms fallback).
  - `installShutdownHandlers(server, { hardExitMs = HARD_EXIT_MS, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: SIGTERM, SIGINT (and SIGBREAK on Windows) start the shutdown with the hard exit timer. When `process.env.AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN === "1"` it also reads stdin lines, and the line `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN` (surrounding spaces and a trailing carriage return ignored) or the end of stdin starts the same shutdown. Without that variable, stdin is never read. D1 sets the variable, keeps the server's stdin piped and writes `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n` on quit.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing process-tree tests.** Create `test/process-tree.test.js`:

```js
// Process trees (spec SP3, process-tree.js changes; planning decision Q3):
// pids that node-pty starts are tracked with trackPid()/untrackPid(), the
// descendant walk finds every level below a pid, and killProcessTree()
// stops a whole tree, including a grandchild that left the process group
// with setsid. On Linux without `ps` (the Docker image), the walk reads /proc.
// The terminal test uses the fake agent from W1, never a real one.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { execFileSync, spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, realpath, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import {
  descendantsFromPsOutput,
  killAllTracked,
  killProcessTree,
  listDescendants,
  listTrackedPids,
  parseProcStat,
  trackPid,
  untrackPid
} from "../server/runtime/process-tree.js";
import { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const POSIX_ONLY = { skip: isWindows ? "process groups and setsid are POSIX-only" : false };
// The only folders besides the fakes' own that a fake agent's PATH holds (R16).
const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];
const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function forceKill(pid) {
  if (!pid) return;
  for (const target of [-pid, pid]) {
    try {
      process.kill(target, "SIGKILL");
    } catch {
      // already gone
    }
  }
}

function pgidOf(pid) {
  return Number(execFileSync("ps", ["-o", "pgid=", "-p", String(pid)], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim());
}

async function waitUntil(probe, label, ms = 5000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + ms;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const value = await probe();
    if (value) return value;
    await delay(25);
  }
  throw new Error(`timed out waiting for ${label}`);
}

// A leader (its own process group, like every tracked child and every PTY)
// that starts two grandchildren: one ordinary child in its group, and one
// with detached: true, which makes libuv call setsid() so it leaves the
// group. It prints both pids.
const LEADER_SOURCE = [
  "const { spawn } = require('node:child_process');",
  "const keep = process.env.GRANDCHILD_IGNORES_TERM === '1'",
  "  ? \"process.on('SIGTERM', () => {}); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);\"",
  "  : 'setInterval(() => {}, 1000);';",
  "const same = spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', keep], { stdio: 'ignore' });",
  "const own = spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', keep], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' });",
  "console.log('PIDS ' + same.pid + ' ' + own.pid);",
  "setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"
].join("\n");

async function startLeader(extraEnv = {}) {
  const leader = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", LEADER_SOURCE], {
    detached: true,
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"],
    env: { ...process.env, ...extraEnv }
  });
  let buffer = "";
  leader.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    buffer += chunk;
  });
  const match = await waitUntil(() => buffer.match(/PIDS (\d+) (\d+)/), "the leader's grandchild pids");
  return { leader, sameGroup: Number(match[1]), ownSession: Number(match[2]) };
}

test("descendantsFromPsOutput walks every level below a pid and nothing else", () => {
  const text = ["    1     0", "   10     1", "   11    10", "   12    11", "   13    10", "   20     1", "   21    20", "garbage", ""].join(
    "\n"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    descendantsFromPsOutput(text, 10).sort((a, b) => a - b),
    [11, 12, 13]
  );
  assert.deepEqual(descendantsFromPsOutput(text, 12), []);
  assert.deepEqual(descendantsFromPsOutput("", 10), []);
});

test("parseProcStat reads the pid and ppid even when the command name holds spaces and ')'", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(parseProcStat("4242 (node) S 17 4242 4242 0 -1 4194560 120 0 0 0\n"), { pid: 4242, ppid: 17 });
  // The name "my tool) R 5 (x": counting from the first ")" would read ppid 5.
  assert.deepEqual(parseProcStat("77 (my tool) R 5 (x) S 1 77 77 0 -1"), { pid: 77, ppid: 1 });
  assert.deepEqual(parseProcStat("78 (a) b) S 9 78 78"), { pid: 78, ppid: 9 });
  for (const bad of ["", "garbage", "12 (sh)", "12 sh S 1", "x (sh) S 1", "12 (sh) S", null, undefined]) {
    assert.equal(parseProcStat(bad), null, JSON.stringify(bad));
  }
});

test("trackPid ignores anything that is not a real pid", () => {
  const before = listTrackedPids();
  for (const bad of [0, -1, 1.5, Number.NaN, "123", null, undefined]) trackPid(bad);
  assert.deepEqual(listTrackedPids(), before);
});

test("listDescendants finds both grandchildren, including the one that called setsid", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const { leader, sameGroup, ownSession } = await startLeader();
  try {
    assert.notEqual(pgidOf(ownSession), pgidOf(leader.pid), "the setsid grandchild left the leader's process group");
    assert.equal(pgidOf(sameGroup), pgidOf(leader.pid));
    const found = await listDescendants(leader.pid);
    assert.ok(found.includes(sameGroup));
    assert.ok(found.includes(ownSession));
    assert.equal(found.includes(leader.pid), false);
  } finally {
    forceKill(ownSession);
    forceKill(sameGroup);
    forceKill(leader.pid);
  }
});

test("killProcessTree stops a grandchild that moved into its own session (setsid)", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const { leader, sameGroup, ownSession } = await startLeader();
  try {
    await killProcessTree(leader.pid, { graceMs: 1500 });
    assert.equal(isAlive(sameGroup), false);
    assert.equal(isAlive(ownSession), false, "a signal to the process group alone would miss this one");
    await waitUntil(() => leader.exitCode !== null || leader.signalCode !== null, "the leader's exit");
  } finally {
    forceKill(ownSession);
    forceKill(sameGroup);
    forceKill(leader.pid);
  }
});

test("killProcessTree sends SIGKILL after the grace period to a setsid grandchild that ignores SIGTERM", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const { leader, sameGroup, ownSession } = await startLeader({ GRANDCHILD_IGNORES_TERM: "1" });
  try {
    await delay(300); // let both grandchildren install their SIGTERM handler
    const started = Date.now();
    await killProcessTree(leader.pid, { graceMs: 500 });
    assert.ok(Date.now() - started >= 450, "it waited for the grace period before SIGKILL");
    assert.equal(isAlive(sameGroup), false);
    assert.equal(isAlive(ownSession), false);
  } finally {
    forceKill(ownSession);
    forceKill(sameGroup);
    forceKill(leader.pid);
  }
});

test("killAllTracked stops a tracked pid and its whole tree, then forgets the pid", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const { leader, sameGroup, ownSession } = await startLeader();
  try {
    trackPid(leader.pid, (listener) => leader.once("exit", listener));
    assert.ok(listTrackedPids().includes(leader.pid));
    await killAllTracked({ graceMs: 1000 });
    assert.equal(isAlive(sameGroup), false);
    assert.equal(isAlive(ownSession), false);
    assert.equal(listTrackedPids().includes(leader.pid), false);
  } finally {
    untrackPid(leader.pid);
    forceKill(ownSession);
    forceKill(sameGroup);
    forceKill(leader.pid);
  }
});

test("untrackPid takes a pid out of the shutdown sweep", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const sleeper = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", "setInterval(() => {}, 1000)"], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" });
  try {
    trackPid(sleeper.pid);
    untrackPid(sleeper.pid);
    await killAllTracked({ graceMs: 200 });
    assert.equal(isAlive(sleeper.pid), true);
  } finally {
    forceKill(sleeper.pid);
  }
});

test("a pid tracked with an exit subscription untracks itself when the process ends", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const brief = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", "setTimeout(() => {}, 100)"], { stdio: "ignore" });
  trackPid(brief.pid, (listener) => brief.once("exit", listener));

});
```

```js
// Spawns children we can reliably clean up, and kills whole process trees
// (not just the immediate child) so a quit or restart never leaves an agent
// CLI or a supervised process running in the background.
//
// Two kinds of tracked process:
// - children started here with spawnTracked() (runs, the builder supervisor,
//   module sessions);
// - pids started elsewhere and registered with trackPid() (the terminal
//   sessions' PTYs: node-pty starts them, so there is no ChildProcess).
// killProcessTree() lists a process's descendants with `ps` BEFORE it sends
// any signal, so a grandchild that left the process group (setsid/setpgid)
// is still found and stopped (spec SP3, process-tree.js changes; Q3). On
// Linux without `ps` (the Docker image has no procps) it reads /proc instead.
import { execFile, spawn, spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { readdir, readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const isLinux = process.platform === "linux";
const trackedChildren = new Set();
// pid -> the entry object trackPid() made. The identity check keeps a late
// exit notice from removing a newer registration of a reused pid.
const trackedPids = new Map();
const PS_ARGS = ["-A", "-o", "pid=,ppid="];
const PS_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000;
const PS_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS = 500;
const PROC_DIR = "/proc";
const NUMERIC = /^\d+$/;

// POSIX: `detached` makes the child the leader of its own process group, so a
// signal to the negative pid reaches it and anything it spawns. Windows has
// no process groups; `taskkill /T` walks the tree instead.
export function spawnTracked(command, args = [], options = {}) {
  const spawnOptions = { ...options };
  if (!isWindows) spawnOptions.detached = true;
  const child = spawn(command, args, spawnOptions);
  trackedChildren.add(child);
  child.once("exit", () => trackedChildren.delete(child));
  return child;
}

// Registers a process this module did not start (a PTY from node-pty), so
// killAllTracked() and killAllTrackedSync() include it. onExit, when given,
// subscribes to its exit, for example (listener) => pty.onExit(() => listener()):
// the pid is then untracked by itself when the process ends.
export function trackPid(pid, onExit) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return;
  const entry = { pid };
  trackedPids.set(pid, entry);
  if (typeof onExit !== "function") return;
  try {
    onExit(() => {
      if (trackedPids.get(pid) === entry) trackedPids.delete(pid);
    });
  } catch {
    // The owner calls untrackPid() itself when the process exits.
  }
}

export function untrackPid(pid) {
  trackedPids.delete(pid);
}

export function listTrackedPids() {
  return [...trackedPids.keys()];
}

// `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` text -> every pid below `pid`, at any depth.
export function descendantsFromPsOutput(text, pid) {
  const children = new Map();
  for (const line of String(text || "").split("\n")) {
    const match = line.match(/^\s*(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s*$/);
    if (!match) continue;
    const child = Number(match[1]);
    const parent = Number(match[2]);
    if (!children.has(parent)) children.set(parent, []);
    children.get(parent).push(child);
  }
  const found = [];
  const seen = new Set([pid]);
  const queue = [pid];
  while (queue.length) {
    const current = queue.shift();
    for (const child of children.get(current) || []) {
      if (seen.has(child)) continue;
      seen.add(child);
      found.push(child);
      queue.push(child);
    }
  }
  return found;
}

// One /proc/<pid>/stat line -> { pid, ppid }, or null when it is not one.
// The 2nd field is the command name in parentheses, and it may itself hold
// spaces and ")" (a program can name itself anything), so the fields after
// it are counted from the LAST ")": first the state, then the ppid.
export function parseProcStat(text) {
  const source = String(text ?? "");
  const open = source.indexOf("(");
  const close = source.lastIndexOf(")");
  if (open < 0 || close < open) return null;
  const pid = source.slice(0, open).trim();
  const [, ppid] = source.slice(close + 1).trim().split(/\s+/);
  if (!NUMERIC.test(pid) || !NUMERIC.test(ppid || "")) return null;
  return { pid: Number(pid), ppid: Number(ppid) };
}

function procLine(statText) {
  const row = parseProcStat(statText);
  return row ? `${row.pid} ${row.ppid}` : null;
}

// Linux without `ps`: the same "pid ppid" lines `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` prints,
// built from /proc/<n>/stat. "" anywhere else or when /proc cannot be read.
// One file at a time: a few hundred tiny in-memory reads, never hundreds of
// open files at once.
async function procPsText() {
  if (!isLinux) return "";
  let names;
  try {
    names = await readdir(PROC_DIR);
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
  const lines = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!NUMERIC.test(name)) continue;
    try {
      const line = procLine(await readFile(`${PROC_DIR}/${name}/stat`, "utf8"));
      if (line) lines.push(line);
    } catch {
      // the process ended between the listing and the read
    }
  }
  return lines.join("\n");
}

// The same, synchronously, for the process.on("exit") sweep.
function procPsTextSync() {
  if (!isLinux) return "";
  let names;
  try {
    names = readdirSync(PROC_DIR);
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
  const lines = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!NUMERIC.test(name)) continue;
    try {
      const line = procLine(readFileSync(`${PROC_DIR}/${name}/stat`, "utf8"));
      if (line) lines.push(line);
    } catch {
      // the process ended between the listing and the read
    }
  }
  return lines.join("\n");
}

// One `ps` run (argv only, at most 2 s). When `ps` cannot run (the Docker
// image node:20-bookworm-slim has no procps), Linux reads /proc instead.
// Windows keeps using taskkill /T, so it returns []. Only when neither `ps`
// nor /proc can be read is the result [], and killProcessTree() then signals
// the process group only.
export async function listDescendants(pid) {
  if (isWindows || !Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return [];
  const psText = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    execFile("ps", PS_ARGS, { timeout: PS_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, (error, stdout) => {
      resolve(error ? null : stdout);
    });
  });
  return descendantsFromPsOutput(psText ?? (await procPsText()), pid);
}

// Checks the whole process group, not just the leader: an agent can exit
// quickly while a grandchild that ignores SIGTERM keeps running.
function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(-pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    try {
      process.kill(pid, 0);
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }
}

// Signals the process group led by pid, or pid alone when it leads none.
// Returns false when neither exists.
function signalTree(pid, signal) {
  try {
    process.kill(-pid, signal);
    return true;
  } catch {
    try {
      process.kill(pid, signal);
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }
}

export async function killProcessTree(pid, { graceMs = 1500 } = {}) {
  if (!pid) return;
  if (isWindows) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => {
      const killer = spawn("taskkill", ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"]);
      killer.once("exit", () => resolve());
      killer.once("error", () => resolve());
    });
    return;
  }
  // List first: once the leader dies, its children are handed to init and
  // the parent-pid walk can no longer find them.
  const descendants = await listDescendants(pid);
  const leaderSignalled = signalTree(pid, "SIGTERM");
  for (const child of descendants) signalTree(child, "SIGTERM");
  const targets = [pid, ...descendants];
  const anyAlive = () => targets.some((target) => isAlive(target));
  if (!leaderSignalled && !anyAlive()) return;
  await new Promise((resolve) => {
    let settled = false;
    const finish = () => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearInterval(poll);
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve();
    };
    // Deliberately not unref()'d: callers await this promise, and an unref'd
    // timer can let Node decide the event loop is empty and exit before it
    // fires, abandoning the still-pending promise.
    const poll = setInterval(() => {
      if (!anyAlive()) finish();
    }, 50);
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      for (const target of targets) {
        if (isAlive(target)) signalTree(target, "SIGKILL");
      }
      // SIGKILL delivery is asynchronous; keep polling so callers can rely on
      // "resolved" meaning "gone", but never wait more than another second.
      setTimeout(finish, 1000);
    }, graceMs);
  });
}

// Used by shutdown() to clean up every tracked child and pid in one pass.
export async function killAllTracked({ graceMs = 1500 } = {}) {
  const children = [...trackedChildren];
  const pids = [...trackedPids.keys()];
  await Promise.allSettled([
    ...children.map((child) => (child.pid ? killProcessTree(child.pid, { graceMs }) : Promise.resolve())),
    ...pids.map((pid) => killProcessTree(pid, { graceMs }))
  ]);
  for (const child of children) trackedChildren.delete(child);
  for (const pid of pids) trackedPids.delete(pid);
}

// Synchronous last resort for the `process.on("exit")` handler, where async
// work cannot run. Best effort: one ps snapshot (on Linux without ps, one
// /proc snapshot), then a single SIGKILL to every tracked group and every
// descendant, no wait for exit.
export function killAllTrackedSync() {
  if (isWindows) {
    for (const child of trackedChildren) {
      try {
        child.kill();
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
    }
    for (const pid of trackedPids.keys()) {
      try {
        spawnSync("taskkill", ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"], { timeout: 2000, windowsHide: true });
      } catch {
        // nothing more we can do synchronously
      }
    }
    return;
  }
  let psText = null;
  try {
    const result = spawnSync("ps", PS_ARGS, { encoding: "utf8", timeout: PS_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS });
    psText = result.error || result.status !== 0 ? null : result.stdout || "";
  } catch {
    psText = null;
  }
  if (psText === null) psText = procPsTextSync();
  const leaders = [...[...trackedChildren].map((child) => child.pid).filter(Boolean), ...trackedPids.keys()];
  // Every tree is listed before anything is signalled.
  const trees = leaders.map((leader) => [leader, descendantsFromPsOutput(psText, leader)]);
  for (const [leader, descendants] of trees) {
    signalTree(leader, "SIGKILL");
    for (const child of descendants) signalTree(child, "SIGKILL");
  }
}
```

(Why `signalTree` on each descendant: for a descendant that leads its own group, such as a setsid grandchild, `kill(-pid)` also reaches anything it started after the `ps` snapshot. For one inside the leader's group, `kill(-pid)` fails and the plain `kill(pid)` is used; that process gets SIGTERM twice, which is harmless. The cost if a pid is reused inside the grace window is the one Q3 accepts.)

```js
// Shutdown (spec SP3, "Persistence, quit and Stop"; planning decision Q4):
// the 8 second hard exit, the shutdown tasks other modules register (the
// terminal sessions, from S7), and the line the desktop shell writes to the
// server's stdin to quit gracefully on every OS.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtemp, realpath, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { spawnTracked } from "../server/runtime/process-tree.js";
import {
  HARD_EXIT_MS,
  SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS,
  STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE,
  registerShutdownTask,
  shutdown
} from "../server/runtime/shutdown.js";
import { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
// The only folders besides the fakes' own on a test server's PATH (R16).
const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];
const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function collectLogs(child) {
  const ref = { text: "" };
  child.stdout?.on("data", (chunk) => {
    ref.text += chunk;
  });
  child.stderr?.on("data", (chunk) => {
    ref.text += chunk;
  });
  return ref;
}

async function waitForReady(child, logsRef, deadlineMs = 20000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + deadlineMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    if (/AGENT_OS_READY:\d+/.test(logsRef.text)) return;
    if (child.exitCode != null) throw new Error(`server exited early (${child.exitCode}):\n${logsRef.text.slice(-2000)}`);
    await delay(100);
  }
  throw new Error(`server never printed AGENT_OS_READY:\n${logsRef.text.slice(-2000)}`);
}

// Resolves { code, signal } when the child exits, or null after ms.
function exitWithin(child, ms) {
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) {
    return Promise.resolve({ code: child.exitCode, signal: child.signalCode });
  }
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), ms);
    child.once("exit", (code, signal) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code, signal });
    });
  });
}

async function killChild(child) {
  if (!child || child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) return;
  child.kill("SIGTERM");
  if (!(await exitWithin(child, 3000))) child.kill("SIGKILL");
}

// The real server with a temp home, set up as every test server that could
// start a session (R15, R16): W1's stand-in login shell, so neither the
// developer's own shell setup nor a real login sh (whose path_helper puts
// /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin first) runs for the sessions'
// login-shell lookup; and on PATH the six fake agents, then the system
// folders only, so agent detection finds a fake before it searches
// /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin. The shims are POSIX only.
async function startServer(home, extraEnv = {}) {
  const fakeBin = path.join(home, "fake-bin");
  if (!isWindows) await makeFakeAgentBin(fakeBin);
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["server/index.js"], {
    cwd: root,
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      PORT: "0",
      AGENT_OS_HOME: home,
      AGENT_OS_TOKEN: "t",
      HERMES_AGENT_OS_SCHEDULER: "0",
      HOME: home,
      USERPROFILE: home,
      SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
      PATH: [...(isWindows ? [] : [fakeBin]), ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter),
      AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN: undefined,
      ...extraEnv
    },
    stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"]
  });
  const logs = collectLogs(child);
  await waitForReady(child, logs);
  return { child, logs };
}

async function withTempHome(fn) {
  // Real path: on macOS os.tmpdir() sits behind a symlink (Global Constraints).
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-shutdown-")));
  try {
    return await fn(home);
  } finally {
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

  test("registerShutdownTask refuses a missing name or a missing function", () => {
    assert.throws(() => registerShutdownTask("", () => {}), TypeError);
    assert.throws(() => registerShutdownTask("   ", () => {}), TypeError);
    assert.throws(() => registerShutdownTask("sessions", null), TypeError);
  });

  test("shutdown() runs every registered task, all at the same time", async () => {
    const ran = [];
    const slow = (name) => async () => {
      await delay(1000);
      ran.push(name);
    };
    const offA = registerShutdownTask("test-a", slow("a"));
    const offB = registerShutdownTask("test-b", slow("b"));
    try {
      const started = Date.now();
      await shutdown({});
      const elapsed = Date.now() - started;
      assert.deepEqual(ran.sort(), ["a", "b"]);
      assert.ok(elapsed >= 950, `took ${elapsed} ms`);
      assert.ok(elapsed < 1900, `took ${elapsed} ms, so the tasks ran one after the other`);
    } finally {
      offA();
      offB();
    }
  });

  test("a task that fails does not stop the others or the shutdown", async () => {
    let otherRan = false;
    const offA = registerShutdownTask("test-throws", () => {
      throw new Error("boom");
    });
    const offB = registerShutdownTask("test-rejects", async () => {
      throw new Error("boom again");
    });
    const offC = registerShutdownTask("test-fine", () => {
      otherRan = true;
    });
    try {
      await shutdown({});
      assert.equal(otherRan, true);
    } finally {
      offA();
      offB();
      offC();
    }
  });

  test("a task that never finishes is cut off at the limit", async () => {
    const off = registerShutdownTask("test-hangs", () => new Promise(() => {}));
    try {
      const started = Date.now();
      await shutdown({ taskLimitMs: 300 });
      assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 2500, `took ${Date.now() - started} ms`);
    } finally {
      off();
    }
  });

  test(
    "tasks run before the kill sweep, so they still see the processes they will stop",
    { skip: isWindows ? "process groups are POSIX-only" : false },
    async () => {
      const child = spawnTracked(process.execPath, ["-e", "setInterval(() => {}, 1000)"], { stdio: "ignore" });
      let aliveWhenTaskRan = null;
      const off = registerShutdownTask("test-order", () => {
        aliveWhenTaskRan = isAlive(child.pid);
      });
      try {
        await shutdown({});
        assert.equal(aliveWhenTaskRan, true);
        assert.equal(isAlive(child.pid), false, "the kill sweep still ran afterwards");
      } finally {
        off();
      }
    }
  );

  test("registering the same name again replaces the task, and the returned function unregisters it", async () => {
    let first = 0;
    let second = 0;
    const offFirst = registerShutdownTask("test-same", () => {
      first += 1;
    });
    const offSecond = registerShutdownTask("test-same", () => {
      second += 1;
    });
    offFirst(); // stale: must not remove the newer task
    await shutdown({});
    assert.deepEqual([first, second], [0, 1]);
    offSecond();
    await shutdown({});
    assert.deepEqual([first, second], [0, 1]);
  });
});

describe("hard exit", () => {
  test(
    "the hard exit ends the process even when a shutdown task never finishes",
    { skip: isWindows ? "Windows has no SIGTERM handler to trigger" : false },
    async () => {
      await withTempHome(async (home) => {
        const script = path.join(home, "hang.mjs");
        const shutdownUrl = pathToFileURL(path.join(root, "server", "runtime", "shutdown.js")).href;
        await writeFile(
          script,
          [
            `import { installShutdownHandlers, registerShutdownTask } from ${JSON.stringify(shutdownUrl)};`,
            'registerShutdownTask("hangs", () => new Promise(() => {}));',
            "installShutdownHandlers(undefined, { hardExitMs: 1000, taskLimitMs: 60000 });",
            'console.log("READY");',
            "setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"
          ].join("\n")
        );
        const child = spawn(process.execPath, [script], {
          cwd: home,
          env: { ...process.env, AGENT_OS_HOME: home, HOME: home, USERPROFILE: home, AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN: undefined },
          stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]
        });
        const logs = collectLogs(child);
        try {
          await (async () => {
            const deadline = Date.now() + 10000;
            while (!logs.text.includes("READY")) {
              if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`no READY:\n${logs.text}`);
              await delay(50);
            }
          })();
          const started = Date.now();
          child.kill("SIGTERM");
          const exit = await exitWithin(child, 5000);
          const elapsed = Date.now() - started;
          assert.ok(exit, "the process did not exit");
          assert.equal(exit.code, 0);
          assert.ok(elapsed >= 900, `exited after ${elapsed} ms, before the hard exit`);
        } finally {
          await killChild(child);
        }
      });
    }
  );
});

  test("with AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1, the line AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN shuts the server down", async () => {
    await withTempHome(async (home) => {

      try {

  test("end of input on stdin also shuts it down (the desktop shell is gone)", async () => {
    await withTempHome(async (home) => {
      const { child } = await startServer(home, { AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN: "1" });
      try {
        child.stdin.end();

        assert.ok(exit, "the server did not exit");
        assert.equal(exit.code, 0);
      } finally {

  test("any other line is ignored", async () => {
    await withTempHome(async (home) => {
      const { child } = await startServer(home, { AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN: "1" });

        child.stdin.write("hello\nAGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN_PLEASE\n");
        assert.equal(await exitWithin(child, 1500), null, "the server stopped on a line that is not the quit line");
        child.stdin.write(`${STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE}\n`);
        assert.ok(await exitWithin(child, HARD_EXIT_MS + 500), "the quit line still works afterwards");
      } finally {

      }

  test("without AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN, stdin is never read", async () => {

        child.stdin.end();
        assert.equal(await exitWithin(child, 1500), null, "the server must keep running");
      } finally {
        await killChild(child);
      }
    });
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Replace `server/runtime/shutdown.js`.** Replace the whole file (lines 1-74) with:

```js
// One place that tears everything down: the scheduler loop, every run, every
// task other modules registered with registerShutdownTask() (the terminal
// sessions, from SP3), every tracked child process and pid, and the
// short-lived live-chat children, before the HTTP server closes. Reused by
// the signal handlers and the desktop shell's stdin line below, and by tests
// that check cleanup directly.
import readline from "node:readline";
import { stopSchedulerLoop } from "./scheduler.js";
import { killAllTracked, killAllTrackedSync } from "./process-tree.js";
import { activeLiveChatChildren } from "./live-chat.js";
import { getRunManager } from "./runs/run-manager.js";

// A quit ends the process this long after it starts, whatever is still
// running (spec SP3, "Persistence, quit and Stop": 8 s, inside the desktop
// shell's 10 s QUIT_GRACE).
export const HARD_EXIT_MS = 8000;
// Each shutdown task gets at most this long, so one stuck task cannot hold the
// kill sweep and server.close() past the hard exit. The sessions task (S7)
// caps itself at the same 7 s.
export const SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS = 7000;
// The desktop shell writes this exact line to the server's stdin to quit
// gracefully on every OS (planning decision Q4).
export const STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN";

const shutdownTasks = new Map();

// Registers fn to run at shutdown, in parallel with the runs' own stop and
// with every other task, and BEFORE the kill sweep (so a task can record why
// its processes end before anything is killed). A second registration under
// the same name replaces the first. Returns a function that unregisters it.
export function registerShutdownTask(name, fn) {
  if (typeof name !== "string" || !name.trim()) throw new TypeError("registerShutdownTask needs a name");
  if (typeof fn !== "function") throw new TypeError("registerShutdownTask needs a function");
  shutdownTasks.set(name, fn);
  return () => {
    if (shutdownTasks.get(name) === fn) shutdownTasks.delete(name);
  };
}

function runGuarded(name, fn, limitMs) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let done = false;
    const finish = () => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve();
    };
    // Not unref()'d: a stuck task must not keep shutdown waiting, but the
    // timer itself has to fire.
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      console.error(`Shutdown step "${name}" took longer than ${limitMs} ms; continuing without it.`);
      finish();
    }, limitMs);
    Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => fn())
      .catch((error) => console.error(`Shutdown step "${name}" failed: ${error?.message || error}`))
      .finally(finish);
  });
}

export async function shutdown({ server, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {}) {
  try {
    stopSchedulerLoop();
  } catch {
    // best effort
  }

  // Runs are marked "stopped" (so their metadata says why they ended) and
  // the registered tasks run, all in parallel and all before the raw kill
  // sweep below.
  await Promise.all([
    (async () => {
      try {
        await getRunManager().stopAll();
      } catch {
        // best effort
      }
    })(),
    ...[...shutdownTasks.entries()].map(([name, fn]) => runGuarded(name, fn, taskLimitMs))
  ]);

  await killAllTracked();

  for (const child of activeLiveChatChildren) {
    try {
      child.kill("SIGTERM");
    } catch {
      // already gone
    }
  }
  activeLiveChatChildren.clear();

  if (server) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => {
      let done = false;
      const finish = () => {
        if (done) return;
        done = true;
        resolve();
      };
      server.close(finish);
      setTimeout(finish, 500).unref?.();
    });
  }
}

export function installShutdownHandlers(server, { hardExitMs = HARD_EXIT_MS, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {}) {
  let triggered = false;
  const trigger = () => {
    if (triggered) return;
    triggered = true;
    const hardExit = setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), hardExitMs);
    hardExit.unref?.();
    shutdown({ server, taskLimitMs }).finally(() => process.exit(0));
  };
  process.on("SIGTERM", trigger);
  process.on("SIGINT", trigger);
  if (process.platform === "win32") process.on("SIGBREAK", trigger);
  // The desktop shell (AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1, stdin piped) quits the
  // server by writing one line, the same on every OS; on Windows there is no
  // other graceful way. End of input means the shell itself is gone. Without
  // the variable, stdin is never read.
  if (process.env.AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN === "1") {
    const lines = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin, crlfDelay: Infinity, terminal: false });
    lines.on("line", (line) => {
      if (line.trim() === STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE) trigger();
    });
    lines.on("close", trigger);
  }
  // process.on("exit") handlers must be synchronous, so this is a
  // best-effort SIGKILL sweep in case the async shutdown() above never ran.
  process.on("exit", () => {
    killAllTrackedSync();
    for (const child of activeLiveChatChildren) {
      try {
        child.kill("SIGKILL");
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
    }
  });
}
```

(The time budget inside the 8 s: the runs' `stopAll()` and the sessions' quit run side by side; the sessions' worst case is the spec's 2 s soft stop plus the 3 s kill grace, well inside the 7 s task limit. When the tasks have stopped their own processes, the kill sweep finds nothing left and is instant, so `server.close()` (at most 0.5 s) still ends before 8 s. The hard exit is the backstop, and its `process.on("exit")` sweep still SIGKILLs every tracked tree.)
