#### Notes

1. **A setsid grandchild of an agent that already exited cannot be found.** Its parent is gone, so it now belongs to pid 1, and the walk from the agent's pid cannot reach it. The Stop sequence always runs while the agent is alive, so this only matters when an agent exits on its own and leaves such a process behind; nothing tracks that case today either. The Help page's Stop wording (U4) allows for it.
2. **Hosts without `ps`.** On Linux, when `ps` cannot run (the Docker image `node:20-bookworm-slim` has no `procps`), the walk and the exit sweep read `/proc/<n>/stat` instead, so a setsid grandchild is still stopped there (this serves runs in Docker; sessions in Docker are out of SP3, R27). `parseProcStat` counts fields from the last `)`, because a command name can hold spaces and `)`. A non-zero `ps` exit (for example a busybox `ps` without `-A`) counts as "`ps` failed". Only when neither `ps` nor `/proc` can be read does the kill fall back to the process group alone; macOS, the CI runners and the desktop targets all have `ps`.
3. **Every `killProcessTree` call now runs `ps` first.** Run stops, run time-outs and builder stops wait for one `ps` (tens of milliseconds, at most 2 s) before the first SIGTERM. The existing tree tests are unchanged and pass.
4. **The time budget (R5).** The sessions task is cut off at 7 s (`SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS`, the same as S7's own `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS`), inside the 8 s hard exit, inside the desktop shell's 10 s `QUIT_GRACE`. A task that uses its whole 7 s leaves the kill sweep less than its 1.5 s grace; the hard exit then ends the process, and its `process.on("exit")` sweep SIGKILLs every tracked tree.
5. **End of stdin quits.** With `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1`, a closed or `/dev/null` stdin ends the server at once (Q4: the desktop shell is gone), so the variable is only for a piped stdin that stays open, which D1 keeps for the app's whole life (R19). The quit line is compared after trimming spaces, so a Windows `\r\n` still matches; any other text is ignored (tested).
6. **Windows exit sweep.** `killAllTrackedSync` runs `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` (synchronous, 2 s limit each) for tracked pids; spawned children keep `child.kill()`.
7. **Checked while drafting.** In a throwaway copy of the repo (not this worktree), with W1's `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`, `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`, `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`, `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` taken from W1's draft, and this file's code blocks applied: the two new test files fail on today's code with exactly the `SyntaxError` lines of Steps 2 and 6; after Steps 3, 7 and 9, `test/shutdown.test.js` gives 12 of 12, `test/portable.test.js` with `test/runs.test.js` 23 of 23, and `test/process-tree.test.js` 10 pass and 2 skipped on macOS, plus the one node-pty test, which fails there only because node-pty arrives with W0. Under W1's runner the three files end with `no-real-agents watcher: no real agent started`. The node-pty test's logic was run once without node-pty (the fake `claude` shim started as its own group leader with the same environment): the grandchild left the group, the walk found it, the stand-in shell reached the fake as `SHELL`, and `killProcessTree` stopped both and untracked the pid. Step 10's two `grep` checks print what they show (`grep -r` listed the importers in a different order, hence "in any order"); the full `npm test` and `npm run build` of Step 10 were not run in this round. In the first drafting round, with the same `process-tree.js`, the whole suite ran under the watcher with `# fail 0` apart from the node-pty test, and the `/proc` fallback was checked in a local `node:24-bookworm-slim` container with no `ps`: the kill tests and the `/proc` test passed, and with the fallback switched off the `/proc` test failed, as it should.

---

### Task S2: Login-shell environment (H2), folder policy (D12), private store folders

Every session starts with the person's own login-shell environment (spec H2), in a folder that passes the folder policy (D12), and keeps its files in private folders (Security 5). This task builds those three foundations, which the launch profiles (S3), the recorder (S5), the manager (S6) and the routes (S8) stand on. It spawns no agent and no terminal.

- `server/runtime/sessions/shell-env.js` reads the login shell once per server, the way VS Code does: the shell runs Node, which prints its own environment as JSON between two random markers, so banners from startup files can't confuse it and values with newlines survive. A hang past 10 s, missing markers or a failing shell give the server's own environment plus the usual install folders, with the quiet notice "Agent OS could not read your login shell's settings, so sessions use a basic environment.". Windows has no login shell, so there the process environment is used as it is. Values Agent OS itself put into the server's environment are not the person's environment (decision Q11a): the keys `loadLocalEnv` added from Agent OS's own env file are registered with `excludeFromSessionEnv()` (Task S8 wires it), are never handed to the login shell, and the fallback and Windows environments leave them out too. A value the person's own startup files set under the same name is still theirs and is kept: nothing is taken out of the login shell's own answer except the resolver shell's own `PWD`, `OLDPWD` and `_` (decision Q7a; Task S3 sets `PWD` to the session's folder). The desktop shell gives the server its port as `AGENT_OS_PORT` (Task D1), an Agent OS name, so the server's own port never reaches a session (a `PORT` the person's own startup files export still does, as in Terminal). The desktop shell also extends the server's `PATH` with folders of its own (`server_path_env` in `main.rs`: Homebrew, `~/.local/bin`, Agent OS's managed Node folder and others), so when it passes the `PATH` the app itself was started with as `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` (Task D1), the login shell starts with that `PATH` instead, as Terminal's login shell does; the person's startup files still add to it. When an npm script started Agent OS (`npm start`, `npm run dev`, `npm run desktop:dev`), what npm added is left out the same way: its own lower-case `npm_*` variables, `INIT_CWD`, `NODE`, `COLOR`, the `EDITOR` npm fills in when the person has none, and the `node_modules/.bin` and `node-gyp-bin` folders npm puts in front of `PATH` (this extends decision Q11a). `sessionEnv()` then turns that environment into a session's: it removes ONLY Agent OS's own variables (`AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*`) and the two Claude nested-session markers, and sets ONLY the terminal variables, the session id and (Claude Code with the H4 opt-in) `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER`.
- `server/runtime/sessions/folders.js` canonicalises a folder with `fs.realpath.native` (on-disk letter case, symlinks resolved) and refuses HOME itself, Agent OS's own folders (AGENT_OS_HOME except its `worktrees/`, and the managed Node folder, planning decision Q12) and anything outside HOME. Comparisons ignore letter case on macOS and Windows. It also lists recent session folders from `meta.json` files, each checked again.
- `server/runtime/store.js` gains the `sessions` and `worktrees` paths, and makes the root, `sessions/` and `worktrees/` 0700, with a chmod when they already exist (today every folder is created with the default mode). Only the root is forgiving: when its chmod fails with EPERM or EACCES (an AGENT_OS_HOME another account owns), Agent OS warns once and carries on instead of failing every store write; `sessions/` and `worktrees/` stay strict.

**Worker notes:**

Every other entry keeps its place. Nothing is taken out of the login shell's own answer.

They are left out of what goes into the login shell, the fallback and the Windows environment, never out of what the login shell gives back; on Windows they match without letter case. It reads `<root>/sessions/<id>/meta.json` and uses only `kind`, `folder`, `folderShown`, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `lastUsedAt` (ISO 8601 text; a row's `lastUsedAt` is the latest of its three times, so a meta.json without `lastUsedAt` still sorts by its start and end). Rows with `kind: "update"` or `folderShown: false` are left out, and each folder is checked again with `checkSessionFolder`, so a folder deleted or moved since, or one that no longer passes the policy, is dropped (Review Focus 4). Task S6 writes `meta.json` with these field names (its `lastUsedAt` is the latest start, resume or end; an OpenClaw session's `folder` is HOME with `folderShown: false`).

```js
// Sessions, files on disk (spec Security 5): Agent OS's own folder, sessions/
// and worktrees/ are private (0700), also when they already existed with the
// default mode. Temp AGENT_OS_HOME only; nothing here starts anything.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { promises as fsPromises } from "node:fs";
import { chmod, mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { ensurePrivateDir, ensureRuntimeStore, runtimePaths } from "../server/runtime/store.js";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const modeSkip = { skip: isWindows ? "Windows has no POSIX file modes" : false };

async function withRuntimeHome(fn) {
  const base = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-store-"));
  const root = path.join(base, "agent-os-home");
  const previous = { AGENT_OS_HOME: process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME, HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: process.env.HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME };
  process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME = root;
  delete process.env.HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME;
  try {
    return await fn({ base, root });
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
    await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

const modeOf = async (dir) => (await stat(dir)).mode & 0o777;

test("ensureRuntimeStore carries on when its own folder can't be made private (another account owns it), warning once; sessions/ and worktrees/ stay strict", modeSkip, async (t) => {
  await withRuntimeHome(async ({ root }) => {
    // The chmod of one folder fails as it does for a folder another account
    // owns; every other chmod is the real one.
    const realChmod = fsPromises.chmod;
    let failOn = path.resolve(root);
    let failCode = "EPERM";
    t.mock.method(fsPromises, "chmod", async (target, mode) => {
      if (path.resolve(String(target)) === failOn) {
        throw Object.assign(new Error(`${failCode}: operation not permitted, chmod '${target}'`), { code: failCode });
      }
      return realChmod(target, mode);
    });

    const paths = await ensureRuntimeStore();
    await ensureRuntimeStore();
    assert.equal(warn.mock.callCount(), 1, "warned once, not on every call");
    assert.deepEqual(warn.mock.calls[0].arguments, [`Agent OS could not make its folder private (0700): ${root}`]);
    assert.equal(await modeOf(paths.sessions), 0o700);
    assert.equal(await modeOf(paths.worktrees), 0o700);
    for (const dir of Object.values(paths)) assert.ok((await stat(dir)).isDirectory(), dir);

    failCode = "EACCES";
    await ensureRuntimeStore();
    assert.equal(warn.mock.callCount(), 1, "EACCES on the root is tolerated the same way");

    // Only the root is tolerated: the same failure on sessions/ or worktrees/,
    // or any other failure on the root, still stops the store.
    for (const strict of [paths.sessions, paths.worktrees]) {
      failOn = path.resolve(strict);
      failCode = "EPERM";
      await assert.rejects(ensureRuntimeStore(), { code: "EPERM" }, strict);
    }
    failOn = path.resolve(root);
    failCode = "EIO";
    await assert.rejects(ensureRuntimeStore(), { code: "EIO" });
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Give store.js the two folders and the private modes.** In `server/runtime/store.js`, replace `runtimePaths()` and `ensureRuntimeStore()` (lines 27-45, from `export function runtimePaths() {` to the closing `}` of `ensureRuntimeStore`) with this block. Nothing else in the file changes.

```js
export function runtimePaths() {
  const root = osRoot();
  return {
    root,
    config: path.join(root, "config"),
    workflows: path.join(root, "workflows"),
    runs: path.join(root, "runs"),
    logs: path.join(root, "logs"),
    memory: path.join(root, "memory"),
    exports: path.join(root, "exports"),
    workspace: path.join(root, "workspace"),
    // Sessions (spec SP3): one folder per session id (meta.json, recording,
    // settings file). Worktrees: separate copies of a person's project (SP4).
    sessions: path.join(root, "sessions"),
    worktrees: path.join(root, "worktrees")
  };
}

// Folders below the root that hold private data (session recordings,
// settings files, copies of a person's projects): only the person's own
// account may open them (spec Security 5). The root is made private too, in
// ensurePrivateRoot below.
const PRIVATE_DIRS = new Set(["sessions", "worktrees"]);

// mkdir -p with mode 0700, then a chmod, because mkdir's mode only applies to
// folders it creates and an older folder may have been made with 0755.
// Windows has no such modes, so there it only makes the folder.
export async function ensurePrivateDir(dir) {
  await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  if (process.platform !== "win32") await fs.chmod(dir, 0o700);
  return dir;
}

// Roots already warned about, so the warning shows once, not on every call.
const warnedRoots = new Set();

// The root is made private like sessions/ and worktrees/, with one exception:
// an AGENT_OS_HOME another account owns can't be chmodded (EPERM, or EACCES
// on the way to it). Throwing then would make every store write fail and stop
// the whole app, so only the root's mode is given up, with a warning.
// sessions/ and worktrees/ stay strict: their chmod still throws.
async function ensurePrivateRoot(root) {
  await fs.mkdir(root, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  if (process.platform === "win32") return;
  try {
    await fs.chmod(root, 0o700);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error?.code !== "EPERM" && error?.code !== "EACCES") throw error;
    if (!warnedRoots.has(root)) {
      warnedRoots.add(root);
      console.warn("Agent OS could not make its folder private (0700): " + root);
    }
  }
}

export async function ensureRuntimeStore() {
  const paths = runtimePaths();
  // The root first, so making a subfolder never creates it with the default mode.
  await ensurePrivateRoot(paths.root);
  await Promise.all(
    Object.entries(paths)
      .filter(([name]) => name !== "root")
      .map(([name, dir]) => (PRIVATE_DIRS.has(name) ? ensurePrivateDir(dir) : fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true })))
  );
  return paths;
}
```

Why the root comes first: `fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true })` of a subfolder would otherwise create a missing root with the default mode. Why the chmod: `mkdir`'s `mode` only applies to folders it creates, so an older install's 0755 folders would stay open (the keystore already does the same, `server/runtime/secrets/keystore.js` `fileWrite`). Why only the root forgives EPERM and EACCES: `ensureRuntimeStore()` runs before store writes, so a root chmod that throws (an AGENT_OS_HOME another account owns, for example a shared folder) would make every write fail and stop the whole app, not just leave one folder's mode weaker. The private data lives in `sessions/` and `worktrees/`, so their chmod still throws. The warning appears once per root folder, not on every call. `fs.chmod` is called through the `fs.promises` object, which the store test replaces with `t.mock.method` to make the root's chmod fail.

```js
// Sessions, the child environment (spec H2 and Security 2): reading the
// person's login-shell environment between random markers, the 10 s limit and
// the fallback with its notice, and exactly which variables a session's
// environment removes, sets and passes through. Nothing here starts an agent
// and no real login shell runs (decision Q1c): the "login shells" are small
// fake scripts in a temp folder and Task W1's stand-in, and HOME is always a
// temp folder.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { chmod, mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";
import {
  FALLBACK_NOTICE,
  LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS,
  NESTED_MARKERS,
  excludeFromSessionEnv,
  getLoginShellEnv,
  resetExcludedForTests,
  resetLoginShellEnvForTests,
  resolveLoginShellEnv,
  sessionEnv
} from "../server/runtime/sessions/shell-env.js";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const posixSkip = { skip: isWindows ? "fake login shells are POSIX shell scripts" : false };
const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// A temp HOME, a system-only PATH, no launch PATH from a desktop shell, no
// excluded names, and a folder for the fake shells. `npm test` is itself an
// npm script, so npm_lifecycle_event is cleared: every test here sees a server
// that no npm script started, unless it says otherwise.
async function withShellWorld(fn) {
  const base = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-shell-env-")));
  const home = path.join(base, "home");
  await mkdir(home, { recursive: true });
  resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
  resetExcludedForTests();
  try {
    return await withEnv(
      {
        HOME: home,
        USERPROFILE: home,
        PATH: SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS.join(path.delimiter),
        AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH: undefined,
        npm_lifecycle_event: undefined,
        AGENT_OS_TOKEN: "secret-session-token",
        HERMES_AGENT_OS_ADMIN_TOKEN: "secret-admin-token",
        SESSIONS_TEST_PLANTED: "planted by the test"
      },
      async () => {
        assert.equal(os.homedir(), home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
        return fn({ base, home });
      }
    );
  } finally {
    resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
    resetExcludedForTests();
    await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

// Writes a fake login shell: `body` runs first; "$last" is the command string
// Agent OS passed (its last argument). Every call records its arguments.
async function fakeShell(dir, name, body) {
  const file = path.join(dir, name);
  const record = path.join(dir, `${name}.args`);
  await writeFile(
    file,
    ["#!/bin/sh", `printf '%s\\n' "$@" >> "${record}"`, "for last; do :; done", body, ""].join("\n"),
    "utf8"
  );
  await chmod(file, 0o755);
  return { file, record };
}

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

async function waitFor(predicate, timeoutMs = 3000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    if (await predicate()) return true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
  }
  return false;
}

        'echo "Good morning from a startup file"',
        `echo '{"PATH":"/printed/by/a/startup/file"}'`,
        'echo "warning: a plugin could not load" >&2',
        'printf "\\033[1;32mcoloured banner\\033[0m\\n"',
        'export FROM_STARTUP_FILE="set by .zprofile"',

    assert.equal(result.env.PATH, process.env.PATH);
    assert.equal(result.env.SESSIONS_TEST_PLANTED, "planted by the test");
    assert.equal(result.env.AGENT_OS_TOKEN, undefined);
  });
});

test("login shell (Review Focus 1): a startup file that asks a question gets no input and no terminal, so it carries on and the environment is read", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    const answered = path.join(base, "answered");
    const terminal = path.join(base, "terminal");
    const { file } = await fakeShell(
      base,
      "asking-shell",
      [
        // Like oh-my-zsh's "update now?" prompt: read one answer from input.
        "printf 'Update now? [Y/n] '",
        `if read answer; then printf 'answer:%s' "$answer" > "${answered}"; else printf 'end of input' > "${answered}"; fi`,
        // A startup step that reads everything it is given.
        "cat > /dev/null",
        // A prompt that insists on the terminal itself: there is none.
        `if (exec 3< /dev/tty) 2>/dev/null; then printf 'terminal' > "${terminal}"; else printf 'no terminal' > "${terminal}"; fi`,
        'export ASKED_FIRST="yes"',
        '/bin/sh -c "$last"'
      ].join("\n")
    );
    const started = Date.now();
    const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: file, timeoutMs: 5000 });
    assert.equal(result.source, "login-shell", "the question did not stall it until the limit");
    assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 5000);
    assert.equal(result.env.ASKED_FIRST, "yes");
    assert.equal(await readFile(answered, "utf8"), "end of input", "Agent OS typed no answer");
    assert.equal(await readFile(terminal, "utf8"), "no terminal", "the shell has no terminal to wait on");
  });
});

test("login shell (Review Focus 1): the limit is 10 seconds, and a shell that hangs past it is killed and the fallback used", posixSkip, async () => {
  assert.equal(LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS, 10000);
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    const pidFile = path.join(base, "hang.pid");
    const { file } = await fakeShell(base, "hanging-shell", `echo $$ > "${pidFile}"\nexec sleep 30`);
    const started = Date.now();
    const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: file, timeoutMs: 1500 });
    assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 6000, "gave up at the limit, not after the 30 s sleep");
    assert.equal(result.source, "fallback");
    assert.equal(result.notice, FALLBACK_NOTICE);
    assert.ok(await waitFor(() => existsSync(pidFile)), "the fake shell started");
    const pid = Number((await readFile(pidFile, "utf8")).trim());
    assert.ok(await waitFor(() => !isAlive(pid)), "the hanging shell was killed");
  });
});

test("login shell: no markers, a failing shell, a missing shell or no PATH all give the fallback and its notice", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base, home }) => {
    const noMarkers = await fakeShell(base, "no-markers", `echo '{"PATH":"/nope"}'`);
    const failing = await fakeShell(base, "failing", 'echo "broken startup file" >&2\nexit 3');
    const noPath = await fakeShell(base, "no-path", '/usr/bin/env -i /bin/sh -c "$last"');
    for (const shell of [noMarkers.file, failing.file, noPath.file, path.join(base, "no-such-shell"), "relative/sh", ""]) {
      const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell });
      assert.equal(result.source, "fallback", String(shell));
      assert.equal(result.notice, "Agent OS could not read your login shell's settings, so sessions use a basic environment.");
      // The server's own environment plus the usual install folders, each once.
      const parts = result.env.PATH.split(path.delimiter);
      assert.deepEqual(parts, [...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS, "/usr/local/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin", path.join(home, ".local", "bin")]);
      assert.equal(result.env.SESSIONS_TEST_PLANTED, "planted by the test");
    }
    // A folder already on PATH is not added twice.
    await withEnv({ PATH: ["/opt/homebrew/bin", ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter) }, async () => {
      const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: noMarkers.file });
      assert.equal(result.env.PATH.split(path.delimiter).filter((dir) => dir === "/opt/homebrew/bin").length, 1);
    });
  });
});

test("login shell: Windows has none, so the process environment is used as it is and no shell runs", async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    const { file, record } = await fakeShell(base, "never-run", '/bin/sh -c "$last"');
    const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: file, platform: "win32" });
    assert.equal(result.source, "process");
    assert.equal(result.notice, null);
    const expected = {};
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(process.env)) if (typeof value === "string") expected[key] = value;
    assert.deepEqual(result.env, expected);
    assert.equal(existsSync(record), false, "no shell was started");
  });
});

test("login shell: names Agent OS put into its own environment (its own env file's keys, decision Q11a) reach neither the login shell, the fallback nor Windows", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    await withEnv(
      { SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV: "loaded by Agent OS", SESSIONS_TEST_KEPT: "the person's own", Sessions_Test_Case: "another spelling" },
      async () => {
        excludeFromSessionEnv(["SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV", "SESSIONS_TEST_CASE", 42, null]);

        const seen = path.join(base, "dotenv-seen");
        const passing = await fakeShell(
          base,
          "passing-shell",
          [`printf '%s' "\${SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV-unset}" > "${seen}"`, '/bin/sh -c "$last"'].join("\n")
        );
        const loginShell = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: passing.file });
        assert.equal(loginShell.source, "login-shell");
        assert.equal(loginShell.env.SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV, undefined);
        assert.equal(loginShell.env.SESSIONS_TEST_KEPT, "the person's own");
        assert.equal(await readFile(seen, "utf8"), "unset", "the person's startup files never receive it");

        const noMarkers = await fakeShell(base, "no-markers", `echo '{"PATH":"/nope"}'`);
        const fallback = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: noMarkers.file });
        assert.equal(fallback.source, "fallback");
        assert.equal(fallback.env.SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV, undefined);
        assert.equal(fallback.env.SESSIONS_TEST_KEPT, "the person's own");
        assert.equal(fallback.env.Sessions_Test_Case, "another spelling", "names keep their letter case apart outside Windows");

        const windows = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ platform: "win32" });
        assert.equal(windows.source, "process");
        assert.equal(windows.env.SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV, undefined);
        assert.equal(windows.env.SESSIONS_TEST_KEPT, "the person's own");
        assert.equal(windows.env.Sessions_Test_Case, undefined, "Windows names ignore letter case");

        // The same name set by the person's own startup file is theirs, so it
        // is kept (H2 removes only Agent OS's own variables).
        const own = await fakeShell(base, "own-shell", ['export SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV="set in .zshrc"', '/bin/sh -c "$last"'].join("\n"));
        assert.equal((await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: own.file })).env.SESSIONS_TEST_FROM_DOTENV, "set in .zshrc");
      }
    );
  });
});

test("login shell: it starts with the PATH the app was started with (AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH), not the folders the desktop shell added (H2, Q11a)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    await withEnv({ PATH: "/opt/extra:/usr/bin:/bin", AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" }, async () => {
      const standIn = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL });
      assert.equal(standIn.source, "login-shell");
      assert.equal(standIn.env.PATH, "/usr/bin:/bin");
      assert.equal(Object.hasOwn(standIn.env, "AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH"), false, "an Agent OS name never reaches a session");

      // It is what the login shell starts with, not its answer: the person's
      // startup files still add to it.
      const seen = path.join(base, "path-seen");
      const own = await fakeShell(
        base,
        "path-shell",
        [`printf '%s' "$PATH" > "${seen}"`, 'export PATH="/from/zprofile:$PATH"', '/bin/sh -c "$last"'].join("\n")
      );
      const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: own.file });
      assert.equal(await readFile(seen, "utf8"), "/usr/bin:/bin");
      assert.equal(result.env.PATH, "/from/zprofile:/usr/bin:/bin");
    });
    // Without it (npm start, the tests) the server's own PATH goes in, as before.
    for (const launchPath of [undefined, ""]) {
      await withEnv({ PATH: "/opt/extra:/usr/bin:/bin", AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH: launchPath }, async () => {
        assert.equal((await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL })).env.PATH, "/opt/extra:/usr/bin:/bin", String(launchPath));
      });
    }
  });
});

// What `npm start` or `npm run dev` adds to the server's environment (checked
// with npm 10): its own lower-case npm_* variables, INIT_CWD, NODE, COLOR,
// EDITOR=vi when the person has no EDITOR or VISUAL, and, in front of PATH,
// node_modules/.bin of the project folder and of every folder above it, then
// npm's own node-gyp-bin.
function npmStart(base) {
  const project = path.join(base, "agent-os");
  return {
    pathEntries: [
      path.join(project, "node_modules", ".bin"),
      path.join(base, "node_modules", ".bin"),
      path.join(path.parse(base).root, "node_modules", ".bin"),
      path.join(base, "npm", "node_modules", "@npmcli", "run-script", "lib", "node-gyp-bin")
    ],
    vars: {
      npm_lifecycle_event: "start",
      npm_lifecycle_script: "node server/index.js",
      npm_package_json: path.join(project, "package.json"),
      npm_package_name: "agent-os-runtime",
      npm_config_prefix: "/x",
      npm_config_cache: path.join(base, "home", ".npm"),
      npm_execpath: "/x/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js",
      INIT_CWD: "/y",
      NODE: process.execPath,
      COLOR: "1"
    }
  };
}

// npm's own names are lower case. Only those are counted: an upper-case name
// such as a developer's own NPM_TOKEN may be in the test process, and it is
// the person's, so it passes through.
const npmNames = (env) => Object.keys(env).filter((key) => key.startsWith("npm_"));

test("login shell: when an npm script started Agent OS (npm start, npm run dev), what npm added reaches neither the login shell, the fallback nor Windows (H2, Q11a)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base, home }) => {
    const npm = npmStart(base);
    const npmPath = [...npm.pathEntries, ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter);
    const personOwn = "/Users/someone/.npm-global";
    await withEnv({ ...npm.vars, PATH: npmPath, EDITOR: "vi", VISUAL: undefined, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX: personOwn }, async () => {
      const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL });
      assert.equal(result.source, "login-shell");
      assert.deepEqual(npmNames(result.env), [], "npm's own variables are gone");
      assert.equal(result.env.NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, personOwn, "the person's own npm setting stays (npm's names are lower case)");
      for (const key of ["INIT_CWD", "NODE", "COLOR", "EDITOR"]) assert.equal(result.env[key], undefined, `${key} was npm's`);
      assert.equal(result.env.PATH, SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS.join(path.delimiter), "npm's folders are gone, the rest keeps its order");
      assert.equal(result.env.SESSIONS_TEST_PLANTED, "planted by the test");

      // An EDITOR copied from VISUAL is npm's too; VISUAL itself is the person's.
      await withEnv({ EDITOR: "code --wait", VISUAL: "code --wait" }, async () => {
        const copied = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL });
        assert.equal(copied.env.EDITOR, undefined);
        assert.equal(copied.env.VISUAL, "code --wait");
      });

      // `npm run desktop:dev`: the PATH the app was started with carries npm's folders too.
      await withEnv({ AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH: [npm.pathEntries[0], "/usr/bin", "/bin"].join(path.delimiter) }, async () => {
        assert.equal((await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL })).env.PATH, "/usr/bin:/bin");
      });

      // An EDITOR the person has passes through npm unchanged, so it is kept,
      // also in the fallback, where no startup file sets it again.
      await withEnv({ EDITOR: "nano" }, async () => {
        const noMarkers = await fakeShell(base, "no-markers", `echo '{"PATH":"/nope"}'`);
        const fallback = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: noMarkers.file });
        assert.equal(fallback.source, "fallback");
        assert.equal(fallback.env.EDITOR, "nano");
        assert.deepEqual(npmNames(fallback.env), []);
        assert.equal(fallback.env.NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, personOwn);
        for (const key of ["INIT_CWD", "NODE", "COLOR"]) assert.equal(fallback.env[key], undefined, key);
        assert.deepEqual(fallback.env.PATH.split(path.delimiter), [...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS, "/usr/local/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin", path.join(home, ".local", "bin")]);
      });

      // Windows: npm fills in notepad.exe, and names ignore letter case.
      await withEnv({ SYSTEMROOT: "C:\\Windows", EDITOR: "C:\\Windows\\notepad.exe" }, async () => {
        const windows = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ platform: "win32" });
        assert.equal(windows.source, "process");
        const npmAnyCase = Object.keys(windows.env).filter((key) => key.toLowerCase().startsWith("npm_"));
        assert.deepEqual(npmAnyCase, [], "Windows names ignore letter case, so NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX counts as npm's too");
        for (const key of ["INIT_CWD", "NODE", "COLOR", "EDITOR"]) assert.equal(windows.env[key], undefined, key);
        assert.equal(windows.env.PATH, SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS.join(path.delimiter));
      });
    });
  });
});

test("login shell: when no npm script started Agent OS, the same names are the person's and pass through", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    const npm = npmStart(base);
    const vars = { ...npm.vars };
    delete vars.npm_lifecycle_event;
    const npmPath = [...npm.pathEntries, ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter);
    await withEnv({ ...vars, PATH: npmPath, EDITOR: "vi", VISUAL: undefined }, async () => {
      const result = await resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL });
      assert.equal(result.source, "login-shell");
      assert.equal(result.env.EDITOR, "vi");
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) assert.equal(result.env[key], value, key);
      assert.equal(result.env.PATH, npmPath);
    });
  });
});

test("getLoginShellEnv resolves once per server: the same promise every call", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withShellWorld(async ({ base }) => {
    const { file, record } = await fakeShell(base, "counted-shell", '/bin/sh -c "$last"');
    await withEnv({ SHELL: file }, async () => {
      const first = getLoginShellEnv();
      const second = getLoginShellEnv();
      assert.equal(first, second);
      assert.equal((await first).source, "login-shell");
      await getLoginShellEnv();
      const calls = () => readFile(record, "utf8").then((text) => text.split("\n").filter((line) => line === "-i").length);
      assert.equal(await calls(), 1, "the shell ran once");
      resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
      assert.notEqual(getLoginShellEnv(), first);
      await getLoginShellEnv();
      assert.equal(await calls(), 2);
    });
  });
});
```

Run: `env -u HERMES_HOME node --test test/sessions-shell-env.test.js`
Expected: FAIL before any test runs: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '…/server/runtime/sessions/shell-env.js' imported from …/test/sessions-shell-env.test.js`.

- [ ] **Step 7: Create `server/runtime/sessions/shell-env.js`.**

```js
// The environment every session starts with (spec H2): the person's own
// login-shell environment, the one Terminal gives them, minus Agent OS's own
// variables and the "you are inside another agent" markers, plus the few
// terminal variables every session sets.
//
// How the login-shell environment is read (VS Code's pattern): the login shell
// runs Node with a one-line script that prints process.env as JSON between two
// random markers. Only the text between the markers is used, so whatever the
// person's startup files print (banners, warnings) cannot confuse it, and the
// output is never parsed as `env` text (values may hold newlines or "=").
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { RUNTIME_VERSION } from "../store.js";

export const LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;
// Variables that make an agent think it runs inside another agent's session.
// Spikes S3 and S6 add the Codex and Cursor ones; until then only Claude
// Code's two are removed (removing less is the safe default, spec H2).
export const NESTED_MARKERS = ["CLAUDECODE", "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT"];
export const FALLBACK_NOTICE = "Agent OS could not read your login shell's settings, so sessions use a basic environment.";

const MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
// Set while the login shell runs, so a person's startup file can tell (like
// VS Code's VSCODE_RESOLVING_ENVIRONMENT). It starts with AGENT_OS_, so it
// never reaches a session.
const RESOLVING_FLAG = "AGENT_OS_RESOLVING_ENVIRONMENT";
// Bookkeeping of the short-lived resolver shell (its folder, the last command
// it ran), not the person's settings (decision Q7a). profiles.js sets a
// session's own PWD. Nothing else is taken out of the login shell's answer.
const RESOLVER_ONLY = new Set(["PWD", "OLDPWD", "_", RESOLVING_FLAG]);

// Names whose values Agent OS itself put into the server's environment: the
// keys loadLocalEnv added from Agent OS's own env file (its `applied` list,
// decision Q11a). They are not the person's environment (H1, H2), so the
// login shell never receives them and the fallback and Windows environments
// leave them out. A value the person's own startup files set under the same
// name is theirs and is kept. server/index.js registers the names once at
// start, right after loadLocalEnv, before the login shell is read. (The
// desktop shell passes the port as AGENT_OS_PORT, an Agent OS name, which is
// removed like every AGENT_OS_ variable.)
const excluded = new Set();

export function excludeFromSessionEnv(keys) {
  for (const key of keys || []) if (typeof key === "string") excluded.add(key);
}

export function resetExcludedForTests() {
  excluded.clear();
}

// Windows variable names ignore letter case, so there the check does too.
function isExcluded(key, platform) {
  if (excluded.has(key)) return true;
  if (platform !== "win32") return false;
  const name = key.toUpperCase();
  for (const item of excluded) if (item.toUpperCase() === name) return true;
  return false;
}

function isAgentOsVariable(key, platform) {
  const name = platform === "win32" ? key.toUpperCase() : key;
  return name.startsWith("AGENT_OS_") || name.startsWith("HERMES_AGENT_OS_");
}

// Agent OS started by an npm script (`npm start`, `npm run dev`, `npm run
// desktop:dev`): npm adds its own npm_* variables (always in lower case),
// INIT_CWD, NODE and COLOR, fills in EDITOR when the person has none (the
// value of VISUAL, else vi, or notepad.exe on Windows), and puts
// node_modules/.bin of the project folder and of each folder above it, and
// its own node-gyp-bin, in front of PATH. They describe how Agent OS was
// started, not the person's environment (H2, the reasoning of decision Q11a),
// so they are left out like the excluded names. An EDITOR the person has
// passes through npm unchanged and is kept; in the login shell the person's
// startup files set their own values again anyway.
const NPM_ADDED = new Set(["INIT_CWD", "NODE", "COLOR"]);

function startedByNpm() {
  return typeof process.env.npm_lifecycle_event === "string" && process.env.npm_lifecycle_event !== "";
}

function isNpmAdded(key, value, platform) {
  // Outside Windows npm's own names are lower case, so a person's own
  // NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX is kept; Windows names ignore letter case.
  if (key.startsWith("npm_") || (platform === "win32" && key.toLowerCase().startsWith("npm_"))) return true;
  const name = platform === "win32" ? key.toUpperCase() : key;
  if (NPM_ADDED.has(name)) return true;
  if (name !== "EDITOR") return false;
  const npmDefault = platform === "win32" ? `${process.env.SYSTEMROOT}\\notepad.exe` : "vi";
  return value === npmDefault || value === process.env.VISUAL;
}

// PATH without the folders npm put in front of it: node_modules/.bin of the
// project folder (where npm's package.json is) and of each folder above it,
// and npm's own node-gyp-bin. Every other entry keeps its place.
function withoutNpmPath(value) {
  const pkg = process.env.npm_package_json;
  const bins = new Set();
  for (let dir = typeof pkg === "string" && path.isAbsolute(pkg) ? path.dirname(pkg) : process.cwd(); ; dir = path.dirname(dir)) {
    bins.add(path.join(dir, "node_modules", ".bin"));
    if (path.dirname(dir) === dir) break;
  }
  const gyp = path.join("@npmcli", "run-script", "lib", "node-gyp-bin");
  return String(value || "")
    .split(path.delimiter)
    .filter((entry) => !bins.has(entry) && !entry.endsWith(gyp))
    .join(path.delimiter);
}

// The server's own environment (text values only) without the excluded names
// and, when an npm script started Agent OS, without what npm added.
function serverEnv(platform) {
  const npm = startedByNpm();
  const env = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(process.env)) {
    if (typeof value !== "string" || isExcluded(key, platform)) continue;
    if (npm && isNpmAdded(key, value, platform)) continue;
    env[key] = value;
  }
  if (npm) {
    for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {
      if (key === "PATH" || (platform === "win32" && key.toUpperCase() === "PATH")) env[key] = withoutNpmPath(env[key]);
    }
  }
  return env;
}

function defaultShell() {
  if (process.env.SHELL) return process.env.SHELL;
  try {
    return os.userInfo().shell || "";
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
}

function shellQuote(value) {
  return `'${String(value).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

// The server's own environment (without the excluded names) plus the folders
// agents are usually installed in, for when the login shell can't be read.
function fallbackResult(platform) {
  const env = serverEnv(platform);
  const parts = String(env.PATH || "").split(path.delimiter).filter(Boolean);
  for (const dir of ["/usr/local/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin", path.join(os.homedir(), ".local", "bin")]) {
    if (!parts.includes(dir)) parts.push(dir);
  }
  env.PATH = parts.join(path.delimiter);
  return { env, source: "fallback", notice: FALLBACK_NOTICE };
}

function parseMarked(text, marker) {
  const start = text.indexOf(marker);
  if (start === -1) return null;
  const end = text.indexOf(marker, start + marker.length);
  if (end === -1) return null;
  let value;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(text.slice(start + marker.length, end));
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) return null;
  const env = {};
  for (const [key, item] of Object.entries(value)) {
    if (typeof item === "string" && !RESOLVER_ONLY.has(key)) env[key] = item;
  }
  // A login shell always has a PATH; without one no agent could be found.
  return env.PATH ? env : null;
}

function readLoginShell(shell, timeoutMs, nodePath) {
  const first = crypto.randomBytes(8).toString("hex");
  const second = crypto.randomBytes(8).toString("hex");
  const marker = first + second;
  // The script joins the two halves, so the whole marker appears only in what
  // Node prints, never in the command text a shell might echo back.
  const script = `const m=${JSON.stringify(first)}+${JSON.stringify(second)};process.stdout.write(m+JSON.stringify(process.env)+m)`;
  const command = `${shellQuote(nodePath)} -e ${shellQuote(script)}`;
  const name = path.basename(shell);
  const args = name === "csh" || name === "tcsh" ? ["-ic", command] : ["-i", "-l", "-c", command];
  // Agent OS's own variables (its session token among them) and the names
  // Agent OS put into its own environment never reach the person's startup
  // files, so what comes back is what Terminal would give.
  const env = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(serverEnv(process.platform))) {
    if (!isAgentOsVariable(key, process.platform)) env[key] = value;
  }
  // The desktop shell extends the server's PATH with folders of its own
  // (server_path_env in main.rs). The login shell gets the PATH the app itself
  // was started with, as Terminal's does (H2, Q11a), without npm's folders
  // when an npm script started the app (`npm run desktop:dev`).
  const launchPath = process.env.AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH;
  if (typeof launchPath === "string" && launchPath) env.PATH = startedByNpm() ? withoutNpmPath(launchPath) : launchPath;
  env[RESOLVING_FLAG] = "1";

  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let settled = false;
    let text = "";
    let bytes = 0;
    let child = null;
    const killGroup = () => {
      if (!child?.pid) return;
      try {
        process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGKILL"); // detached: the shell leads its own process group
      } catch {
        try {
          child.kill("SIGKILL");
        } catch {
          // already gone
        }
      }
    };
    const finish = (result) => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      process.removeListener("exit", killGroup);
      resolve(result);
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      killGroup();
      finish(null);
    }, timeoutMs);
    process.once("exit", killGroup);
    try {
      // detached: a new session with no terminal, so an interactive shell
      // never waits for one (VS Code does the same).
      child = spawn(shell, args, { cwd: os.homedir(), env, detached: true, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] });
    } catch {
      finish(null);
      return;
    }
    child.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
      if (settled) return;
      bytes += Buffer.byteLength(chunk);
      if (bytes > MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES) {
        killGroup();
        finish(null);
        return;
      }
      text += chunk;
      // Done as soon as Node has printed; the shell's own logout files are
      // not waited for.
      const parsed = parseMarked(text, marker);
      if (parsed) finish(parsed);
    });
    child.stderr.on("data", () => {});
    child.once("error", () => finish(null));
    child.once("close", () => finish(parseMarked(text, marker)));
  });
}

// { env, source: "login-shell" | "fallback" | "process", notice }. Never throws:
// anything that goes wrong (no shell, a hang past timeoutMs, no markers, a
// non-zero exit before printing) gives the fallback and its notice.
export async function resolveLoginShellEnv({
  shell = defaultShell(),
  timeoutMs = LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS,
  nodePath = process.execPath,
  platform = process.platform
} = {}) {
  // Windows has no login shell: the process environment is used as it is (H2),
  // without the names Agent OS put there itself.
  if (platform === "win32") return { env: serverEnv(platform), source: "process", notice: null };
  if (typeof shell !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(shell)) return fallbackResult(platform);
  const env = await readLoginShell(shell, timeoutMs, nodePath);
  return env ? { env, source: "login-shell", notice: null } : fallbackResult(platform);
}

let cached = null;

// Resolved once per server (spec H2): every caller gets the same promise.
export function getLoginShellEnv() {
  if (!cached) cached = resolveLoginShellEnv();
  return cached;
}

export function resetLoginShellEnvForTests() {
  cached = null;
}

// A session's environment from `baseEnv` (the login-shell environment), as a
// new object. Removes ONLY Agent OS's own variables (AGENT_OS_*,
// HERMES_AGENT_OS_*) and the nested-session markers; sets the terminal
// variables, the session id and, for Claude Code with the H4 opt-in on,
// CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER. Never sets HOME, USERPROFILE, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR,
// CODEX_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HERMES_HOME, any OPENCLAW_* variable or
// CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB (H1, H2): those pass through as the person
// has them. Windows variable names ignore case, so there the checks do too.
export function sessionEnv(
  baseEnv,
  { sessionId, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION, claudeFullscreen = false, agentId, platform = process.platform } = {}
) {
  const fold = (key) => (platform === "win32" ? key.toUpperCase() : key);
  const additions = {
    TERM: "xterm-256color",
    COLORTERM: "truecolor",
    TERM_PROGRAM: "AgentOS",
    TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION: String(agentOsVersion),
    AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID: String(sessionId || "")
  };
  if (agentId === "claude" && claudeFullscreen === true) additions.CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER = "1";
  const replaced = new Set(Object.keys(additions).map(fold));
  const env = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(baseEnv || {})) {
    if (typeof value !== "string") continue;
    const name = fold(key);
    if (name.startsWith("AGENT_OS_") || name.startsWith("HERMES_AGENT_OS_")) continue;
    if (NESTED_MARKERS.includes(name)) continue;
    if (replaced.has(name)) continue;
    env[key] = value;
  }
  return Object.assign(env, additions);
}
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `detached: true` puts the shell in a new session with no terminal, so an interactive shell never stops to wait for one; it also makes the shell the leader of its own process group, which is why the timeout kills `-child.pid` (the shell and the `node -e` it started).
- The result is taken as soon as both markers have arrived (the shell's logout files are not waited for). A shell that exits before printing, prints no markers, or prints an environment without `PATH` gives the fallback.
- `process.once("exit", killGroup)` makes sure a shell still running when the server quits during those 10 s does not outlive it.
- Excluded names (`excludeFromSessionEnv`) are taken out of what goes INTO the login shell, the fallback and the Windows environment, never out of what the login shell gives back. So the `HERMES_HOME` or `PORT` of Agent OS's own dev env file never reaches a session, but a `PORT` or `HERMES_HOME` that the person's own `.zshrc` exports still does, exactly as in Terminal (H2 removes ONLY Agent OS's own variables). Do not also filter the parsed result: that would remove the person's own values.
- `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` replaces only the `PATH` that goes INTO the login shell. The desktop shell starts the server with `PATH=server_path_env()`, which adds Homebrew, `~/.local/bin`, Agent OS's managed Node folder (`~/.agent-os/node/bin`) and other install folders in front of the app's own `PATH`; a login shell keeps those entries (macOS's `path_helper` appends them after the system folders), so without this every session would see folders Terminal's login shell never has, the managed `node` and `npm` among them. Task D1 passes the app's own `PATH` under this name. The variable is an `AGENT_OS_` name, so it is never handed to the login shell and never reaches a session. When it is missing or empty (`npm start`, the tests), the server's own `PATH` goes in as before. The fallback keeps the server's own `PATH` plus the usual folders, as spec H2 says.
- `npm start` (browser mode and the server on its own), `npm run dev` and `npm run desktop:dev` start Agent OS through npm, and npm hands the server more than the person's environment: its own `npm_*` variables (always lower case: `npm_config_*`, `npm_lifecycle_*`, `npm_package_*`, `npm_execpath` and others), `INIT_CWD`, `NODE`, `COLOR`, `EDITOR` (filled in from `VISUAL`, else `vi`, when the person has none), and `node_modules/.bin` of the project folder and of every folder above it, then its own `node-gyp-bin`, in front of `PATH` (checked with npm 10.9 while planning). A login shell keeps inherited values and macOS's `path_helper` keeps extra `PATH` entries, so without this every session would get `EDITOR=vi`, npm's config overrides and Agent OS's own `tsc`, `vite`, `tauri` and `concurrently`. `serverEnv()` feeds the login shell's input, the fallback and Windows, so all three leave them out; `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` gets the same `PATH` cleanup, because under `npm run desktop:dev` the app itself was started by npm. An `EDITOR` the person has passes through npm unchanged, so only npm's fill-in is dropped, and a person's own upper-case `NPM_CONFIG_*` stays outside Windows. `npm test` is an npm script too, so `withShellWorld` clears `npm_lifecycle_event` and the npm test plants it.
- The resolver gives the shell no input (`stdin` is ignored, so a startup file's question reads end of input) and no terminal (`detached`), and ignores everything outside its markers; a startup file that hangs is cut off at the limit (Review Focus 1, tested with fake shells that print junk, ask a question and hang).

Expected: `# tests 14`, `# pass 14`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`. It takes about 2 s (the hang test waits 1.5 s for its limit). The result is the same through `npm test` (an npm script itself): `withShellWorld` clears `npm_lifecycle_event`, and only the npm test plants it.

```js
// Sessions, the folder policy (spec D12 and SP3 "Folder policy", planning
// decision Q12): which folders a session may start in, and the list of recent
// folders. Nothing here starts an agent or a session; every test uses a temp
// HOME, AGENT_OS_HOME and managed Node folder, never the real ones.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, realpath, rename, rm, symlink, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { checkSessionFolder, recentSessionFolders } from "../server/runtime/sessions/folders.js";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const posixSkip = { skip: isWindows ? "symlinks and POSIX paths" : false };
// macOS and Windows volumes usually ignore letter case; most Linux ones don't.
const CASE_INSENSITIVE_DISK = existsSync(os.tmpdir().toUpperCase());

const MESSAGE = {
  not_absolute: "Type the full path, starting with / (or a drive letter on Windows).",
  missing: "That folder doesn't exist.",
  not_a_directory: "That is a file, not a folder.",
  is_home: "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.",
  outside_home: "Pick a folder inside your home folder.",
  inside_agent_os: "Agent OS's own folder can't be used."
};

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// A temp world: HOME with a project, Agent OS's own folder inside HOME (as it
// is by default), the managed Node folder inside HOME, and a folder outside HOME.
async function withFolders(fn) {
  const base = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-folders-")));
  const home = path.join(base, "home");
  const agentOsHome = path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os");
  const managedRoot = path.join(home, ".agent-os");
  const dirs = {
    base,
    home,
    agentOsHome,
    managedRoot,
    project: path.join(home, "projects", "app"),
    worktrees: path.join(agentOsHome, "worktrees"),
    worktree: path.join(agentOsHome, "worktrees", "app-copy"),
    workspace: path.join(agentOsHome, "workspace"),
    managedBin: path.join(managedRoot, "node", "bin"),
    outside: path.join(base, "outside", "real"),
    file: path.join(home, "notes.txt")
  };
  for (const dir of [dirs.project, dirs.worktree, dirs.workspace, dirs.managedBin, dirs.outside]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(dirs.file, "hello\n");
  try {
    return await withEnv(
      { HOME: home, USERPROFILE: home, AGENT_OS_HOME: agentOsHome, HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined, AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: managedRoot },
      async () => {
        assert.equal(os.homedir(), home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
        return fn(dirs);
      }
    );
  } finally {
    await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

function refused(result, code) {
  assert.deepEqual(result, { ok: false, code, message: MESSAGE[code] });
}

test("folder policy: a real folder inside HOME is accepted, as its real path and name", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ project }) => {
    assert.deepEqual(await checkSessionFolder(project), { ok: true, path: project, name: "app" });
    assert.deepEqual(await checkSessionFolder(`${project}/`), { ok: true, path: project, name: "app" }, "a trailing slash is fine");
    assert.deepEqual(await checkSessionFolder(`  ${project}  `), { ok: true, path: project, name: "app" }, "spaces around a typed path are ignored");
  });
});

test("folder policy: HOME itself is refused", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ home }) => {
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(home), "is_home");
  });
});

test("folder policy: Agent OS's own folder and everything in it are refused, except worktrees/", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ agentOsHome, workspace, worktrees, worktree }) => {
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(agentOsHome), "inside_agent_os");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(workspace), "inside_agent_os");
    assert.equal((await checkSessionFolder(worktrees)).ok, true);
    assert.deepEqual(await checkSessionFolder(worktree), { ok: true, path: worktree, name: "app-copy" });
  });
});

test("folder policy: the managed Node folder is Agent OS's own folder too (Q12)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ managedRoot, managedBin }) => {
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(managedRoot), "inside_agent_os");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(managedBin), "inside_agent_os");
  });
});

test("folder policy: an upper-case spelling of AGENT_OS_HOME is still Agent OS's folder (macOS and Windows ignore case)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ home, workspace }) => {
    const upper = path.join(home, ".HERMES-AGENT-OS");
    for (const platform of ["darwin", "win32"]) {
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(workspace, { agentOsHome: upper, platform }), "inside_agent_os");
    }
  });
});

test("folder policy: an upper-case spelling of HOME is still HOME (macOS and Windows ignore case)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ home, project }) => {
    const upperHome = home.toUpperCase();
    for (const platform of ["darwin", "win32"]) {
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(home, { home: upperHome, platform }), "is_home");
      assert.equal((await checkSessionFolder(project, { home: upperHome, platform })).ok, true, "still inside HOME");
    }
  });
});

test(
  "folder policy: a typed upper-case path into Agent OS's folder is refused (disk that ignores case)",
  { skip: isWindows || !CASE_INSENSITIVE_DISK ? "needs a POSIX disk that ignores letter case" : false },
  async () => {
    await withFolders(async ({ home, workspace }) => {
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(path.join(home, ".HERMES-AGENT-OS", "workspace")), "inside_agent_os");
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(workspace.toUpperCase()), "inside_agent_os");
    });
  }
);

test(
  "folder policy: on a case-sensitive Linux disk an upper-case HOME spelling is another folder",
  { skip: isWindows || CASE_INSENSITIVE_DISK ? "needs a disk that keeps letter case apart" : false },
  async () => {
    await withFolders(async ({ home, project }) => {
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(project, { home: home.toUpperCase(), platform: "linux" }), "outside_home");
    });
  }

test("folder policy: a symlink that leads out of HOME, or into Agent OS's folder, is refused", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ home, outside, workspace, project }) => {
    const escape = path.join(home, "looks-local");
    const sneaky = path.join(home, "looks-like-a-project");
    const fine = path.join(home, "shortcut-to-app");
    await symlink(outside, escape);
    await symlink(workspace, sneaky);
    await symlink(project, fine);
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(escape), "outside_home");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(sneaky), "inside_agent_os");
    assert.deepEqual(await checkSessionFolder(fine), { ok: true, path: project, name: "app" }, "a symlink inside HOME resolves to its real folder");
  });
});

test("folder policy: HOME reached through a symlink still counts as HOME", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ base, home, project }) => {
    const homeLink = path.join(base, "home-link");
    await symlink(home, homeLink);
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(home, { home: homeLink }), "is_home");
    assert.equal((await checkSessionFolder(project, { home: homeLink })).ok, true);
  });
});

test("folder policy: a file, a missing path, a relative path and empty input are refused", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withFolders(async ({ home, file, outside }) => {
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(file), "not_a_directory");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(path.join(home, "no-such-folder")), "missing");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(path.join(file, "below-a-file")), "missing");
    refused(await checkSessionFolder(outside), "outside_home");
    for (const input of ["projects/app", "~/projects/app", "", "   ", null, undefined, 42, `${home}/a\0b`]) {
      refused(await checkSessionFolder(input), "not_absolute");
    }
  });
});

async function writeMeta(agentOsHome, id, meta) {
  const dir = path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", id);
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(path.join(dir, "meta.json"), typeof meta === "string" ? meta : JSON.stringify(meta));
}
```

```js
// The folder policy for sessions (spec D12, SP3 "Folder policy"): any real
// folder inside the person's HOME; never HOME itself; never Agent OS's own
// folders (AGENT_OS_HOME, except its worktrees/, and the managed Node folder,
// planning decision Q12). Sessions never use the runs sandbox (resolveRunCwd);
// runs stay sandboxed as today. Inside the folder the agent asks its own
// permissions, exactly as in Terminal.
import { realpath as realpathCallback, promises as fs } from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { managedNodeRoot } from "../setup/managed-node.js";
import { readJson, runtimePaths } from "../store.js";

// fs.realpath.native gives the letter case stored on disk on macOS and Windows
// (the plain JavaScript fs.realpath keeps whatever case was typed).
const realpathNative = promisify(realpathCallback.native);

const MESSAGES = {
  not_absolute: "Type the full path, starting with / (or a drive letter on Windows).",
  missing: "That folder doesn't exist.",
  unreadable: "Agent OS can't open that folder.",
  not_a_directory: "That is a file, not a folder.",
  is_home: "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.",
  outside_home: "Pick a folder inside your home folder.",
  inside_agent_os: "Agent OS's own folder can't be used."
};

function refuse(code, message = MESSAGES[code]) {
  return { ok: false, code, message };
}

// macOS and Windows volumes usually ignore letter case, so every comparison
// there does too (the 0.3.2 security fix was exactly such a case bypass).
function foldCase(value, platform) {
  return platform === "darwin" || platform === "win32" ? value.toLowerCase() : value;
}

function isSameOrInside(child, parent, platform) {
  const c = foldCase(child, platform);
  const p = foldCase(parent, platform);
  if (c === p) return true;
  return c.startsWith(p.endsWith(path.sep) ? p : p + path.sep);
}

// The real path of a folder the input is compared with, or the path as given
// when it does not exist (nothing real can be inside a missing folder).
async function canonical(dir) {
  try {
    return await realpathNative(dir);
  } catch {
    return path.resolve(dir);
  }
}

// { ok: true, path, name } or { ok: false, code, message }. `path` is the
// real path (symlinks resolved, on-disk letter case), so a symlink can't
// escape: the resolved path is what must pass.
export async function checkSessionFolder(
  input,
  { home = os.homedir(), agentOsHome = runtimePaths().root, managedRoot = managedNodeRoot(), platform = process.platform } = {}
) {
  const typed = typeof input === "string" ? input.trim() : "";
  if (!typed || typed.includes("\0") || !path.isAbsolute(typed)) return refuse("not_absolute");
  let real;
  try {
    real = await realpathNative(typed);
  } catch (error) {
    const gone = error?.code === "ENOENT" || error?.code === "ENOTDIR";
    return gone ? refuse("missing") : refuse("missing", MESSAGES.unreadable);
  }
  let info;
  try {
    info = await fs.stat(real);
  } catch {
    return refuse("missing");
  }
  if (!info.isDirectory()) return refuse("not_a_directory");

  const [homeReal, agentOsReal, managedReal] = await Promise.all([canonical(home), canonical(agentOsHome), canonical(managedRoot)]);
  if (foldCase(real, platform) === foldCase(homeReal, platform)) return refuse("is_home");
  const inWorktrees = isSameOrInside(real, path.join(agentOsReal, "worktrees"), platform);
  if (isSameOrInside(real, agentOsReal, platform) && !inWorktrees) return refuse("inside_agent_os");
  if (isSameOrInside(real, managedReal, platform)) return refuse("inside_agent_os");
  if (!isSameOrInside(real, homeReal, platform)) return refuse("outside_home");
  return { ok: true, path: real, name: path.basename(real) };
}

// The latest of the row's times. Task S6 writes lastUsedAt (the latest start,
// resume or end); startedAt and endedAt still count, so a meta.json without
// lastUsedAt sorts by them.
function lastUsedMs(meta) {
  const times = [meta.lastUsedAt, meta.startedAt, meta.endedAt]
    .filter((value) => typeof value === "string")
    .map((value) => Date.parse(value))
    .filter(Number.isFinite);
  return times.length ? Math.max(...times) : null;
}

// The folders of earlier sessions, newest first, each checked again (a folder
// that was deleted or moved, or no longer passes the policy, is left out). Update
// sessions (the agent's own checkout) and sessions whose folder Agent OS did
// not choose (OpenClaw, folderShown false) are not offered.
export async function recentSessionFolders({ limit = 8 } = {}) {
  const dir = runtimePaths().sessions;
  let entries;
  try {
    entries = await fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
  const metas = await Promise.all(
    entries.filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory()).map((entry) => readJson(path.join(dir, entry.name, "meta.json"), null))
  );
  const candidates = [];
  for (const meta of metas) {
    if (!meta || typeof meta !== "object" || Array.isArray(meta)) continue;
    if (meta.kind === "update" || meta.folderShown === false) continue;
    if (typeof meta.folder !== "string" || !meta.folder) continue;
    const at = lastUsedMs(meta);
    if (at !== null) candidates.push({ folder: meta.folder, at });
  }
  candidates.sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
  const max = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(limit) || 0));
  const out = [];
  const seenTyped = new Set();
  const seenReal = new Set();
  for (const { folder, at } of candidates) {
    if (out.length >= max) break;
    if (seenTyped.has(folder)) continue;
    seenTyped.add(folder);
    const check = await checkSessionFolder(folder);
    if (!check.ok || seenReal.has(check.path)) continue;
    seenReal.add(check.path);
    out.push({ path: check.path, name: check.name, lastUsedAt: new Date(at).toISOString() });
  }
  return out;
}
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `promisify(fs.realpath.native)` is used on purpose (spec: "Canonicalise with `fs.realpath.native`"): it returns the letter case stored on disk on macOS and Windows; the plain JavaScript `fs.realpath` keeps the typed case.
- HOME, AGENT_OS_HOME and the managed folder are canonicalised too (on macOS a temp HOME under `/var/…` is really `/private/var/…`). A folder that does not exist is compared as given, because nothing real can be inside it.
- On a disk that ignores case (macOS), `realpath.native` already returns the on-disk case, so the upper-case tests pass through it; on Linux CI (case-sensitive disk) the same tests prove the case-folding itself. CI runs both.

#### Notes

Deliberate choices and limits a reviewer should know:

1. **The login shell runs as `-i -l -c <command>` (`-ic` for csh and tcsh),** VS Code's exact form, not the literal `-ilc` the contract shows. Same meaning for sh, bash and zsh; separate flags also work for fish.
2. **No automated test and no step of this task runs a real login shell** (decision Q1c). The fake shells and Task W1's stand-in run the command through the real `/bin/sh -c`, so the quoting is checked by a real shell parser, but the first real login shell (the owner's zsh with his startup files) is read in Task E2's live checks on his Mac.
3. **Only Claude Code's two nested-session markers are removed** until spikes S3 and S6 name the Codex and Cursor ones (Task E2 turns their results into follow-ups that add to `NESTED_MARKERS`). Removing less is the safe default of spec H2.
4. **Worktrees still have to be inside HOME.** When AGENT_OS_HOME is set outside HOME, its `worktrees/` folders are refused as `outside_home`: the stricter reading of D12 ("any real directory under the user's HOME ... except AGENT_OS_HOME/worktrees/"). It only matters to SP4's worktree offer.
5. **`missing` also covers a folder that exists but can't be opened** (EACCES, ELOOP), with its own sentence "Agent OS can't open that folder."; the code list stays the contract's six. Typed input is trimmed of surrounding spaces. Task U3 shows `message` as it is.
6. **Only the root forgives a failed chmod.** When AGENT_OS_HOME is a folder another account owns, its chmod fails with EPERM or EACCES; throwing would make every store write fail and stop the app, so `ensureRuntimeStore()` warns once per root folder (`Agent OS could not make its folder private (0700): <root>`) and carries on. Any other error on the root, and every chmod error on `sessions/` or `worktrees/`, still throws. The Docker image runs as root and never hits this.
7. **The login shell starts with the app's own `PATH`, not the server's.** The desktop shell's `server_path_env` adds install folders (Agent OS's managed Node folder among them) so the server can find agents; those are Agent OS's additions, not the person's environment (H2 "as Terminal.app gives it", Q11a). `readLoginShell` hands the login shell `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` (set by Task D1) instead. Detection (`detect.js`) still searches the server's own `PATH`, so finding an agent is unchanged; only what a session's commands see changes. The fallback keeps the server's `PATH` plus the usual folders, as spec H2 says.
8. **Agent OS started by an npm script (extends decision Q11a; for the hand-off (owner)).** `npm start` (browser mode and the server on its own), `npm run dev` and `npm run desktop:dev` add npm's own values to the server's environment: lower-case `npm_*` variables, `INIT_CWD`, `NODE`, `COLOR`, `EDITOR=vi` when the person has no `EDITOR` or `VISUAL`, and the project's `node_modules/.bin` folders and npm's `node-gyp-bin` in front of `PATH`. They describe how Agent OS was started, not the person's environment (H2 "as Terminal.app gives it", the reasoning of Q11a), so the login shell's input, the fallback and the Windows environment leave them out, and the login shell's own answer is never filtered. An `EDITOR` the person has is kept, because npm passes it on unchanged; only an `EDITOR` equal to npm's fill-in (the value of `VISUAL`, or `vi`, or Windows' `notepad.exe`) is dropped. Two deliberate limits, both only in the fallback and on Windows (in the login shell, startup files that set these values still set them): a person's own `EDITOR` that is exactly npm's fill-in is dropped too, because the two look the same; and a person's own lower-case `npm_config_*` variable is dropped, because npm's own names look the same (an upper-case `NPM_CONFIG_*` is kept outside Windows). The installed desktop app never starts through npm, so it is unaffected; only a developer's `npm run desktop:dev` is. Detection is unchanged: `detect.js` still searches the server's own `PATH`.

---

### Task S3: Launch profiles (H3, H4), session errors and settings, resume argv, the update kind

This task decides exactly how each of the five agents starts in a session, and proves it with the profile snapshot test the spec requires. `buildSessionProfile()` returns the command (the person's own binary from detection, H1), the argv (only the H3 additions, from the spec's "Launch profiles" and "Resume per agent" tables), the working folder (the folder policy from S2; OpenClaw starts in HOME until spike S5), and the environment (S2's H2 environment plus the H4 fullscreen opt-in, read from the stored settings at each launch). It never copies a headless run plan's env or argv (Q11), so Cursor's `--trust` and Hermes' `HERMES_HOME` can't leak in. A second check, `assertSessionArgvSafe()`, refuses any argv outside the agent's H3 allowance or on the blocked lists, as defence in depth. The task also adds the shared errors module every sessions module throws from (`errors.js`, ruling R4), the stored session settings (`<AGENT_OS_HOME>/config/sessions.json`, 0600), the session form of Claude Code's settings file (no `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`, Q9), and the `update` kind (`hermes update`, nothing added). Nothing here spawns a process; the manager (S6) does that with what this returns. The snapshot test covers the SP3 expectations only (no hook variables; `--settings` only with an OpenRouter or Local brain); SP4 adds its own expectations when hooks arrive.

**Worker notes:**
- Run every command from the worktree root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). Never commit, push, tag or set `CI=true`. Never start a real agent: these tests build profiles and never spawn them; the fake agent files they write exit at once if anything ever ran them. Never read `.env` files or the `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw` or `~/.hermes` folders.
- The profile tests use a temp `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `AGENT_OS_HOME` and `AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT`, and remove `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV` and `BASH_ENV`. `SHELL` points at a small script in the temp folder that exports a few variables the way a person's startup files would and then hands over to W1's stand-in login shell (`FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` from `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`, ruling R15), so no real shell and no startup file is ever read; the fallback test points `SHELL` at a file that does not exist. They use the file key store (`AGENT_OS_KEYSTORE=file`, so the macOS Keychain is never touched). The OpenRouter key in them is a made-up `sk-or-v1-SESSIONTEST-…` value.
- The argv flags here are the spec's, even where the repo has never seen them (`claude --session-id`, `codex resume --last`, `agent --resume`, `hermes --in` / `--resume latest`, `openclaw tui --session`); spikes S2 to S6 check them on the owner's Mac (planning decision Q10). Do not "fix" them from `--help` output.
- A PreToolUse hook ("Fact-Forcing Gate") may refuse the first Bash command, the first Write of a new file or an `rm`. State the facts it asks for, then retry the same call. In zsh, quote separator strings such as `"====="`.
- Retry until every listed check is green; report anything that could not be done.
