  - `export const SESSION_AGENT_LABEL = { claude: "Claude Code", codex: "Codex", cursor: "Cursor", hermes: "Hermes", openclaw: "OpenClaw" }` (frozen): the short names every session message, tab and dialog uses (ruling R6; S6 imports and re-exports it from `manager.js`). Every per-agent lookup in `profiles.js` goes through `Object.hasOwn`, so `"constructor"`, `"__proto__"`, `"toString"` and other prototype names are never taken for an agent.
  - `export async function buildSessionProfile({ agentId, folder, sessionId, kind = "agent", resume = null, settings, detected, brain = null, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION } = {})` → `{ command, args, cwd, env, agentSessionId, settingsFile, softStop, resumeMode, folderShown, notes }`:
    - `resume` is `null` for a fresh start, or `{ agentSessionId: string | null }` (the value kept in meta.json) to resume an ended agent session; the update kind ignores it (an update is never resumed). `settings` undefined → `readSessionSettings()`; `detected` undefined → `getAdapter(agentId).detect()`.
    - `command`: `detected.path`; when detection found nothing, the first `claude` / `codex` / `agent` then `cursor-agent` / `hermes` / `openclaw` on the login shell's `PATH` (Q8).
    - `args` (start / resume):

      | Agent | Start | Resume |
      |---|---|---|
      | claude | `--session-id <new uuid>` (+ `--settings <file>` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `--resume <agentSessionId>` (+ the same `--settings` rule) |
      | codex | `-C <folder> -c tui.notification_method=osc9 -c tui.notifications=["agent-turn-complete","approval-requested"] -c tui.notification_condition=always` (+ `codexBrainArgs` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `resume --last` + the same `-c` options and brain options, in the same folder |
      | cursor | `--workspace <folder>` | `--resume --workspace <folder>` |
      | hermes | `--in <folder>` (kind `update`: exactly `update`) | `--resume latest --in <folder>` |
      | openclaw | `tui --session agentos-<sessionId>` | the same |

    - `cwd`: the real path from `checkSessionFolder(folder)`; OpenClaw: `os.homedir()` while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false (the folder is ignored, `folderShown: false`).
    - `env`: `sessionEnv((await getLoginShellEnv()).env, { sessionId, agentOsVersion, claudeFullscreen, agentId })`; for a node-shebang CLI inside the managed Node folder, `withSiblingNodePath` puts its own folder first on `PATH` (Q7); then `PWD` is set to `cwd`.
    - `agentSessionId`: Claude a new `crypto.randomUUID()` (or the resumed one); OpenClaw `agentos-<sessionId>`; Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the update kind `null`.
    - `settingsFile`: `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/sessions/<sessionId>/claude-settings.json` (0600, folder 0700) for Claude with an OpenRouter or Local brain, written from `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession: true })` after `assertSafeClaudeSettings`; otherwise `null`.
    - `softStop`: `"claude-bg"` (Claude), `"openclaw-abort"` (OpenClaw), otherwise `null`. `resumeMode`: `"id"` (Claude, OpenClaw), `"fallback"` (Codex, Cursor, Hermes), `null` (update). `notes`: `[FALLBACK_NOTICE]` when the login shell could not be read, else `[]`.
    - Errors (all `sessionError` unless noted):

      | status | code | message |
      |---|---|---|
      | 400 | `unknown_agent` | Agent OS can't start a session for that agent. |
      | 404 | `unknown_session` | That session doesn't exist anymore. (a `sessionId` that is not a v4 uuid) |
      | 400 | `unknown_kind` | Agent OS can't start that kind of session. |
      | 400 | `update_not_available` | Only Hermes is updated in a session. |
      | 409 | `agent_not_installed` | `<label>` isn't installed, or Agent OS can't find it. Install it in Setup, then try again. (`<label>` is `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL[agentId]`, for example "Hermes") |
      | 400 | `folder_refused` | the folder policy's message; `error.extra.code` holds its code (`is_home`, `outside_home`, ...) |
      | 409 | `not_resumable` | This Claude Code conversation can't be resumed. (a Claude resume without a valid uuid) |
      | 500 | `unsafe_argv` | Agent OS stopped `<label>` from starting: its command line had an option Agent OS never adds. (`<label>` is `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL[agentId]`, or "this agent" for an unknown id) |
      | (none) | `openrouter_key_missing`, `base_url_without_credential` | `brainError`s from `buildClaudeSettings` / `codexBrainArgs`, unchanged |

  - `export function assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args)`: throws `unsafe_argv` unless `agentId` is one of `SESSION_AGENTS` (an own key, never a prototype name), `args` is exactly one of the shapes in the table above and none of its option names (or its leading subcommand) is on `BLOCKED_AGENT_FLAGS` (via `containsBlockedFlag`), is `--bare`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--mcp-config`, `--accept-hooks`, `--yolo`, `--trust` or `--no-alt-screen`, contains `dangerously`, `bypass`, `full-access` or `skip-permission`, is `--tui` for Hermes, or is Cursor's `-f` / `--force` (via `hasCursorForceFlag`). Codex `-c` values must be one of the exact notification options or `codexBrainArgs` keys. Values (folders, ids, models) are checked by shape, so a folder named `--force-demo` is allowed.

```js
// Sessions, the stored session settings (spec "Browser terminal", H4) and the

// CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB for a session; headless runs keep it).
// Temp AGENT_OS_HOME only; nothing here starts anything.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { buildClaudeSettings } from "../server/runtime/builders/brain-launch.js";
import { readSessionSettings, writeSessionSettings } from "../server/runtime/sessions/settings.js";

};
const OPENROUTER_BRAIN = { mode: "openrouter", model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6" };

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

async function withRuntimeHome(fn) {
  const home = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-session-settings-"));
  try {
    return await withEnv({ AGENT_OS_HOME: home, HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined }, () => fn(home));
  } finally {
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js`** with exactly this content. It is the only home of the sessions' error shape and id pattern (ruling R4): S5 (recorder) and S6 (manager) import it and never create or overwrite it, `manager.js` re-exports `SESSION_ID_RE` and `sessionError`, and S8's routes answer every `sessionError` with `res.status(err.status).json(errorBody(err))`.

```js
// Errors and ids shared by the sessions modules (profiles, settings, recorder,
// manager, routes, WebSocket). The only home of all four (ruling R4).

// A crypto.randomUUID() value (planning decision Q39). Every route and the
// WebSocket check an id with it before any file path is built.
export const SESSION_ID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

export function isSessionId(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && SESSION_ID_RE.test(value);
}

// status = the HTTP status; code = the answer's `error` word; extra = more
// answer fields (folder_refused: { code }, the folder policy's code).
export function sessionError(status, code, message, extra = {}) {
  const error = new Error(message);
  error.status = status;
  error.code = code;
  error.extra = extra && typeof extra === "object" ? { ...extra } : {};
  return error;
}

// The JSON answer for a sessionError: { error, message, ...extra }.
export function errorBody(err) {
  return { error: err.code, message: err.message, ...err.extra };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `server/runtime/sessions/settings.js`.**

```js
// The stored session settings (spec "Browser terminal", H4). Only the setting
// that changes how an agent starts lives on the server: "Use Claude Code's
// fullscreen view in Agent OS", off by default. The terminal's own settings
// (kitty keyboard, WebGL) stay in the browser.
import path from "node:path";
import { ensureRuntimeStore, readJson, runtimePaths, writeJson } from "../store.js";
import { sessionError } from "./errors.js";

const KEYS = ["claudeFullscreen"];

function settingsFile() {
  return path.join(runtimePaths().config, "sessions.json");
}

// Off when the file is missing, broken, or holds anything but true.
export async function readSessionSettings() {
  const raw = await readJson(settingsFile(), null);
  return { claudeFullscreen: raw?.claudeFullscreen === true };
}

// Only the known boolean key is accepted; anything else is refused (the route
// answers 400) and nothing is written. The file is private (0600, writeJson).
export async function writeSessionSettings(patch) {
  const keys = patch && typeof patch === "object" && !Array.isArray(patch) ? Object.keys(patch) : [];
  if (!keys.length || keys.some((key) => !KEYS.includes(key) || typeof patch[key] !== "boolean")) {
    throw sessionError(400, "invalid_settings", "Only the Claude Code fullscreen setting (on or off) can be changed here.");
  }
  const next = { ...(await readSessionSettings()), ...patch };
  await ensureRuntimeStore();
  await writeJson(settingsFile(), next);
  return next;
}
```

`writeJson` (`server/runtime/store.js`) writes a temp file with mode 0600 and renames it over the old one, so `sessions.json` is 0600 even when an older copy was 0644. `ensureRuntimeStore()` runs first, so a first-ever write never creates AGENT_OS_HOME with the default mode.

```js
// The settings for one run on `brain`. `helper` is the key's read helper
// (openRouterKeyHelper()); without it an OpenRouter run is refused.
// `forSession: true` (an interactive session, planning decision Q9) leaves out
// CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB; headless runs keep it.
export function buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession = false } = {}) {
  const scrub = !forSession;
  let settings;
  if (brain.mode === "openrouter") {
    if (!helper) throw brainError("openrouter_key_missing", MISSING_KEY_MESSAGE);
    settings = {
      apiKeyHelper: helperCommandLine(helper),
      env: claudeEnv(OPENROUTER_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, "", brain.model, { scrub })
    };
  } else {
    // "ollama" is a stand-in the local server ignores; it only has to be there
    // so Claude Code doesn't send the claude.ai sign-in.
    settings = { env: claudeEnv(brain.local.baseUrl, "ollama", brain.local.model, { scrub }) };
  }
  assertSafeClaudeSettings(settings);
  return settings;
}
```

```js
  COLORTERM: "24bit",
  CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER: undefined,
  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB: undefined,
  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: undefined,
  HERMES_HOME: undefined
};

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

function shQuote(value) {
  return `'${String(value).replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'`;
}

// A temp world with fake agent binaries (never run), a project folder, and a
// login shell that does what a person's startup files might do (print a
// banner, export variables, put a folder of its own first on PATH) and then
// hands over to W1's stand-in login shell, which runs Agent OS's command with
// /bin/sh and reads no startup file.
async function withProfileEnv(fn, { startupLines = [] } = {}) {
  const base = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-profiles-")));
  const ctx = {
    base,
    home: path.join(base, "home"),
    agentOsHome: path.join(base, "agent-os-home"),
    managedRoot: path.join(base, "managed"),
    bin: path.join(base, "bin"),
    loginOnly: path.join(base, "login-only-bin"),
    detected: {}
  };
  ctx.project = path.join(ctx.home, "projects", "app");
  for (const dir of [ctx.project, ctx.agentOsHome, ctx.managedRoot, ctx.bin, ctx.loginOnly]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  for (const agentId of SESSION_AGENTS) {
    const file = path.join(ctx.bin, BINARIES[agentId]);
    await writeFile(file, "#!/bin/sh\necho 'fake agent: these tests never start it' >&2\nexit 1\n");
    await chmod(file, 0o755);
    ctx.detected[agentId] = { installed: true, path: file, version: "9.9.9", features: {} };
  }
  ctx.shell = path.join(base, "fake-login-shell");
  await writeFile(
    ctx.shell,
    [
      "#!/bin/sh",
      'echo "Good morning from a chatty startup file"',
      'export FROM_STARTUP_FILE="set in a startup file"',
      'export AGENT_OS_FROM_STARTUP="must never reach a session"',
      `PATH=${shQuote(ctx.loginOnly)}:"$PATH"`,
      "export PATH",
      ...startupLines,
      `exec ${shQuote(FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL)} "$@"`,
      ""
    ].join("\n")
  );
  await chmod(ctx.shell, 0o755);
  setKeystoreForTest();
  resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
  try {
    return await withEnv(
      {
        ...PLANTED,
        HOME: ctx.home,
        USERPROFILE: ctx.home,
        AGENT_OS_HOME: ctx.agentOsHome,
        HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined,
        AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: ctx.managedRoot,
        AGENT_OS_KEYSTORE: "file",
        SHELL: ctx.shell,
        // The variables that point a shell at startup files (ruling R15).
        ZDOTDIR: undefined,
        ENV: undefined,
        BASH_ENV: undefined,
        PATH: [ctx.bin, ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter)
      },
      async () => {
        assert.equal(os.homedir(), ctx.home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
        return await fn(ctx);
      }
    );
  } finally {
    resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
    setKeystoreForTest();
    await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

function start(ctx, agentId, extra = {}) {
  return buildSessionProfile({
    agentId,
    folder: ctx.project,
    sessionId: crypto.randomUUID(),
    settings: { claudeFullscreen: false },
    detected: ctx.detected[agentId],
    brain: null,
    agentOsVersion: VERSION,
    ...extra
  });
}

// Security 2 and H1-H4 for one profile's environment against the login shell's.
function assertSessionEnvironment(env, loginEnv, { sessionId, cwd, flicker, where }) {
  assert.equal(env.TERM, "xterm-256color", where);
  assert.equal(env.COLORTERM, "truecolor", where);
  assert.equal(env.TERM_PROGRAM, "AgentOS", `${where}: never vscode`);
  assert.equal(env.TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION, VERSION, where);
  assert.equal(env.AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID, sessionId, where);
  assert.equal(env.PWD, cwd, where);
  assert.equal(env.CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER, flicker ? "1" : undefined, `${where}: NO_FLICKER only with the opt-in, Claude Code only`);
  assert.equal(env.CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB, undefined, `${where}: never the env scrub`);
  assert.equal(env.AGENT_OS_HOOK_URL, undefined, `${where}: no hook variables in SP3`);
  assert.equal(env.AGENT_OS_HOOK_TOKEN, undefined, `${where}: no hook variables in SP3`);
  for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {
    if (key === "AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID") continue;
    assert.ok(!key.startsWith("AGENT_OS_") && !key.startsWith("HERMES_AGENT_OS_"), `${where}: ${key} is removed`);
  }
  for (const marker of NESTED_MARKERS) assert.equal(env[marker], undefined, `${where}: ${marker} is removed`);
  // H1: HOME and the agents' config folders as the person has them.
  assert.equal(env.HOME, loginEnv.HOME, where);
  assert.equal(env.CODEX_HOME, PLANTED.CODEX_HOME, where);
  assert.equal(env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME, PLANTED.XDG_CONFIG_HOME, where);
  for (const key of ["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "HERMES_HOME"]) assert.equal(env[key], undefined, `${where}: ${key} is never set`);
  assert.ok(!Object.keys(env).some((key) => key.startsWith("OPENCLAW_")), `${where}: no OpenClaw state variable is set`);
  // Everything else from the login shell passes through unchanged...
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(loginEnv)) {
    if (key.startsWith("AGENT_OS_") || key.startsWith("HERMES_AGENT_OS_") || NESTED_MARKERS.includes(key)) continue;
    if (ADDED.includes(key) || key === "CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER") continue;
    assert.equal(env[key], value, `${where}: ${key} passes through unchanged`);
  }
  // ...and nothing else is added.
  for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {
    if (key in loginEnv) continue;
    assert.ok(ADDED.includes(key) || (flicker && key === "CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER"), `${where}: ${key} was added`);
  }
}

// ---- a temp AGENT_OS_HOME only (the argv check reads runtimePaths().sessions) ----

async function withRuntimeHome(fn) {
  const home = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-session-settings-"));
  try {
    return await withEnv({ AGENT_OS_HOME: home, HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined }, () => fn(home));
  } finally {
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

test("profile snapshot (SP3): every agent's argv and environment, with the fullscreen opt-in off and on", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withProfileEnv(async (ctx) => {
    const login = await getLoginShellEnv();
    assert.equal(login.source, "login-shell");
    assert.equal(login.env.FROM_STARTUP_FILE, "set in a startup file", "the login shell's own settings are used");
    assert.equal(login.env.AGENT_OS_TOKEN, undefined, "Agent OS's token never reaches the login shell");
    assert.equal(login.env.CLAUDECODE, "1", "the server's own markers reach the login shell, and sessions remove them");
    for (const claudeFullscreen of [false, true]) {
      for (const agentId of SESSION_AGENTS) {
        const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
        const where = `${agentId}, opt-in ${claudeFullscreen ? "on" : "off"}`;
        const profile = await start(ctx, agentId, { sessionId, settings: { claudeFullscreen } });
        assert.equal(profile.command, ctx.detected[agentId].path, `${where}: the detected binary, never a shell`);
        assert.equal(profile.settingsFile, null, `${where}: no --settings without an OpenRouter or Local brain`);
        assert.deepEqual(profile.notes, [], where);
        const expected = {
          claude: { args: ["--session-id", profile.agentSessionId], cwd: ctx.project, softStop: "claude-bg", resumeMode: "id", folderShown: true },
          codex: { args: ["-C", ctx.project, ...TUI], cwd: ctx.project, softStop: null, resumeMode: "fallback", folderShown: true },
          cursor: { args: ["--workspace", ctx.project], cwd: ctx.project, softStop: null, resumeMode: "fallback", folderShown: true },
          hermes: { args: ["--in", ctx.project], cwd: ctx.project, softStop: null, resumeMode: "fallback", folderShown: true },
          openclaw: { args: ["tui", "--session", `agentos-${sessionId}`], cwd: ctx.home, softStop: "openclaw-abort", resumeMode: "id", folderShown: false }
        }[agentId];
        assert.deepEqual(
          { args: profile.args, cwd: profile.cwd, softStop: profile.softStop, resumeMode: profile.resumeMode, folderShown: profile.folderShown },
          expected,
          where
        );
        if (agentId === "claude") {
          assert.match(profile.agentSessionId, UUID, `${where}: Claude gets its own --session-id uuid`);
          assert.notEqual(profile.agentSessionId, sessionId, `${where}: separate from Agent OS's session id (Q39)`);
        } else if (agentId === "openclaw") {
          assert.equal(profile.agentSessionId, `agentos-${sessionId}`, where);
        } else {
          assert.equal(profile.agentSessionId, null, `${where}: no id source until its spike`);
        }
        assertSessionEnvironment(profile.env, login.env, {
          sessionId,
          cwd: expected.cwd,
          flicker: agentId === "claude" && claudeFullscreen,
          where
        });
      }
    }
  });
});

test("profiles: Claude Code on OpenRouter or Local gets --settings with its own private file, without the env scrub", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withProfileEnv(async (ctx) => {
    await storeOpenRouterKey(KEY);
    const helper = await openRouterKeyHelper();
    for (const brain of [OPENROUTER_BRAIN, LOCAL_BRAIN]) {
      const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
      const profile = await start(ctx, "claude", { sessionId, brain });
      const file = path.join(ctx.agentOsHome, "sessions", sessionId, "claude-settings.json");
      assert.deepEqual(profile.args, ["--session-id", profile.agentSessionId, "--settings", file], brain.mode);
      assert.equal(profile.settingsFile, file);
      const written = JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8"));
      assert.deepEqual(written, buildClaudeSettings(brain, brain.mode === "openrouter" ? helper : null, { forSession: true }));
      assert.equal("CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB" in written.env, false);
      assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(written).includes(KEY), "the key itself is never written");
      if (brain.mode === "openrouter") assert.equal(written.apiKeyHelper, helperCommandLine(helper));
      assert.equal((await stat(file)).mode & 0o777, 0o600);
      assert.equal((await stat(path.dirname(file))).mode & 0o777, 0o700);
      assert.equal((await stat(runtimePaths().sessions)).mode & 0o777, 0o700);
      assert.equal(profile.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL, (await getLoginShellEnv()).env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL, "the brain reaches Claude through the file, not the environment");
    }
    // A plan brain, even with a model, adds nothing (H3 allows no --model).
    const plan = await start(ctx, "claude", { brain: { mode: "plan", model: "opus" } });
    assert.deepEqual(plan.args, ["--session-id", plan.agentSessionId]);
  });
});

test("profiles: resume argv per agent (Claude by its uuid; Hermes, Codex and Cursor by the fallback; OpenClaw by its key)", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withProfileEnv(async (ctx) => {
    const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
    const claudeId = crypto.randomUUID();
    const resume = (agentId, agentSessionId = null) => start(ctx, agentId, { sessionId, resume: { agentSessionId } });

    const claude = await resume("claude", claudeId);
    assert.deepEqual([claude.args, claude.agentSessionId, claude.resumeMode], [["--resume", claudeId], claudeId, "id"]);
    const codex = await resume("codex");
    assert.deepEqual([codex.args, codex.cwd, codex.resumeMode], [["resume", "--last", ...TUI], ctx.project, "fallback"]);
    const cursor = await resume("cursor");
    assert.deepEqual([cursor.args, cursor.resumeMode], [["--resume", "--workspace", ctx.project], "fallback"]);
    const hermes = await resume("hermes");
    assert.deepEqual([hermes.args, hermes.resumeMode], [["--resume", "latest", "--in", ctx.project], "fallback"]);
    const openclaw = await resume("openclaw", `agentos-${sessionId}`);
    assert.deepEqual([openclaw.args, openclaw.agentSessionId, openclaw.cwd], [["tui", "--session", `agentos-${sessionId}`], `agentos-${sessionId}`, ctx.home]);

    // Claude resumes with --settings under the same rule as at start.
    await storeOpenRouterKey(KEY);
    const withBrain = await start(ctx, "claude", { sessionId, resume: { agentSessionId: claudeId }, brain: OPENROUTER_BRAIN });
    assert.deepEqual(withBrain.args, ["--resume", claudeId, "--settings", path.join(ctx.agentOsHome, "sessions", sessionId, "claude-settings.json")]);

    for (const bad of [null, "", "not-a-uuid", "../../etc"]) {
      await assert.rejects(
        () => resume("claude", bad),
        (error) => error.status === 409 && error.code === "not_resumable" && error.message === "This Claude Code conversation can't be resumed.",
        String(bad)
      );
    }
  });
});

test("profiles: the update kind is exactly `hermes update` in the checked folder, for Hermes only", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withProfileEnv(async (ctx) => {
    const checkout = path.join(ctx.home, ".hermes", "hermes-agent");
    await mkdir(checkout, { recursive: true });
    const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
    const update = await start(ctx, "hermes", { kind: "update", folder: checkout, sessionId, settings: { claudeFullscreen: true } });
    assert.deepEqual(
      { args: update.args, cwd: update.cwd, softStop: update.softStop, resumeMode: update.resumeMode, agentSessionId: update.agentSessionId, settingsFile: update.settingsFile },
      { args: ["update"], cwd: checkout, softStop: null, resumeMode: null, agentSessionId: null, settingsFile: null }
    );
    assert.equal(update.env.AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID, sessionId);
    assert.equal(update.env.CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER, undefined);
    const resumed = await start(ctx, "hermes", { kind: "update", folder: checkout, resume: { agentSessionId: null } });
    assert.deepEqual(resumed.args, ["update"], "an update session is never resumed");
    for (const agentId of ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "openclaw"]) {
      await assert.rejects(
        () => start(ctx, agentId, { kind: "update", folder: checkout }),
        (error) => error.status === 400 && error.code === "update_not_available" && error.message === "Only Hermes is updated in a session.",
        agentId
      );
    }
    await assert.rejects(() => start(ctx, "hermes", { kind: "update", folder: ctx.home }), (error) => error.code === "folder_refused");
  });
});

test("profiles: a folder outside the policy is refused with its own code and sentence", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withProfileEnv(async (ctx) => {
    const cases = [
      [ctx.home, "is_home", "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it."],
      [ctx.agentOsHome, "inside_agent_os", "Agent OS's own folder can't be used."],
      [ctx.bin, "outside_home", "Pick a folder inside your home folder."],
      ["projects/app", "not_absolute", "Type the full path, starting with / (or a drive letter on Windows)."],
      [path.join(ctx.home, "missing"), "missing", "That folder doesn't exist."]
    ];
    for (const [folder, folderCode, message] of cases) {
      await assert.rejects(
        () => start(ctx, "codex", { folder }),
        (error) => error.status === 400 && error.code === "folder_refused" && error.extra.code === folderCode && error.message === message,
        folder
      );
    }
    // The profile's folder is the real path (symlinks resolved).
    const link = path.join(ctx.home, "app-link");
    await symlink(ctx.project, link);
    assert.equal((await start(ctx, "hermes", { folder: link })).cwd, ctx.project);
  });
});

test("assertSessionArgvSafe accepts exactly the H3 shapes, and folders whose names look like flags", async () => {
  await withRuntimeHome(async () => {
    const uuid = "123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000";
    const folder = path.resolve("/Users/someone/projects/app");
    const settings = path.join(runtimePaths().sessions, uuid, "claude-settings.json");
    const accepted = [
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--settings", settings]],
      ["claude", ["--resume", uuid, "--settings", settings]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, ...TUI]],
      ["codex", ["resume", "--last", ...TUI]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, ...TUI, "--oss", "--local-provider", "ollama", "-m", "qwen3-coder:30b", "-c", "model_context_window=65536"]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, ...TUI, ...codexBrainArgs({ mode: "openrouter", model: "openai/gpt-5.2" }, { command: "/usr/bin/security", args: ["find-generic-password", "-w"] })]],
      ["cursor", ["--workspace", folder]],
      ["cursor", ["--resume", "--workspace", folder]],
      ["hermes", ["--in", folder]],
      ["hermes", ["--resume", "latest", "--in", folder]],
      ["hermes", ["update"]],
      ["openclaw", ["tui", "--session", `agentos-${uuid}`]]
    ];
    for (const odd of ["--force-demo", "bypassPermissions", "dangerously-fun", "-f"]) {
      const weird = path.resolve(`/Users/someone/${odd}`);
      accepted.push(["codex", ["-C", weird, ...TUI]], ["cursor", ["--workspace", weird]], ["hermes", ["--in", weird]]);
    }
    for (const [agentId, args] of accepted) assert.doesNotThrow(() => assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args), `${agentId} ${args.join(" ")}`);
  });
});

test("assertSessionArgvSafe refuses anything outside H3: bypass, yolo, trust, MCP and hook options, extra flags", async () => {
  await withRuntimeHome(async () => {
    const uuid = "123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000";
    const folder = path.resolve("/Users/someone/projects/app");
    const refused = [
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--dangerously-skip-permissions"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--bare"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--disable-slash-commands"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--strict-mcp-config"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--mcp-config", "/tmp/mcp.json"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--model", "opus"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", uuid, "--settings", "/tmp/other-settings.json"]],
      ["claude", ["--session-id", "not-a-uuid"]],
      ["claude", []],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox"]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, "--yolo"]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, "--no-alt-screen"]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, "--full-auto"]],
      ["codex", ["-C", folder, "-c", 'sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"']],

      ["cursor", ["--workspace", folder, "-f"]],

      ["cursor", ["--workspace", folder, "--model", "auto"]],

      ["openclaw", ["tui", "--session", "agentos-runs"]],
      ["openclaw", ["chat"]],
      ["openclaw", ["tui", "--session", `agentos-${uuid}`, "--url", "ws://127.0.0.1:1"]],
      ["gemini", ["--help"]],
      ["codex", "-C /tmp"],
      // Prototype names are never agents (ruling R6): no shape is found for them.
      ["constructor", ["--session-id", uuid]],
      ["__proto__", ["--session-id", uuid]],
      ["toString", ["tui", "--session", `agentos-${uuid}`]],
      ["hasOwnProperty", ["--workspace", folder]]
    ];
    for (const [agentId, args] of refused) {
      assert.throws(
        () => assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args),

        `${agentId} ${JSON.stringify(args)}`

    }
    // The sentence names the agent by its short name, or "this agent".
    assert.throws(

    );
    for (const agentId of ["gemini", "constructor", "__proto__", "toString"]) {
      assert.throws(
        () => assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, ["--session-id", uuid]),
        (error) => error.message === "Agent OS stopped this agent from starting: its command line had an option Agent OS never adds.",
        agentId
      );
    }
  });
});
```

```js
// How each agent starts in a session (spec "Launch profiles", "Resume per
// agent", "Session kinds"; harness rules H1-H4; planning decisions Q7-Q11):
//   - the person's own binary, from detection (H1); argv only, never a shell;
//   - only the H3 additions, checked again by assertSessionArgvSafe;
//   - the H2 environment from shell-env.js, never a run plan's env or argv
//     (Q11: Cursor's --trust and Hermes' HERMES_HOME must not leak in);
//   - the H4 fullscreen opt-in, read from the stored settings at each launch.
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { constants as fsConstants, promises as fs } from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { containsBlockedFlag } from "../agent-flags.js";
import { getAdapter } from "../agents/index.js";
import {
  LOCAL_CONTEXT_TOKENS,
  SAFE_MODEL_ARG,
  assertSafeClaudeSettings,
  buildClaudeSettings,
  codexBrainArgs,
  keyHelper
} from "../builders/brain-launch.js";
import { hasCursorForceFlag } from "../runs/run-manager.js";
import { withSiblingNodePath } from "../safety.js";
import { managedNodeRoot } from "../setup/managed-node.js";
import { RUNTIME_VERSION, ensurePrivateDir, ensureRuntimeStore, runtimePaths } from "../store.js";
import { SESSION_ID_RE, sessionError } from "./errors.js";
import { checkSessionFolder } from "./folders.js";
import { readSessionSettings } from "./settings.js";
import { getLoginShellEnv, sessionEnv } from "./shell-env.js";

export const SESSION_AGENTS = Object.freeze(["claude", "codex", "cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"]);
// The short names every session message, tab and dialog uses ("Codex", not
// the adapter's "Codex CLI"), so one dialog never names an agent two ways.
export const SESSION_AGENT_LABEL = Object.freeze({
  claude: "Claude Code",
  codex: "Codex",
  cursor: "Cursor",
  hermes: "Hermes",
  openclaw: "OpenClaw"
});
// Spike S5 checks whether OpenClaw's work honours the folder its TUI starts
// in. Until then (the safe default) no folder is offered or claimed: the TUI
// starts in the person's HOME and the panel says "Set by OpenClaw".
export const OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED = false;

// A crypto.randomUUID() value: Agent OS's session ids and Claude's --session-id.
const UUID = SESSION_ID_RE;
const OPENCLAW_KEY = /^agentos-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;
// The names detection looks for, in its order (cursor.js tries agent first).
const BINARY_NAMES = { claude: ["claude"], codex: ["codex"], cursor: ["agent", "cursor-agent"], hermes: ["hermes"], openclaw: ["openclaw"] };
// Codex's own notifications as OSC 9, so the mirror sees them (spec table).
const CODEX_TUI_OPTIONS = [
  "-c", "tui.notification_method=osc9",
  "-c", 'tui.notifications=["agent-turn-complete","approval-requested"]',
  "-c", "tui.notification_condition=always"
];

// Every per-agent lookup goes through this (ruling R6): a plain `map[id]`
// would take "constructor", "__proto__" or "toString" from Object.prototype.
function ownValue(map, key) {
  return typeof key === "string" && Object.hasOwn(map, key) ? map[key] : undefined;
}

function hasBrainKeys(brain) {
  return brain?.mode === "openrouter" || brain?.mode === "local";
}

async function findOnPath(names, pathValue) {
  const dirs = String(pathValue || "").split(path.delimiter).filter((dir) => dir && path.isAbsolute(dir));
  for (const name of names) {
    const candidates = process.platform === "win32" ? [`${name}.exe`, `${name}.cmd`, name] : [name];
    for (const dir of dirs) {
      for (const candidate of candidates) {
        const file = path.join(dir, candidate);
        try {
          if (!(await fs.stat(file)).isFile()) continue;
          if (process.platform !== "win32") await fs.access(file, fsConstants.X_OK);
          return file;
        } catch {
          // not here; keep looking
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return "";
}

// H1: the path detection found. Q8: when detection found nothing, one more
// look over the login shell's PATH (it can hold folders the server's lacks).
async function findAgentCommand(agentId, detected, loginEnv) {
  if (detected?.installed && typeof detected.path === "string" && path.isAbsolute(detected.path)) return detected.path;
  const found = await findOnPath(ownValue(BINARY_NAMES, agentId) || [], loginEnv.PATH ?? loginEnv.Path);
  if (found) return found;
  throw sessionError(
    409,
    "agent_not_installed",
    `${ownValue(SESSION_AGENT_LABEL, agentId)} isn't installed, or Agent OS can't find it. Install it in Setup, then try again.`
  );
}

// Q7: a CLI inside Agent OS's managed Node folder runs on the Node beside it.
function insideManagedNode(command) {
  const fold = (value) => (process.platform === "darwin" || process.platform === "win32" ? value.toLowerCase() : value);
  return fold(path.resolve(command)).startsWith(fold(path.resolve(managedNodeRoot())) + path.sep);
}

// Spec "Launch profiles", Claude Code: <AGENT_OS_HOME>/sessions/<id>/claude-settings.json
// (0600, in a 0700 folder) with only the brain keys, without
// CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB (Q9). It holds the key's read command, never the key.
async function writeSessionClaudeSettings(sessionId, brain) {
  const settings = buildClaudeSettings(brain, brain.mode === "openrouter" ? await keyHelper() : null, { forSession: true });
  assertSafeClaudeSettings(settings);
  const paths = await ensureRuntimeStore();
  const dir = await ensurePrivateDir(path.join(paths.sessions, sessionId));
  const file = path.join(dir, "claude-settings.json");
  await fs.writeFile(file, `${JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
  if (process.platform !== "win32") await fs.chmod(file, 0o600);
  return file;
}

// The launch profile for one session start or resume:
// { command, args, cwd, env, agentSessionId, settingsFile, softStop, resumeMode, folderShown, notes }.
// `resume` is null for a fresh start, or { agentSessionId } (from meta.json)
// to continue an ended agent session. `kind: "update"` is `hermes update`.
export async function buildSessionProfile({
  agentId,
  folder,
  sessionId,
  kind = "agent",
  resume = null,
  settings,
  detected,
  brain = null,
  agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION
} = {}) {
  if (!SESSION_AGENTS.includes(agentId)) throw sessionError(400, "unknown_agent", "Agent OS can't start a session for that agent.");
  if (!UUID.test(String(sessionId || ""))) throw sessionError(404, "unknown_session", "That session doesn't exist anymore.");
  if (kind !== "agent" && kind !== "update") throw sessionError(400, "unknown_kind", "Agent OS can't start that kind of session.");
  if (kind === "update" && agentId !== "hermes") throw sessionError(400, "update_not_available", "Only Hermes is updated in a session.");
  const label = ownValue(SESSION_AGENT_LABEL, agentId);

  const shell = await getLoginShellEnv();
  const command = await findAgentCommand(agentId, detected === undefined ? await getAdapter(agentId).detect() : detected, shell.env);

  let cwd = os.homedir();
  let folderShown = true;
  if (kind === "agent" && agentId === "openclaw" && !OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED) {
    folderShown = false;
  } else {
    const check = await checkSessionFolder(folder);
    if (!check.ok) throw sessionError(400, "folder_refused", check.message, { code: check.code });
    cwd = check.path;
  }

  const current = settings ?? (await readSessionSettings());
  let env = sessionEnv(shell.env, { sessionId, agentOsVersion, claudeFullscreen: current?.claudeFullscreen === true, agentId });
  if (insideManagedNode(command)) env = withSiblingNodePath(command, env);
  // What a shell sets after `cd <folder>`; the login shell's own PWD was dropped.
  env.PWD = cwd;

  const resuming = kind === "agent" && resume !== null && resume !== undefined;
  let args;
  let agentSessionId = null;
  let settingsFile = null;
  let softStop = null;
  let resumeMode = null;
  if (kind === "update") {
    // Session kinds: exactly `hermes update`, no --yes and no H3 additions.
    args = ["update"];
  } else if (agentId === "claude") {
    if (resuming) {
      if (!UUID.test(String(resume.agentSessionId || ""))) {
        throw sessionError(409, "not_resumable", `This ${label} conversation can't be resumed.`);
      }
      agentSessionId = resume.agentSessionId;
      args = ["--resume", agentSessionId];
    } else {
      agentSessionId = crypto.randomUUID(); // Q39: a second uuid, separate from the session id
      args = ["--session-id", agentSessionId];
    }
    // H3: --settings only when the file has something to carry (SP3: an OpenRouter or Local brain).
    if (hasBrainKeys(brain)) {
      settingsFile = await writeSessionClaudeSettings(sessionId, brain);
      args.push("--settings", settingsFile);
    }
    softStop = "claude-bg";
    resumeMode = "id";
  } else if (agentId === "codex") {
    const brainArgs = hasBrainKeys(brain) ? codexBrainArgs(brain, brain.mode === "openrouter" ? await keyHelper() : null) : [];
    // Fallback resume (until spike S3 confirms an id source): the latest conversation, in the same folder (cwd).
    args = resuming ? ["resume", "--last", ...CODEX_TUI_OPTIONS, ...brainArgs] : ["-C", cwd, ...CODEX_TUI_OPTIONS, ...brainArgs];
    resumeMode = "fallback";
  } else if (agentId === "cursor") {
    // No model option (H3): the person picks models inside Cursor, as in Terminal.
    args = resuming ? ["--resume", "--workspace", cwd] : ["--workspace", cwd];
    resumeMode = "fallback";
  } else if (agentId === "hermes") {
    // The person's configured interface (H4): never a forced --tui.
    args = resuming ? ["--resume", "latest", "--in", cwd] : ["--in", cwd];
    resumeMode = "fallback";
  } else {
    // Resume is the same start command: the key names the conversation.
    agentSessionId = `agentos-${sessionId}`;
    args = ["tui", "--session", agentSessionId];
    softStop = "openclaw-abort";
    resumeMode = "id";
  }
  assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args);
  return {
    command,
    args,
    cwd,
    env,
    agentSessionId,
    settingsFile,
    softStop,
    resumeMode,
    folderShown,
    notes: shell.notice ? [shell.notice] : []
  };
}

// ---- the H3 check ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

const NEVER = ["--bare", "--disable-slash-commands", "--strict-mcp-config", "--mcp-config", "--accept-hooks", "--yolo", "--trust", "--no-alt-screen"];
const NEVER_WORDS = /dangerously|bypass|full-access|skip-permission/i;
const QUOTED = '"(?:[^"\\\\]|\\\\.)*"';
// Exactly the -c values Agent OS adds: the notification options, then
// codexBrainArgs (OpenRouter or Local). Nothing else may be configured.
const CODEX_CONFIG = [
  /^tui\.notification_method=osc9$/,
  /^tui\.notifications=\["agent-turn-complete","approval-requested"\]$/,
  /^tui\.notification_condition=always$/,
  /^model_provider="openrouter"$/,
  /^model_providers\.openrouter\.name="OpenRouter"$/,
  /^model_providers\.openrouter\.base_url="https:\/\/openrouter\.ai\/api\/v1"$/,
  /^model_providers\.openrouter\.wire_api="responses"$/,
  new RegExp(`^model_providers\\.openrouter\\.auth=\\{command=${QUOTED}, args=\\[(?:${QUOTED}(?:, ${QUOTED})*)?\\]\\}$`),
  /^shell_environment_policy\.ignore_default_excludes=false$/,
  new RegExp(`^model_context_window=${LOCAL_CONTEXT_TOKENS}$`)
];

function isFolderValue(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && !value.includes("\0") && path.isAbsolute(value);
}

function isSessionSettingsFile(value) {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(value)) return false;
  const dir = path.dirname(value);
  return path.basename(value) === "claude-settings.json" && UUID.test(path.basename(dir)) && path.dirname(dir) === runtimePaths().sessions;
}

const SHAPES = {
  claude(args) {
    if (args.length !== 2 && args.length !== 4) return false;
    if ((args[0] !== "--session-id" && args[0] !== "--resume") || !UUID.test(args[1])) return false;
    return args.length === 2 || (args[2] === "--settings" && isSessionSettingsFile(args[3]));
  },
  codex(args) {
    let i;
    if (args[0] === "-C" && isFolderValue(args[1])) i = 2;
    else if (args[0] === "resume" && args[1] === "--last") i = 2;
    else return false;
    while (i < args.length) {
      const flag = args[i];
      const value = args[i + 1];
      if (flag === "-c" && CODEX_CONFIG.some((pattern) => pattern.test(String(value)))) i += 2;
      else if (flag === "-m" && SAFE_MODEL_ARG.test(String(value))) i += 2;
      else if (flag === "--local-provider" && value === "ollama") i += 2;
      else if (flag === "--oss") i += 1;
      else return false;
    }
    return true;
  },
  cursor(args) {
    const rest = args[0] === "--resume" ? args.slice(1) : args;
    return rest.length === 2 && rest[0] === "--workspace" && isFolderValue(rest[1]);
  },
  hermes(args) {
    if (args.length === 1) return args[0] === "update";
    const rest = args[0] === "--resume" && args[1] === "latest" ? args.slice(2) : args;
    return rest.length === 2 && rest[0] === "--in" && isFolderValue(rest[1]);
  },
  openclaw(args) {
    return args.length === 3 && args[0] === "tui" && args[1] === "--session" && OPENCLAW_KEY.test(args[2]);
  }
};

function isBlockedWord(word, agentId) {
  const name = word.split("=")[0];
  return containsBlockedFlag(word) || NEVER.includes(name) || NEVER_WORDS.test(word) || (agentId === "hermes" && name === "--tui");
}

// Throws unless `args` is exactly one of the argv shapes above (spec H3: only
// additive options) and holds nothing from the blocked lists.
export function assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args) {
  const shape = ownValue(SHAPES, agentId);
  const label = ownValue(SESSION_AGENT_LABEL, agentId) || "this agent";
  const refuse = () =>
    sessionError(500, "unsafe_argv", `Agent OS stopped ${label} from starting: its command line had an option Agent OS never adds.`);
  if (!shape || !Array.isArray(args) || !args.every((arg) => typeof arg === "string")) throw refuse();
  // Option names and a leading subcommand are checked against the blocked
  // lists. Values (folders, ids, model names, Codex -c settings) never start
  // with "-" and are checked by shape instead, so a folder named
  // "--force-demo" or "bypassPermissions" is still allowed.
  const words = args.filter((arg, index) => index === 0 || arg.startsWith("-"));
  if (words.some((word) => isBlockedWord(word, agentId))) throw refuse();
  if (agentId === "cursor" && hasCursorForceFlag({ command: "agent", args })) throw refuse();
  if (!shape(args)) throw refuse();
}
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `profiles.js` imports `run-manager.js` only for `hasCursorForceFlag`; there is no import loop (nothing under `server/runtime/runs/` imports the sessions modules).
- The OpenClaw key `agentos-<sessionId>` fits the adapter's existing `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` (`server/runtime/agents/openclaw.js` line 242).
- The Claude settings file holds `apiKeyHelper` (a command that prints the key) and model names, never the key itself (the same rule as headless runs).

#### Notes

1. **`PWD` is the session's folder (ruling R14, decision Q7a).** S2 drops the resolver shell's own `PWD`, `OLDPWD` and `_`; `profiles.js` sets `PWD` to `cwd`, as a shell does after `cd <folder>` in Terminal. It is the one variable beyond H2's "set" list, a deliberate fidelity choice; the snapshot test pins it.
2. **Argv flags the repo has never seen are the spec's** (`claude --session-id`, `codex resume --last`, `agent --resume`, `hermes --in` / `--resume latest`, `openclaw tui --session`); spikes S2 to S6 check them on the owner's Mac (Q10). The Codex fallback resume is `resume --last` plus the same `-c` and brain options, without `-C` (the working folder is the session's folder); spike S3 also checks that `codex resume` takes the `-c` options after the subcommand.
3. **Q8 without `which()`.** `which()` (`server/runtime/safety.js`) searches only the server's own `PATH` and takes no `PATH` argument, so `profiles.js` has a small private `findOnPath` over the login shell's `PATH`, in detection's name order (`agent` before `cursor-agent`). `detect.js` is not changed.
4. **Brains.** A plan brain with a model adds nothing (Claude "opus", Cursor "auto"): H3 allows no `--model` for sessions (Q9); a brain passed for Hermes or OpenClaw is ignored. `buildClaudeSettings` and `codexBrainArgs` may throw `brainError`s (`openrouter_key_missing`, `base_url_without_credential`) with a `.code` and no `.status`; S6 lets them through and S8 answers them with `builderErrorResponse`.
5. **A stale Claude settings file is kept** when a session later resumes on the Plan brain: it is 0600, holds only the key's read command (never the key) and is no longer passed. Deleting the session folder removes it.
6. **The test login shell (ruling R15).** The profile tests set `SHELL` to a temp script that exports a few variables the way a person's startup files would and then `exec`s `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`; the fallback test points `SHELL` at a file that does not exist. Neither runs a real shell or reads a startup file. The wrapper exists because the snapshot must prove that the login shell's own values, and its own `PATH` folder, reach a session while Agent OS's own variables do not.
7. **`hasCursorForceFlag` is exported from `run-manager.js`** (one word) rather than moved into `agent-flags.js`; `assertSessionArgvSafe` calls it as `hasCursorForceFlag({ command: "agent", args })`.

---

### Task S4: pty-host and mirror (headless xterm, serialize, modes, query answers, alerts, counted output)

This task builds the two engine pieces that sit right next to an agent's terminal program. `pty-host.js` runs the program in a real pseudo-terminal (PTY, the kind of "fake keyboard and screen" Terminal.app gives a program) through node-pty: argv only, never a shell, with exactly the environment and folder it is given, never the server's own environment (which holds `AGENT_OS_TOKEN`). It loads node-pty lazily, so a server without it still starts, and it registers each PTY's pid with `trackPid` so quit and Hold to stop all reach sessions. `mirror.js` keeps the server's own copy of each session's screen with xterm.js's headless terminal. That copy gives a window that attaches later the exact screen and the modes the serializer leaves out, answers the three standard terminal questions only while no window is the writer, forwards alerts (BEL, OSC 9/99/777) raw, and reports "counted output" for the 20 s activity rule. Nothing here knows about sessions, routes or sockets; S6 wires the pieces together.

Two facts about the real packages shape this task:
- `term.write()` in xterm.js is asynchronous, so a snapshot taken synchronously can miss output that the mirror has received but not yet read. That output would be lost for the window that attaches. `snapshot()` therefore returns a Promise that is built inside a write callback, so it covers exactly the output written before the call, never more and never less. The manager (S6) registers a new window as "waiting", takes the snapshot, then sends the snapshot and the output that arrived meanwhile, so nothing is lost or sent twice.
- `@xterm/addon-serialize` reads xterm.js internals (`terminal._core`), so the headless terminal and the serialize addon must come from the same xterm.js build. W0 pins the set built from the same commit as `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304`: `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301` and `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301` (the browser terminal, U2, loads the same unicode11 build). All three are CommonJS bundles, so `mirror.js` loads them with a default import, never a named ESM import.

**Files:**
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js`
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js`
- Test: `test/sessions-pty.test.js` (new; 12 tests in Step 2, 14 after Step 10)
- Test: `test/sessions-mirror.test.js` (new; 12 tests)
- No existing file changes. (`server/runtime/process-tree.js` is S1's; this task only imports from it.)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - S1, `server/runtime/process-tree.js`: `trackPid(pid, onExit?)`, where `onExit` is a subscribe function `(listener) => unsubscribe` that trackPid calls once so the pid untracks itself when the process ends; `untrackPid(pid)`; and `killAllTracked({ graceMs })`, which stops every tracked child and every tracked pid with its whole tree. pty-host passes the PTY handle's own `onExit` as that subscribe function, and still calls `untrackPid(pid)` itself on exit (harmless twice).
  - W0, in `dependencies` at exact versions: `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.14`, `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301`.
  - W1, `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`:
    - `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = all six agent names, mode = "tui" })` writes an executable shim `<dir>/<name>` for each name. In mode `tui` (no `FAKE_AGENT_MODE` in the environment) the fake prints one line `FAKE_ARGV <json>` whose `argv` holds its arguments as JSON strings, then the prompt `> `; it echoes typed text (`you said: <text>`), and `exit <n>` typed at the prompt makes it exit with code n (planning decision Q2).
    - `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`: the stand-in login shell, the only `SHELL` any test uses (never `/bin/sh`).
  - node-pty typings (`typings/node-pty.d.ts`): `spawn(file, args: string[], { name, cols, rows, cwd, env, encoding })` → `IPty` with `pid`, `onData: IEvent<string>`, `onExit: IEvent<{ exitCode: number, signal?: number }>` (the signal is a number), `write`, `resize`, `kill(signal?)` (default SIGHUP; "@throws Will throw when signal is used on Windows"), `pause()`, `resume()`. Each `IEvent` returns an `IDisposable`.
  - @xterm/headless typings: `new Terminal(options & { cols, rows })`, `write(data, callback?)` ("the data is processed asynchronously. Provide a callback to know when the data was processed"), `onData`, `onBell`, `onWriteParsed`, `parser.registerCsiHandler(id, cb)` / `registerEscHandler` / `registerOscHandler(ident, cb)` ("Return true if the sequence was handled; false if we should try a previous handler ... The most recently added handler is tried first"), `modes: IModes` (`bracketedPasteMode`, `mouseTrackingMode: 'none'|'x10'|'vt200'|'drag'|'any'`, `sendFocusMode`, `applicationCursorKeysMode`; no mouse encoding and no kitty flags), `buffer.active` (`type`, `baseY`, `getLine(y).translateToString(true)`), `unicode.activeVersion` ("(EXPERIMENTAL)", needs `allowProposedApi: true`), `vtExtensions.kittyKeyboard`.
  - @xterm/addon-serialize typings: `new SerializeAddon()`, `serialize(options?)` (includes the alternate screen and the modes in `IModes`, but not mouse encoding or kitty flags).
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js`):
  - `export const PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer."`
  - `export function ptyAvailable()` → `Promise<{ ok: true, reason: null } | { ok: false, reason: string }>`. It loads node-pty once and runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY once (a probe). A missing module is final; a failed probe is retried after 30 s.
  - `export async function spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker })` → `PtyHandle`:
    `{ pid, write(data), resize(cols, rows), kill(signal = "SIGTERM"), pause(), resume(), onData(cb) → unsubscribe, onExit(cb) → unsubscribe }`.
    - `command` and `cwd` must be absolute, `args` a string array, and `env` an explicit object (never `process.env` by default): otherwise `TypeError`.
    - Errors: plain `Error`s with `code: "pty_unavailable"` (message `PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON`) or `code: "spawn_failed"`. The manager (S6) checks `ptyAvailable()` before it spawns and answers 503 `pty_unavailable` itself, and turns any spawn error into its own 500 `start_failed`.
    - `onExit` delivers `{ exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null }`: the signal as a NAME (`"SIGTERM"`, `"SIGKILL"`), and `exitCode: null` when a signal ended it. A listener added after the end is still called once.
    - Output that arrives before the first `onData` listener is kept (up to 1 MB) and handed to that first listener.
    - `trackPid(pid, handle.onExit)` right after the spawn; `untrackPid(pid)` on exit.
    - `tracker` (`{ trackPid, untrackPid }`) is for tests only; it defaults to process-tree's.
  - `export function setPtyLoaderForTests(fn | null)`: tests only.
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js`):
  - `export function createMirror({ cols, rows, onQueryReply, onAlert, now = Date.now })` → `Mirror`:
    - `write(chunk: string)`;
    - `resize(cols, rows)` (cols 2-500, rows 1-200; anything else ignored);
    - `snapshot()` → **`Promise<{ data, cols, rows, modes }>`**, where `modes = { altScreen: boolean, bracketedPaste: boolean, mouseTracking: "none"|"x10"|"vt200"|"drag"|"any", mouseEncoding: "default"|"sgr"|"sgr-pixels", focusReporting: boolean, cursorKeysApp: boolean, kittyFlags: number }`. It covers exactly the chunks written before the call;
    - `setWriterAttached(boolean)`: while false, DA1 (`ESC[?1;2c`), cursor position (`ESC[<row>;<col>R`, and the `ESC[?…R` form) and kitty (`ESC[?<flags>u`) replies go to `onQueryReply(reply)`. Every other reply xterm.js would make is dropped, and nothing is sent while a writer is attached;
    - `onCountedOutput(cb)` → unsubscribe: fires at most every 250 ms when the text above the bottom 6 rows changed or the screen scrolled since the last check;
    - `dispose()`.
    - `onAlert(raw)`: `"bel"`, or `"<osc number>;<payload>"`, for example `"9;Approval requested"` or `"777;notify;Codex;Waiting"`, capped at 4096 characters.
  - `export function isUserInput(data)` → `false` for a frame made only of terminal replies (DA1/DA2/DA3, cursor position, status, kitty flags, mode reports, XTVERSION, DECRQSS, OSC colour replies), focus reports (`ESC[I`, `ESC[O`) or mouse-motion reports (SGR and default encoding). Otherwise `true`: keys, paste, clicks, the wheel. An empty frame is `false`.
  - `export const COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS = 6, COUNTED_CHECK_MS = 250, MIRROR_SCROLLBACK = 1000, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT = 4096`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing PTY host tests.** Create `test/sessions-pty.test.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// The PTY host: an agent's own terminal program running in a real
// pseudo-terminal through node-pty. Argv only, exactly the environment and
// folder it is given, signals reported by name, flow control (pause/resume),
// and the pid tracked so quit and Hold to stop all reach it.
// Programs here are tiny Node scripts written to a temp folder, or W1's TUI
// fakes. No real agent ever runs.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, realpath, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";
import { killAllTracked } from "../server/runtime/process-tree.js";
import {
  PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON,
  ptyAvailable,
  setPtyLoaderForTests,
  spawnPty
} from "../server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js";
import { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const SKIP_POSIX = { skip: isWindows ? "PTY tests use POSIX shims and signals" : false };
const SAMPLE_UUID = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555";

const SLEEPER = "setInterval(() => {}, 1000);\n";
const ENV_PROBE = [
  "const info = {",
  "  marker: process.env.SESSION_MARKER ?? null,",
  "  token: process.env.AGENT_OS_TOKEN ?? null,",
  "  term: process.env.TERM ?? null,",
  "  cwd: process.cwd()",
  "};",
  "process.stdout.write('ENV ' + JSON.stringify(info) + '\\n');"
].join("\n");
const SIZE_PROBE = [
  "const report = () => process.stdout.write('SIZE ' + process.stdout.columns + 'x' + process.stdout.rows + '\\n');",
  "report();",
  "process.stdout.on('resize', report);",
  "setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"
].join("\n");
const TICKER = "setInterval(() => process.stdout.write('tick\\n'), 20);\n";

async function withTempDir(fn) {
  // realpath: on macOS os.tmpdir() is a symlink, and a program's cwd is the real path.
  const dir = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-pty-")));
  try {
    return await fn(dir);
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

// The system folders of every test that runs a fake agent: never Homebrew's
// or /usr/local, where a real agent could live.
const SYSTEM_PATH = "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin";

// A small, explicit environment. SHELL is the suite's stand-in login shell
// (the only SHELL a test uses), so nothing ever runs the developer's own
// shell setup.
function ptyEnv(home, extra = {}) {
  return { PATH: SYSTEM_PATH, HOME: home, SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, TERM: "xterm-256color", LANG: "en_US.UTF-8", ...extra };
}

async function writeScript(dir, name, source) {
  const file = path.join(dir, name);
  await writeFile(file, source, "utf8");
  return file;
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function waitFor(predicate, { timeoutMs = 10000, intervalMs = 20, what = "the condition" } = {}) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const value = await predicate();
    if (value) return value;
    await sleep(intervalMs);
  }
  throw new Error(`timed out waiting for ${what}`);
}

function collect(handle) {
  const out = { text: "" };
  handle.onData((chunk) => {
    out.text += chunk;
  });
  return out;
}

// Resolves with the exit info, or null when the program has not ended in time.
function exitOf(handle, timeoutMs = 10000) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), timeoutMs);
    timer.unref?.();
    handle.onExit((info) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(info);
    });
  });
}

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

test("spawnPty refuses a program without its full path, odd arguments, a relative folder, or no explicit environment", async () => {
  await assert.rejects(() => spawnPty({ command: "claude", args: [], cwd: os.tmpdir(), env: {} }), TypeError);
  await assert.rejects(() => spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: ["ok", 3], cwd: os.tmpdir(), env: {} }), TypeError);
  await assert.rejects(() => spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [], cwd: "relative/folder", env: {} }), TypeError);
  await assert.rejects(
    () => spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [], cwd: os.tmpdir() }),
    /never passes on the server's own/
  );
});

    await assert.rejects(

    );
  } finally {

});

});

test("kill reports the signal by name, and a listener added after the end still hears about it", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {

    const second = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir) });
    try {

      first.kill(); // SIGTERM by default
      assert.deepEqual(await firstExit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGTERM" });

      const secondExit = exitOf(second);
      second.kill("SIGKILL");
      assert.deepEqual(await secondExit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" });
      assert.deepEqual(await exitOf(second), { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }, "a listener added after the end");

      second.write("ignored");
      second.resize(80, 24);
      second.pause();
      second.resume();

test("pause stops the program's output until resume", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {
    const script = await writeScript(dir, "ticker.mjs", TICKER);
    const handle = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir) });
    try {
      let chunks = 0;
      handle.onData(() => {
        chunks += 1;
      });
      await waitFor(() => chunks > 0, { what: "the first tick" });
      handle.pause();
      await sleep(200); // let anything already on its way arrive
      const frozen = chunks;
      await sleep(400);
      assert.equal(chunks, frozen, "no output arrives while paused");
      handle.resume();
      await waitFor(() => chunks > frozen, { what: "output after resume" });
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});

test("the pid is tracked at the start (with an onExit subscription) and untracked at the end", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {
    const script = await writeScript(dir, "sleeper.mjs", SLEEPER);
    const calls = [];
    let trackedOnExit = null;
    const tracker = {
      trackPid: (pid, onExit) => {
        trackedOnExit = onExit;
        calls.push(["track", pid]);
      },
      untrackPid: (pid) => calls.push(["untrack", pid])
    };
    const handle = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir), tracker });
    try {
      assert.deepEqual(calls, [["track", handle.pid]]);
      assert.equal(typeof trackedOnExit, "function");
      const heard = [];
      trackedOnExit((info) => heard.push(info));
      const exit = exitOf(handle);
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
      assert.deepEqual(await exit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" });
      assert.deepEqual(calls, [["track", handle.pid], ["untrack", handle.pid]]);
      assert.deepEqual(heard, [{ exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }]);
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});

test("killAllTracked (quit and Hold to stop all) reaches a PTY program too", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {
    const script = await writeScript(dir, "sleeper.mjs", SLEEPER);
    const handle = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir) });
    try {
      const exit = exitOf(handle);
      await killAllTracked({ graceMs: 500 });
      const info = await exit;
      assert.ok(info, "the program ended");
      assert.ok(["SIGTERM", "SIGKILL"].includes(info.signal), `ended by ${info.signal}`);
      assert.equal(isAlive(handle.pid), false);
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});
```

```js
// Runs an agent's own terminal program inside a real pseudo-terminal (PTY)
// with node-pty, the way Terminal.app does: argv only (never a shell), the
// environment it is given (never the server's own, which holds
// AGENT_OS_TOKEN) and the folder it is given.
//
// node-pty is a native module, so it is loaded only when a session needs it.
// A server without it (the portable test, Docker) still starts and simply
// reports that sessions can't start.
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { trackPid, untrackPid } from "../process-tree.js";

export const PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer.";

const DEFAULT_TRACKER = Object.freeze({ trackPid, untrackPid });
const EARLY_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 1024 * 1024; // characters kept until the first listener
const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
const PROBE_RETRY_MS = 30000;
const realLoader = () => import("node-pty");

let loader = realLoader;
let loading = null;
let availability = null;
let probeFailedAt = 0;

function loadNodePty() {
  if (!loading) {
    loading = Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => loader())
      .then((mod) => {
        // node-pty is CommonJS: spawn sits on the namespace or on `default`.
        const pty = typeof mod?.spawn === "function" ? mod : mod?.default;
        if (typeof pty?.spawn !== "function") throw new Error("node-pty has no spawn()");
        return { ok: true, pty };
      })
      .catch((error) => ({ ok: false, error }));
  }
  return loading;
}

// Tests only: replace how node-pty is loaded. null puts the real import back.
export function setPtyLoaderForTests(fn) {
  loader = typeof fn === "function" ? fn : realLoader;
  loading = null;
  availability = null;
  probeFailedAt = 0;
}

// The probe gets only what a program needs to start, never the server's
// secrets.
function probeEnv() {
  const env = {};
  for (const key of ["PATH", "SystemRoot", "SYSTEMROOT", "TEMP", "TMP"]) {
    const value = process.env[key];
    if (typeof value === "string" && value) env[key] = value;
  }
  return env;
}

// Runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY, which proves the whole chain
// works (on macOS that includes node-pty's spawn-helper being executable).
function probe(pty) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let child;
    try {
      child = pty.spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", "process.exit(0)"], {
        name: "xterm-256color",
        cols: 80,
        rows: 24,
        cwd: os.tmpdir(),
        env: probeEnv(),
        encoding: "utf8"
      });
    } catch (error) {
      reject(error);
      return;
    }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      try {
        child.kill();
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
      reject(new Error("the terminal module did not answer in time"));
    }, PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS);
    child.onData(() => {}); // keep the output flowing so the exit is reported
    child.onExit(({ exitCode }) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(exitCode);
    });
  });
}

async function checkAvailability() {
  const loaded = await loadNodePty();
  if (!loaded.ok) return { ok: false, reason: PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON };
  try {
    if ((await probe(loaded.pty)) === 0) return { ok: true, reason: null };
  } catch {
    // reported below
  }
  probeFailedAt = Date.now();
  return { ok: false, reason: PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON };
}

// { ok: true, reason: null } or { ok: false, reason }. A module that does not
// load stays unavailable; a failed probe is tried again after 30 s, because
// it may have been a passing problem (for example too many processes).
export function ptyAvailable() {
  if (availability && probeFailedAt && Date.now() - probeFailedAt > PROBE_RETRY_MS) {
    availability = null;
    probeFailedAt = 0;
  }
  if (!availability) availability = checkAvailability();
  return availability;
}

function ptyUnavailableError() {
  const error = new Error(PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON);
  error.code = "pty_unavailable";
  return error;
}

function toSize(value, fallback, max) {
  const number = Number(value);
  return Number.isInteger(number) && number >= 1 && number <= max ? number : fallback;
}

function stringEnv(env) {
  const clean = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(env)) {
    if (typeof value === "string") clean[key] = value;
  }
  return clean;
}

// node-pty reports the signal as a number (0 when there was none).
function signalName(signal) {
  if (typeof signal === "string" && signal) return signal;
  if (!Number.isInteger(signal) || signal <= 0) return null;
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(os.constants.signals)) {
    if (value === signal) return name;
  }
  return String(signal);
}

function safeCall(listener, value) {
  try {
    listener(value);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Agent OS: a terminal listener failed:", error);
  }
}

export async function spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker = DEFAULT_TRACKER } = {}) {
  if (typeof command !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(command)) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs the full path of the program to run.");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(args) || args.some((arg) => typeof arg !== "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs its arguments as a list of strings.");
  }
  if (typeof cwd !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(cwd)) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs the full path of the folder to start in.");
  }
  if (!env || typeof env !== "object" || Array.isArray(env)) {
    // Without an env, node-pty would pass on process.env, which holds AGENT_OS_TOKEN.
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs an explicit environment; it never passes on the server's own.");
  }
  const loaded = await loadNodePty();
  if (!loaded.ok) throw ptyUnavailableError();

  const childEnv = stringEnv(env);
  let child;
  try {
    child = loaded.pty.spawn(command, [...args], {
      name: childEnv.TERM || "xterm-256color",
      cols: toSize(cols, 120, 500),
      rows: toSize(rows, 32, 200),
      cwd,
      env: childEnv,
      encoding: "utf8"
    });
  } catch (error) {
    const failure = new Error(`Could not start ${path.basename(command)}: ${error?.message || error}`);
    failure.code = "spawn_failed";
    throw failure;
  }

  const pid = child.pid;
  const dataListeners = new Set();
  const exitListeners = new Set();
  let early = [];
  let earlyChars = 0;
  let exitInfo = null;

  child.onData((chunk) => {
    if (dataListeners.size > 0) {
      for (const listener of [...dataListeners]) safeCall(listener, chunk);
      return;
    }
    if (early && earlyChars + chunk.length <= EARLY_OUTPUT_LIMIT) {
      early.push(chunk);
      earlyChars += chunk.length;
    }
  });

  // The first listener also receives what arrived before it (in order, just
  // after this call returns). Later listeners get only new output.
  function onData(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function") return () => {};
    dataListeners.add(listener);
    if (early) {
      const kept = early;
      early = null;
      if (kept.length) {
        queueMicrotask(() => {
          for (const chunk of kept) safeCall(listener, chunk);
        });
      }
    }
    return () => {
      dataListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  // A listener added after the end is still told, once.
  function onExit(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function") return () => {};
    if (exitInfo) {
      const info = exitInfo;
      queueMicrotask(() => safeCall(listener, info));
      return () => {};
    }
    exitListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      exitListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  child.onExit(({ exitCode, signal }) => {
    const name = signalName(signal);
    exitInfo = Object.freeze({
      exitCode: name ? null : Number.isInteger(exitCode) ? exitCode : null,
      signal: name
    });
    try {
      tracker.untrackPid(pid);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Agent OS: could not untrack a terminal program:", error);
    }
    const listeners = [...exitListeners];
    exitListeners.clear();
    for (const listener of listeners) safeCall(listener, exitInfo);
  });

  const handle = Object.freeze({
    pid,
    write(data) {
      if (exitInfo || typeof data !== "string" || data.length === 0) return;
      try {
        child.write(data);
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    resize(nextCols, nextRows) {
      const width = toSize(nextCols, 0, 500);
      const height = toSize(nextRows, 0, 200);
      if (exitInfo || !width || !height) return;
      try {
        child.resize(width, height);
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    kill(signal = "SIGTERM") {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        // node-pty throws when a signal is named on Windows.
        if (process.platform === "win32") child.kill();
        else child.kill(signal);
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
    },
    pause() {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        child.pause();
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    resume() {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        child.resume();
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    onData,
    onExit
  });

  try {
    // Quit and Hold to stop all (killAllTracked) reach this program from now on.
    tracker.trackPid(pid, onExit);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Agent OS: could not track a terminal program:", error);
  }
  return handle;
}
```

```js
// The session mirror: the server's headless copy of a session's screen.
// Snapshot and modes for reattach, the three standard terminal questions
// answered only while no writer is attached, raw alerts, counted output for
// the 20 s activity rule, and what counts as user input. No process runs here:
// the tests write terminal output straight into the mirror.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import xtermHeadless from "@xterm/headless";
import { ALERT_RAW_LIMIT, COUNTED_CHECK_MS, createMirror, isUserInput } from "../server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js";

// @xterm/headless is a CommonJS bundle: its classes sit on the default export.
const { Terminal } = xtermHeadless;
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

const DEFAULT_MODES = {
  altScreen: false,
  bracketedPaste: false,
  mouseTracking: "none",
  mouseEncoding: "default",
  focusReporting: false,
  cursorKeysApp: false,
  kittyFlags: 0
};

// Waits until everything written so far is on the mirror's screen and a
// counted-output check has had time to run.
async function settle(mirror) {
  await mirror.snapshot();
  await sleep(COUNTED_CHECK_MS * 2 + 100);
}

// Writes a snapshot into a fresh terminal of the same size, the way a browser
// terminal restores one, and reads the screen back.
async function replay(snapshot) {
  const term = new Terminal({ cols: snapshot.cols, rows: snapshot.rows, logLevel: "off" });
  await new Promise((resolve) => term.write(snapshot.data, resolve));
  const buffer = term.buffer.active;
  const lines = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < term.rows; y += 1) lines.push(buffer.getLine(buffer.baseY + y)?.translateToString(true) ?? "");
  const result = { lines, cursor: [buffer.cursorX, buffer.cursorY], screen: buffer.type };
  term.dispose();
  return result;
}

test("a snapshot restores the screen, the cursor and the alternate screen in a fresh terminal", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    mirror.write("\x1b[1mbold\x1b[0m plain\r\nsecond line\r\n\x1b[32mgreen\x1b[0m");
    const normal = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(normal.cols, 40);
    assert.equal(normal.rows, 10);
    const restored = await replay(normal);
    assert.deepEqual(restored.lines.slice(0, 3), ["bold plain", "second line", "green"]);
    assert.deepEqual(restored.cursor, [5, 2]);
    assert.equal(restored.screen, "normal");

    mirror.write("\x1b[?1049h\x1b[Hin the alt screen");
    const alt = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(alt.modes.altScreen, true);
    const restoredAlt = await replay(alt);
    assert.equal(restoredAlt.screen, "alternate");
    assert.equal(restoredAlt.lines[0], "in the alt screen");
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("a snapshot covers exactly the output written before it was asked for, never later output", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    mirror.write("first");
    const pending = mirror.snapshot();
    mirror.write("\r\nsecond"); // written after the request: goes to the window as live output instead
    const early = await replay(await pending);
    assert.deepEqual(early.lines.slice(0, 2), ["first", ""]);
    const later = await replay(await mirror.snapshot());
    assert.deepEqual(later.lines.slice(0, 2), ["first", "second"]);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

    const on = await mirror.snapshot();
```
