#### Notes

1. **`claude agents --json` output is an assumption (owner item, spike S0).** The spec names the commands but no output format, and nothing in the repo has seen them. `findBackgroundAgent` accepts an array, `{ agents: [...] }` or `{ sessions: [...] }`, entries whose `kind` or `type` is "background", matched by `id`/`sessionId`/`session_id` against the session's `agentSessionId` or by `pid`, and it never passes an id that starts with `-` to `claude stop`. Anything it does not recognise means "not found", and Stop goes straight to the kill. So a Claude Code task moved with `/bg` that this parser cannot find may keep running after Stop (the Help page says so, ruling R24). The S0 spike should record the real output so the parser can be tightened.
2. **OpenClaw's Gateway abort waits for spike S5.** Until then its soft stop makes no CLI call and Stop answers `OPENCLAW_STOP_NOTE`. When S5 confirms the abort command, it goes into `soft-stop.js` inside the same 2 s limit, and these change with it: the note, Task U3's `stopResultNote` (it repeats the rule for a tab opened later, because the note is not kept in meta.json) and Task S10's gateway tripwire assertion (it must narrow to `start`, `stop` and `restart`, never be dropped).
3. **A process that outlives the kill.** Stop then answers after a bounded wait (1 s after the kill) with the session's real status, not "exited"; the page follows the next state frame, and the record still says "stopped by you" when the process ends.
4. **Edges the quit leaves to recovery.** A session that starts after the quit began is not in `shutdownAll`'s list: Task S1's kill sweep ends it (its PTY pid is tracked) and the next start's recovery marks it "ended (Agent OS quit)". A Stop pressed while a Resume of the same session is still starting answers the ended summary.
5. **Two 7 s limits on purpose.** `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS` repeats `shutdown.js`'s `SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS`, because `shutdownAll` is also called directly (Task S10's test, these tests) and must end by itself. On a hang, `shutdown.js` logs its "took longer than 7000 ms" line a few milliseconds before this guard fires; both end the wait.
6. **`soft-stop.js` is tested on its own** (it is in the contract's Stop and quit section). The end-to-end quit through a real server (SIGTERM and the desktop's stdin line, ruling R18) is Task S8's test; this task proves the same order with fakes and real PTYs.

### Task S8: REST routes, local-only guard, server wiring, startup recovery

The session engine (S1-S7) can create, stop and resume terminals, but nothing outside the server can reach it yet. This task adds the HTTP surface in `server/runtime/sessions/routes.js`: exactly the routes in the spec's `routes.js` row, the fixed paths (`folders`, `settings`, `quit-check`) registered before `/:id`, and every `:id` checked against `SESSION_ID_RE` before the manager or the disk is touched (Q39). Every refusal is answered the one way ruling R4 sets: a `sessionError` with `res.status(err.status).json(errorBody(err))`, a brain error with the builders' own `builderErrorResponse`, and anything else with a plain 500 that names no file. `POST /api/sessions` hands the agent and folder to `manager.create`, which checks the agent, Look only, the terminal module and the folder policy, in that order; its folder refusal comes back as 400 `{ error: "folder_refused", code, message }`, so the dialog can show the policy's own sentence (Q14). Sessions exist only in local mode, so `local-session.js` exports `isLocalMode()` and a `requireLocalMode` middleware that answers 404 `not_available` in the public demo and in the admin-token public mode.

`server/index.js` mounts both routers behind that guard. It runs `recoverStaleSessions()` and `enforceRecordingCap()` before `app.listen`, each in its own try/catch, so no request ever sees a session still marked live from a previous run (Q13, ruling R11). In local mode only, it starts reading the login-shell environment in the background after `AGENT_OS_READY`, so start-up never waits for it (Q23). It keeps the keys Agent OS's own `.env` file added out of the login shell sessions read their environment from (`excludeFromSessionEnv`, ruling R13), and reads its port from `AGENT_OS_PORT` first (the name the desktop shell uses, Task D1), so the server's own port never reaches an agent.

A real-server test proves the quit end to end (ruling R18): with a live fake Claude Code whose `claude agents --json` never answers, the desktop's stdin line or SIGTERM writes "ended (Agent OS quit)" into meta.json before the agent gets any signal, and the server is gone within 8 s. Because every local-mode server now reads its login shell after READY, the older test files that start a server set `SHELL` to Task W1's stand-in login shell (ruling R15, decision Q1c). The WebSocket is Task S9.

```js
const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function waitFor(check, timeoutMs = 10000, what = "a condition") {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const value = await check();
    if (value) return value;
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
    await delay(50);
  }
}

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// A temp HOME, a separate AGENT_OS_HOME inside it, local mode, and W1's
// stand-in login shell (R15). HOME is the realpath of the temp folder: on
// macOS os.tmpdir() sits behind a symlink.
async function withSessionsEnv(fn, extra = {}) {
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-sessions-routes-")));
  const agentOsHome = path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os");
  await mkdir(agentOsHome, { recursive: true });
  try {
    return await withEnv(
      {
        ...MODE_KEYS,
        HOME: home,
        USERPROFILE: home,
        AGENT_OS_HOME: agentOsHome,
        HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined,
        AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: path.join(home, ".agent-os"),
        HERMES_HOME: undefined,
        SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
        ...extra
      },
      async () => {
        assert.equal(os.homedir(), home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
        return fn({ home, agentOsHome });
      }
    );
  } finally {
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

      calls.push(["create", input]);
      return summary(NEW_ID, { agentId: input.agentId, status: "starting" });
    },
    async get(id) {
      calls.push(["get", id]);
      if (id === KNOWN_ID) return summary(id);
      throw sessionError(404, "unknown_session", "That session doesn't exist anymore.");
    },
    async stop(id, options) {
      calls.push(["stop", id, options]);
      if (id !== KNOWN_ID) throw sessionError(404, "unknown_session", "That session doesn't exist anymore.");
      return { ...summary(id, { status: "exited", endedBy: "stop", endedAt: "2026-10-14T10:05:00.000Z" }), note: null };
    },
    async resume(id) {
      calls.push(["resume", id]);
      return summary(id, { status: "starting" });
    },
    async dismiss(id) {
      calls.push(["dismiss", id]);
      return summary(id, { dismissed: true });
    },
    async quitCheck() {
      calls.push(["quitCheck"]);
      return { live: [{ id: KNOWN_ID, title: "Claude Code · project", kind: "agent" }] };
    },
    // Synchronous like the real one (ruling R8). Not recorded in `calls`: the
    // recordings routes ask it, and the fixed-path test counts only quitCheck.
    isLive(id) {
      return id === KNOWN_ID;
    }
  };
  return { manager, calls };
}

// The two routers on a real port, mounted the way server/index.js mounts them.
async function withSessionsApp(manager, fn) {
  const app = express();
  app.use(express.json());
  app.use("/api/sessions", requireLocalMode, createSessionsRouter({ manager }));
  app.use("/api/recordings", requireLocalMode, createRecordingsRouter({ manager }));
  app.use((error, _req, res, _next) => res.status(500).json({ error: "test_handler", message: error.message }));
  const server = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    const listening = app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => resolve(listening));
  });
  const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`;
  const api = async (method, url, body) => {
    const response = await fetch(`${base}${url}`, {
      method,
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body)
    });
    const text = await response.text();
    let json = null;
    try {
      json = JSON.parse(text);
    } catch {
      json = null;
    }
    return { status: response.status, headers: response.headers, json, text };
  };
  try {
    return await fn(api);
  } finally {
    server.closeAllConnections?.();
    await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(resolve));
  }
}

const EVERY_ROUTE = [
  ["GET", "/api/sessions"],

  ["GET", `/api/sessions/${KNOWN_ID}/recording`],

];

test("POST /api/sessions hands the agent and folder to the manager and answers its refusals with their own status", async () => {
  await withSessionsEnv(async () => {
    const { manager, calls } = stubManager();
    manager.create = async (input) => {
      calls.push(["create", input]);
      if (input.folder === "/Users/you") {
        throw sessionError(400, "folder_refused", "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.", {
          code: "is_home"
        });
      }
      if (input.agentId === "bash") {
        throw sessionError(400, "unknown_agent", "Agent OS can't start a session for that agent.");
      }
      if (input.folder === "/Users/you/needs-key") {
        throw brainError("openrouter_key_missing", "Add your OpenRouter key in Setup, then try again.");
      }
      return summary(NEW_ID, { agentId: input.agentId, status: "starting" });
    };
    await withSessionsApp(manager, async (api) => {
      const home = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "claude", folder: "/Users/you" });
      assert.equal(home.status, 400);
      assert.deepEqual(home.json, {
        error: "folder_refused",
        message: "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.",
        code: "is_home"
      });

      const agent = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "bash", folder: "/Users/you/project" });
      assert.equal(agent.status, 400);
      assert.deepEqual(agent.json, { error: "unknown_agent", message: "Agent OS can't start a session for that agent." });

      const brain = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "claude", folder: "/Users/you/needs-key" });
      assert.equal(brain.status, 409, "a brain error keeps the status builderErrorResponse gives it");
      assert.equal(brain.json.error, "openrouter_key_missing");

      const created = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "claude", folder: "/Users/you/project" });
      assert.equal(created.status, 201);
      assert.equal(created.json.id, NEW_ID);
      assert.deepEqual(calls.at(-1), ["create", { agentId: "claude", folder: "/Users/you/project" }]);

      // The page cannot choose the kind, the program, its argv, its environment
      // or its working folder: only the agent and folder reach the manager
      // (spec: an update session is never created by POST /api/sessions; the
      // agent's path comes from detection and its argv from H3).
      const extra = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", {
        agentId: "claude",
        folder: "/Users/you/project",
        kind: "update",
        command: "/bin/sh",
        args: ["-c", "id"],
        env: { CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB: "1" },
        cwd: "/"
      });
      assert.equal(extra.status, 201);
      assert.deepEqual(
        calls.at(-1),
        ["create", { agentId: "claude", folder: "/Users/you/project" }],
        "only the agent and folder reach the manager: no kind, command, argv, env or cwd from the page"
      );

      // OpenClaw picks its own folder for now: the dialog sends null.
      const openclaw = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "openclaw", folder: null });
      assert.equal(openclaw.status, 201);
      assert.deepEqual(calls.at(-1), ["create", { agentId: "openclaw", folder: null }]);
    });
  });
});

// A session folder the way Tasks S5 and S6 leave it on disk: meta.json (it
// says "exited") and, unless `cast` is false, a one-event recording.
async function writeSessionFixture(agentOsHome, id, { cast = true } = {}) {
  const dir = path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", id);
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(
    path.join(dir, "meta.json"),
    JSON.stringify({
      version: 1,
      id,
      kind: "agent",
      agentId: "claude",
      agentLabel: "Claude Code",
      folder: "/Users/you/project",
      folderName: "project",
      folderShown: true,
      status: "exited",
      createdAt: "2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z",
      startedAt: "2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z",
      endedAt: "2026-10-14T10:05:00.000Z",
      exitCode: 0,
      signal: null,
      endedBy: null,
      dismissed: false
    })
  );
  if (cast) {
    await writeFile(
      path.join(dir, "screen.cast"),
      `${JSON.stringify({ version: 2, width: 120, height: 32, timestamp: 1 })}\n[0.1,"o","hi"]\n`
    );
  }
  return dir;
}

  await withSessionsEnv(async ({ agentOsHome }) => {
    const dir = path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", KNOWN_ID);

    const newerHeader = JSON.stringify({ version: 2, width: 120, height: 32, timestamp: 2 });

      assert.equal(onlyCurrent.status, 200);

      assert.equal(onlyCurrent.text, `${newerHeader}\n[0.5,"o","new"]\n`);

      await writeFile(path.join(dir, "screen.prev.cast"), `${olderHeader}\n[0.1,"o","old"]\n`);

      const noFiles = await api("GET", `/api/sessions/${noRecordingId}/recording`);
      assert.equal(noFiles.status, 404);
      assert.deepEqual(noFiles.json, { error: "recording_missing", message: "That recording doesn't exist anymore." });

      await stat(path.join(endedDir, "meta.json")); // the session stays, with Resume

      const again = await api("DELETE", `/api/sessions/${endedId}/recording`);

      assert.equal(again.json.error, "recording_missing");

});
```

```js
// Local mode: neither the public demo (DEMO_PUBLIC=1) nor the admin-token
// public mode (HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 or HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE=1).
// Sessions (real agent terminals) exist only here.
export function isLocalMode() {
  return !isDemoPublic() && !authRequired();
}

// Every sessions and recordings address answers as if it did not exist
// outside local mode (spec Security 1). The sessions WebSocket makes the same
// check itself (server/runtime/sessions/ws.js), because Express middleware
// never runs for an upgrade request.
export function requireLocalMode(_req, res, next) {
  if (!isLocalMode()) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "not_available" });
    return;
  }
  next();
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the routes.** Create `server/runtime/sessions/routes.js`:

```js
// HTTP surface for sessions (SP3): each agent's own terminal, running in a
// folder the person picked. Like the agents and Team Room routers, nothing
// here takes a command, an argument or a binary path from the request: the
// body carries an agent id and a folder, and the manager checks both (the
// fixed agent list and the folder policy, D12) before anything starts. Every
// :id is checked with isSessionId (SESSION_ID_RE) before anything reads the
// disk or asks the manager (planning decision Q39). server/index.js mounts
// both routers behind requireLocalMode: outside local mode none of these
// addresses exist.
import express from "express";
import { builderErrorResponse } from "../builders/resolve.js";
import { errorBody, isSessionId } from "./errors.js";
import { recentSessionFolders } from "./folders.js";
import { getSessionManager } from "./manager.js";
import { ptyAvailable } from "./pty-host.js";
import { deleteRecording, listRecordings, openRecording, recordingsRemovedByCap } from "./recorder.js";
import { readSessionSettings, writeSessionSettings } from "./settings.js";
import { getLoginShellEnv } from "./shell-env.js";

const MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS = 8;
const UNKNOWN_SESSION = { error: "unknown_session", message: "That session doesn't exist anymore." };
const INTERNAL_ERROR = { error: "internal_error", message: "Something went wrong with sessions. Try again." };

// Express 4 does not catch a rejected promise from a handler, so every handler
// goes through this.
function handle(fn) {
  return (req, res) => {
    Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => fn(req, res))
      .catch((error) => sendError(error, res));
  };
}

// A sessionError (errors.js) carries its own HTTP status and code.
function isSessionError(error) {
  return Number.isInteger(error?.status) && typeof error?.code === "string";
}

// Ruling R4: a sessionError is answered with its own status and
// errorBody(err), { error, message, ...extra } (a refused folder carries the
// policy's `code`, decision Q14). A brain error from the Brain settings has
// no status of its own and gets the one the builders routes give it. Anything
// else is a plain 500 that never echoes its message, which could name a file.
function sendError(error, res) {
  if (res.headersSent) {
    res.destroy();
    return;
  }
  if (isSessionError(error)) {
    res.status(error.status).json(errorBody(error));
    return;
  }
  const brain = builderErrorResponse(error);
  if (brain) {
    res.status(brain.status).json(brain.body);
    return;
  }
  console.error(error);
  res.status(500).json(INTERNAL_ERROR);
}

// Which sessions run right now: the manager's own live view (ruling R8), in
// which a session still closing its recording counts as live (meta.json can
// already say "exited" by then, and during a quit). When the manager cannot
// say, the recorder falls back to meta.json.
function liveCheck(manager) {
  return typeof manager.isLive === "function" ? (id) => manager.isLive(id) : undefined;
}

function drainedOrClosed(res) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const done = () => {
      res.off("drain", done);
      res.off("close", done);
      resolve();
    };
    res.on("drain", done);
    res.on("close", done);
  });
}

// Planning decision Q26, as the recorder streams it: one header line, the
// older segment's events, then the newer segment's events. openRecording
// throws its 404 before anything is sent; a client that goes away stops the
// read.
async function streamRecording(id, res) {
  const { lines } = await openRecording(id);
  res.status(200);
  res.setHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-asciicast");
  res.setHeader("Cache-Control", "no-store");
  for await (const line of lines) {
    if (res.destroyed) break;
    if (!res.write(line)) await drainedOrClosed(res);
  }
  res.end();
}

export function createSessionsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {}) {
  // Case sensitive like the app ("/api/sessions/FOLDERS" is not the folders
  // address; as an id it fails SESSION_ID_RE).
  const router = express.Router({ caseSensitive: true });

  // The login-shell environment is read in the background (it can take up to
  // 10 s; planning decision Q23). The list never waits for it: it reports the
  // notice once it is known, and null until then.
  let environmentNotice = null;
  function followLoginShellEnv() {
    Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => getLoginShellEnv())
      .then((result) => {
        environmentNotice = typeof result?.notice === "string" ? result.notice : null;
      })
      .catch(() => {});
  }

  router.param("id", (_req, res, next, id) => {
    if (!isSessionId(id)) {
      res.status(404).json(UNKNOWN_SESSION);
      return;
    }
    next();
  });

  router.get(
    "/",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      followLoginShellEnv();
      const includeUpdate = req.query.kind === "all";
      const [sessions, pty] = await Promise.all([manager.list({ includeUpdate }), ptyAvailable()]);
      const ptyOk = pty?.ok === true;
      res.json({
        sessions,
        environmentNotice,
        pty: { ok: ptyOk, reason: ptyOk ? null : (pty?.reason ?? null) },
        maxLive: MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS
      });
    })
  );

  // Agent sessions only: the update kind is started by the update service
  // through the manager, never over HTTP. The manager checks the agent, Look
  // only, the terminal module and the folder (a typed one in the browser, a
  // picked one in the desktop app), in that order; its folder refusal
  // carries the policy's code (Q14).
  router.post(
    "/",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      const body = req.body && typeof req.body === "object" && !Array.isArray(req.body) ? req.body : {};
      const session = await manager.create({ agentId: body.agentId, folder: body.folder });
      res.status(201).json(session);
    })
  );

  // Fixed paths first, so none of them is ever taken for an :id.
  router.get(
    "/folders",
    handle(async (_req, res) => {
      res.json({ folders: await recentSessionFolders() });
    })
  );

  router.get(
    "/settings",
    handle(async (_req, res) => {
      res.json(await readSessionSettings());
    })
  );

  // settings.js accepts only { claudeFullscreen: true | false }; anything
  // else is its 400 invalid_settings, and nothing is written.
  router.put(
    "/settings",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await writeSessionSettings(req.body));
    })
  );

  router.post(
    "/quit-check",
    handle(async (_req, res) => {
      res.json(await manager.quitCheck());
    })
  );

  router.get(
    "/:id",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await manager.get(req.params.id));
    })
  );

  // The Stop sequence's answer as it is (Task S7): the summary plus `note`
  // (OpenClaw's honest note, or null), with no wrapper. Stopping a session
  // that has already ended answers its unchanged summary.
  router.post(
    "/:id/stop",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await manager.stop(req.params.id, { by: "stop" }));
    })
  );

  router.post(
    "/:id/resume",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await manager.resume(req.params.id));
    })
  );

  router.post(
    "/:id/dismiss",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await manager.dismiss(req.params.id));
    })
  );

  router.get(
    "/:id/recording",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      await streamRecording(req.params.id, res);
    })
  );

  router.delete(
    "/:id/recording",
    handle(async (req, res) => {
      res.json(await deleteRecording(req.params.id, { isLive: liveCheck(manager) }));
    })
  );

  return router;
}

// Session recordings (Runs, "Session recordings" tab). The list is read from
// disk by recorder.js, so it also holds sessions from earlier runs of the
// server; which ones are live comes from the manager. `removedByCap` counts
// the recordings the 1 GB cap deleted since this server started (planning
// decision Q38).
export function createRecordingsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {}) {
  const router = express.Router({ caseSensitive: true });
  router.get(
    "/",
    handle(async (_req, res) => {
      const recordings = await listRecordings({ isLive: liveCheck(manager) });
      res.json({ recordings, removedByCap: recordingsRemovedByCap() });
    })
  );
  return router;
}
```

```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Child process: the real server with Task W1's six fake agents
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// A temp HOME (its realpath) with a "project" folder and, on POSIX, W1's six
// fake agents in <home>/fake-bin (all six names, ruling R16). The fakes answer
// the detection probes (--version, --help, auth status) and `claude agents
// --json` at once, and otherwise run a small terminal program that prints
// FAKE_ARGV and a prompt. They live under os.tmpdir(), which the
// no-real-agents watcher allows.
async function makeHome(prefix) {
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix)));
  await mkdir(path.join(home, "project"), { recursive: true });
  if (!isWindows) await makeFakeAgentBin(path.join(home, "fake-bin"));
  return home;
}

async function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const probe = net.createServer();
    probe.once("error", reject);
    probe.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const { port } = probe.address();
      probe.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

// Never passed on to the server unless a test sets one on purpose.
// AGENT_OS_PORT is the desktop shell's port name, which the server reads
// before PORT.
const CLEARED_KEYS = [
  "HERMES_HOME",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME",
  // Detection searches it before PATH, so it could find a real agent (R16).
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS",
  "DEMO_PUBLIC",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_ADMIN_TOKEN",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_ENABLE_EXEC",
  "AGENT_OS_LIVE_CHAT",
  "AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN",
  "AGENT_OS_PACKAGED",
  "AGENT_OS_PORT",
  "AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN",
  "NODE_ENV",
  "CLAUDECODE",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT"
];

function serverEnv(home, port, extra = {}) {
  const env = {
    ...process.env,
    PORT: String(port),
    HOST: "127.0.0.1",
    HOME: home,
    USERPROFILE: home,
    AGENT_OS_HOME: path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: path.join(home, ".agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_TOKEN: TOKEN,
    HERMES_AGENT_OS_SCHEDULER: "0",
    // The login shell sessions read their environment from: W1's stand-in
    // (ruling R15), which keeps the PATH below. Never the developer's own
    // shell setup, and never a real login sh either: on macOS it runs
    // path_helper, which puts /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin (where real
    // agents live) on the sessions' PATH.
    SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
    // The six fakes first, then system folders only (ruling R16; not Node's
    // own folder, which can hold real agents).
    ...(isWindows ? {} : { PATH: [path.join(home, "fake-bin"), ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter) })
  };
  for (const key of CLEARED_KEYS) {
    if (!(key in extra)) delete env[key];
  }
  return { ...env, ...extra };
}

// `stdin: "pipe"` keeps the server's stdin open, the way the desktop shell
// starts it (Q4); the stdin quit test writes the shutdown line into it.
async function startServer(home, extra = {}, { stdin = "ignore" } = {}) {
  const port = await freePort();
  const startedAt = Date.now();
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["server/index.js"], {
    cwd: root,
    env: serverEnv(home, port, extra),
    stdio: [stdin, "pipe", "pipe"]
  });
  // A write into a server that has just exited must not crash the test run.
  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
  const logs = { text: "" };
  child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    logs.text += chunk;
  });
  child.stderr.on("data", (chunk) => {
    logs.text += chunk;
  });
  const deadline = Date.now() + 20000;
  while (!/AGENT_OS_READY:\d+/.test(logs.text)) {
    if (child.exitCode != null) throw new Error(`server exited early (${child.exitCode}):\n${logs.text.slice(-2000)}`);
    if (Date.now() > deadline) {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      throw new Error(`server did not start:\n${logs.text.slice(-2000)}`);
    }
    await delay(25);
  }
  return { child, port, logs, readyAfterMs: Date.now() - startedAt };
}

// SIGTERM, then up to 10 s (the server's own hard exit is 8 s), then SIGKILL.
async function stopServer(server) {
  const { child } = server;
  if (child.exitCode != null || child.signalCode != null) return;
  child.kill("SIGTERM");
  await new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      resolve();
    }, 10000);
    child.once("exit", () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve();
    });
  });
}

async function api(port, method, url, body) {
  const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${url}`, {
    method,
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "x-agent-os-token": TOKEN },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body)
  });
  const text = await response.text();
  let json = null;
  try {
    json = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    json = null;
  }
  return { status: response.status, headers: response.headers, json, text };
}

// Resolves { code, signal } when the child exits, or null after ms.
function exitWithin(child, ms) {
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) {
    return Promise.resolve({ code: child.exitCode, signal: child.signalCode });
  }
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), ms);
    child.once("exit", (code, signal) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code, signal });
    });
  });
}

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    return error.code === "EPERM";
  }
}

// W1's fake writes one JSON object per line into FAKE_AGENT_LOG.
async function readFakeLog(file) {
  let text = "";
  try {
    text = await readFile(file, "utf8");
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
  const entries = [];
  for (const line of text.split("\n")) {
    if (!line.trim()) continue;
    try {
      entries.push(JSON.parse(line));
    } catch {
      // a line still being written; the next read has it
    }
  }
  return entries;
}

test("wiring: sessions mount behind requireLocalMode, recovery and the cap run before listen, the login shell after READY in local mode, .env keys and PORT stay out of sessions", async () => {
  const source = await readFile(path.join(root, "server", "index.js"), "utf8");
  const at = (needle) => {
    const index = source.indexOf(needle);
    assert.notEqual(index, -1, `server/index.js should contain: ${needle}`);
    return index;
  };
  const sessionsMount = at(
    'app.use("/api/sessions", requireLocalMode, createSessionsRouter({ manager: sessionManager }));'
  );
  const recordingsMount = at(
    'app.use("/api/recordings", requireLocalMode, createRecordingsRouter({ manager: sessionManager }));'
  );
  const pageFallback = at("app.use(express.static(dist));");
  const recovery = at("await sessionManager.recoverStaleSessions();");
  const cap = at("await enforceRecordingCap();");
  const listen = at("const server = app.listen(");
  const ready = at("console.log(`AGENT_OS_READY:${port}`);");
  const loginShell = at("if (isLocalMode()) getLoginShellEnv().catch(");
  assert.ok(sessionsMount < pageFallback && recordingsMount < pageFallback, "mounted before the page fallback");
  assert.ok(recovery < listen && cap < listen, "recovery and the cap run before the server listens");
  assert.ok(loginShell > ready, "the login shell starts only after READY");
  assert.ok(
    at("excludeFromSessionEnv(envFile.applied)") > at("loadLocalEnv("),
    "the keys the local .env file added are kept out of sessions right after it is loaded"
  );
  assert.match(
    source,
    /process\.env\.AGENT_OS_PORT \?\? process\.env\.PORT/,
    "the port comes from AGENT_OS_PORT first (the desktop shell), then PORT"
  );
});

});

      const ended = await waitFor(

  // The SP3 "done when" quit item, end to end through the real server (ruling
  // R18): a live session, then a quit, once through the desktop shell's stdin
  // line (with AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1 and a piped stdin, the way Task D1
  // starts the server) and once through SIGTERM. When SIGTERM reaches the
  // agent, the fake copies its session's meta.json into its log, which proves
  // "ended (Agent OS quit)" was written before any signal. `claude agents
  // --json` (the soft stop) never answers in mode agents-hang, and the server
  // must still be gone within its 8 s hard exit.
  for (const [how, extra, stdin, quit] of [
    [
      "the desktop's stdin line",
      { AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN: "1" },
      "pipe",
      (child) => child.stdin.write("AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n")
    ],
    ["SIGTERM", {}, "ignore", (child) => child.kill("SIGTERM")]
  ]) {
    test(`quit with a live session (${how}): meta.json says quit before the agent gets a signal, and the server exits within 8 s`, async () => {
      const home = await makeHome("agent-os-sessions-quit-");
      const agentOsHome = path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os");
      const fakeLog = path.join(home, "fake.log");
      const server = await startServer(
        home,
        {
          ...extra,
          FAKE_AGENT_MODE: "agents-hang",
          FAKE_AGENT_LOG: fakeLog,
          // The fake fills in its own AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID (the id is only
          // known after the session is created).
          FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM: path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", "{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}", "meta.json")
        },
        { stdin }
      );
      const leftovers = [];
      try {
        assert.equal((await api(server.port, "POST", "/api/admin/execution-gate", { enabled: true, confirm: true })).status, 200);
        const created = await api(server.port, "POST", "/api/sessions", {
          agentId: "claude",
          folder: path.join(home, "project")
        });
        assert.equal(created.status, 201, created.text);
        const id = created.json.id;
        await waitFor(
          async () => (await api(server.port, "GET", `/api/sessions/${id}`)).json?.status === "live",
          15000,
          "the session to go live"
        );
        const started = await waitFor(
          async () => (await readFakeLog(fakeLog)).find((entry) => entry.event === "start"),
          5000,
          "the fake's start entry"
        );
        const agentPid = started.pid;
        leftovers.push(agentPid);
        assert.ok(isAlive(agentPid), "the agent runs before the quit");

        const quitAt = Date.now();
        const exited = exitWithin(server.child, 8000);
        quit(server.child);
        const exit = await exited;
        assert.ok(exit, `the server did not exit within 8 s:\n${server.logs.text.slice(-2000)}`);
        assert.equal(exit.code, 0, server.logs.text.slice(-2000));
        assert.ok(Date.now() - quitAt < 8000, `the quit took ${Date.now() - quitAt} ms`);

        const entries = await readFakeLog(fakeLog);
        const term = entries.find((entry) => entry.event === "sigterm" && entry.pid === agentPid);
        assert.ok(term, `the agent got SIGTERM; the fake's log: ${JSON.stringify(entries)}`);
        assert.equal(term.snapshotError, undefined, "meta.json was readable when SIGTERM arrived");
        const snapshot = JSON.parse(term.snapshot);
        assert.equal(snapshot.id, id);
        assert.equal(snapshot.status, "exited", "meta.json said ended before the agent got any signal");
        assert.equal(snapshot.endedBy, "quit");

        const onDisk = JSON.parse(await readFile(path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", id, "meta.json"), "utf8"));
        assert.equal(onDisk.status, "exited");
        assert.equal(onDisk.endedBy, "quit");

        await waitFor(() => !isAlive(agentPid), 3000, "the agent's process to be gone");
        // The soft stop's `claude agents --json` never answered; its 2 s limit ended it.
        const asked = entries.find((entry) => entry.event === "agents");
        assert.ok(asked, "the soft stop asked claude agents --json");
        leftovers.push(asked.pid);
        await waitFor(() => !isAlive(asked.pid), 3000, "the hung claude agents call to be gone");
      } finally {
        for (const pid of leftovers) {
          if (!isAlive(pid)) continue;
          try {
            process.kill(pid, "SIGKILL");
          } catch {
            // already gone
          }
        }
        await stopServer(server);
        await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
      }
    });
  }
});
```

### Task S9: WebSocket endpoint: upgrade security, writer/viewer protocol, back-pressure

A session's terminal reaches the page over one WebSocket per window: `/api/sessions/:id/attach`. Express middleware never runs for an upgrade request, so the existing gate does not protect it, and `originCheckMiddleware` must not be reused (it lets GET and a missing Origin through and compares only the hostname, so any local port would pass). This task adds `server/runtime/sessions/ws.js` with its own check of every upgrade (spec Security 1): local mode only; the path, checked lower-cased, exactly `/api/sessions/<id>/attach` with no query string (Q40); an allowed Host that carries the port this server is bound to; an Origin that is exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://localhost:<port>` (the Vite dev page only with `AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1`, never in a production or packaged run); the `agent_os_session_<port>` cookie compared in constant time; and a session that still runs (an unknown or ended session is refused like every other failure, Q40). Any failure writes 403 and destroys the socket. After the upgrade, the session manager (Tasks S6 and S7) owns the rules (which window is the writer, `seq` and `ack`, pausing the terminal, closing a window 4 MB behind or still lagging after the terminal has been paused for 10 s) and sends every frame itself, the snapshot first; `ws.js` only checks and translates frames, and enforces the WebSocket's own limits (`maxPayload` 1 MB, 64 KB per raw client frame). The Vite dev proxy gains `ws: true`, and `npm run dev` sets `AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1` through a three-line launcher, so it works in every operating system's shell. The tests drive the real server with the `ws` client, Task W1's six fake agents and its stand-in login shell: every Security 1 case, then each protocol rule from the SP3 "done when" list and the server half of Review Focus items 2 and 3 (one input frame over 64 KB; the same session in two windows, one of them slow or asleep), end to end.

**Files:**
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/ws.js`
- Create: `scripts/dev-server.mjs`
- Modify: `server/index.js`: one import after `import { excludeFromSessionEnv, getLoginShellEnv } from "./runtime/sessions/shell-env.js";` (added by Task S8), and one call between the end of the `app.listen(...)` block and `installShutdownHandlers(server);` (line 1858 today; Task S8's additions move it further down).
- Modify: `vite.config.ts:15-20` (the `server.proxy` entry)
- Modify: `package.json:10` (the `dev` script)
- Test: `test/sessions-ws.test.js` (new)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - `server/runtime/local-session.js` (existing, plus Task S8): `isLocalMode()` (Task S8 exports it), `parseHostHeader(value)` (lower-cased hostname, port dropped), `isAllowedHost(hostname)`, `cookieNameFor(port)` → `"agent_os_session_<port>"`, `sessionToken`.
  - `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js` (Task S3, the only home of the id pattern, R4): `isSessionId(value)` (true only for a lower-case `crypto.randomUUID()` value, `SESSION_ID_RE`).
  - `server/runtime/sessions/manager.js` (Tasks S6 and S7): `PAUSE_LAG_BYTES` (524288) and `PAUSED_DROP_MS` (10000), tests only; `get(id)` → `Promise<SessionSummary>` (throws a 404 `unknown_session` sessionError for an unknown id); `attach(id, { id, send(frame), close(reason) })` → `Promise<{ snapshot, detach() }>`: the manager itself sends `{t:"snapshot", data, cols, rows, modes}`, then `{t:"state", status, …}`, then `{t:"out", seq, d}` and `{t:"alert", raw}` frames, calls `close("too_far_behind")` (more than 4 MB behind, or still more than 512 KB behind once the terminal has been paused for `PAUSED_DROP_MS`, R10 and decision Q41) or `close("session_ended")`, and throws a 409 `session_ended` sessionError for an ended session. `focus(id, attachmentId)`, `write(id, attachmentId, data)`, `resize(id, attachmentId, cols, rows)`, `ack(id, attachmentId, seq)` are synchronous and return `boolean` (false = dropped). The manager enforces the writer, the resize bounds, the 64 KB `in` limit in UTF-8 bytes, `seq` as the running UTF-8 byte count from 0 per window, and the flow rules. When the process ends it sends `{t:"state", status: "exited", exitCode, signal, endedBy}` and then closes every window with `"session_ended"`; Task S7's Stop sets `endedBy: "stop"`. Task S4's mirror gives `alert` frames `raw` as `"bel"` or `"<osc number>;<payload>"`.
  - `server/index.js` (Task S8): the module-scope `const sessionManager = getSessionManager();`, the `port` variable (the real bound port once listening), the import line `import { excludeFromSessionEnv, getLoginShellEnv } from "./runtime/sessions/shell-env.js";`, and `installShutdownHandlers(server);` right after the `app.listen(...)` block. REST (Task S8): `POST /api/admin/execution-gate`, `POST /api/sessions` (201 `SessionSummary`), `GET /api/sessions/:id`, `POST /api/sessions/:id/stop` (200), `POST /api/session/claim` (sets the session cookie).
  - `ws@8.22.0` (Task W0): `import { WebSocketServer } from "ws"` (ESM wrapper with named exports); `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, maxPayload })`; `wss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, cb(ws))`; on a socket: `ws.send(string)`, `ws.close(code, reason)` (reason at most 123 bytes), `ws.readyState` / `ws.OPEN`, events `message (data: Buffer, isBinary: boolean)`, `close`, `error`. A message over `maxPayload` makes ws close the socket with code 1009. Client side (tests): `import WebSocket from "ws"`; `new WebSocket(url, { headers, origin, handshakeTimeout })`; a non-101 answer emits `error` with the message `Unexpected server response: <status>` when no `unexpected-response` listener is set (`lib/websocket.js`).
  - Task W1, `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`: `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names })`, `FAKE_AGENT_NAMES` (the six names `claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw`; R16) and `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` (the only `SHELL` a test uses, R15). These behaviours of `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`: prints `FAKE_ARGV <json>` and `> ` at start; echoes typed characters; `you said: <line>` for an unknown line; `flood <KiB>` ending with `FLOOD DONE <KiB>`; `ask` (DA1 `ESC[c` and DSR `ESC[6n`) and `ask after <ms>` (the same two questions after the delay); a reply typed back prints `REPLY <json>`; `alt on`, `paste on`, `bell`, `osc9 <text>`; it dies on SIGTERM.
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/ws.js`):
  - `export const MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1048576`, `export const MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES = 65536`.
  - `export const CLOSE_CODES = { too_far_behind: 4000, session_ended: 4001, attach_failed: 4004 }` (R12): the WebSocket close code for each manager close reason; the close reason text is the same word, and clients decide by the word. Client meaning (Task U1): `too_far_behind` → attach again for a fresh snapshot; `session_ended` → the session ended, show the ended state and do not attach again; `attach_failed` (the manager could not attach this window for any reason other than the session ending; a session that ended between the upgrade check and the attach closes with `session_ended`) → do not retry at once.
  - `export function allowedOrigins(port, env = process.env)` → the exact Origin strings accepted for this port.
  - `export function checkUpgradeRequest(req, { port })` → `{ ok: true, sessionId } | { ok: false, reason }` (pure; `reason` is one of `method`, `upgrade`, `mode`, `path`, `host`, `origin`, `cookie`, for tests only, never sent or logged).
  - `export function parseClientFrame(data, isBinary)` → `{ t: "focus" } | { t: "in", d } | { t: "resize", cols, rows } | { t: "ack", seq } | null`.
  - `export function attachSessionsUpgrade(server, { getPort, manager })`: installs the `upgrade` listener. Every upgrade request to this server goes through it; anything that is not a correct attach to a running session (an unknown or ended session included) gets `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` and a destroyed socket.
  - The frame protocol on the wire (JSON text, one message per frame): client → server `{t:"focus"}`, `{t:"in", d}`, `{t:"resize", cols, rows}`, `{t:"ack", seq}`; server → client `{t:"snapshot", data, cols, rows, modes}` (always first), `{t:"state", status, exitCode?, signal?, endedBy?}`, `{t:"out", seq, d}`, `{t:"alert", raw}`. A client frame over 64 KB (the whole raw frame, in bytes, R12), a binary frame, non-JSON, or an unknown or malformed frame is dropped without an answer and the socket stays open; a message over 1 MB closes the socket (1009).
  - `scripts/dev-server.mjs`: sets `process.env.AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN = "1"`, then imports `server/index.js`. `npm run dev` = `concurrently "node --watch scripts/dev-server.mjs" "vite --host 127.0.0.1"`.
  - `vite.config.ts`: `"/api": { target: \`http://127.0.0.1:${apiPort}\`, changeOrigin: true, ws: true }`.

```js
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import net from "node:net";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { after, before, describe, test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import WebSocket from "ws";
import { cookieNameFor, sessionToken } from "../server/runtime/local-session.js";
import { PAUSED_DROP_MS, PAUSE_LAG_BYTES } from "../server/runtime/sessions/manager.js";
import {
  CLOSE_CODES,
  MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES,
  MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES,
  allowedOrigins,
  checkUpgradeRequest,
  parseClientFrame
} from "../server/runtime/sessions/ws.js";
import { FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const SKIP_POSIX = isWindows ? "POSIX only: W1's fake agents and stand-in login shell are sh scripts" : false;

const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function waitFor(check, timeoutMs = 10000, what = "a condition") {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const value = await check();
    if (value) return value;
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
    await delay(25);
  }
}

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. The pure checks
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const PORT = 8123;
const ID = "3f2c9a7e-1b4d-4c8e-9f00-0123456789ab";
// Local mode, no dev flag, no extra hosts.
const CLEAN = {
  DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE: undefined,
  AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN: undefined,
  AGENT_OS_PACKAGED: undefined,
  NODE_ENV: undefined,
  AGENT_OS_ALLOWED_HOSTS: undefined
};

// A correct upgrade request for session ID on PORT; `over` replaces parts.
function upgradeRequest(over = {}) {
  const { headers: headerOver = {}, ...rest } = over;
  const headers = {
    host: `127.0.0.1:${PORT}`,
    origin: `http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}`,
    cookie: `${cookieNameFor(PORT)}=${encodeURIComponent(sessionToken)}`,
    upgrade: "websocket",
    connection: "Upgrade",
    ...headerOver
  };
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(headers)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete headers[key];
  }
  return { method: "GET", url: `/api/sessions/${ID}/attach`, headers, ...rest };
}

const check = (over, port = PORT) => checkUpgradeRequest(upgradeRequest(over), { port });
const frame = (text) => parseClientFrame(Buffer.from(text, "utf8"), false);

      sessionId: ID
    });
    assert.deepEqual(check({ headers: { host: `[::1]:${PORT}` } }), { ok: true, sessionId: ID });
    const among = `theme=dark; ${cookieNameFor(PORT)}=${encodeURIComponent(sessionToken)}; other=1`;
    assert.deepEqual(check({ headers: { cookie: among } }), { ok: true, sessionId: ID });
  });
});

test("checkUpgradeRequest: the session cookie for this port is required and compared exactly, in constant time", async (t) => {
  await withEnv(CLEAN, async () => {
    const name = cookieNameFor(PORT);
    for (const [label, headers] of [
      ["no cookie", { cookie: undefined }],
      ["a wrong value", { cookie: `${name}=not-the-token` }],
      ["another port's cookie", { cookie: `${cookieNameFor(PORT + 1)}=${encodeURIComponent(sessionToken)}` }],
      ["one character more", { cookie: `${name}=${encodeURIComponent(sessionToken)}x` }],
      ["not valid percent-encoding", { cookie: `${name}=%E0%A4%A` }],
      ["the token in a header instead", { cookie: undefined, "x-agent-os-token": sessionToken }]
    ]) {
      assert.deepEqual(check({ headers }), { ok: false, reason: "cookie" }, label);
    }

    // Security 1: the comparison is crypto.timingSafeEqual (ws.js imports the
    // same `crypto` object), never `===`. The spy calls through to the real
    // function and is removed when this test ends.
    const spy = t.mock.method(crypto, "timingSafeEqual");
    assert.deepEqual(check(), { ok: true, sessionId: ID });
    assert.equal(spy.mock.callCount(), 1, "the cookie is compared with crypto.timingSafeEqual");
    // The token with its last character changed: same length, wrong value.
    const sameLength = sessionToken.slice(0, -1) + (sessionToken.endsWith("0") ? "1" : "0");
    assert.equal(Buffer.byteLength(sameLength), Buffer.byteLength(sessionToken));
    assert.deepEqual(check({ headers: { cookie: `${name}=${encodeURIComponent(sameLength)}` } }), {
      ok: false,
      reason: "cookie"
    });
    assert.equal(spy.mock.callCount(), 2, "a same-length wrong token is compared the same way");
  });
});

test("parseClientFrame: the four client frames, in bounds, and nothing else", () => {
  assert.equal(MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, 1024 * 1024);
  assert.equal(MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES, 64 * 1024);
  assert.deepEqual(CLOSE_CODES, { too_far_behind: 4000, session_ended: 4001, attach_failed: 4004 });

  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"focus"}'), { t: "focus" });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"in","d":"ls\\r"}'), { t: "in", d: "ls\r" });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"resize","cols":120,"rows":32}'), { t: "resize", cols: 120, rows: 32 });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"resize","cols":2,"rows":1}'), { t: "resize", cols: 2, rows: 1 });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"resize","cols":500,"rows":200}'), { t: "resize", cols: 500, rows: 200 });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"ack","seq":4096}'), { t: "ack", seq: 4096 });
  assert.deepEqual(frame('{"t":"ack","seq":0}'), { t: "ack", seq: 0 });

  for (const text of [
    '{"t":"resize","cols":1,"rows":24}',
    '{"t":"resize","cols":501,"rows":24}',
    '{"t":"resize","cols":80,"rows":0}',
    '{"t":"resize","cols":80,"rows":201}',
    '{"t":"resize","cols":80.5,"rows":24}',
    '{"t":"resize","cols":"80","rows":"24"}',
    '{"t":"ack","seq":-1}',
    '{"t":"ack","seq":1.5}',
    '{"t":"ack","seq":"10"}',
    '{"t":"in","d":""}',
    '{"t":"in","d":5}',
    '{"t":"in"}',
    '{"t":"snapshot","data":""}',
    '{"t":"nope"}',
    "[]",
    "null",
    '"focus"',
    "not json"
  ]) {
    assert.equal(frame(text), null, text);
  }
  assert.equal(parseClientFrame(Buffer.from('{"t":"focus"}'), true), null, "binary frames are ignored");

  // The 64 KB limit is on the whole frame as sent, in bytes (R12).
  const prefix = '{"t":"in","d":"';
  const suffix = '"}';
  const fits = `${prefix}${"a".repeat(MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES - prefix.length - suffix.length)}${suffix}`;
  assert.equal(Buffer.byteLength(fits), MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES);
  assert.equal(frame(fits)?.t, "in");
  const tooBig = `${prefix}${"a".repeat(MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES - prefix.length - suffix.length + 1)}${suffix}`;
  assert.equal(frame(tooBig), null);
  // Bytes, not characters: 33,000 "é" are fewer than 64 K characters but
  // more than 64 KB.
  const accents = JSON.stringify({ t: "in", d: "é".repeat(33000) });
  assert.ok(accents.length < MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES && Buffer.byteLength(accents) > MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES);
  assert.equal(frame(accents), null);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the endpoint.** Create `server/runtime/sessions/ws.js`:

```js
// The sessions WebSocket: /api/sessions/:id/attach (spec SP3, "WebSocket
// protocol", and Security 1).
//
// Express middleware never runs for an upgrade request, so this endpoint has
// its own check, run on every upgrade before anything else. The REST gate's
// helpers are deliberately not reused: originCheckMiddleware lets GET and a
// missing Origin through and compares only the hostname (any local port would
// pass), and the REST gate also accepts the x-agent-os-token header. Here:
//   - local mode only (never the public demo or the admin-token public mode);
//   - the path, checked lower-cased, must be exactly /api/sessions/<id>/attach,
//     with no query string (planning decision Q40);
//   - Host must be an allowed host AND carry the port this server is bound to;
//   - Origin is required and must be exactly http://127.0.0.1:<port> or
//     http://localhost:<port>; the Vite dev page (port 5173) only when
//     AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1, and never in a production or packaged run;
//   - the session cookie agent_os_session_<port>, compared in constant time;
//   - the session must exist and still run (Q40: an unknown id and an ended
//     session are refused like every other failure; an ended one has no live
//     screen, and its recording is in Runs).
// Any failure: write 403 and destroy the socket. Nothing from the request is
// ever logged.
//
// After the upgrade each socket is one attachment. The session manager owns
// the rules (which attachment is the writer, seq and ack, pausing the
// terminal, closing an attachment that falls 4 MB behind or still lags once
// the terminal has been paused for 10 s) and sends every frame itself, the
// snapshot first. This file checks and translates frames.
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import { cookieNameFor, isAllowedHost, isLocalMode, parseHostHeader, sessionToken } from "../local-session.js";
import { isSessionId } from "./errors.js";

// ws closes a socket that sends a bigger message (close code 1009).
export const MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
// A client frame bigger than this, counted over the whole raw frame in bytes
// (in practice an `in` paste), is refused: dropped before it reaches the
// terminal, and the socket stays open. The page splits big pastes.
export const MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
// The close code for each reason a window is closed with (4000-4999 are free
// for applications). The close reason text is the same word, and clients
// decide by the word, never by the number.
export const CLOSE_CODES = { too_far_behind: 4000, session_ended: 4001, attach_failed: 4004 };

const DEV_ORIGINS = ["http://127.0.0.1:5173", "http://localhost:5173"];
const ATTACH_PATH = /^\/api\/sessions\/([^/]+)\/attach$/;
const FORBIDDEN = "HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n";

function devOriginAllowed(env) {
  return env.AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN === "1" && env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && env.AGENT_OS_PACKAGED !== "1";
}

// The exact Origin values an attach may carry, for the port this server is
// bound to.
export function allowedOrigins(port, env = process.env) {
  const own = [`http://127.0.0.1:${port}`, `http://localhost:${port}`];
  return devOriginAllowed(env) ? [...own, ...DEV_ORIGINS] : own;
}

// The port written in a Host header ("127.0.0.1:8090", "[::1]:8090"), as text.
function hostHeaderPort(value) {
  const match = /:(\d{1,5})$/.exec(String(value || "").trim());
  return match ? match[1] : "";
}

// One cookie's value, or "" when it is missing or not valid percent-encoding.
// (The shared cookie parser throws on that; a throw here would stop the
// server, since no Express error handler runs for an upgrade.)
function cookieValue(header, name) {
  for (const part of String(header || "").split(";")) {
    const index = part.indexOf("=");
    if (index === -1 || part.slice(0, index).trim() !== name) continue;
    try {
      return decodeURIComponent(part.slice(index + 1).trim());
    } catch {
      return "";
    }
  }
  return "";
}

function sameSecret(provided, expected) {
  const a = Buffer.from(String(provided || ""), "utf8");
  const b = Buffer.from(String(expected || ""), "utf8");
  if (a.length === 0 || a.length !== b.length) return false;
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

function refused(reason) {
  return { ok: false, reason };
}

// Security 1 as a pure check of the upgrade request (no I/O).
export function checkUpgradeRequest(req, { port }) {
  const headers = req?.headers || {};
  if (req?.method !== "GET") return refused("method");
  if (String(headers.upgrade || "").toLowerCase() !== "websocket") return refused("upgrade");
  if (!isLocalMode()) return refused("mode");

  const url = String(req.url || "");
  if (url.includes("?") || url.includes("#")) return refused("path");
  const lower = url.toLowerCase();
  const match = ATTACH_PATH.exec(lower);
  if (!match || lower !== url || !isSessionId(match[1])) return refused("path");

  const boundPort = Number(port);
  if (!Number.isInteger(boundPort) || boundPort <= 0) return refused("host");
  if (!isAllowedHost(parseHostHeader(headers.host)) || hostHeaderPort(headers.host) !== String(boundPort)) {
    return refused("host");
  }

  if (typeof headers.origin !== "string" || !allowedOrigins(boundPort).includes(headers.origin)) {
    return refused("origin");
  }

  if (!sameSecret(cookieValue(headers.cookie, cookieNameFor(boundPort)), sessionToken)) return refused("cookie");

  return { ok: true, sessionId: match[1] };
}

// A client frame, checked: the four frame types with their bounds, or null.
// Viewer input and a viewer's resize are dropped by the manager, not here.
export function parseClientFrame(data, isBinary) {
  if (isBinary) return null;
  const buffer = Buffer.isBuffer(data) ? data : Array.isArray(data) ? Buffer.concat(data) : Buffer.from(data);
  if (buffer.length > MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES) return null;
  let frame;
  try {
    frame = JSON.parse(buffer.toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  if (!frame || typeof frame !== "object" || Array.isArray(frame)) return null;
  if (frame.t === "focus") return { t: "focus" };
  if (frame.t === "in") return typeof frame.d === "string" && frame.d.length > 0 ? { t: "in", d: frame.d } : null;
  if (frame.t === "resize") {
    const { cols, rows } = frame;
    const fits = Number.isInteger(cols) && Number.isInteger(rows) && cols >= 2 && cols <= 500 && rows >= 1 && rows <= 200;
    return fits ? { t: "resize", cols, rows } : null;
  }
  if (frame.t === "ack") return Number.isSafeInteger(frame.seq) && frame.seq >= 0 ? { t: "ack", seq: frame.seq } : null;
  return null;
}

// Writes 403 and destroys the socket (spec Security 1). The timer covers a
// client that never reads the answer.
function refuse(socket) {
  if (socket.destroyed) return;
  socket.once("finish", () => socket.destroy());
  socket.end(FORBIDDEN);
  setTimeout(() => socket.destroy(), 1000).unref?.();
}

// Q40: an unknown session is refused like every other failure, and so is an
// ended one (it has no live screen to attach to; its recording is in Runs).
async function liveSession(manager, id) {
  try {
    const session = await manager.get(id);
    return Boolean(session) && session.status !== "exited";
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function safely(fn) {
  try {
    const result = fn();
    if (result && typeof result.then === "function") result.then(undefined, () => {});
  } catch {
    // the session ended or the frame was not allowed: nothing to tell this socket
  }
}

function dispatch(manager, sessionId, attachmentId, frame) {
  safely(() => {
    if (frame.t === "focus") return manager.focus(sessionId, attachmentId);
    if (frame.t === "in") return manager.write(sessionId, attachmentId, frame.d);
    if (frame.t === "resize") return manager.resize(sessionId, attachmentId, frame.cols, frame.rows);
    return manager.ack(sessionId, attachmentId, frame.seq);
  });
}

function closeWord(reason) {
  return typeof reason === "string" && Object.hasOwn(CLOSE_CODES, reason) ? reason : "too_far_behind";
}

function serveAttachment(ws, sessionId, manager) {
  const attachmentId = crypto.randomUUID();
  let detach = null;
  let closed = false;

  // What the manager holds for this socket. The manager sends the snapshot,
  // then the state, then output and alerts, in that order.
  const attachment = {
    id: attachmentId,
    send(frame) {
      if (!closed && ws.readyState === ws.OPEN) ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame));
    },
    close(reason) {
      if (closed) return;
      const word = closeWord(reason);
      ws.close(CLOSE_CODES[word], word);
    }
  };

  // A protocol error (for example a message over maxPayload) is followed by
  // "close"; without a listener it would be thrown and stop the server.
  ws.on("error", () => {});
  ws.on("close", () => {
    closed = true;
    const done = detach;
    detach = null;
    if (done) safely(done);
  });

  const ready = Promise.resolve()
    .then(() => manager.attach(sessionId, attachment))
    .then((attached) => {
      if (closed) {
        safely(() => attached.detach());
        return false;
      }
      detach = () => attached.detach();
      return true;
    })
    .catch((error) => {
      if (!closed) {
        const word = error?.code === "session_ended" ? "session_ended" : "attach_failed";
        ws.close(CLOSE_CODES[word], word);
      }
      return false;
    });

  // Frames wait until the window is attached, and keep their order.
  ws.on("message", (data, isBinary) => {
    const frame = parseClientFrame(data, isBinary);
    if (!frame) return;
    ready.then((ok) => {
      if (ok && !closed) dispatch(manager, sessionId, attachmentId, frame);
    });
  });
}

// Installs the upgrade listener on the HTTP server. With a listener present,
// Node hands EVERY upgrade request to it, so anything that is not a correct
// attach is refused here too.
export function attachSessionsUpgrade(server, { getPort, manager }) {
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, maxPayload: MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES });

  server.on("upgrade", (req, socket, head) => {
    socket.on("error", () => socket.destroy());
    let verdict;
    try {
      verdict = checkUpgradeRequest(req, { port: getPort() });
    } catch {
      verdict = refused("error");
    }
    if (!verdict.ok) {
      refuse(socket);
      return;
    }
    liveSession(manager, verdict.sessionId)
      .then((isLive) => {
        if (!isLive || socket.destroyed) {
          refuse(socket);
          return;
        }
        wss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => serveAttachment(ws, verdict.sessionId, manager));
      })
      .catch(() => refuse(socket));
  });
}
```
