```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. The real server, driven with the ws client
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];
const TOKEN = "test-token-123";

// A temp HOME (its realpath) with a "project" folder and, on POSIX, Task W1's
// six fake agents in <home>/fake-bin (all six names, R16, so detection never
// finds a real agent in a fixed folder first). The tests start the fake
// `claude`: it answers the detection probes and `agents --json` at once; as a
// session it prints FAKE_ARGV and a prompt, echoes what is typed, and runs
// the typed commands these tests use: flood, ask, ask after, alt, paste,
// bell, osc9 ("you said: <line>" for anything else). It lives under
// os.tmpdir() and test/, which the no-real-agents watcher allows.
async function makeHome(prefix) {
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix)));
  await mkdir(path.join(home, "project"), { recursive: true });
  if (!isWindows) await makeFakeAgentBin(path.join(home, "fake-bin"), { names: FAKE_AGENT_NAMES });
  return home;
}

async function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const probe = net.createServer();
    probe.once("error", reject);
    probe.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const { port } = probe.address();
      probe.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

// Never passed on to the server unless a test sets one on purpose.
// AGENT_OS_PORT would win over PORT (Task S8 reads it first).
const CLEARED_KEYS = [
  "AGENT_OS_PORT",
  "HERMES_HOME",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME",
  // Detection searches it before PATH (R16).
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS",
  "DEMO_PUBLIC",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_ADMIN_TOKEN",
  "HERMES_AGENT_OS_ENABLE_EXEC",
  "AGENT_OS_LIVE_CHAT",
  "AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN",
  "AGENT_OS_PACKAGED",
  "AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN",
  "AGENT_OS_ALLOWED_HOSTS",
  "FAKE_AGENT_MODE",
  "NODE_ENV",
  "CLAUDECODE",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT"
];

function serverEnv(home, port, extra = {}) {
  const env = {
    ...process.env,
    PORT: String(port),
    HOST: "127.0.0.1",
    HOME: home,
    USERPROFILE: home,
    AGENT_OS_HOME: path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: path.join(home, ".agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_TOKEN: TOKEN,
    HERMES_AGENT_OS_SCHEDULER: "0",
    // The login shell sessions read their environment from: W1's stand-in
    // (R15), which keeps the PATH below. Never the developer's own shell
    // setup, and never a real login sh either: on macOS it runs path_helper,
    // which puts /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin (where real agents live)
    // on the sessions' PATH.
    SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
    // The fake folder first, then system folders only (R16; not Node's own
    // folder, which can hold real agents).
    ...(isWindows ? {} : { PATH: [path.join(home, "fake-bin"), ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter) })
  };
  for (const key of CLEARED_KEYS) {
    if (!(key in extra)) delete env[key];
  }
  return { ...env, ...extra };
}

async function startServer(home, extra = {}) {
  const port = await freePort();
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["server/index.js"], {
    cwd: root,
    env: serverEnv(home, port, extra),
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]
  });
  const logs = { text: "" };
  child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    logs.text += chunk;
  });
  child.stderr.on("data", (chunk) => {
    logs.text += chunk;
  });
  const deadline = Date.now() + 20000;
  while (!/AGENT_OS_READY:\d+/.test(logs.text)) {
    if (child.exitCode != null) throw new Error(`server exited early (${child.exitCode}):\n${logs.text.slice(-2000)}`);
    if (Date.now() > deadline) {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      throw new Error(`server did not start:\n${logs.text.slice(-2000)}`);
    }
    await delay(25);
  }
  return { child, port, logs };
}

// SIGTERM, then up to 10 s (the server's own hard exit is 8 s), then SIGKILL.
async function stopServer(server) {
  const { child } = server;
  if (child.exitCode != null || child.signalCode != null) return;
  child.kill("SIGTERM");
  await new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      resolve();
    }, 10000);
    child.once("exit", () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve();
    });
  });
}

async function api(port, method, url, body) {
  const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${url}`, {
    method,
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "x-agent-os-token": TOKEN },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body)
  });
  const text = await response.text();
  let json = null;
  try {
    json = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    json = null;
  }
  return { status: response.status, json, text };
}

async function gateOn(port) {
  const gate = await api(port, "POST", "/api/admin/execution-gate", { enabled: true, confirm: true });
  assert.equal(gate.status, 200, gate.text);
}

async function createSession(port, home) {
  const created = await api(port, "POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "claude", folder: path.join(home, "project") });
  assert.equal(created.status, 201, created.text);
  return created.json.id;
}

async function stopSession(port, id) {
  await api(port, "POST", `/api/sessions/${id}/stop`, {}).catch(() => {});
}

const ownOrigin = (port) => `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;
const attachPath = (id) => `/api/sessions/${id}/attach`;
const cookieFor = (port) => `${cookieNameFor(port)}=${encodeURIComponent(TOKEN)}`;

// Everything one socket received, for the assertions below.
function trackClient(ws) {
  const client = {
    ws,
    frames: [],
    outText: "",
    outBytes: 0,
    lastSeq: 0,
    autoAck: false,
    closed: null,
    closedAt: null,
    lastFrameAt: Date.now(),
    send(value) {
      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) ws.send(JSON.stringify(value));
    },
    ack() {
      client.send({ t: "ack", seq: client.lastSeq });
    },
    // The snapshot's screen plus every output since, as one text.
    screen() {
      const snapshot = client.frames.find((item) => item.t === "snapshot");
      return `${snapshot ? snapshot.data : ""}${client.outText}`;
    },
    close() {
      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN || ws.readyState === WebSocket.CONNECTING) ws.close();
    }
  };
  ws.on("message", (data) => {
    let value;
    try {
      value = JSON.parse(String(data));
    } catch {
      return;
    }
    client.frames.push(value);
    client.lastFrameAt = Date.now();
    if (value.t === "out") {
      client.outText += value.d;
      client.outBytes += Buffer.byteLength(value.d, "utf8");
      client.lastSeq = value.seq;
      if (client.autoAck) client.ack();
    }
  });
  ws.on("close", (code, reason) => {
    client.closed = { code, reason: String(reason) };
    client.closedAt = Date.now();
  });
  ws.on("error", () => {});
  return client;
}

// One upgrade attempt: { opened: true, client } or { opened: false, error }.
function tryUpgrade(port, urlPath, { origin, cookie, host, headers = {} } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const sent = { ...headers };
    if (cookie !== undefined) sent.Cookie = cookie;
    if (host !== undefined) sent.Host = host;
    const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}${urlPath}`, {
      headers: sent,
      ...(origin === undefined ? {} : { origin }),
      handshakeTimeout: 5000
    });
    const client = trackClient(ws);
    let settled = false;
    const finish = (result) => {
      if (!settled) {
        settled = true;
        resolve(result);
      }
    };
    ws.once("open", () => finish({ opened: true, client }));
    ws.once("error", (error) => finish({ opened: false, error: String(error?.message || error) }));
    ws.once("close", () => finish({ opened: false, error: "closed before opening" }));
  });
}

function expectRefused(result, label) {
  if (result.opened) result.client.close();
  assert.equal(result.opened, false, `${label}: the upgrade should be refused`);
  assert.match(result.error, /Unexpected server response: 403/, `${label}: ${result.error}`);
}

// A window that is attached: its snapshot and its first state have arrived.
async function openClient(port, id, { origin = ownOrigin(port) } = {}) {
  const result = await tryUpgrade(port, attachPath(id), { origin, cookie: cookieFor(port) });
  assert.equal(result.opened, true, `the attach should open: ${result.error}`);
  const { client } = result;
  await waitFor(() => client.frames.some((item) => item.t === "state"), 5000, "the snapshot and state frames");
  assert.equal(client.frames[0].t, "snapshot", "the snapshot is always the first frame");
  return client;
}

async function waitForScreen(client, pattern, timeoutMs = 10000) {
  await waitFor(() => pattern.test(client.screen()), timeoutMs, `${pattern} on the screen`);
}

// Resolves once no listed socket has received a frame for quietMs.
async function waitQuiet(clients, quietMs, timeoutMs) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const last = Math.max(...clients.map((client) => client.lastFrameAt));
    if (Date.now() - last >= quietMs) return;
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`output never went quiet within ${timeoutMs} ms`);
    await delay(50);
  }
}

test("the public demo refuses every upgrade, even one that is right in every other way", async () => {
  const home = await makeHome("agent-os-ws-demo-");
  const server = await startServer(home, { DEMO_PUBLIC: "1" });
  try {
    expectRefused(
      await tryUpgrade(server.port, attachPath(crypto.randomUUID()), {
        origin: ownOrigin(server.port),
        cookie: cookieFor(server.port)
      }),
      "demo mode"
    );
  } finally {
    await stopServer(server);
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

describe("the attach endpoint on a real server", { skip: SKIP_POSIX }, () => {
  let main = null;

  before(async () => {
    const home = await makeHome("agent-os-ws-");
    const server = await startServer(home);
    await gateOn(server.port);
    const securityId = await createSession(server.port, home);
    main = { home, server, port: server.port, securityId };
  });

  after(async () => {
    if (!main) return;
    await stopSession(main.port, main.securityId);
    await stopServer(main.server);
    await rm(main.home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  // A fresh session for one test; every window it opened is closed and the
  // session is stopped afterwards.
  async function withSession(fn) {
    const id = await createSession(main.port, main.home);
    const clients = [];
    const open = async () => {
      const client = await openClient(main.port, id);
      clients.push(client);
      return client;
    };
    try {
      await fn({ id, open });
    } finally {
      for (const client of clients) client.close();
      await stopSession(main.port, id);
    }
  }

  // -- Security 1 -----------------------------------------------------------

  test("a correct upgrade opens: the manager's snapshot comes first, then the state", async () => {
    const client = await openClient(main.port, main.securityId);
    try {
      const [snapshot, state] = client.frames;
      assert.equal(snapshot.t, "snapshot");
      assert.equal(typeof snapshot.data, "string");
      assert.ok(Number.isInteger(snapshot.cols) && Number.isInteger(snapshot.rows));
      assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(snapshot.modes).sort(), [
        "altScreen",
        "bracketedPaste",
        "cursorKeysApp",
        "focusReporting",
        "kittyFlags",
        "mouseEncoding",
        "mouseTracking"
      ]);
      assert.equal(state.t, "state");
      assert.ok(["starting", "live", "idle"].includes(state.status), state.status);
    } finally {
      client.close();
    }
    // The cookie the real login hands out works the same way.
    const claim = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${main.port}/api/session/claim`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ token: TOKEN })
    });
    const cookie = (claim.headers.get("set-cookie") || "").split(";")[0];
    const viaClaim = await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(main.securityId), { origin: ownOrigin(main.port), cookie });
    assert.equal(viaClaim.opened, true, viaClaim.error);
    viaClaim.client.close();
  });

  test("Origin: missing, foreign, another local port, a trailing slash, and the Vite dev page without the flag are refused", async () => {
    for (const [label, origin] of [
      ["no Origin", undefined],
      ["a foreign Origin", "https://evil.example"],
      ["127.0.0.1 on another port", `http://127.0.0.1:${main.port + 1}`],
      ["localhost on another port", `http://localhost:${main.port + 1}`],
      ["a trailing slash", `http://127.0.0.1:${main.port}/`],
      ["the Vite dev page without AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1", "http://127.0.0.1:5173"]
    ]) {
      expectRefused(
        await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(main.securityId), { origin, cookie: cookieFor(main.port) }),
        label
      );
    }
  });

  test("the path is checked lower-cased and may not carry a query string", async () => {
    const id = main.securityId;
    for (const urlPath of [
      `/API/sessions/${id}/attach`,
      `/api/Sessions/${id}/attach`,
      `/api/sessions/${id}/ATTACH`,
      `/api/sessions/${id.toUpperCase()}/attach`,
      `/api/sessions/${id}/attach/`,
      `/api/sessions/${id}/attach?token=${TOKEN}`
    ]) {
      expectRefused(
        await tryUpgrade(main.port, urlPath, { origin: ownOrigin(main.port), cookie: cookieFor(main.port) }),
        urlPath
      );
    }
  });

  test("the session cookie is required and must match", async () => {
    const origin = ownOrigin(main.port);
    for (const [label, options] of [
      ["no cookie", { origin }],
      ["a wrong cookie", { origin, cookie: `${cookieNameFor(main.port)}=not-the-token` }],
      ["the token under another port's cookie", { origin, cookie: `${cookieNameFor(main.port + 1)}=${encodeURIComponent(TOKEN)}` }],
      ["the token in the x-agent-os-token header instead", { origin, headers: { "x-agent-os-token": TOKEN } }],
      ["a cookie that is not valid percent-encoding", { origin, cookie: `${cookieNameFor(main.port)}=%E0%A4%A` }]
    ]) {
      expectRefused(await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(main.securityId), options), label);
    }
    // The server is still up after the broken cookie.
    const fine = await openClient(main.port, main.securityId);
    fine.close();
  });

  test("an unknown, malformed or ended session is refused like any other failure", async () => {
    const good = { origin: ownOrigin(main.port), cookie: cookieFor(main.port) };
    expectRefused(await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(crypto.randomUUID()), good), "an unknown session id");
    expectRefused(await tryUpgrade(main.port, "/api/sessions/not-a-session/attach", good), "a malformed id");
    const ended = await createSession(main.port, main.home);
    await stopSession(main.port, ended);
    await waitFor(
      async () => (await api(main.port, "GET", `/api/sessions/${ended}`)).json?.status === "exited",
      15000,
      "the stopped session to end"
    );
    expectRefused(await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(ended), good), "an ended session");
  });

  test("Host must be allowed and carry this server's port", async () => {
    const good = { origin: ownOrigin(main.port), cookie: cookieFor(main.port) };
    for (const [label, host] of [
      ["a forged Host", `evil.example:${main.port}`],
      ["a Host without a port", "127.0.0.1"],
      ["a Host with another port", `127.0.0.1:${main.port + 1}`]
    ]) {
      expectRefused(await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(main.securityId), { ...good, host }), label);
    }
    const viaLocalhost = await tryUpgrade(main.port, attachPath(main.securityId), {
      host: `localhost:${main.port}`,
      origin: `http://localhost:${main.port}`,
      cookie: cookieFor(main.port)
    });
    assert.equal(viaLocalhost.opened, true, viaLocalhost.error);
    viaLocalhost.client.close();
  });

  test("any other upgrade address gets 403 and is never left hanging", async () => {
    for (const urlPath of ["/api/runs", "/", "/api/sessions"]) {
      expectRefused(
        await tryUpgrade(main.port, urlPath, { origin: ownOrigin(main.port), cookie: cookieFor(main.port) }),
        urlPath
      );
    }
  });

  // -- The frame protocol ---------------------------------------------------

  test("Review Focus 3, two windows: writer by focus, the viewer's keys are dropped, and the last focus wins", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      const b = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "typed-before-focus\r" }); // nobody is the writer yet
      await delay(400);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "from-a\r" });
      await waitForScreen(b, /you said: from-a/);
      b.send({ t: "in", d: "viewer-b\r" }); // b is a viewer
      await delay(400);
      b.send({ t: "focus" });
      b.send({ t: "in", d: "from-b\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: from-b/);
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "viewer-a\r" }); // a is a viewer now
      await delay(400);
      b.send({ t: "in", d: "marker\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: marker/);
      for (const client of [a, b]) {
        assert.doesNotMatch(client.outText, /typed-before-focus/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(client.outText, /viewer-b/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(client.outText, /viewer-a/);
      }
    });
  });

  test("Review Focus 3, two windows: only the writer's resize reaches the terminal, and out-of-range sizes are ignored", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const writer = await open();
      const viewer = await open();
      await waitForScreen(writer, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      // A new window's snapshot carries the terminal's size right now.
      const sizeNow = async () => {
        const probe = await open();
        const { cols, rows } = probe.frames[0];
        probe.close();
        return `${cols}x${rows}`;
      };
      const start = await sizeNow();
      writer.send({ t: "focus" });
      viewer.send({ t: "resize", cols: 77, rows: 22 });
      await delay(300);
      assert.equal(await sizeNow(), start, "a viewer's resize changes nothing");

      writer.send({ t: "resize", cols: 91, rows: 27 });
      await waitFor(async () => (await sizeNow()) === "91x27", 5000, "the writer's resize");

      for (const bad of [
        { cols: 1, rows: 27 },
        { cols: 501, rows: 27 },
        { cols: 91, rows: 0 },
        { cols: 91, rows: 201 },
        { cols: 90.5, rows: 27 },
        { cols: "80", rows: "24" }
      ]) {
        writer.send({ t: "resize", ...bad });
      }
      await delay(300);
      assert.equal(await sizeNow(), "91x27", "out-of-range sizes are ignored");
    });
  });

  test("seq is the running UTF-8 byte count of out frames, from 0 after each window's snapshot", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "café ✓\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: café ✓/);
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "flood 20\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /FLOOD DONE 20/, 15000);
      const counted = (client) => {
        let total = 0;
        for (const item of client.frames.filter((value) => value.t === "out")) {
          total += Buffer.byteLength(item.d, "utf8");
          assert.equal(item.seq, total, "seq is the running UTF-8 byte count");
        }
        return total;
      };
      assert.ok(counted(a) >= 20 * 1024);
      assert.ok(
        a.frames.some((item) => item.t === "out" && Buffer.byteLength(item.d, "utf8") > item.d.length),
        "multi-byte text counts bytes, not characters"
      );
      const b = await open();
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "after\r" });
      await waitForScreen(b, /you said: after/);
      assert.ok(counted(b) > 0, "a later window counts from 0 after its own snapshot");
    });
  });

  test("Review Focus 3, back-pressure: the terminal pauses only when every window lags, resumes when one catches up, and a window 4 MB behind is closed and reattaches with a fresh screen", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      const b = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "flood 2930\r" }); // about 3 MB
      await waitFor(() => a.outBytes > 100000, 15000, "the flood to start");
      await waitQuiet([a, b], 1500, 30000);
      assert.ok(a.outBytes >= PAUSE_LAG_BYTES, `paused too early: ${a.outBytes} bytes`);
      assert.ok(a.outBytes < 2930 * 1024, `never paused: ${a.outBytes} bytes`);
      assert.doesNotMatch(a.outText, /FLOOD DONE/);

      // One window catching up is enough to resume (long before the 10 s
      // paused limit).
      b.autoAck = true;
      b.ack();
      await waitForScreen(b, /FLOOD DONE 2930/, 60000);
      assert.equal(a.closed, null, "about 3 MB behind is under the 4 MB limit, so it stays open");

      // More than 4 MB behind: closed with a reason; the window that keeps up stays.
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "flood 1954\r" }); // about 2 MB more
      await waitFor(() => a.closed !== null, 60000, "the lagging window to be closed");
      assert.deepEqual(a.closed, { code: CLOSE_CODES.too_far_behind, reason: "too_far_behind" });
      await waitForScreen(b, /FLOOD DONE 1954/, 60000);
      assert.equal(b.closed, null);

      // The closed window's client attaches again and gets a fresh screen.
      const again = await open();
      assert.match(again.frames[0].data, /FLOOD DONE 1954/, "the new snapshot shows the latest screen");
    });
  });

  test("Review Focus 3, back-pressure: windows that never ack are closed once the terminal has been paused for 10 s, and the terminal runs on", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ id, open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      const b = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "flood 2930\r" }); // about 3 MB: never 4 MB behind
      await waitFor(() => a.outBytes > 100000, 15000, "the flood to start");
      await waitQuiet([a, b], 1500, 30000);
      assert.ok(a.outBytes < 2930 * 1024, "paused while every window lags");
      assert.equal(a.closed, null);
      assert.equal(b.closed, null);
      const pausedBy = Math.max(a.lastFrameAt, b.lastFrameAt);

      // Neither window ever acks (a hidden window, an asleep second screen).
      await waitFor(() => a.closed !== null && b.closed !== null, PAUSED_DROP_MS + 15000, "both lagging windows to be closed");
      for (const client of [a, b]) {
        assert.deepEqual(client.closed, { code: CLOSE_CODES.too_far_behind, reason: "too_far_behind" });
        assert.ok(
          client.closedAt - pausedBy >= PAUSED_DROP_MS - 2000,
          `closed ${client.closedAt - pausedBy} ms after the pause, before the 10 s limit`
        );
      }

      // The agent is never left blocked on its own output: the flood finishes.
      await waitFor(
        async () => {
          const viewer = await openClient(main.port, id);
          const done = /FLOOD DONE 2930/.test(viewer.frames[0].data);
          viewer.close();
          if (!done) await delay(500);
          return done;
        },
        60000,
        "the flood to finish after the lagging windows were closed"
      );
    });
  });

  test("Review Focus 3, back-pressure: with no window left the terminal never pauses, and a closed window leaves the count at once", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ id, open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      const b = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "flood 2930\r" });
      await waitFor(() => a.outBytes > 100000, 15000, "the flood to start");
      await waitQuiet([a, b], 1500, 30000);
      assert.ok(a.outBytes < 2930 * 1024, "paused while every window lags");
      a.close();
      b.close();
      // With no window left the terminal must run on: short-lived viewers look
      // at the screen until the flood is done.
      await waitFor(
        async () => {
          const viewer = await openClient(main.port, id);
          const done = /FLOOD DONE 2930/.test(viewer.frames[0].data);
          viewer.close();
          if (!done) await delay(500);
          return done;
        },
        60000,
        "the flood to finish with no window attached"
      );
    });
  });

  test("Review Focus 2, limits: one input frame over 64 KB (in bytes) is refused on the server, a message over 1 MB closes the socket, junk frames are ignored", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "y".repeat(70000) }); // a frame of about 70 KB
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "é".repeat(33000) }); // 33,000 characters, about 66 KB
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "after-big\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: after-big/);
      assert.doesNotMatch(a.outText, /y{50}/, "the frame over 64 KB never reached the terminal");
      assert.doesNotMatch(a.outText, /é{50}/, "64 KB counts bytes, not characters");
      assert.equal(a.closed, null, "a refused frame leaves the socket open");

      a.send({ t: "in", d: `${"z".repeat(4000)}\r` });
      await waitFor(() => /you said: z{4000}/.test(a.outText), 15000, "a 4 KB line to come back");

      a.ws.send("not json");
      a.ws.send(Buffer.from([1, 2, 3]));
      a.send({ t: "nope" });
      a.send({ t: "ack", seq: -5 });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "still-open\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: still-open/);
      assert.equal(a.closed, null);

      const big = await open();
      big.ws.send("x".repeat(MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES + 1024));
      await waitFor(() => big.closed !== null, 10000, "the oversized message to close the socket");
      assert.equal(big.closed.code, 1009);
    });
  });

  test("terminal queries: while a writer is attached only the writer answers, never the server's mirror", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "ask\r" });
      await waitFor(
        () => a.outText.includes("\u001b[c") && a.outText.includes("\u001b[6n"),
        5000,
        "the fake's DA1 and DSR queries"
      );
      await delay(1500);
      assert.doesNotMatch(a.outText, /REPLY/, "nobody answered for the silent writer");
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "\u001b[?62;22c" }); // the writer's own terminal answers DA1
      await waitForScreen(a, /REPLY "\\u001b\[\?62;22c"/, 5000);
      assert.equal((a.outText.match(/REPLY/g) || []).length, 1, "exactly the writer's one reply");
    });
  });

  test("terminal queries: with no writer attached, the server's mirror answers DA1", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ id, open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "ask after 4000\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /ask after 4000/); // the echo: the line, with its Enter, reached the fake
      a.close(); // no writer when the query comes
      const reply = await waitFor(
        async () => {
          const viewer = await openClient(main.port, id);
          const match = /REPLY "(\\u001b\[\?[0-9;]*c)"/.exec(viewer.frames[0].data);
          viewer.close();
          if (!match) await delay(500);
          return match;
        },
        15000,
        "the fake to print the mirror's DA1 reply"
      );
      assert.ok(reply, "the mirror answered DA1 while no window was the writer");
    });
  });

  test("alerts and state: BEL and OSC 9 arrive raw, and Stop sends exited with endedBy stop, then closes with session_ended", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ id, open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "bell\r" });
      await waitFor(() => a.frames.some((item) => item.t === "alert" && item.raw === "bel"), 5000, "the BEL alert");
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "osc9 hello-alert\r" });
      await waitFor(
        () => a.frames.some((item) => item.t === "alert" && item.raw === "9;hello-alert"),
        5000,
        "the OSC 9 alert"
      );
      const stopped = await api(main.port, "POST", `/api/sessions/${id}/stop`, {});
      assert.equal(stopped.status, 200, stopped.text);
      const ended = await waitFor(
        () => a.frames.find((item) => item.t === "state" && item.status === "exited"),
        15000,
        "the exited state"
      );
      assert.equal(ended.endedBy, "stop");
      await waitFor(() => a.closed !== null, 5000, "the socket to close");
      assert.deepEqual(a.closed, { code: 4001, reason: "session_ended" });
    });
  });

  test("reattach restores the screen and the modes", async () => {
    await withSession(async ({ open }) => {
      const a = await open();
      await waitForScreen(a, /FAKE_ARGV/);
      a.send({ t: "focus" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "alt on\r" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "paste on\r" });
      a.send({ t: "in", d: "marker-in-alt\r" });
      await waitForScreen(a, /you said: marker-in-alt/);
      a.close();
      const b = await open();
      const [snapshot] = b.frames;
      assert.equal(snapshot.modes.altScreen, true);
      assert.equal(snapshot.modes.bracketedPaste, true);
      assert.match(snapshot.data, /you said: marker-in-alt/);
    });
  });
});

describe("the Vite dev origin on real servers", { skip: SKIP_POSIX }, () => {
  async function withDevServer(extra, fn) {
    const home = await makeHome("agent-os-ws-dev-");
    const server = await startServer(home, extra);
    let id = null;
    try {
      await gateOn(server.port);
      id = await createSession(server.port, home);
      await fn(server.port, id);
    } finally {
      if (id) await stopSession(server.port, id);
      await stopServer(server);
      await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  }

  test("with AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1 the Vite dev page attaches", async () => {
    await withDevServer({ AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN: "1" }, async (port, id) => {
      for (const origin of ["http://127.0.0.1:5173", "http://localhost:5173", ownOrigin(port)]) {
        const result = await tryUpgrade(port, attachPath(id), { origin, cookie: cookieFor(port) });
        assert.equal(result.opened, true, `${origin}: ${result.error}`);
        result.client.close();
      }
    });
  });

  test("AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1 is ignored in a packaged run", async () => {
    await withDevServer({ AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN: "1", AGENT_OS_PACKAGED: "1" }, async (port, id) => {
      expectRefused(
        await tryUpgrade(port, attachPath(id), { origin: "http://127.0.0.1:5173", cookie: cookieFor(port) }),
        "the Vite dev page in a packaged run"
      );
      const own = await tryUpgrade(port, attachPath(id), { origin: ownOrigin(port), cookie: cookieFor(port) });
      assert.equal(own.opened, true, own.error);
      own.client.close();
    });
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 11: The dev proxy and the dev flag.**

(a) In `vite.config.ts`, replace:

```ts
    server: {
      port: 5173,
      proxy: {
        "/api": `http://127.0.0.1:${apiPort}`
      }
    }
```

with:

```ts
    server: {
      port: 5173,
      proxy: {
        // The object form, so the proxy also carries WebSocket upgrades (a
        // session's terminal, /api/sessions/:id/attach). changeOrigin keeps the
        // Host the API server checks (127.0.0.1:<apiPort>); the page's Origin
        // (http://127.0.0.1:5173) reaches the server unchanged, and the server
        // accepts it only when `npm run dev` set AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1.
        "/api": { target: `http://127.0.0.1:${apiPort}`, changeOrigin: true, ws: true }
      }
    }
```

(Vite 6.4.3 turns today's string form into `{ target, changeOrigin: true }` and proxies an upgrade only when `ws` is true; `changeOrigin` must be written out in the object form, or the server would see `Host: 127.0.0.1:5173` and refuse it. `rewriteWsOrigin` stays off, so the Origin is not rewritten.)

(b) Create `scripts/dev-server.mjs`:

```js
// `npm run dev` starts the API server through this file. It marks the run as a
// development run, so the sessions WebSocket also accepts the Vite dev page's
// origin (http://127.0.0.1:5173 or http://localhost:5173). A packaged or
// production server ignores the flag (server/runtime/sessions/ws.js).
// Setting it here, instead of writing "AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1 node ..." in
// package.json, works the same in every operating system's shell.
process.env.AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN = "1";
await import("../server/index.js");
```

#### Notes

1. **The dev script runs a launcher.** Written inline (`AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1 node --watch …`), the flag would work only in a POSIX shell, and `concurrently` runs Windows commands through `cmd`, so `npm run dev` would break on Windows; no cross-platform env tool is installed. `scripts/dev-server.mjs` sets the variable and imports the server. The flag still comes only from `npm run dev`; the dev-wiring test checks that `npm start`, `server/index.js` and the desktop shell never set it.
2. **Every upgrade goes through this listener.** Once an `upgrade` listener exists, Node hands it every upgrade request (without one, Node answers an upgrade like a normal page request, checked on Node 22). `ws.js` therefore refuses any other upgrade address with 403 too. A future WebSocket endpoint must be added to this listener, not as a second one.
3. **Extra allowed hosts do not open the WebSocket (deliberate).** `AGENT_OS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (a container's hostname) passes the Host check, but the Origin list is only `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` on the bound port, as Security 1 says. A browser on another hostname can use the REST pages but not a session terminal. Recorded so nobody "fixes" it by widening the Origin list.
4. **An ended session gets a bare 403 (R12).** The browser reports a refused upgrade as close 1006 with no reason, so a window cannot tell "ended" from "dropped" by the socket alone; the page decides from its session list (Task U2's `ended` prop and its reconnect rule).
5. **No size frame for viewers (deliberate limit).** The agent draws for the writer's size; a viewer of another size may wrap lines differently until it takes the keys, and a new window's snapshot carries the size at that moment. A `{t:"size", cols, rows}` server frame would let viewers match; SP3's single window does not need it.
6. **No shutdown task for the WebSocket server.** `shutdown()` ends with `process.exit`, and the manager closes every window with `session_ended` as it stops each session, so nothing extra closes sockets at quit.

### Task S10: Hold to stop all and the palette's "Stop all agent work" include sessions

"Hold to stop all" (the red button in the top bar) and the palette's stop today stop agent runs and Team Rooms only. From SP3 a person's most important live work is a session, so the spec (D11, "Hold to stop all"; planning decision Q16; ruling R22) says the hold stops every session of both kinds (`agent` and `update`) together with the runs, with one result toast and no dialog, and still never calls the Hermes or OpenClaw service controls. This task adds sessions to the shared stop logic (`src/ui/stopAllShared.ts`), wires the real requests (`src/ui/stopAll.ts`), lists sessions in the palette's dialog, and makes every sentence about the stop true again: the toast counts sessions, an OpenClaw session gets the honest "may still be finishing its last step" note, and the palette item becomes "Stop all agent work" (it no longer stops only runs; the hold keeps its name "Hold to stop all"). The Safety page and the hold's hidden hint say what is stopped and, as before, what is not (D11); the Safety page also names the two honest limits of a session's Stop, in the Help page's own words.

Why the order inside the stop: sessions and Team Rooms start stopping at the same moment (Q16, R22). Runs start as soon as the rooms are done, exactly as today (a stopped room starts no next turn), and they never wait for a session: a session's Stop takes a few seconds (the agent's own soft stop, then the process tree), and an emergency stop must not hold runs back for that.

```js
test("a list that never answers ends in the time limit, and is told apart from 'nothing running'", async () => {
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    const { deps: d, calls } = deps({ listRuns: never, listRooms: never, listSessions: never });
    const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(d);
    assert.equal(result.unreachable, true);
    assert.equal(calls.stopRun.length + calls.stopRoom.length + calls.stopSession.length, 0);
    const text = stop.stopAllMessage(result);
    assert.equal(text.tone, "danger");
    assert.match(text.message, /nothing was stopped/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(text.message, /Nothing was running/);
  });
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    // Runs answer, rooms do not: the runs are stopped, and the message says a room may carry on.
    const { deps: d, calls } = deps({ listRuns: async () => ({ runs: [run("a", "agent")] }), listRooms: never });
    const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(d);
    assert.deepEqual(calls.stopRun, ["a"]);
    assert.equal(result.unreachable, false);
    assert.equal(result.roomsChecked, false);
    const text = stop.stopAllMessage(result);
    assert.equal(text.tone, "warn");
    assert.match(text.message, /Couldn't read the list of Team Rooms/);
    assert.match(text.message, /Stopped 1 run\./);
  });
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    // Runs never answer, rooms answer with nothing: nothing was stopped, and the message says which list it could not read.
    const { deps: d } = deps({ listRuns: never, listRooms: async () => ({ rooms: [] }) });
    const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(d);
    assert.equal(result.unreachable, false);
    assert.equal(result.runsChecked, false);
    const text = stop.stopAllMessage(result);
    assert.equal(text.tone, "warn");
    assert.equal(text.message, "Couldn't read the list of runs, so no run was stopped. Check Runs.");
    assert.doesNotMatch(text.message, /Nothing was running|nothing to stop/);
  });
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    // Runs answer with nothing, rooms never answer: no run was running, and a room between turns may still carry on.
    const { deps: d } = deps({ listRooms: never });
    const text = stop.stopAllMessage(await stop.stopEverythingWith(d));
    assert.equal(text.tone, "warn");
    assert.match(text.message, /^No agent run was running\. Couldn't read the list of Team Rooms/);
  });
  // A reply that is not a list counts as no reply.
  const { deps: bad } = deps({
    listRuns: async () => ({ runs: "oops" }),
    listRooms: async () => ({ rooms: null }),
    listSessions: async () => ({ sessions: { id: "s1" } })
  });
  assert.equal((await stop.stopEverythingWith(bad)).unreachable, true);
});
```

```js
    assert.equal(result.unreachable, false);
    assert.deepEqual(stop.stopAllMessage(result), {
      message: "Stopped 1 run. Couldn't read the list of sessions, so no session was stopped. Check Sessions.",
      tone: "warn"
    });
  });
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    const { deps: d } = deps({ listSessions: never });
    const text = stop.stopAllMessage(await stop.stopEverythingWith(d));
    assert.equal(text.message, "No agent run was running. Couldn't read the list of sessions, so no session was stopped. Check Sessions.");
    assert.doesNotMatch(text.message, /nothing to stop|Nothing was running/);
    assert.equal(text.tone, "warn");
  });
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    const { deps: d, calls } = deps({ listRuns: never, listRooms: never, listSessions: never });
    const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(d);
    assert.equal(calls.stopSession.length, 0);
    assert.deepEqual(stop.stopAllMessage(result), {
      message: "Couldn't reach Agent OS, so nothing was stopped. Try again, or stop each session on Sessions and each run on Runs.",
      tone: "danger"
    });
  });
  // A reply that is not a list is treated like no reply.
  const { deps: bad } = deps({ listSessions: async () => ({ sessions: "oops" }) });
  assert.equal((await stop.lookForStoppable(bad)).sessionsChecked, false);
});

test("an OpenClaw session that was stopped adds the honest note: OpenClaw may still finish the step it was on", async () => {
  const { deps: d } = deps({ listSessions: async () => ({ sessions: [session("oc", { agentId: "openclaw" }), session("cc")] }) });
  const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(d);
  assert.equal(result.openClawStopped, 1);
  assert.deepEqual(stop.stopAllMessage(result), { message: "Stopped 2 sessions. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step.", tone: "ok" });
  // No OpenClaw session stopped, no note: a failed OpenClaw stop is reported as a failure only.
  const { deps: failed } = deps({
    listSessions: async () => ({ sessions: [session("oc", { agentId: "openclaw" })] }),
    stopSession: async () => {
      throw new Error("refused");
    }
  });
  assert.doesNotMatch(stop.stopAllMessage(await stop.stopEverythingWith(failed)).message, /finishing its last step/);
});

test("withSessionAnswers: not_available means no session can run here; unknown_session, or an answer that says it ended by itself, is 'already ended'", async () => {
  // The refusal request() in src/api.ts throws: an ApiError whose message is the server's short code.
  const apiError = (code, status) => Object.assign(new Error(code), { name: "ApiError", status, detail: "" });

  // Sessions only exist when Agent OS runs on this computer (local mode); elsewhere the list answers not_available.
  const notHere = stop.withSessionAnswers(
    deps({
      listSessions: async () => {
        throw apiError("not_available", 404);
      }
    }).deps
  );
  const quiet = await stop.stopEverythingWith(notHere);
  assert.equal(quiet.sessionsChecked, true);
  assert.deepEqual(stop.stopAllMessage(quiet), { message: "Nothing was running, so there was nothing to stop.", tone: "neutral" });

  // Any other failure of the list still means the list could not be read.
  for (const thrown of [apiError("internal_error", 500), new Error("Failed to fetch"), null]) {
    const wrapped = stop.withSessionAnswers(
      deps({
        listSessions: async () => {
          throw thrown;
        }
      }).deps
    );
    assert.equal((await stop.stopEverythingWith(wrapped)).sessionsChecked, false, String(thrown));
  }

  const stopOne = (stopSession) =>
    stop.stopEverythingWith(stop.withSessionAnswers(deps({ listSessions: async () => ({ sessions: [session("s1")] }), stopSession }).deps));
  const counts = (result) => [result.sessionsStopped, result.sessionsAlreadyEnded, result.sessionsFailed];
  assert.deepEqual(counts(await stopOne(async () => ({ id: "s1", status: "exited", endedBy: "stop", note: null }))), [1, 0, 0], "stopped by this stop");
  assert.deepEqual(
    counts(await stopOne(async () => ({ id: "s1", status: "exited", endedBy: null, exitCode: 0, note: null }))),
    [0, 1, 0],
    "it had ended by itself"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(counts(await stopOne(async () => ({ id: "s1", status: "exited", endedBy: "quit", note: null }))), [0, 1, 0], "it ended when Agent OS quit");
  assert.deepEqual(
    counts(
      await stopOne(async () => {
        throw apiError("unknown_session", 404);
      })
    ),
    [0, 1, 0],
    "it is gone"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    counts(
      await stopOne(async () => {
        throw Object.assign(new Error("gone"), { code: "unknown_session" });
      })
    ),
    [0, 1, 0],
    "a refusal that carries `code` works too"
  );
  for (const thrown of [apiError("internal_error", 500), apiError("not_available", 404), new Error("Failed to fetch"), "a string", undefined]) {
    assert.deepEqual(
      counts(
        await stopOne(async () => {
          throw thrown;
        })
      ),
      [0, 0, 1],
      String(thrown)
    );
  }
  // An answer this logic does not recognise is a stop the server said yes to.
  assert.deepEqual(counts(await stopOne(async () => ({ ok: true }))), [1, 0, 0]);
});
```

```ts
// The logic behind "Hold to stop all" and the palette's "Stop all agent work" (design spec D11,
// SP2 ruling R14, SP3 ruling R22 and planning decision Q16), with no imports except types, so the
// logic tests can load it straight from src/ with Node. The pieces that talk to Agent OS (listRuns,
// stopRun, listTeamRooms, stopTeamRoom, the sessions list and each session's Stop) and the agent-work
// rule (agentWork.ts) are passed in; stopAll.ts passes the real ones.
//
// What it stops: every session that has not ended, of both kinds (an agent's own terminal, and an
// agent's updater running as an `update` session); every AGENT run that is queued or running; and every
// Team Room that is running (a room between two turns has no active run, so stopping runs alone would
// miss it and its next turn would start), plus the room the server holds its active slot for even if it
// still reads "needs you" (a decision was just made and the room is about to resume).
// It never touches the Hermes background service or the OpenClaw Gateway (it never calls their service
// controls), and it never interrupts Agent OS's own setup jobs: stopping a gateway restart can leave the
// gateway down, and stopping an install can leave a half-installed tool. A session's Stop is the same Stop
// sequence as the Sessions page's Stop session: the agent's own soft stop, then its whole process tree.
import type { RunMeta, TeamRoomSummary } from "../types";

const ACTIVE = new Set(["queued", "running"]);
// The one session status that means there is nothing left to stop. Every other one (starting, live,
// waiting, idle, held, and any we have not heard of) is stopped: an emergency stop errs toward stopping.
const SESSION_ENDED = "exited";

// A hung server must never leave a button on "Stopping…" for ever.
export const LIST_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;
export const STOP_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000;

// What `stopRoom` hands back when the server said the room was not running: it had ended by itself
// between the look and the stop. It is counted apart, never as a room we stopped.
export const ROOM_ALREADY_ENDED = "room_already_ended";
// The same for a session (withSessionAnswers below): it had ended by itself before the stop reached it.
export const SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED = "session_already_ended";

// The most runs the server returns for one list (the cap in listRuns in
// server/runtime/runs/run-manager.js). It lists the newest first and cannot
// filter by status, so if the list comes back full, older runs were not seen.
export const MAX_RUNS = 1000;

export type StoppableRun = Pick<RunMeta, "id" | "kind" | "status"> & { title?: string };
export type StoppableRoom = Pick<TeamRoomSummary, "id" | "status"> & { task?: string };
// The fields of a session (GET /api/sessions?kind=all; SessionSummary in
// server/runtime/sessions/manager.js) that this logic reads. A full SessionSummary fits it.
export interface StoppableSession {
  id: string;
  status: string;
  kind?: string;
  agentId?: string;
  agentLabel?: string;
  folderName?: string;
  folderShown?: boolean;
}

export interface StopAllDeps {
  listRuns: (limit: number) => Promise<{ runs: StoppableRun[] }>;
  stopRun: (id: string) => Promise<unknown>;
  // `activeRoomId` is the room the server holds its one active slot for (GET /api/team-rooms). Older
  // servers do not send it.
  listRooms: () => Promise<{ rooms: StoppableRoom[]; activeRoomId?: string | null }>;
  stopRoom: (id: string) => Promise<unknown>;
  // Every session of both kinds (GET /api/sessions?kind=all) and one session's Stop
  // (POST /api/sessions/:id/stop, which answers the session's summary).
  listSessions: () => Promise<{ sessions: StoppableSession[] }>;
  stopSession: (id: string) => Promise<unknown>;
  isAgentWork: (run: { kind: string }) => boolean;
}

// Wraps the real requests so that a stop the server answers with `room_not_running` (the room ended
// by itself between the look and the stop) hands back ROOM_ALREADY_ENDED instead of failing. That is
// not a failure, and it is not a stop we made either: the words count it apart. Any other refusal
// still fails as before. Lives here, not in stopAll.ts, so the logic tests can reach it.
export function withEndedRooms(deps: StopAllDeps): StopAllDeps {
  return {
    ...deps,
    stopRoom: async (id) => {
      try {
        return await deps.stopRoom(id);
      } catch (error) {
        const code = typeof error === "object" && error !== null ? (error as { code?: unknown }).code : undefined;
        if (code === "room_not_running") return ROOM_ALREADY_ENDED;
        throw error;
      }
    }
  };
}

// The short code of a refusal. A TeamRoomError carries it in `code`; an ApiError (src/api.ts request())
// keeps the server's short code in `message`.
function refusalCode(error: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof error !== "object" || error === null) return undefined;
  const { code, name, message } = error as { code?: unknown; name?: unknown; message?: unknown };
  if (typeof code === "string") return code;
  return name === "ApiError" && typeof message === "string" ? message : undefined;
}

// A Stop answer (the session's summary) that says the session had ended before this stop: it reads
// "exited", and not because of a Stop (it ended by itself, or when Agent OS quit).
function endedOnItsOwn(answer: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof answer !== "object" || answer === null) return false;
  const { status, endedBy } = answer as { status?: unknown; endedBy?: unknown };
  return status === SESSION_ENDED && endedBy !== "stop";
}

// Wraps the real session requests:
// - the list: sessions exist only when Agent OS runs on this computer (local mode). Anywhere else every
//   sessions route answers `not_available`, so no session can be running: that is a list read, with
//   nothing in it. Any other failure still means the list could not be read.
// - one stop: `unknown_session`, or an answer that says the session had ended by itself, hands back
//   SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED (counted apart, never as a session we stopped). Any other refusal still fails.
export function withSessionAnswers(deps: StopAllDeps): StopAllDeps {
  return {
    ...deps,
    listSessions: async () => {
      try {
        return await deps.listSessions();
      } catch (error) {
        if (refusalCode(error) === "not_available") return { sessions: [] };
        throw error;
      }
    },
    stopSession: async (id) => {
      try {
        const answer = await deps.stopSession(id);
        return endedOnItsOwn(answer) ? SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED : answer;
      } catch (error) {
        if (refusalCode(error) === "unknown_session") return SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED;
        throw error;
      }
    }
  };
}

// What a look found. A list that could not be read leaves its part empty and its
// `...Checked` flag false: "nothing found" is only said when the list was read.
export interface StopLook {
  runs: StoppableRun[];
  rooms: StoppableRoom[];
  sessions: StoppableSession[];
  // Active runs left alone on purpose because they are setup or service jobs.
  skipped: number;
  // True when the run list was full, so older runs may not have been checked.
  listTruncated: boolean;
  runsChecked: boolean;
  roomsChecked: boolean;
  sessionsChecked: boolean;
}

export interface StopAllResult {
  // Active agent runs we tried to stop, and how each went. `timedOut` = no answer in time, so
  // the run may well have stopped, or may still be running: it is not "could not be stopped".
  found: number;
  stopped: number;
  failed: number;
  timedOut: number;
  // Running Team Rooms we tried to stop, and how each went.
  rooms: number;
  roomsStopped: number;
  roomsFailed: number;
  roomsTimedOut: number;
  // Rooms among those that had already ended by themselves when the stop reached them.
  // They are part of `rooms`, but not of `roomsStopped`.
  roomsAlreadyEnded: number;
  // Sessions (both kinds) that had not ended, and how each stop went, counted the same way.
  sessions: number;
  sessionsStopped: number;
  sessionsFailed: number;
  sessionsTimedOut: number;
  sessionsAlreadyEnded: number;
  // OpenClaw sessions among the stopped ones: their terminal is closed, but OpenClaw's Gateway may
  // still finish the step it was on (spec "Stop sequence"), so the words say so.
  openClawStopped: number;
  skipped: number;
  runsChecked: boolean;
  roomsChecked: boolean;
  sessionsChecked: boolean;
  // Nothing could be read at all: nothing was stopped.
  unreachable: boolean;
  listTruncated: boolean;
}

type Outcome = "ok" | "timeout" | "error" | "ended";

// Waits for a promise for at most `ms`. Never rejects: it says how it went. A timeout is not an
// error: the request may well have been carried out.
function attempt(promise: Promise<unknown>, ms: number): Promise<Outcome> {
  return new Promise<Outcome>((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve("timeout"), ms);
    promise.then(
      (value) => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        resolve(value === ROOM_ALREADY_ENDED || value === SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED ? "ended" : "ok");
      },
      () => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        resolve("error");
      }
    );
  });
}

// The answer, or null when the request failed or did not answer in time.
async function readWithin<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T | null> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    return await Promise.race([
      promise,
      new Promise<null>((resolve) => {
        timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), ms);
      })
    ]);
  } catch {
    return null;
  } finally {
    if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

// Looks at what is running. Never throws.
//
// A room is stoppable when it reads "running", and also when the server names it as its active room
// whatever it reads: a room whose decision was just made can still read "needs you" on disk while the
// server already holds its one active slot and is getting ready to resume it. Asking the server which
// room that is costs nothing extra: it comes with the same room list.
export async function lookForStoppable(deps: StopAllDeps): Promise<StopLook> {
  const [runsAnswer, roomsAnswer, sessionsAnswer] = await Promise.all([
    readWithin(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.listRuns(MAX_RUNS)), LIST_TIMEOUT_MS),
    readWithin(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.listRooms()), LIST_TIMEOUT_MS),
    readWithin(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.listSessions()), LIST_TIMEOUT_MS)
  ]);
  // A reply that is not a list is treated like no reply: we could not check.
  const runList = runsAnswer && Array.isArray(runsAnswer.runs) ? runsAnswer.runs : null;
  const roomList = roomsAnswer && Array.isArray(roomsAnswer.rooms) ? roomsAnswer.rooms : null;
  const sessionList = sessionsAnswer && Array.isArray(sessionsAnswer.sessions) ? sessionsAnswer.sessions : null;
  const activeId = roomList && typeof roomsAnswer?.activeRoomId === "string" && roomsAnswer.activeRoomId ? roomsAnswer.activeRoomId : null;
  const active = (runList || []).filter((run) => ACTIVE.has(run.status));
  const runs = active.filter((run) => deps.isAgentWork(run));
  const rooms = (roomList || []).filter((room) => room.status === "running" || room.id === activeId);
  // The server holds a room the list did not show (the list is capped): it is still stopped.
  if (activeId !== null && !rooms.some((room) => room.id === activeId)) rooms.push({ id: activeId, status: "running" });
  // An entry with no usable id cannot be stopped by id, so it is never sent.
  const sessions = (sessionList || []).filter(
    (session) => typeof session === "object" && session !== null && typeof session.id === "string" && session.id !== "" && session.status !== SESSION_ENDED
  );
  return {
    runs,
    rooms,
    sessions,
    skipped: active.length - runs.length,
    listTruncated: runList !== null && runList.length >= MAX_RUNS,
    runsChecked: runList !== null,
    roomsChecked: roomList !== null,
    sessionsChecked: sessionList !== null
  };
}

function tally(outcomes: Outcome[]) {
  return {
    stopped: outcomes.filter((o) => o === "ok").length,
    failed: outcomes.filter((o) => o === "error").length,
    timedOut: outcomes.filter((o) => o === "timeout").length,
    alreadyEnded: outcomes.filter((o) => o === "ended").length
  };
}

// Stops what the look found. Sessions and rooms start together (planning decision Q16). Runs follow the
// rooms: stopping a room sets its "stop" flag as well as stopping its current turn, so no next turn starts
// when that turn ends. Runs never wait for a session, whose Stop takes a few seconds (the agent's soft stop,
// then the kill). Nothing is read again afterwards, so a stop never waits on an extra request.
export async function stopWhatWasFound(deps: StopAllDeps, look: StopLook): Promise<StopAllResult> {
  const sessionList = look.sessions ?? [];
  const sessionsDone = Promise.all(
    sessionList.map((session) => attempt(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.stopSession(session.id)), STOP_TIMEOUT_MS))
  );
  const roomOutcomes = await Promise.all(
    look.rooms.map((room) => attempt(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.stopRoom(room.id)), STOP_TIMEOUT_MS))
  );
  const runOutcomes = await Promise.all(
    look.runs.map((run) => attempt(Promise.resolve().then(() => deps.stopRun(run.id)), STOP_TIMEOUT_MS))
  );
  const sessionOutcomes = await sessionsDone;
  const runs = tally(runOutcomes);
  const rooms = tally(roomOutcomes);
  const sessions = tally(sessionOutcomes);
  const sessionsChecked = look.sessionsChecked === true;
  return {
    found: look.runs.length,
    stopped: runs.stopped,
    failed: runs.failed,
    timedOut: runs.timedOut,
    rooms: look.rooms.length,
    roomsStopped: rooms.stopped,
    roomsFailed: rooms.failed,
    roomsTimedOut: rooms.timedOut,
    roomsAlreadyEnded: rooms.alreadyEnded,
    sessions: sessionList.length,
    sessionsStopped: sessions.stopped,
    sessionsFailed: sessions.failed,
    sessionsTimedOut: sessions.timedOut,
    sessionsAlreadyEnded: sessions.alreadyEnded,
    openClawStopped: sessionList.filter((session, index) => session.agentId === "openclaw" && sessionOutcomes[index] === "ok").length,
    skipped: look.skipped,
    runsChecked: look.runsChecked,
    roomsChecked: look.roomsChecked,
    sessionsChecked,
    unreachable: !look.runsChecked && !look.roomsChecked && !sessionsChecked,
    listTruncated: look.listTruncated
  };
}

export async function stopEverythingWith(deps: StopAllDeps): Promise<StopAllResult> {
  return stopWhatWasFound(deps, await lookForStoppable(deps));
}

// ---- the words ----------------------------------------------------------------

const runWord = (n: number) => `${n} run${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
const roomWord = (n: number) => `${n} Team Room${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
const sessionWord = (n: number) => `${n} session${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;

// "a", "a and b", "a, b and c".
function listWords(parts: string[]): string {
  if (parts.length <= 1) return parts[0] ?? "";
  return `${parts.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} and ${parts[parts.length - 1]}`;
}

// Where to look afterwards: Sessions for sessions, Runs for runs, Team Room for rooms.
function checkWhere(runs: number, rooms: number, sessions = 0): string {
  const places: string[] = [];
  if (sessions > 0) places.push("Sessions");
  if (runs > 0) places.push("Runs");
  if (rooms > 0) places.push("Team Room");
  return `check ${listWords(places.length > 0 ? places : ["Runs"])}`;
}

// "2 runs", "1 Team Room", "2 runs and 1 Team Room", "1 session, 2 runs and 1 Team Room".
export function thingsWord(runs: number, rooms: number, sessions = 0): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (sessions > 0) parts.push(sessionWord(sessions));
  if (runs > 0) parts.push(runWord(runs));
  if (rooms > 0) parts.push(roomWord(rooms));
  return parts.length > 0 ? listWords(parts) : runWord(0);
}

// How the palette's list names a session: the same words as the Sessions page (sessionTitle in
// src/ui/sessionsShared.ts): "<agent> · <folder>", "<agent> · Set by OpenClaw", "<agent> update".
// "—" means unknown.
export function sessionStopTitle(session: StoppableSession): string {
  const agent = session.agentLabel || session.agentId || "Agent";
  if (session.kind === "update") return `${agent} update`;
  if (session.folderShown === false) return `${agent} · Set by OpenClaw`;
  return `${agent} · ${session.folderName || "—"}`;
}

export function stopAllMessage(result: StopAllResult): { message: string; tone: "ok" | "warn" | "danger" | "neutral" } {
  if (result.unreachable) {
    return {
      message: "Couldn't reach Agent OS, so nothing was stopped. Try again, or stop each session on Sessions and each run on Runs.",
      tone: "danger"
    };
  }
  // A result from before sessions were stopped has no session fields: they read as "checked, none".
  const sessionsFound = result.sessions ?? 0;
  const sessionsStopped = result.sessionsStopped ?? 0;
  const sessionsFailed = result.sessionsFailed ?? 0;
  const sessionsTimedOut = result.sessionsTimedOut ?? 0;
  const sessionsEnded = result.sessionsAlreadyEnded ?? 0;
  const sessionsChecked = result.sessionsChecked !== false;
  // Said whenever the list was full: never claim "nothing was running" then.
  const notChecked = result.listTruncated ? " Older runs were not checked." : "";
  // Said for every list that could not be read: what it holds was not stopped.
  const unread = [
    result.runsChecked ? "" : " Couldn't read the list of runs, so no run was stopped. Check Runs.",
    sessionsChecked ? "" : " Couldn't read the list of sessions, so no session was stopped. Check Sessions.",
    result.roomsChecked ? "" : " Couldn't read the list of Team Rooms, so a room that is between two turns may still carry on. Check Team Room."
  ].join("");
  // Said whenever setup or service jobs were left running, so the person knows why.
  const left =
    result.skipped === 0
      ? ""
      : result.skipped === 1
        ? " 1 setup or service job was left running. It is not agent work; manage it in Setup or Agents."
        : ` ${result.skipped} setup or service jobs were left running. They are not agent work; manage them in Setup or Agents.`;
  const total = result.found + result.rooms + sessionsFound;
  if (total === 0) {
    if (unread) {
      // A list could not be read, so "nothing was running" cannot be said; the run list, if read, had nothing to stop.
      const head = result.runsChecked ? "No agent run was running." : "";
      return { message: `${head}${unread}${left}`.trim(), tone: "warn" };
    }
    if (result.listTruncated) {
      const head = result.skipped > 0 ? `No agent work was running in the newest ${MAX_RUNS} runs.` : `None of the newest ${MAX_RUNS} runs were running.`;
      return { message: `${head}${left}${notChecked}`, tone: "warn" };
    }
    const head = result.skipped > 0 ? "No agent work was running, so there was nothing to stop." : "Nothing was running, so there was nothing to stop.";
    return { message: `${head}${left}`, tone: "neutral" };
  }
  const stoppedAny = result.stopped + result.roomsStopped + sessionsStopped > 0;
  const failedAny = result.failed + result.roomsFailed + sessionsFailed > 0;
  const timedOutAny = result.timedOut + result.roomsTimedOut + sessionsTimedOut > 0;
  // Rooms and sessions that ended by themselves before the stop reached them: said apart, never as "stopped".
  const roomsEnded = result.roomsAlreadyEnded ?? 0;
  const endedAny = roomsEnded + sessionsEnded > 0;
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (stoppedAny) parts.push(`Stopped ${thingsWord(result.stopped, result.roomsStopped, sessionsStopped)}.`);
  else if (failedAny || timedOutAny || !endedAny) parts.push("Nothing was confirmed stopped.");
  if (failedAny) {
    parts.push(
      `${thingsWord(result.failed, result.roomsFailed, sessionsFailed)} could not be stopped: ${checkWhere(result.failed, result.roomsFailed, sessionsFailed)}.`
    );
  }
  if (timedOutAny) {
    // No answer is not "could not be stopped": the stop may have gone through.
    const n = result.timedOut + result.roomsTimedOut + sessionsTimedOut;
    parts.push(
      `Agent OS did not answer in time about ${thingsWord(result.timedOut, result.roomsTimedOut, sessionsTimedOut)}, so ${n === 1 ? "it" : "they"} may still be running: ${checkWhere(result.timedOut, result.roomsTimedOut, sessionsTimedOut)}.`
    );
  }
  if (endedAny) {
    // "So there was nothing to stop" is said only when that is known: nothing else happened and every list
    // was read in full. With a list that could not be read (or was full), only what was seen is said.
    const ended = thingsWord(0, roomsEnded, sessionsEnded);
    const onlyEnded = !stoppedAny && !failedAny && !timedOutAny && !unread && !result.listTruncated;
    parts.push(onlyEnded ? `${ended} had already ended, so there was nothing to stop.` : `${ended} had already ended.`);
  }
  // OpenClaw's terminal is closed, but its Gateway may still finish the step it was on (spec "Stop sequence").
  if ((result.openClawStopped ?? 0) > 0) parts.push("OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step.");
  const clean = !failedAny && !timedOutAny;
  const calm = clean && !result.listTruncated && !unread;
  return {
    message: `${parts.join(" ")}${unread}${left}${notChecked}`,
    tone: calm ? (stoppedAny ? "ok" : "neutral") : "warn"
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Wire the real requests.** Replace the whole of `src/ui/stopAll.ts` with:

```ts
import { listRuns, listTeamRooms, request, stopRun, stopTeamRoom } from "../api";
import { isAgentWork } from "./agentWork";
import type { StoppableSession } from "./stopAllShared";
import { lookForStoppable, stopEverythingWith, stopWhatWasFound, withEndedRooms, withSessionAnswers } from "./stopAllShared";

// What "Hold to stop all" stops (design spec D11, SP2 ruling R14, SP3 ruling R22 and planning decision
// Q16): every session that has not ended, of both kinds (an agent's own terminal, and an agent's updater
// running as an `update` session), every AGENT run that is queued or running, including Team Room turns,
// and every Team Room that is running (a room between two turns has no active run, so it would otherwise
// start its next turn). A session is stopped with the same Stop as the Sessions page's Stop session,
// without its question: the hold is the emergency stop.
// It never touches the Hermes background service or the OpenClaw Gateway (it never calls their service
// controls), and it never interrupts Agent OS's own setup jobs: stopping a gateway restart can leave the
// gateway down, and stopping an install can leave a half-installed tool.
//
// The logic and the words are in stopAllShared.ts (no imports but types, so the logic
// tests can load it). This file hands it the real requests and the agent-work rule.
//
// Which kinds are Agent OS's own jobs (and so are not stopped) lives in agentWork.ts.
// Any other kind, including "agent", "team-turn", a missing kind and a kind we have
// not heard of, IS stopped: an emergency stop errs toward stopping agent work.
export { MAX_RUNS, sessionStopTitle, stopAllMessage, thingsWord } from "./stopAllShared";
export type { StopAllResult, StopLook } from "./stopAllShared";

// A room that ended on its own between the look and the stop (the server answers room_not_running)
// is not a failure, and was not stopped by us either: withEndedRooms (stopAllShared.ts) counts it apart.
// withSessionAnswers does the same for a session, and reads "sessions are not available here" (Agent OS
// not running on this computer) as "no session is running".
export const realStopAllDeps = withSessionAnswers(
  withEndedRooms({
    listRuns: (limit) => listRuns({ limit }),
    stopRun: (id) => stopRun(id),
    listRooms: () => listTeamRooms(),
    stopRoom: (id) => stopTeamRoom(id),
    // Both kinds of session: kind=all (planning decision Q24).
    listSessions: () => request<{ sessions: StoppableSession[] }>("/api/sessions?kind=all"),
    stopSession: (id) => request<unknown>(`/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/stop`, { method: "POST", body: "{}" }),
    isAgentWork
  })
);

export function stopEverything() {
  return stopEverythingWith(realStopAllDeps);
}

// The palette's "Stop all agent work" looks first, shows what it would stop, and stops only on a yes.
export const lookForWhatToStop = () => lookForStoppable(realStopAllDeps);
export const stopWhatWasLookedAt = (look: Parameters<typeof stopWhatWasFound>[1]) => stopWhatWasFound(realStopAllDeps, look);
```

- [ ] **Step 7: List sessions in the palette's dialog.** Replace the whole of `src/ui/components/StopAllRunsModal.tsx` with:

```tsx
// "Stop all agent work" from the ⌘K palette. It is the keyboard way to do what "Hold to stop all" does, so it
// follows the same rule (SP2 ruling R14, SP3 ruling R22, planning decision Q16): sessions of both kinds and
// agent work only, never the Hermes or OpenClaw background service and never Agent OS's own setup jobs, and
// the same time limits (src/ui/stopAllShared.ts). It looks at what is really running first, says what it
// would stop, and only stops once the person confirms.
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { StopAllResult, StopLook } from "../stopAll";
import { lookForWhatToStop, sessionStopTitle, stopAllMessage, stopWhatWasLookedAt, thingsWord } from "../stopAll";
import AgentConfirmModal from "./AgentConfirmModal";

const SHOWN_TITLES = 5;

export default function StopAllRunsModal({
  onClose,
  onDone
}: {
  onClose: () => void;
  // Called with the result when everything was stopped, so the window can say so (the same toast as the hold).
  onDone?: (result: StopAllResult) => void;
}) {
  // null = still looking.
  const [look, setLook] = useState<StopLook | null>(null);
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState("");
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const alive = useRef(true);

  async function lookAgain() {
    const next = await lookForWhatToStop();
    if (alive.current) setLook(next);
    return next;
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    alive.current = true;
    void lookAgain();
    return () => {
      alive.current = false;
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  const runs = look?.runs ?? [];
  const rooms = look?.rooms ?? [];
  const sessions = look?.sessions ?? [];
  const count = runs.length + rooms.length + sessions.length;

  async function confirm() {
    if (!look || count === 0) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setNotice("");
    const result = await stopWhatWasLookedAt(look);
    if (!alive.current) return;
    setBusy(false);
    const clean =
      result.failed + result.timedOut + result.roomsFailed + result.roomsTimedOut + result.sessionsFailed + result.sessionsTimedOut === 0;
    if (clean) {
      if (onDone) onDone(result);
      onClose();
      return;
    }
    // Some did not stop, or did not answer in time. Say which, and look again at what is still going.
    setNotice(stopAllMessage(result).message);
    await lookAgain();
  }

  const unreadAll = look !== null && !look.runsChecked && !look.roomsChecked && !look.sessionsChecked;
  const readAll = look !== null && look.runsChecked && look.roomsChecked && look.sessionsChecked;
  const unreadSessions = look !== null && !unreadAll && !look.sessionsChecked;
  const unreadRuns = look !== null && !unreadAll && !look.runsChecked;
  const unreadRooms = look !== null && !unreadAll && !look.roomsChecked;
  const titles = [
    ...sessions.map((session) => ({ key: `session-${session.id}`, text: `Session: ${sessionStopTitle(session)}` })),
    ...rooms.map((room) => ({ key: `room-${room.id}`, text: `Team Room: ${room.task || room.id}` })),
    ...runs.map((run) => ({ key: `run-${run.id}`, text: run.title || run.id }))
  ];
  const openClawListed = sessions.some((session) => session.agentId === "openclaw");

  return (
    <AgentConfirmModal
      title="Stop all agent work?"
      confirmLabel={count > 0 ? `Stop ${thingsWord(runs.length, rooms.length, sessions.length)}` : "Stop all agent work"}
      confirmDisabled={look === null || count === 0}
      busy={busy}
      danger
      onConfirm={() => void confirm()}
      onClose={() => (busy ? null : onClose())}
    >
      {look === null ? <p role="status">Looking at what is running…</p> : null}
      {unreadAll ? (
        <p className="os-launch__error" role="alert">
          Couldn&apos;t read what is running. Agent OS did not answer in time. Close this and try again, or stop each session on Sessions and each
          run on Runs.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {unreadSessions ? (
        <p className="os-launch__error" role="alert">
          Couldn&apos;t read the list of sessions, so sessions are not listed. Check Sessions.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {unreadRuns ? (
        <p className="os-launch__error" role="alert">
          Couldn&apos;t read the list of runs, so runs are not listed. Check Runs.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {unreadRooms ? (
        <p className="os-launch__error" role="alert">
          Couldn&apos;t read the list of Team Rooms, so a room that is between two turns is not listed and may still carry on. Check Team Room.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {look && count === 0 && !unreadAll && !notice ? (
        <p>
          {!readAll
            ? "Nothing is running in the lists Agent OS could read."
            : look.skipped > 0
              ? "No agent work is running right now."
              : look.listTruncated
                ? "None of the newest runs are running."
                : "Nothing is running right now."}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {look && count > 0 ? (
        <>
          <p>
            This stops {thingsWord(runs.length, rooms.length, sessions.length)} that {count === 1 ? "is" : "are"} running now. Anything an agent
            already did stays done.
          </p>
          <ul>
            {titles.slice(0, SHOWN_TITLES).map((item) => (
              <li key={item.key}>{item.text}</li>
            ))}
            {count > SHOWN_TITLES ? <li>and {count - SHOWN_TITLES} more</li> : null}
          </ul>
          {openClawListed ? <p>OpenClaw may still finish its last step after the terminal closes.</p> : null}
        </>
      ) : null}
      {look && look.skipped > 0 ? (
        <p>
          {look.skipped === 1
            ? "1 setup or service job is left running. It is not agent work; manage it in Setup or Agents."
            : `${look.skipped} setup or service jobs are left running. They are not agent work; manage them in Setup or Agents.`}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {look && look.listTruncated ? <p>The list was full, so older runs were not checked.</p> : null}
      {notice ? (
        <p className="os-launch__error" role="alert">
          {notice}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </AgentConfirmModal>
  );
}
```

(Old behaviour fixed in passing: with one list unread and nothing found, the dialog used to say "Nothing is running right now." next to "Couldn't read the list of runs". It now says "Nothing is running in the lists Agent OS could read.")
