- [ ] **Step 12: Write the end-to-end test.** Append to the end of `test/stop-all.test.js`:

```js
// ---- end to end: real sessions of both kinds, stopped through the Stop route (in process) ---------
//
// The real session manager and the real sessions router (behind requireLocalMode, as server/index.js
// mounts it) on a real port, with W1's TUI-like fake agents on PATH, W1's stand-in login shell as SHELL
// and a temp HOME (H1: tests only; planning decision Q1c). The runs and rooms are fakes here (their own
// tests cover them), so this test is about the sessions: both kinds are found by GET
// /api/sessions?kind=all, each is stopped through POST /api/sessions/:id/stop, nothing but those two
// requests is ever made, and W1's gateway tripwire (FAKE_AGENT_LOG) shows that no session's Stop ran a
// Hermes or OpenClaw service control itself (design spec D11 and SP3 "done when").

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

async function waitFor(predicate, { timeoutMs = 15000, intervalMs = 50 } = {}) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    if (await predicate()) return;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, intervalMs));
  }
  throw new Error("timed out waiting for condition");
}

// The same answer rules as request() in src/api.ts: a refusal throws an ApiError whose message is the server's code.
async function httpJson(url, options = {}) {
  const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...options });
  const body = await response.json().catch(() => null);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw Object.assign(new Error(body?.error || `${response.status}`), { name: "ApiError", status: response.status, detail: body?.message || "" });
  }
  return body;
}

// The fakes' event log (W1): one JSON line per event, each with name, pid and at.
async function readFakeLog(file) {
  const text = await readFile(file, "utf8").catch((error) => {
    if (error.code === "ENOENT") return "";
    throw error;
  });
  return text
    .split("\n")
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
}

test(
  "end to end: the hold stops a real agent session, an OpenClaw session and a fake updater's update session through their Stop, with the runs, and never asks for a service control",
  { skip: isWindows ? "the fake agents are POSIX shims (the sessions engine's own tests cover Windows)" : false },
  async () => {
    // Real paths: on macOS os.tmpdir() sits behind a symlink, and the folder policy compares real paths.
    const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-stopall-home-")));
    const agentOsHome = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-stopall-data-")));
    const bin = path.join(home, "fake-bin");
    const folder = path.join(home, "projects", "my-app");
    const logFile = path.join(home, "fake.log");
    try {
      await mkdir(folder, { recursive: true });
      // All six names in the TUI mode (planning decision Q1c), then the hermes shim again as the fake
      // updater, so the update session is an updater waiting at its question.
      await makeFakeAgentBin(bin);
      await makeFakeAgentBin(bin, { names: ["hermes"], mode: "updater" });
      await withEnv(
        {
          HOME: home,
          USERPROFILE: home,
          AGENT_OS_HOME: agentOsHome,
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined,
          AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: path.join(home, ".agent-os"),
          SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
          PATH: [bin, ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter),
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS: undefined,
          // W1's tripwire: every fake (the sessions and any soft-stop CLI call) logs here. The login-shell
          // environment is read after resetLoginShellEnvForTests() below, so the sessions inherit it.
          FAKE_AGENT_LOG: logFile,
          FAKE_AGENT_MODE: undefined,
          HERMES_HOME: undefined,
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_ENABLE_EXEC: undefined,
          DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE: undefined,
          HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH: undefined
        },
        async () => {
          assert.equal(os.homedir(), home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
          clearDetectCaches();
          resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
          await setExecutionGateStatus({ enabled: true, reason: "stop-all test" });
          const manager = createSessionManager();
          const requests = [];
          const app = express();
          app.use((req, _res, next) => {
            requests.push(`${req.method} ${req.originalUrl}`);
            next();
          });
          app.use(express.json());
          app.use("/api/sessions", requireLocalMode, createSessionsRouter({ manager }));
          // A service control that must never be reached (D11).
          app.post("/api/agents/:id/service/:action", (_req, res) => res.status(500).json({ error: "service_control_called" }));
          app.use((error, _req, res, _next) => res.status(500).json({ error: error.message }));
          const server = await new Promise((resolve) => {
            const listening = app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => resolve(listening));
          });
          const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`;
          const ids = [];
          try {
            const claude = await manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder });
            // OpenClaw picks its own folder for now (OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED is false), so no folder is sent.
            const openclaw = await manager.create({ agentId: "openclaw", folder: null });
            const update = await manager.createUpdateSession({ agentId: "hermes", folder });
            assert.equal(update.kind, "update");
            ids.push(claude.id, openclaw.id, update.id);
            // Each fake terminal program has started (its first output takes it out of "starting") and keeps running.
            for (const id of ids) {
              await waitFor(async () => (await manager.get(id)).status !== "starting");
              assert.notEqual((await manager.get(id)).status, "exited", `${id} keeps running until it is stopped`);
            }

            const runsStopped = [];
            const result = await stop.stopEverythingWith(
              stop.withSessionAnswers({
                listRuns: async () => ({ runs: [run("a1", "agent"), run("gw", "service")] }),
                stopRun: async (id) => {
                  runsStopped.push(id);
                  return {};
                },
                listRooms: async () => ({ rooms: [] }),
                stopRoom: async () => ({}),
                listSessions: () => httpJson(`${base}/api/sessions?kind=all`),
                stopSession: (id) => httpJson(`${base}/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/stop`, { method: "POST", body: "{}" }),
                isAgentWork: work.isAgentWork
              })
            );

            assert.equal(result.sessionsChecked, true);
            assert.equal(result.sessions, 3, "both kinds are found: two agent sessions and the update session");
            assert.equal(result.sessionsStopped, 3);
            assert.equal(result.sessionsFailed + result.sessionsTimedOut + result.sessionsAlreadyEnded, 0);
            assert.equal(result.openClawStopped, 1);
            assert.deepEqual(runsStopped, ["a1"], "the agent run is stopped; the Hermes gateway job (a service run) is left alone");
            for (const id of ids) {
              const after = await manager.get(id);
              assert.equal(after.status, "exited", id);
              assert.equal(after.endedBy, "stop", id);
            }
            assert.deepEqual(stop.stopAllMessage(result), {
              message:
                "Stopped 3 sessions and 1 run. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step. 1 setup or service job was left running. It is not agent work; manage it in Setup or Agents.",
              tone: "ok"
            });
            const others = requests.filter(
              (line) => line !== "GET /api/sessions?kind=all" && !/^POST \/api\/sessions\/[0-9a-f-]+\/stop$/.test(line)
            );
            assert.deepEqual(others, [], "only the sessions list and each session's Stop were requested");
            assert.equal(requests.filter((line) => line.startsWith("POST ")).length, 3, "one Stop per session");

            const entries = await readFakeLog(logFile);
            // Each fake terminal program started as its session, and its own Stop ended it with SIGTERM.
            const started = entries.filter((entry) => entry.event === "start");
            assert.deepEqual(started.map((entry) => entry.name).sort(), ["claude", "hermes", "openclaw"]);
            const updater = started.find((entry) => entry.name === "hermes");
            assert.equal(updater.mode, "updater");
            assert.deepEqual(updater.argv, ["update"], "the update session runs the fake updater");
            for (const entry of started) {
              assert.ok(entries.some((other) => other.event === "sigterm" && other.pid === entry.pid), `${entry.name} was stopped with SIGTERM`);
            }
            // No HTTP request is not enough: a session's own Stop could run `hermes gateway stop` or
            // `openclaw gateway stop` itself. The OpenClaw soft stop makes no CLI call yet (Task S7, until
            // spike S5), so any "gateway" line in the fakes' log is a service control.
            assert.deepEqual(entries.filter((entry) => entry.event === "gateway"), [], "no session stop touched a Gateway or service");
          } finally {
            await manager.shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" });
            // The exit handler writes meta.json once the process has ended; wait for it, so nothing writes
            // into the temp folders after they are removed.
            for (const id of ids) {
              await waitFor(
                async () => {
                  try {
                    return JSON.parse(await readFile(path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions", id, "meta.json"), "utf8")).status === "exited";
                  } catch {
                    return false;
                  }
                },
                { timeoutMs: 5000 }
              ).catch(() => {});
            }
            server.closeAllConnections?.();
            await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(resolve));
            resetLoginShellEnvForTests();
            clearDetectCaches();
          }
        }
      );
    } finally {
      await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 });
      await rm(agentOsHome, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 });
    }
  }
);
```

(d) Create `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/holdsessions.mjs`:

```js
// Task S10: Hold to stop all and the palette's "Stop all agent work" include sessions (both kinds).
//   node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/holdsessions.mjs
//
// The sessions list and each session's Stop are STUBBED with context.route, in the shapes of
// server/runtime/sessions/routes.js (GET /api/sessions?kind=all; POST /api/sessions/:id/stop, which
// answers the summary plus `note`), so this probe needs no live session and starts none. Everything else
// (runs, Team Rooms, the shell, the Safety page) is the real throwaway server.
const W = 1470, H = 956;
const json = (route, body, status = 200) => route.fulfill({ status, contentType: "application/json", body: JSON.stringify(body) });
const isList = (url) => url.pathname === "/api/sessions" && url.searchParams.get("kind") === "all";
const isStop = (url) => /^\/api\/sessions\/[^/]+\/stop$/.test(url.pathname);
const NOW = new Date().toISOString();
const OPENCLAW_NOTE = "Stopped the terminal. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step.";
const summary = (over) => ({
  id: "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  kind: "agent",
  agentId: "claude",
  agentLabel: "Claude Code",
  folder: "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
  folderName: "my-app",
  folderShown: true,
  branch: null,
  status: "live",
  stateSince: NOW,
  startedAt: NOW,
  endedAt: null,
  exitCode: null,
  signal: null,
  endedBy: null,
  dismissed: false,
  brain: null,
  resume: { available: false, reason: null, fallback: false },
  alerts: "basic",
  recordingBytes: 0,
  ...over
});
const SESSIONS = [
  summary({}),
  summary({ id: "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", kind: "update", agentId: "hermes", agentLabel: "Hermes", folderName: "hermes-agent" }),
  summary({ id: "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", agentId: "openclaw", agentLabel: "OpenClaw", folderShown: false, folderName: "you" }),
  summary({ id: "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444", agentId: "codex", agentLabel: "Codex", status: "exited", endedAt: NOW, exitCode: 0 })
];
const LIST = { sessions: SESSIONS, environmentNotice: null, pty: { ok: true, reason: null }, maxLive: 8 };

export default async function ({ browser, openPage, shot, pass, fail }) {
  const check = (ok, name, why = "") => (ok ? pass(name) : fail(name, String(why).slice(0, 300)));
  const toastTexts = (tab) => tab.locator(".os-toast").allTextContents();
  const hold = async (tab) => {
    await tab.locator(".os-holdstop").hover();
    await tab.mouse.down();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1500);
    await tab.mouse.up();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1500);
  };
  const stubSessions = async (context, stopped) => {
    await context.route(isList, (route) => json(route, LIST));
    await context.route(isStop, (route) => {
      const id = new URL(route.request().url()).pathname.split("/")[3];
      stopped.push(id);
      const found = SESSIONS.find((s) => s.id === id) || summary({ id });
      const note = found.agentId === "openclaw" ? OPENCLAW_NOTE : null;
      return json(route, { ...found, status: "exited", endedAt: new Date().toISOString(), endedBy: "stop", signal: "SIGTERM", note });
    });
  };

  // 1. A full hold stops both kinds of session that have not ended: one toast, no dialog, no service control.
  {
    const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, W, H, "fleet");
    const stopped = [];
    const seen = [];
    tab.on("request", (request) => {
      const url = new URL(request.url());
      seen.push(`${request.method()} ${url.pathname}`);
    });
    await stubSessions(context, stopped);
    await hold(tab);
    const toasts = await toastTexts(tab);
    const text = toasts.join(" | ");
    check(toasts.length === 1, "one result toast", text);
    check(/^Stopped 3 sessions\./.test(text), "the toast counts the three running sessions (an agent, an update, OpenClaw)", text);
    check(/OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step\./.test(text), "the honest OpenClaw note", text);
    check(stopped.length === 3 && !stopped.includes(SESSIONS[3].id), "the ended Codex session is not stopped again", stopped.join(","));
    check((await tab.locator('[role="dialog"]').count()) === 0, "no dialog");
    check(!seen.some((line) => line.includes("/service/")), "no service control was requested", seen.filter((l) => l.includes("service")).join(","));
    check(!text.includes("—"), "no em dash in the toast", text);
    await shot(tab, "holdsessions", W, H, "toast");
    await context.close();
  }

  // 2. The palette's "Stop all agent work" names each session before the yes, at 1280x720.
  {
    const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, 1280, 720, "fleet");
    const stopped = [];
    await stubSessions(context, stopped);
    await tab.locator(".os-palette-trigger--field").click();
    await tab.keyboard.type("Stop all agent work");
    await tab.waitForTimeout(200);
    await tab.keyboard.press("Enter");
    await tab.getByText("Session: Claude Code · my-app").waitFor({ timeout: 10000 });
    const dialog = tab.getByRole("dialog");
    const body = (await dialog.innerText()) || "";
    check(/Stop all agent work\?/.test(body), "the dialog title", body);
    check(/Session: Hermes update/.test(body) && /Session: OpenClaw · Set by OpenClaw/.test(body), "both kinds are listed by name", body);
    check(!/Codex/.test(body), "an ended session is not listed", body);
    check(/OpenClaw may still finish its last step after the terminal closes\./.test(body), "the OpenClaw sentence comes before the yes", body);
    check(!body.includes("—"), "no em dash in the dialog", body);
    const confirm = dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Stop 3 sessions" });
    const box = await confirm.boundingBox();
    check(box !== null && box.y + box.height <= 720, "the confirm button is on screen at 1280x720", JSON.stringify(box));
    await shot(tab, "holdsessions", 1280, 720, "palette-dialog");
    await confirm.click();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1500);
    check((await tab.locator('[role="dialog"]').count()) === 0, "the dialog closes after a clean stop");
    check(stopped.length === 3, "each listed session got its own Stop", stopped.join(","));
    check(/^Stopped 3 sessions\./.test((await toastTexts(tab)).join(" ")), "the same toast as the hold");
    await context.close();
  }

  // 3. Sessions not available here (not local mode): no session can run, so nothing is said about them.
  {
    const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, W, H, "fleet");
    await context.route(isList, (route) => json(route, { error: "not_available" }, 404));
    await hold(tab);
    const text = (await toastTexts(tab)).join(" ");
    check(/Nothing was running, so there was nothing to stop\./.test(text) && !/session/i.test(text), "not_available reads as no session", text);
    await context.close();
  }

  // 4. The sessions list fails: the toast says so, and never "nothing to stop".
  {
    const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, W, H, "fleet");
    await context.route(isList, (route) => json(route, { error: "internal_error" }, 500));
    await hold(tab);
    const text = (await toastTexts(tab)).join(" ");
    check(/Couldn't read the list of sessions, so no session was stopped\. Check Sessions\./.test(text), "an unread list is said", text);
    check(!/nothing to stop/.test(text), "never 'nothing to stop' when a list was not read", text);
    await context.close();
  }

  // 5. The words on screen: the Safety page and the hold's description.
  {
    const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, W, H, "safety");
    const stopText = ((await tab.locator(".os-saf-stop").innerText()) || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ");
    check(/stops every session and every agent run/.test(stopText), "Safety says sessions are stopped", stopText);
    check(/does not stop the Hermes background service or the OpenClaw Gateway/.test(stopText), "D11 words", stopText);
    check(/choose Stop all agent work/.test(stopText), "the palette item by its new name", stopText);
    check(/\/bg may keep running/.test(stopText) && /OpenClaw may still finish its last step/.test(stopText), "the two honest limits of a session's Stop", stopText);
    check(!stopText.includes("—"), "no em dash", stopText);
    const hint = await tab.evaluate(() => (document.getElementById("os-holdstop-hint")?.textContent || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim());
    check(/every session and every agent run/.test(hint) && /Stop all agent work/.test(hint), "the hold's description", hint);
    await context.close();
  }
}
```

1. **Copy for the owner's review (E1, decision Q32).** The palette item and dialog names are the decided "Stop all agent work" / "Stop all agent work?" (R22). Try again, or stop each session on Sessions and each run on Runs.", "<n> session(s) had already ended…" and "OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step." (the spec's Stop result note without "Stopped the terminal."); in the dialog "Couldn't read the list of sessions, so sessions are not listed. Check Sessions." and "Nothing is running in the lists Agent OS could read."; on the Safety page the Help page's own sentence about the two honest limits (/bg, OpenClaw). The screenshots in Step 15 show the toast and the dialog.
2. **Deliberate: no `src/sessionsApi.ts` here.** S10 runs before U1, so `stopAll.ts` calls `request()` from `src/api.ts` for `GET /api/sessions?kind=all` and `POST /api/sessions/:id/stop`, and `stopAllShared.ts` defines `StoppableSession` instead of importing `SessionSummary` (U1 adds it to `src/types.ts`). `sessionStopTitle` repeats the words of U1's `sessionTitle` (pure files import types only, so neither can import the other); U1's test "Stop all names a session with the same words as the Sessions page" keeps the two equal.
3. **Known limit: a race with another Stop.** A session stopped from the Sessions page or another window between the hold's look and its own Stop answers `endedBy: "stop"`, so this hold counts it as "Stopped". The server cannot tell whose Stop it was; the session is stopped either way.
4. **Follow-up when spike S5 lands (S7 note 2).** Once OpenClaw's soft stop calls the Gateway's abort, the end-to-end test's `gateway` assertion narrows to `args[1]` in `start`, `stop` and `restart`; it is never dropped.
5. **Outside local mode** (the public demo, or `HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE` / `HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH`) every hold reads `GET /api/sessions?kind=all` and gets 404 `not_available`, which `withSessionAnswers` turns into "no session"; the browser still logs that 404 as a failed request in its console.
6. **The audit harness's login shell.** S10 is the first task after S8 that runs the audit harness, and from S8 on a local-mode server reads its login shell after it starts. Step 14 (a) therefore gives the throwaway server the stand-in login shell (R15, Q1c) on its existing `env` line, so no line number moves; U1's harness step later replaces that `env` block with its own.

### Task D1: Desktop shell: hide on close, Reopen and Show item, custom Quit, quit events, dialog plugin, accelerators

Today the desktop shell (`desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`) stops the Node server the moment the window closes, and ⌘Q goes through Tauri's predefined Quit item, which ends the app before anything can ask (map-desktop-packaging §1: `PredefinedMenuItem::quit` is AppKit's `terminate:`, which only reaches `RunEvent::Exit`, and `Exit` cannot be prevented). With live sessions that loses the person's work without a word. This task makes the shell follow the spec's "Persistence, quit and Stop" and "Desktop shell changes" sections, with planning decisions Q4-Q6c:

- **macOS:** closing the window only hides it (sessions keep running); a Dock click (`RunEvent::Reopen`) or the new "Show Agent OS" menu item brings it back.
- **Windows and Linux:** closing the window means quit (no tray in this work), so it goes through the quit flow.
- **Quit flow** (the custom "Quit Agent OS" item, ⌘Q on macOS only; closing the window on Windows/Linux; `ExitRequested`): the shell prevents the exit, shows, unminimizes and focuses the window, emits `agentos://quit-requested`, and waits for the page. If no `agentos://quit-shown` arrives within 2 s, no page can ask, so it quits. After `quit-shown` it waits for `agentos://quit-answer { quit }` with no time limit; a second quit request while the question is open does nothing; a page that loads again drops an open question, so the next quit asks again. The page's side (the question itself) is Task U1; until U1 lands, ⌘Q simply quits after 2 s.
- **Quitting** means: write the line `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN` into the server's stdin (the server is started with `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1` and a piped stdin that stays open for the app's whole life, Q4, so this works on Windows too), wait up to `QUIT_GRACE` (10 s; the server's own hard limit is 8 s), then force it at once (SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows). If the line cannot be written, unix sends SIGTERM at once instead.
- **A termination signal** to the app (SIGTERM/SIGINT) does not ask (Q5a): it runs the same graceful server stop and exits.
- **Routes that cannot ask** (Q5b, ruling R19, owner): the Dock's Quit, the app switcher's Quit, logging out and an approved update's restart reach only `RunEvent::Exit`, which cannot be prevented, so they run the same graceful stop without the question. The in-app "Install & restart" asks first in the page (Task U1). Spike S7 (Task E2) records what the Dock's Quit and the app switcher's Quit really do.
- **Keys:** on Windows and Linux the menu takes no keys at all (no Edit menu, no Window menu, no Hide; Reload and Quit without accelerators), so Ctrl+C, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+M and Ctrl+H reach the agent's terminal (Q6b). macOS keeps its ⌘ keys.
- **Folder picker:** `tauri-plugin-dialog` (crate `"2"`, npm `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog@2.8.3`, on the owner's approved list) with only `dialog:allow-open` granted, for the New session dialog's "Choose folder…" (Task U3 uses it).
- **Page packages (ruling R3):** Step 1 installs both page packages in one step, `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog@2.8.3` and `@tauri-apps/api@2.12.1` (Q6, owner: the version already in `package-lock.json`, which Task U1's quit listener imports from `@tauri-apps/api/event`), both pinned exactly, after the orchestrator has recorded the owner's yes in the ledger (Step 0). U1 only checks that both are there.
- **Port variable (ruling R13, Q11a):** the server gets its port as `AGENT_OS_PORT=0` instead of `PORT=0`. The server's environment reaches every session through the login shell minus the `AGENT_OS_` names, so an un-prefixed `PORT=0` would make an agent's dev server bind a random port. Task S8 makes the server read `AGENT_OS_PORT` first. For the same reason the server also gets `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH`, the `PATH` this app was started with (H2): Task S2 starts the login shell with it, so the folders `server_path_env()` puts in front of the server's own `PATH` do not reach sessions that way, and the login shell starts from the same `PATH` Terminal.app's does.
- **Time budget (ruling R5):** the server's sessions quit is cut off at 7 s, the server's own hard exit is 8 s, and the shell's `QUIT_GRACE` is 10 s, so a server that is not stuck always ends on its own before the shell forces it.

The quit rules live in a small pure state machine (`QuitFlow`) with Rust unit tests (`cargo test`), so they are checked without starting the app.

  - Menu item ids `"agentos-quit"` ("Quit Agent OS"; ⌘Q on macOS, no accelerator elsewhere) and `"agentos-show"` ("Show Agent OS", macOS app menu, no accelerator); `"reload"` stays (no accelerator on Windows and Linux).

  - 18 Rust unit tests in `main.rs` (15 on Windows, where the three stdin tests that use `sh` are left out); Task D2's CI job runs them with `cargo test --locked`.

**Rust you can read without knowing Rust:** `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` means "this line only exists when building for macOS", and `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]` means Windows and Linux. `Mutex` is a lock, so two threads never change the same value at once. `cargo build` compiles the shell; `cargo test` compiles it together with the `#[cfg(test)]` modules and runs their `#[test]` functions.

describe("desktop quit plumbing (the page and the shell must agree on these names)", async () => {
  const main = await read("desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs");

  test("the quit question travels as three events, with no custom command", () => {
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT: &str = "agentos:\/\/quit-requested";/);
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT: &str = "agentos:\/\/quit-shown";/);
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT: &str = "agentos:\/\/quit-answer";/);
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs\(2\);/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(main, /invoke_handler|#\[tauri::command\]/, "a remote window cannot call a custom command without an AppManifest");
  });

  test("Quit is a custom menu item (⌘Q on macOS only), and the predefined Quit item is gone", () => {
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_MENU_ID: &str = "agentos-quit";/);
    assert.match(main, /const SHOW_MENU_ID: &str = "agentos-show";/);
    assert.match(main, /"Quit Agent OS"/);
    assert.match(main, /"Show Agent OS"/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(main, /PredefinedMenuItem::quit/, "the predefined Quit ends the app before anything can ask");
    // Every accelerator is set inside a macOS-only line: Windows and Linux menus take no keys from the terminal.
    const accelerators = [...main.matchAll(/\.accelerator\(/g)].length;
    const macOnly = [...main.matchAll(/#\[cfg\(target_os = "macos"\)\]\s*let \w+ = \w+\.accelerator\(/g)].length;
    assert.ok(accelerators > 0 && accelerators === macOnly, `${accelerators} accelerators, ${macOnly} of them macOS-only`);
  });

  test("the server gets its port as AGENT_OS_PORT, is asked to quit through its stdin, and gets 10 s before it is forced", () => {
    const start = main.indexOf("fn spawn_server(");
    const end = main.indexOf("fn parse_ready_line(");
    assert.ok(start >= 0 && end > start, "fn spawn_server comes right before fn parse_ready_line");
    const spawnServer = main.slice(start, end);
    // The server's environment reaches every session through the login shell minus the AGENT_OS_ names,
    // so an un-prefixed PORT=0 would make an agent's own dev server bind a random port.
    assert.match(spawnServer, /\.env\("AGENT_OS_PORT", "0"\)/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(spawnServer, /\.env\("PORT"/);
    // The PATH the app was started with, for the login shell (H2): not the one server_path_env extends.
    assert.match(spawnServer, /\.env\("AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH"/);
    assert.match(spawnServer, /\.env\("AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN", "1"\)/);
    assert.match(spawnServer, /\.stdin\(Stdio::piped\(\)\)/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(spawnServer, /Stdio::null\(\)/, "the server's stdin is never closed at start");
    assert.match(main, /const SHUTDOWN_LINE: &str = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\\n";/);
    assert.match(main, /const QUIT_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs\(10\);/);
  });

  test("closing the window hides it on macOS and asks to quit elsewhere; Reopen shows it again", () => {
    assert.match(main, /api\.prevent_close\(\)/);
    assert.match(main, /RunEvent::Reopen/);
    assert.match(main, /api\.prevent_exit\(\)/);
    assert.match(main, /RESTART_EXIT_CODE/, "an approved update restart is let through");
  });
});

        assert_eq!(QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT, "agentos://quit-shown");
        assert_eq!(QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, "agentos://quit-answer");
        assert_eq!(QUIT_MENU_ID, "agentos-quit");
        assert_eq!(SHOW_MENU_ID, "agentos-show");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_quit_grace_outlasts_the_servers_own_hard_exit() {
        // server/runtime/shutdown.js exits by itself after 8 s at the latest.
        assert_eq!(QUIT_GRACE, Duration::from_secs(10));
        assert_eq!(QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT, Duration::from_secs(2));
        assert_eq!(SHUTDOWN_LINE, "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n");
    }
}

#[cfg(all(test, unix))]
mod stop_server_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

    // A stand-in for the server: `sh`, with the same piped stdin the real server gets.
    fn server_running(script: &str) -> ServerState {
        let child = Command::new("sh")
            .args(["-c", script])
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .expect("sh starts");
        Arc::new(Mutex::new(Some(child)))
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_server_is_asked_through_its_stdin_and_ends_on_its_own() {
        let seen = env::temp_dir().join(format!("agentos-stdin-line-{}", std::process::id()));
        let script = format!("read line; printf '%s' \"$line\" > '{}'; exit 0", seen.display());
        let state = server_running(&script);
        let started = Instant::now();
        assert_eq!(stop_server_within(&state, Duration::from_secs(5)), Some(true));
        assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(4), "it ended on its own, long before the grace ran out");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(&seen).expect("the line was written"), "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&seen);
        assert!(state.lock().unwrap().is_none(), "the server is taken out of the state");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_server_that_does_not_stop_is_forced_after_the_grace() {
        let state = server_running("exec sleep 30");
        let started = Instant::now();
        assert_eq!(stop_server_within(&state, Duration::from_millis(300)), Some(false));
        assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stopping_with_no_server_does_nothing() {
        let state: ServerState = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
        assert_eq!(stop_server_within(&state, Duration::from_millis(10)), None);
    }
}

```rust

// ---- the quit flow ---------------------------------------------------------
//
// Quitting can end the person's live sessions, so it asks first, through the page:
//   1. a quit request arrives (the Quit Agent OS item, closing the window on Windows/Linux, or
//      an exit request); the shell prevents the exit, shows the window and emits
//      agentos://quit-requested;
//   2. the page answers agentos://quit-shown as soon as it shows its question (or
//      agentos://quit-answer { quit: true } at once when no session is live);
//   3. if no quit-shown arrives within QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT, no page can ask, so the quit goes on;
//   4. after quit-shown the shell waits for agentos://quit-answer { quit } with no time limit.
//      { quit: false } keeps everything running; { quit: true } stops the server (stop_server:
//      the server ends every session and run, then exits) and exits the app.
// Events only: `listen` and `emit` are in core:default (capabilities/default.json). A custom
// `invoke` command would need an AppManifest, because the window's page is on 127.0.0.1.

/// What the shell does next.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum QuitStep {
    /// Nothing: a question is already open, a quit is already under way, or nobody asked.
    Nothing,
    /// Ask the page (this is question number `round`) and start the QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT clock.
    Ask(u64),
    /// Stop the server and exit.
    Quit,
}

/// Where the quit flow is. Pure, so the rules are unit tested.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct QuitFlow {
    /// A question was sent to the page and not answered yet.
    asking: bool,
    /// The page said the question is on screen.
    shown: bool,
    /// The quit is under way: from here on the app is allowed to exit.
    quitting: bool,
    /// Counts the questions, so a 2 s clock left over from an answered question does nothing.
    round: u64,
}

impl QuitFlow {
    /// A quit request. `page_can_ask` is false when no page could show a question (the loading
    /// page is still up, or the server is gone): then the quit goes on at once.
    fn request(&mut self, page_can_ask: bool) -> QuitStep {
        if self.quitting || self.asking {
            return QuitStep::Nothing;
        }
        if !page_can_ask {
            self.quitting = true;
            return QuitStep::Quit;
        }
        self.asking = true;
        self.shown = false;
        self.round += 1;
        QuitStep::Ask(self.round)
    }

    /// agentos://quit-shown.
    fn shown(&mut self) {
        if self.asking {
            self.shown = true;
        }
    }

    /// agentos://quit-answer. An answer nobody asked for is ignored.
    fn answer(&mut self, quit: bool) -> QuitStep {
        if !self.asking {
            return QuitStep::Nothing;
        }
        self.asking = false;
        self.shown = false;
        if quit {
            self.quitting = true;
            QuitStep::Quit
        } else {
            QuitStep::Nothing
        }
    }

    /// QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT has passed since question `round` was sent.
    fn no_answer_in_time(&mut self, round: u64) -> QuitStep {
        if !self.asking || self.shown || self.round != round {
            return QuitStep::Nothing;
        }
        self.asking = false;
        self.quitting = true;
        QuitStep::Quit
    }

    /// The page started loading again (for example View > Reload). A question it was showing is
    /// gone, so the person must be able to quit again. A question it had not shown yet is left to
    /// the QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT clock, which then quits.
    fn page_gone(&mut self) {
        if self.asking && self.shown {
            self.asking = false;
            self.shown = false;
        }
    }

    fn exit_allowed(&self) -> bool {
        self.quitting
    }
}

/// `{ "quit": true }` or `{ "quit": false }`; anything else is not an answer.
fn quit_answer(payload: &str) -> Option<bool> {
    serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(payload).ok()?.get("quit")?.as_bool()
}

/// Only the server's own page (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/) has the quit question. The loading
/// page that shows while the server starts does not.
fn is_server_page(scheme: &str, host: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    scheme == "http" && host == Some("127.0.0.1")
}

fn page_can_ask(app: &AppHandle) -> bool {
    let server_running = app
        .state::<ServerState>()
        .lock()
        .map(|guard| guard.is_some())
        .unwrap_or(false);
    let on_server_page = app
        .get_webview_window("main")
        .and_then(|window| window.url().ok())
        .is_some_and(|url| is_server_page(url.scheme(), url.host_str()));
    server_running && on_server_page
}

fn show_main_window(app: &AppHandle) {
    if let Some(window) = app.get_webview_window("main") {
        let _ = window.unminimize();
        let _ = window.show();
        let _ = window.set_focus();
    }
}

fn request_quit(app: &AppHandle) {
    let can_ask = page_can_ask(app);
    let step = app
        .state::<QuitState>()
        .lock()
        .map(|mut flow| flow.request(can_ask))
        .unwrap_or(QuitStep::Quit);
    match step {
        QuitStep::Ask(round) => ask_page(app, round),
        QuitStep::Quit => finish_quit(app),
        QuitStep::Nothing => {}
    }
}

/// Shows the window (on macOS it may be hidden) and asks the page. If the page has not said
/// within QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT that its question is on screen, nobody can answer, so the quit goes on.
fn ask_page(app: &AppHandle, round: u64) {
    show_main_window(app);
    // If the event cannot be sent, no question appears, and the clock below quits.
    let _ = app.emit(QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT, ());
    let handle = app.clone();
    thread::spawn(move || {
        thread::sleep(QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT);
        let step = handle
            .state::<QuitState>()
            .lock()
            .map(|mut flow| flow.no_answer_in_time(round))
            .unwrap_or(QuitStep::Nothing);
        if step == QuitStep::Quit {
            finish_quit(&handle);
        }
    });
}

/// Stops the server (it ends every session and run first) and then exits the app. Runs on its own
/// thread, so the window stays responsive while the server finishes.
fn finish_quit(app: &AppHandle) {
    let handle = app.clone();
    let server = Arc::clone(app.state::<ServerState>().inner());
    thread::spawn(move || {
        stop_server(&server);
        handle.exit(0);
    });
}

fn quit_allowed(app: &AppHandle) -> bool {
    app.state::<QuitState>()
        .lock()
        .map(|flow| flow.exit_allowed())
        .unwrap_or(true)
}

/// The page's two answers: "the question is on screen" and "quit or not".
fn listen_for_quit_answers(app: &tauri::App) {
    let handle = app.handle().clone();
    app.listen(QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT, move |_event| {
        if let Ok(mut flow) = handle.state::<QuitState>().lock() {
            flow.shown();
        }
    });
    let handle = app.handle().clone();
    app.listen(QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, move |event| {
        let Some(quit) = quit_answer(event.payload()) else {
            return;
        };
        let step = handle
            .state::<QuitState>()
            .lock()
            .map(|mut flow| flow.answer(quit))
            .unwrap_or(QuitStep::Nothing);
        if step == QuitStep::Quit {
            finish_quit(&handle);
        }
    });
}
```

/// The menu.
/// - macOS: Agent OS (About, Show Agent OS, Hide ⌘H, Quit Agent OS ⌘Q), Edit (so ⌘C/⌘V work in
///   text fields), View > Reload ⌘R, Window > Minimize ⌘M.
/// - Windows and Linux: Agent OS (About, Quit Agent OS) and View > Reload, with NO keyboard
///   shortcuts at all. There a menu shortcut is a Ctrl key, and every Ctrl key belongs to the
///   agent's terminal (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+A, ...). The predefined Edit, Minimize and
///   Hide items carry fixed Ctrl shortcuts that cannot be removed, so they are left out; the web
///   view handles copy and paste in text fields by itself. Closing the window is how you quit.
/// Quit is a custom item: the predefined one ends the app before anything can ask.
fn build_menu(app: &tauri::App) -> tauri::Result<()> {
    let handle = app.handle();

    let quit = MenuItemBuilder::with_id(QUIT_MENU_ID, "Quit Agent OS");
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    let quit = quit.accelerator("CmdOrCtrl+Q");
    let quit = quit.build(handle)?;

    let reload = MenuItemBuilder::with_id(RELOAD_MENU_ID, "Reload");
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    let reload = reload.accelerator("CmdOrCtrl+R");
    let reload = reload.build(handle)?;
    let view_menu = SubmenuBuilder::new(handle, "View").item(&reload).build()?;

    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    let menu = {
        let show = MenuItemBuilder::with_id(SHOW_MENU_ID, "Show Agent OS").build(handle)?;
        let app_menu = SubmenuBuilder::new(handle, "Agent OS")
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::about(handle, None, None)?)
            .separator()
            .item(&show)
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::hide(handle, None)?)
            .separator()
            .item(&quit)
            .build()?;
        let edit_menu = SubmenuBuilder::new(handle, "Edit")
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::undo(handle, None)?)
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::redo(handle, None)?)
            .separator()
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::cut(handle, None)?)
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::copy(handle, None)?)
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::paste(handle, None)?)
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::select_all(handle, None)?)
            .build()?;
        let window_menu = SubmenuBuilder::new(handle, "Window")
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::minimize(handle, None)?)
            .build()?;
        MenuBuilder::new(handle)
            .item(&app_menu)
            .item(&edit_menu)
            .item(&view_menu)
            .item(&window_menu)
            .build()?
    };

    #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
    let menu = {
        let app_menu = SubmenuBuilder::new(handle, "Agent OS")
            .item(&PredefinedMenuItem::about(handle, None, None)?)
            .separator()
            .item(&quit)
            .build()?;
        MenuBuilder::new(handle).item(&app_menu).item(&view_menu).build()?
    };

    app.set_menu(menu)?;

    app.on_menu_event(|app, event| match event.id().as_ref() {
        RELOAD_MENU_ID => {
            if let Some(window) = app.get_webview_window("main") {
                let _ = window.eval("window.location.reload()");
            }
        }
        QUIT_MENU_ID => request_quit(app),
        SHOW_MENU_ID => show_main_window(app),
        _ => {}
    });
    Ok(())
}

```rust
fn main() {
    let server_state: ServerState = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));

    #[cfg(unix)]
    install_signal_handler(Arc::clone(&server_state));

    let context = tauri::generate_context!();

    // The updater plugin refuses to start without a signing public key in
    // tauri.conf.json (`plugins.updater.pubkey`), and Agent OS has no key yet.
    // So register it only when one is configured; until then the update
    // banner finds no updater and stays hidden. See desktop/README.md.
    let updater_configured = context
        .config()
        .plugins
        .0
        .get("updater")
        .and_then(|cfg| cfg.get("pubkey"))
        .and_then(|key| key.as_str())
        .is_some_and(|key| !key.trim().is_empty());

    let mut builder = tauri::Builder::default()
        // The stock macOS menu has items we don't want (and a Close Window
        // entry); the custom menu in setup() replaces it.
        .enable_macos_default_menu(false)
        // relaunch() after an update the user approved.
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_process::init())
        // "Show in Finder" on the Workspace page. Only the reveal permission is
        // granted (capabilities/default.json), so a page cannot open or run files.
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
        // "Choose folder…" in the New session dialog. Only the open dialog is
        // granted (dialog:allow-open); it hands the page the path the person picked.
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_dialog::init());
    if updater_configured {
        builder = builder.plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build());
    }

    builder
        .manage(server_state)
        .manage(Mutex::new(QuitFlow::default()))
        .setup(|app| {
            let window = app
                .get_webview_window("main")
                .expect("the \"main\" window is declared in tauri.conf.json");

            start_server(app, &window);
            build_menu(app)?;
            listen_for_quit_answers(app);
            Ok(())
        })
        // A page that starts loading again cannot be showing an earlier quit question.
        .on_page_load(|webview, payload| {
            if payload.event() == tauri::webview::PageLoadEvent::Started {
                if let Ok(mut flow) = webview.state::<QuitState>().lock() {
                    flow.page_gone();
                }
            }
        })
        .on_window_event(|window, event| {
            if let tauri::WindowEvent::CloseRequested { api, .. } = event {
                api.prevent_close();
                // macOS: closing the window only hides it, and sessions keep running.
                // The Dock icon, or Agent OS > Show Agent OS, brings it back.
                #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
                {
                    let _ = window.hide();
                }
                // Windows and Linux have no tray in this work, so closing the
                // window means quitting, which asks first.
                #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
                request_quit(window.app_handle());
            }
        })
        .build(context)
        .expect("error while building the Agent OS desktop app")
        .run(|app_handle, event| match event {
            // Something asked the app to exit (the last window went away, or app.exit()).
            // Unless our own quit flow already decided, it goes through the flow. An update
            // the person approved restarts the app with RESTART_EXIT_CODE, which cannot be
            // prevented: it is let through, and Exit below still stops the server first.
            tauri::RunEvent::ExitRequested { api, code, .. } => {
                if code != Some(tauri::RESTART_EXIT_CODE) && !quit_allowed(app_handle) {
                    api.prevent_exit();
                    request_quit(app_handle);
                }
            }
            // macOS: a click on the Dock icon while the window is hidden.
            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
            tauri::RunEvent::Reopen { .. } => show_main_window(app_handle),
            // The app is ending, by any route (including routes that cannot be asked
            // about, such as the Dock's Quit or logging out). Stop the server, gracefully.
            tauri::RunEvent::Exit => stop_server(&app_handle.state::<ServerState>()),
            _ => {}
        });
}

- [ ] **Step 7: Replace the signal handler.** Replace lines 314-332 (from ``/// A plain `kill <pid>` on this app skips Tauri's own quit path entirely, so`` through the closing `}` of `install_signal_handler`) with:

```rust
/// A plain `kill <pid>` on this app (or the computer logging out) skips Tauri's own
/// quit path entirely, so without this the server would be left running. It does not
/// ask first (planning decision Q5a): there may be nobody to answer, and a logout must
/// not hang on a question. The server still ends its sessions and runs on its own
/// (stop_server), then the app exits. signal-hook delivers the signal to an ordinary
/// thread (not real signal context), where taking a mutex is safe.
#[cfg(unix)]
fn install_signal_handler(state: ServerState) {
    use signal_hook::consts::{SIGINT, SIGTERM};
    use signal_hook::iterator::Signals;

    let Ok(mut signals) = Signals::new([SIGTERM, SIGINT]) else {
        return; // best effort: normal quit paths still work
    };
    thread::spawn(move || {
        if signals.forever().next().is_some() {
            stop_server(&state);
            std::process::exit(0);
        }
    });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Replace `kill_server` with the graceful stop.** Replace lines 272-312 (from `/// Stops the server. Called from the window-close handler, from the app-exit` through the closing `}` of `kill_server`) with:

```rust
/// Stops the server and waits for it, at most `grace`.
///
/// It asks through the server's stdin (every OS): it writes SHUTDOWN_LINE and closes the pipe.
/// The server then runs its own quit steps (it records every live session as ended by the quit,
/// stops all sessions and runs, and exits; its own hard limit is 8 s). If the line cannot be
/// written, unix falls back to SIGTERM at once. A server still running after `grace` is forced:
/// SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` (the whole tree) on Windows.
///
/// Returns None when no server was running, Some(true) when it ended on its own, and
/// Some(false) when it had to be forced. Safe to call more than once: `take()` makes later
/// calls do nothing.
fn stop_server_within(state: &ServerState, grace: Duration) -> Option<bool> {
    let mut child = state.lock().ok().and_then(|mut guard| guard.take())?;

    // `stdin` is dropped at the end of this match, which closes the pipe: end of input is the
    // same request to the server.
    let asked = match child.stdin.take() {
        Some(mut stdin) => stdin
            .write_all(SHUTDOWN_LINE.as_bytes())
            .and_then(|()| stdin.flush())
            .is_ok(),
        None => false,
    };
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        if !asked {
            unsafe {
                libc::kill(child.id() as i32, libc::SIGTERM);
            }
        }
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let _ = asked;

    let deadline = Instant::now() + grace;
    loop {
        match child.try_wait() {
            Ok(Some(_)) => return Some(true), // ended on its own: the normal case
            Ok(None) if Instant::now() < deadline => thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)),
            _ => break,
        }
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
        let _ = Command::new("taskkill")
            .args(["/PID", &child.id().to_string(), "/T", "/F"])
            .creation_flags(0x0800_0000) // CREATE_NO_WINDOW
            .status();
    }

    let _ = child.kill();
    let _ = child.wait();
    Some(false)
}

/// Stops the server with the full QUIT_GRACE. Called from the quit flow, from the app's Exit
/// event and (unix) from the signal thread, because each covers a different way of quitting.
fn stop_server(state: &ServerState) {
    let _ = stop_server_within(state, QUIT_GRACE);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Start the server with an open stdin and AGENT_OS_PORT, then fix the top of the file.**

(Step 1 checked that the server reads `AGENT_OS_PORT`.) Replace `spawn_server` (lines 180-202, from `fn spawn_server(launch: &Launch, token: &str) -> std::io::Result<Child> {` through its closing `}`) with:

```rust
fn spawn_server(launch: &Launch, token: &str) -> std::io::Result<Child> {
    let mut command = Command::new(&launch.node);
    command
        .arg(&launch.entry)
        // AGENT_OS_PORT=0: let the OS pick a free port, so two copies never collide.
        // An AGENT_OS_ name, not PORT: the server's environment reaches every session
        // through the login shell minus the AGENT_OS_ names, and an agent's own dev
        // server must not see PORT=0.
        .env("AGENT_OS_PORT", "0")
        .env("AGENT_OS_TOKEN", token)
        .env("AGENT_OS_STATIC_DIR", &launch.static_dir)
        .env("AGENT_OS_PACKAGED", "1")
        // The server reads its stdin for SHUTDOWN_LINE (see stop_server_within).
        .env("AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN", "1")
        // The PATH this app was started with (launchd's on macOS). The server starts the
        // login shell with it, so a session's PATH begins where Terminal.app's does, not
        // with the folders server_path_env adds (H2, decision Q11a).
        .env("AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH", env::var_os("PATH").unwrap_or_default())
        .env("PATH", server_path_env())
        // Kept open for the server's whole life: the quit request travels through it,
        // and if this app ever dies, the pipe closes and the server shuts down by itself.
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped());
    if let Some(dir) = &launch.working_dir {
        command.current_dir(dir);
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
        command.creation_flags(0x0800_0000); // CREATE_NO_WINDOW
    }
    command.spawn()
}
```

Replace the constants and types (lines 40-53, from `/// What the server prints on stdout once it is listening.` through `type ServerState = Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>>;`) with:

```rust
/// What the server prints on stdout once it is listening.
const READY_LINE_PREFIX: &str = "AGENT_OS_READY:";
/// How long to wait for that line before showing an error.
const READY_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20);
/// How many trailing stderr lines the error page can show.
const STDERR_TAIL_LINES: usize = 20;
/// How long a quitting app waits for the server to end every session and run and
/// exit on its own before forcing it. The server's own hard limit is 8 s
/// (server/runtime/shutdown.js), so this is enough for any server that is not stuck.
const QUIT_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
/// The line that asks the server to quit. The server reads its stdin only when
/// AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1 (set in spawn_server) and treats this exact line, or the
/// end of its input, like SIGTERM. It is the only graceful route on Windows, where
/// the server has no console to send a signal to.
const SHUTDOWN_LINE: &str = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n";
/// How long the page has to say its quit question is on screen. After that no page
/// can ask, so the quit goes on.
const QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
/// Shell -> page: the person wants to quit (no payload).
const QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT: &str = "agentos://quit-requested";
/// Page -> shell: the quit question is on screen.
const QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT: &str = "agentos://quit-shown";
/// Page -> shell: the answer, `{ "quit": true | false }`.
const QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT: &str = "agentos://quit-answer";
/// The custom "Quit Agent OS" menu item.
const QUIT_MENU_ID: &str = "agentos-quit";
/// "Show Agent OS" in the macOS app menu: brings the hidden window back.
const SHOW_MENU_ID: &str = "agentos-show";
/// View > Reload.
const RELOAD_MENU_ID: &str = "reload";

/// The running server, shared between the window, the exit handler and the
/// signal thread. `None` once it has been shut down.
type ServerState = Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>>;
/// Where the quit flow is (see QuitFlow).
type QuitState = Mutex<QuitFlow>;
```

```rust
//! Agent OS desktop shell.
//!
//! Agent OS is a Node server plus a web UI. This app does not rewrite any of
//! that in Rust: it ships its own copy of Node 24 and the bundled server,
//! starts them as a child process, waits for the server to say which port it
//! picked, then points a native window at it, already logged in.
//!
//! ```text
//!   Agent OS.app
//!     |-- this Rust shell (window, menu, quit handling)
//!     |      spawns -->  resources/node/bin/node resources/server/server.mjs
//!     |                    AGENT_OS_PORT=0  AGENT_OS_TOKEN=<random>  AGENT_OS_STATIC_DIR=...
//!     |                    AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1 (stdin stays open: the quit line)
//!     |      reads  <--  stdout "AGENT_OS_READY:<port>"
//!     |      opens  -->  http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?launch=<token>&desktop=1
//! ```
//!
//! The most important job here is cleanup: when the app quits, by any route,
//! the server must end every session and run it started, then stop. Because
//! sessions are the person's live work, quitting asks first through the page
//! (the quit flow, near the end of this file), and on macOS closing the window
//! only hides it.
```

#### Notes

1. **A page that loads again drops an open quit question** (`QuitFlow::page_gone`, through `Builder::on_page_load`). A second quit request while the question is open does nothing (Q6), so without this a View > Reload while the question was showing would leave the app unable to quit except by force. A question the page had not shown yet still quits on the 2 s clock.
2. **After the grace the server is forced at once** (SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows), not through the old `kill_server`, which would add a second SIGTERM and a second full grace (20 s at worst). If the quit line cannot be written, unix sends SIGTERM at once instead. If the app dies without reaching `RunEvent::Exit` (a crash), the server's stdin closes and Task S1's end-of-input rule shuts the server down by itself.
3. **Routes that cannot ask (owner, Q5a, Q5b, ruling R19).** The Dock icon's Quit, Quit from the app switcher, logging out and an approved update's restart (`RESTART_EXIT_CODE`, which `prevent_exit()` ignores) reach only `RunEvent::Exit` in tao 0.37.1 and Tauri 2.12.1, and a termination signal skips Tauri altogether; all of them run the graceful stop without the question, although the spec (L521) lists them among the routes that ask. The update restart is covered in the page: Task U1's "Install & restart" asks first. Spike S7 (Task E2) checks ⌘Q and the Quit item, and records what the Dock's Quit and the app switcher's Quit really do.
4. **Windows and Linux menus lose Edit, Window and Hide (Q6b).** muda 0.20's predefined items carry fixed Ctrl accelerators that cannot be removed, so the items are left out. Copy and paste in text fields then rely on WebView2 and WebKitGTK handling the keys themselves, and WebView2's own browser keys (Ctrl+R or F5 reload, Ctrl+P print) may still act where the page does not cancel the key (xterm cancels the keys it handles). Neither is checked at run time here: there is no Windows or Linux computer, and Task D2's CI job only compiles the shell and runs its unit tests. A later Windows spike should try both.
5. **Fresh crates (owner FYI).** `tauri-plugin-dialog` 2.8.3 (npm and crate) was published on 2026-10-14, as was `tauri-plugin-fs` 2.7.1, the new dependency it brings. Both require `tauri ^2.12`, so the locked tauri 2.12.1 stays. `rfd` 0.16 uses GTK3 on Linux, which release.yml's apt list already brings in (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` depends on `libgtk-3-dev`). The 3.0.0 alphas of both crates on crates.io are outside `"2"`; if `cargo build` picks a later 2.x `tauri-plugin-dialog`, Step 11 pins the lock back to 2.8.3 (ruling R3).

With the macOS and Windows/Linux `cfg` lines swapped, the Windows/Linux menu and the close-means-quit path also built with no warning on macOS. Tauri 2.12.1's own source confirms the APIs used: `App` implements `Listener` (app listeners get every plain `emit`, including the page's), the event plugin's `emit` command calls `app.emit`, `PageLoadEvent` derives `PartialEq`, `WebviewWindow::url()` answers on the main thread without waiting on the event loop, `ExitRequested` carries `code: Option<i32>`, and `prevent_exit()` ignores `RESTART_EXIT_CODE`. ### Task D2: Packaging and CI: node-pty in the bundle, platform/arch, portable test, desktop check job

Sessions run each agent in a real terminal through `node-pty`, a native module (compiled C++ plus, on macOS, a small helper program called `spawn-helper`). esbuild cannot put a native module inside the one-file server bundle (`build/server/server.mjs`), so without this task the desktop app would ship a server that cannot open a terminal. Following the spec's "Dependencies and packaging" and planning decisions Q20-Q22, this task:

- keeps `node-pty` out of the bundle (esbuild `external`, together with `ws`'s optional `bufferutil` and `utf-8-validate`) and copies only what node-pty needs at run time next to `server.mjs`: `build/server/node_modules/node-pty/{lib, package.json, prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>}`, which is exactly where Node looks for it from `server.mjs`;
- picks the prebuilt folder for the computer the app will run on, not the one building it: `scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs` and `scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs` gain `--platform`/`--arch` (same names as `scripts/fetch-node.mjs`), and `release.yml` passes `matrix.node_platform`/`matrix.node_arch` (the Intel Mac app is cross-built on an Apple-silicon runner, so `process.arch` would be wrong);
- stops the build when that prebuilt folder is missing, checks every copied binary's CPU by reading its file header instead of running it (a cross-built binary cannot run on the build machine), and gives `spawn-helper` mode 0755;
- does the copy before `prepare-desktop.mjs`'s `--skip-node` early return (the release always passes `--skip-node`);
- adds a `desktop` job to `ci.yml` that builds the Rust shell (debug, no installer) and runs its unit tests (Task D1's `cargo test`) on Linux, macOS and Windows, so "the desktop shell builds on all three OSes in CI" (spec, SP3 done when) is checked on every pull request;
- extends `test/portable.test.js`: the bundle copied to a temp folder and started the way the desktop app starts it (`AGENT_OS_PORT=0`, no `PORT`, decision Q11a) still boots, finds node-pty next to itself (`GET /api/sessions` reports `pty: { ok: true, reason: null }`), and opens a real terminal; without node-pty it still boots and says sessions cannot start (the lazy import in `pty-host.js`, which also keeps the Docker image booting).

The Docker image (`Dockerfile`, `node:20-bookworm-slim`, no compiler) is not changed, and sessions inside it are out of scope for SP3 (decision Q44): the image only has to build and boot. node-pty ships prebuilt Linux binaries for x64 and arm64, so its install script (`node scripts/prebuild.js || node-gyp rebuild`) never needs a compiler there. A test checks that both Linux prebuilds exist; the full Docker build is an optional check by the orchestrator.

The bundled servers in these tests follow the test rules of decision Q1c even though they start no session: from Task S8 on, a server in local mode reads its login shell right after READY, so each one gets W1's stand-in login shell (`SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`, never the developer's own shell and never `/bin/sh`) and a `PATH` of the six fake agents plus `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` only.

- Create: `scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs` (`parseTargetArgs`, `binaryArches`, `copyNodePty`).
- Modify: `scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs` (whole file, 66 lines).
- Modify: `scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs` (whole file, 57 lines).
- Modify: `.github/workflows/release.yml` lines 210-213 (the "Prepare desktop resources" step and its comment).
- Modify: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (a `desktop` job appended after line 65).
- Modify: `desktop/README.md` (the "Build it" list item 2, the "To build for another machine's CPU" paragraph, a new "Terminals (node-pty)" part, "Tested on", and the "Releasing" sentence that names `prepare-desktop.mjs --skip-node`; anchored by their text, because Task D1 moved the line numbers).
- Test: create `test/packaging.test.js`; modify `test/portable.test.js` (its `node:fs/promises` import line, one new import, and the whole `describe("bundled server runs outside the repo", …)` block: lines 72-151 once Tasks S1 and S8 have run (S1 adds its import line after line 13; S8 Step 10 (d) adds two lines inside the bundled-server test)); modify `test/release-config.test.js` (one new `describe` block at the end, after the blocks Task D1 added).

**Interfaces:**

```js
// node-pty next to the packaged server (design spec "Dependencies and packaging", planning decision Q21).
// scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs copies node-pty's lib/, package.json and ONE prebuilt folder next to the
// server bundle, checks each copied binary's CPU from its file header (never by running it: a cross-built
// binary cannot run here), and gives macOS's spawn-helper mode 0755. These tests use made-up headers and
// the real node_modules/node-pty. Nothing is spawned.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { binaryArches, copyNodePty, parseTargetArgs } from "../scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const realNodePty = path.join(root, "node_modules", "node-pty");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";

// The smallest file headers that say "built for this CPU", written the way each format defines them.
const X64 = 0x01000007;
const ARM64 = 0x0100000c;
function machO(cpu) {
  const b = Buffer.alloc(64);
  b.writeUInt32LE(0xfeedfacf, 0);
  b.writeUInt32LE(cpu, 4);
  return b;
}
function universalMachO(cpus) {
  const b = Buffer.alloc(8 + 20 * cpus.length + 32);
  b.writeUInt32BE(0xcafebabe, 0);
  b.writeUInt32BE(cpus.length, 4);
  cpus.forEach((cpu, i) => b.writeUInt32BE(cpu, 8 + 20 * i));
  return b;
}
function elf(machine) {
  const b = Buffer.alloc(64);
  b.set([0x7f, 0x45, 0x4c, 0x46, 2, 1], 0);
  b.writeUInt16LE(machine, 18);
  return b;
}
function pe(machine) {
  const b = Buffer.alloc(256);
  b.write("MZ", 0, "latin1");
  b.writeUInt32LE(0x80, 0x3c);
  b.write("PE\0\0", 0x80, "latin1");
  b.writeUInt16LE(machine, 0x84);
  return b;
}

async function withTemp(fn) {
  const dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-packaging-"));
  try {
    return await fn(dir);
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

test("parseTargetArgs: this computer by default, --platform/--arch when given, a clear refusal otherwise", () => {
  const here = { platform: "darwin", arch: "arm64" };
  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetArgs([], here), { platform: "darwin", arch: "arm64" });
  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetArgs(["--skip-node", "--platform", "darwin", "--arch", "x64"], here), { platform: "darwin", arch: "x64" });
  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetArgs(["--arch", "x64", "--platform", "win32"], here), { platform: "win32", arch: "x64" });
  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetArgs(["--platform", "linux"], here), { platform: "linux", arch: "arm64" });
  assert.throws(() => parseTargetArgs(["--platform", "freebsd"], here), /^Error: Unsupported target freebsd\/arm64\. Use darwin\|linux\|win32 with x64\|arm64\.$/);
  assert.throws(() => parseTargetArgs(["--arch", "ia32"], { platform: "win32", arch: "x64" }), /Unsupported target win32\/ia32/);
  assert.throws(() => parseTargetArgs(["--platform"], here), /--platform needs a value/);
  assert.throws(() => parseTargetArgs(["--platform", "--arch", "x64"], here), /--platform needs a value/);
  assert.throws(() => parseTargetArgs([], { platform: "sunos", arch: "x64" }), /Unsupported target sunos\/x64/);
});

test("binaryArches reads the CPU from Mach-O, universal Mach-O, ELF and PE headers, and nothing else", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(machO(X64)), ["x64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(machO(ARM64)), ["arm64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(universalMachO([X64, ARM64])), ["x64", "arm64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(elf(62)), ["x64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(elf(183)), ["arm64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(pe(0x8664)), ["x64"]);
  assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(pe(0xaa64)), ["arm64"]);
  // A shell script, 32-bit Intel binaries of each kind, cut-off files, and empty input: no CPU we ship for.
  for (const other of [Buffer.alloc(0), Buffer.from("#!/bin/sh\necho hi\n"), machO(0x7), elf(3), pe(0x14c), Buffer.from("MZ"), Buffer.from([0x7f, 0x45, 0x4c, 0x46])]) {
    assert.deepEqual(binaryArches(other), []);
  }
});

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the copy module.** Create `scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs`:

```js
// node-pty next to the packaged server (design spec "Dependencies and packaging", planning decision Q21).
//
// esbuild cannot put a native module inside server.mjs, so scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs keeps
// "node-pty" external and calls copyNodePty() to put the package next to the bundle, in
// build/server/node_modules/node-pty/, where Node finds it from server.mjs. Only what node-pty needs at
// run time is copied: lib/, package.json, and ONE prebuilt folder, prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>, for the
// computer the app will run on. That can differ from this computer: the release workflow builds the
// Intel Mac app on an Apple-silicon runner.
//
// The copied binaries are never run (a cross-built one could not run here). Each one's file header is
// read instead, to check it was built for the target's CPU, and macOS's spawn-helper (the small program
// node-pty starts for every terminal) gets mode 0755.
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { chmod, cp, mkdir, readdir, readFile, rm, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";

export const TARGET_PLATFORMS = ["darwin", "linux", "win32"];
export const TARGET_ARCHES = ["x64", "arm64"];

// What node-pty 1.2 loads at run time, per system: lib/utils.js loadNativeModule() looks in build/Release,
// build/Debug, then prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>; lib/unixTerminal.js starts <that folder>/spawn-helper on
// macOS; on Windows lib/windowsPtyAgent.js loads conpty.node and conpty_console_list.node.
const REQUIRED = {
  darwin: ["pty.node", "spawn-helper"],
  linux: ["pty.node"],
  win32: ["conpty.node", "conpty_console_list.node"]
};

// The target computer: this one, unless --platform and/or --arch name another. Same names as
// scripts/fetch-node.mjs (Node's process.platform and process.arch).
export function parseTargetArgs(argv, { platform = process.platform, arch = process.arch } = {}) {
  const target = { platform, arch };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const flag = argv[i];
    if (flag !== "--platform" && flag !== "--arch") continue;
    const value = argv[i + 1];
    if (!value || value.startsWith("--")) {
      throw new Error(`${flag} needs a value, for example ${flag === "--platform" ? "--platform darwin" : "--arch x64"}.`);
    }
    target[flag === "--platform" ? "platform" : "arch"] = value;
    i += 1;
  }
  if (!TARGET_PLATFORMS.includes(target.platform) || !TARGET_ARCHES.includes(target.arch)) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported target ${target.platform}/${target.arch}. Use darwin|linux|win32 with x64|arm64.`);
  }
  return target;
}

// The CPUs a binary was built for, read from its header; [] when it is not a 64-bit Mach-O, universal
// Mach-O, ELF or PE file for x64 or arm64.
//   Mach-O (64-bit): magic 0xfeedfacf, stored little-endian; the CPU type is at byte 4.
//   Universal Mach-O: magic 0xcafebabe (0xcafebabf with 64-bit entries), big-endian; the number of
//     entries is at byte 4, then one entry per CPU (20 or 32 bytes) whose first field is its CPU type.
//   ELF: 0x7f "ELF"; byte 5 is the byte order (1 little, 2 big); the machine is 2 bytes at byte 18.
//   PE (Windows .node, .dll, .exe): "MZ"; the PE header's offset is at byte 0x3c, where "PE\0\0" is
//     followed by the machine, 2 bytes, little-endian.
const MACHO_CPU = new Map([
  [0x01000007, "x64"],
  [0x0100000c, "arm64"]
]);
const ELF_MACHINE = new Map([
  [62, "x64"],
  [183, "arm64"]
]);
const PE_MACHINE = new Map([
  [0x8664, "x64"],
  [0xaa64, "arm64"]
]);

export function binaryArches(buffer) {
  if (!Buffer.isBuffer(buffer) || buffer.length < 8) return [];
  if (buffer.readUInt32LE(0) === 0xfeedfacf) {
    const arch = MACHO_CPU.get(buffer.readUInt32LE(4));
    return arch ? [arch] : [];
  }
  const universal = buffer.readUInt32BE(0);
  if (universal === 0xcafebabe || universal === 0xcafebabf) {
    const entry = universal === 0xcafebabe ? 20 : 32;
    const count = buffer.readUInt32BE(4);
    const arches = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count && 8 + (i + 1) * entry <= buffer.length; i += 1) {
      const arch = MACHO_CPU.get(buffer.readUInt32BE(8 + i * entry));
      if (arch && !arches.includes(arch)) arches.push(arch);
    }
    return arches;
  }
  if (buffer[0] === 0x7f && buffer[1] === 0x45 && buffer[2] === 0x4c && buffer[3] === 0x46) {
    if (buffer.length < 20) return [];
    const machine = buffer[5] === 2 ? buffer.readUInt16BE(18) : buffer.readUInt16LE(18);
    const arch = ELF_MACHINE.get(machine);
    return arch ? [arch] : [];
  }
  if (buffer[0] === 0x4d && buffer[1] === 0x5a && buffer.length >= 0x40) {
    const offset = buffer.readUInt32LE(0x3c);
    if (offset + 6 > buffer.length || buffer.readUInt32LE(offset) !== 0x00004550) return [];
    const arch = PE_MACHINE.get(buffer.readUInt16LE(offset + 4));
    return arch ? [arch] : [];
  }
  return [];
}

async function listFiles(dir) {
  const files = [];
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) files.push(...(await listFiles(full)));
    else files.push(full);
  }
  return files.sort();
}

const withSlashes = (relative) => relative.split(path.sep).join("/");

// Copies node-pty from `from` (normally node_modules/node-pty) to `to` for one target computer.
// Returns { prebuild, files, bytes }: `files` are relative to `to`, with "/" separators, sorted.
// Throws, with a plain sentence, when node-pty is missing, has no prebuilt binary for the target, misses a
// file it needs there, or a copied binary was built for another CPU.
export async function copyNodePty({ from, to, platform, arch }) {
  const prebuild = `${platform}-${arch}`;
  if (!existsSync(path.join(from, "package.json")) || !existsSync(path.join(from, "lib"))) {
    throw new Error(`node-pty is not installed (nothing at ${from}). Run npm ci first, then build again.`);
  }
  const source = path.join(from, "prebuilds", prebuild);
  if (!existsSync(source)) {
    throw new Error(
      `node-pty has no prebuilt binary for ${prebuild} (looked in ${source}). Sessions could not start in that app, so the build stops here.`
    );
  }
  await rm(to, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await mkdir(to, { recursive: true });
  await cp(path.join(from, "package.json"), path.join(to, "package.json"));
  await cp(path.join(from, "lib"), path.join(to, "lib"), {
    recursive: true,
    filter: (file) => !file.endsWith(".map") && !file.endsWith(".test.js")
  });
  const target = path.join(to, "prebuilds", prebuild);
  // Debug symbols (.pdb, about 10 MB on Windows) are not needed to run.
  await cp(source, target, { recursive: true, filter: (file) => !file.endsWith(".pdb") });

  for (const name of REQUIRED[platform]) {
    if (!existsSync(path.join(target, name))) throw new Error(`node-pty's ${prebuild} prebuild has no ${name}.`);
  }
  for (const file of await listFiles(target)) {
    if (!/\.(node|dll|exe)$/.test(file) && path.basename(file) !== "spawn-helper") continue;
    const arches = binaryArches(await readFile(file));
    if (!arches.includes(arch)) {
      const built = arches.length > 0 ? arches.join(" and ") : "an unknown CPU";
      throw new Error(`${withSlashes(path.relative(to, file))} is built for ${built}, not ${arch}.`);
    }
  }
  if (platform === "darwin") {
    // node-pty starts spawn-helper for every terminal, so it must be runnable. Set the mode, then check it
    // (a Windows computer has no such mode bits, so it cannot check).
    const helper = path.join(target, "spawn-helper");
    await chmod(helper, 0o755);
    if (process.platform !== "win32") {
      const mode = (await stat(helper)).mode & 0o777;
      if (mode !== 0o755) throw new Error(`spawn-helper has mode ${mode.toString(8)}, not 755.`);
    }
  }
  const files = await listFiles(to);
  let bytes = 0;
  for (const file of files) bytes += (await stat(file)).size;
  return { prebuild, files: files.map((file) => withSlashes(path.relative(to, file))), bytes };
}
```
