```js
describe("bundled server runs outside the repo", () => {
  let bundleDir = null;
  let skipReason = "";
  // The prebuilt node-pty folder the bundle carries when it is built for this computer.
  const hostPrebuild = `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`;

  before(async () => {
    const distDir = path.join(root, "dist");
    if (!existsSync(distDir)) {
      skipReason = "dist/ is missing; run `npm run build` before this test.";
      return;
    }
    await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const build = spawn(process.execPath, ["scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs"], {
        cwd: root,
        stdio: "inherit"
      });
      build.once("error", reject);
      build.once("exit", (code) => (code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`build-server-bundle.mjs exited ${code}`))));
    });
    const candidate = path.join(root, "build", "server");
    if (existsSync(path.join(candidate, "server.mjs"))) {
      bundleDir = candidate;
    } else {
      skipReason = "build-server-bundle.mjs did not produce build/server/server.mjs";
    }
  });

  // The bundle in a temp folder, outside the repo, with a temp HOME (tests only, H1), started the
  // way the desktop shell starts it: AGENT_OS_PORT=0 and no PORT (decision Q11a).
  async function startBundle(tmpServer, tmpHome) {
    // The six fake agents first on PATH, then the system folders only (decision Q1c): nothing the
    // server looks up can reach a real agent in /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin. POSIX only.
    const fakeBin = path.join(tmpHome, "fake-bin");
    if (!isWindows) await makeFakeAgentBin(fakeBin);
    const env = {
      ...process.env,
      AGENT_OS_PORT: "0",
      AGENT_OS_STATIC_DIR: path.join(tmpServer, "web"),
      AGENT_OS_HOME: tmpHome,
      AGENT_OS_TOKEN: "t",
      AGENT_OS_PACKAGED: "1",
      HERMES_AGENT_OS_SCHEDULER: "0",
      // Keep agent detection away from the developer's real CLIs (~/.local/bin etc.).
      HOME: tmpHome,
      USERPROFILE: tmpHome,
      // In local mode the server reads the login shell's environment right after READY (SP3):
      // W1's stand-in login shell, never the developer's own shell setup, never a real login sh.
      SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
      PATH: [...(isWindows ? [] : [fakeBin]), "/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"].join(path.delimiter)
    };
    delete env.PORT; // the desktop shell never passes PORT
    const child = spawn(process.execPath, [path.join(tmpServer, "server.mjs")], {
      cwd: tmpServer,
      env,
      stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]
    });
    return { child, logs: collectLogs(child) };
  }

  async function sessionsList(base) {
    const response = await fetch(`${base}/api/sessions`, { headers: { "x-agent-os-token": "t" } });
    assert.equal(response.status, 200);
    return response.json();
  }

  test("boots from a temp dir as the desktop app starts it, serves the UI, reports packaged mode, and finds node-pty next to itself", async (t) => {
    if (!bundleDir) {
      t.skip(skipReason);
      return;
    }
    // The bundle carries node-pty for this computer next to server.mjs, where Node looks for it.
    const ptyDir = path.join(bundleDir, "node_modules", "node-pty");
    assert.ok(existsSync(path.join(ptyDir, "package.json")), "node-pty's package.json is in the bundle");
    assert.ok(existsSync(path.join(ptyDir, "lib", "index.js")), "node-pty's lib/ is in the bundle");
    assert.deepEqual(await readdir(path.join(ptyDir, "prebuilds")), [hostPrebuild], "only this computer's prebuilt binary");
    const bundleInfo = JSON.parse(await readFile(path.join(bundleDir, "bundle.json"), "utf8"));
    assert.equal(bundleInfo.target, hostPrebuild);
    // node-pty stays outside server.mjs: esbuild cannot bundle a native module.
    const serverSource = await readFile(path.join(bundleDir, "server.mjs"), "utf8");
    assert.match(serverSource, /["']node-pty["']/, "server.mjs still imports node-pty by name");
    assert.doesNotMatch(serverSource, /loadNativeModule/, "node-pty's own code is not inside server.mjs");

    const tmpServer = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-bundle-"));
    const tmpHome = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-bundle-home-"));
    await cp(bundleDir, tmpServer, { recursive: true });
    const { child, logs } = await startBundle(tmpServer, tmpHome);
    try {
      const port = await waitForReady(child, logs);
      // AGENT_OS_PORT=0 let the system pick a free port; without it the server would take 8090.
      assert.notEqual(port, 8090, "the bundle reads AGENT_OS_PORT, the desktop shell's name for its port");
      const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

      const homepage = await fetch(`${base}/`);
      assert.equal(homepage.status, 200);
      assert.match(await homepage.text(), /<html/i);

      const health = await fetch(`${base}/api/health`);
      assert.equal(health.status, 200);
      const healthBody = await health.json();
      assert.equal(healthBody.packaged, true);

      const exportPrepare = await fetch(`${base}/api/admin/export/prepare`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "x-agent-os-token": "t", "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: "{}"
      });
      assert.equal(exportPrepare.status, 409);

      // The packaged server, outside the repo, loads node-pty from its own folder and starts a
      // program in a terminal with it (pty-host.js's probe; on macOS that runs spawn-helper).
      const sessions = await sessionsList(base);
      assert.deepEqual(sessions.pty, { ok: true, reason: null }, `${logs.text.slice(-1500)}`);
    } finally {
      await killChild(child);
      await rm(tmpServer, { recursive: true, force: true });
      await rm(tmpHome, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  });

  test("without node-pty the bundled server still boots, and says sessions cannot start", async (t) => {
    if (!bundleDir) {
      t.skip(skipReason);
      return;
    }
    const tmpServer = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-bundle-nopty-"));
    const tmpHome = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-bundle-nopty-home-"));
    await cp(bundleDir, tmpServer, { recursive: true });
    await rm(path.join(tmpServer, "node_modules"), { recursive: true, force: true });
    const { child, logs } = await startBundle(tmpServer, tmpHome);
    try {
      const port = await waitForReady(child, logs);
      const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;
      assert.equal((await fetch(`${base}/api/health`)).status, 200, "it boots: node-pty is only loaded when a terminal is needed");
      const sessions = await sessionsList(base);
      // The plain reason from pty-host.js (PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON).
      assert.deepEqual(sessions.pty, { ok: false, reason: "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer." });
    } finally {
      await killChild(child);
      await rm(tmpServer, { recursive: true, force: true });
      await rm(tmpHome, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  });

  test(
    "the node-pty copied with the bundle opens a real terminal (spawn-helper is still runnable after the copy)",
    { skip: isWindows ? "uses /bin/sh as the terminal program" : false },
    async (t) => {
      if (!bundleDir) {
        t.skip(skipReason);
        return;
      }
      const tmpServer = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-bundle-pty-"));
      try {
        await cp(bundleDir, tmpServer, { recursive: true });
        // Resolved the way server.mjs resolves it: from the bundle's own folder.
        const nodePty = createRequire(path.join(tmpServer, "server.mjs"))("node-pty");
        // spawn(file, args, options) → IPty with onData and onExit (node-pty 1.2, typings/node-pty.d.ts).
        const term = nodePty.spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "printf pty-ok"], {
          name: "xterm-256color",
          cols: 80,
          rows: 24,
          cwd: tmpServer,
          env: { PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" }
        });
        let output = "";
        term.onData((data) => {
          output += data;
        });
        const exitCode = await new Promise((resolve) => term.onExit(({ exitCode: code }) => resolve(code)));
        const deadline = Date.now() + 2000;
        while (!output.includes("pty-ok") && Date.now() < deadline) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
        assert.equal(exitCode, 0);
        assert.match(output, /pty-ok/);
      } finally {
        await rm(tmpServer, { recursive: true, force: true });
      }
    }
  );
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Bundle with node-pty next to the server.** Replace the whole of `scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs` with:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Bundles server/index.js into one file the desktop app can run straight out
// of its resources folder, with no repo checkout and no `npm install` step.
// See server/runtime/env.js (AGENT_OS_ENV_FILE), server/index.js
// (AGENT_OS_STATIC_DIR), and server/runtime/builder-service.js
// (AGENT_OS_PACKAGED) for the env overrides that make the bundle behave the
// same as running from source once import.meta.url no longer points at a
// real checkout.
//
//   node scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs                               # for this computer
//   node scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs --platform darwin --arch x64  # for another one
//
// --platform / --arch name the computer the app will run on (the same names as
// scripts/fetch-node.mjs). They choose which of node-pty's prebuilt binaries is
// copied next to the bundle (scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs): the release workflow
// builds the Intel Mac app on an Apple-silicon runner.
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { cp, mkdir, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { copyNodePty, parseTargetArgs } from "./node-pty-bundle.mjs";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const distDir = path.join(root, "dist");
const outDir = path.join(root, "build", "server");

async function main() {
  const target = parseTargetArgs(process.argv.slice(2));

  if (!existsSync(distDir)) {
    console.error(
      "dist/ is missing. Run `npm run build` first, then retry `npm run build:server-bundle`."
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }

  await rm(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await mkdir(outDir, { recursive: true });

  await build({
    entryPoints: [path.join(root, "server", "index.js")],
    outfile: path.join(outDir, "server.mjs"),
    platform: "node",
    format: "esm",
    target: "node24",
    bundle: true,
    logLevel: "info",
    // @elizaos/core is optional (server/runtime/eliza.js already lazy-loads
    // it in a try/catch); the desktop app ships without it.
    // node-pty is a native module, so it cannot go inside server.mjs: it is
    // copied next to the bundle below, and server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js
    // imports it on first use (a server without it still boots).
    // bufferutil and utf-8-validate are optional speed-ups the `ws` package
    // tries to load in a try/catch; they are not installed.
    external: ["@elizaos/core", "node-pty", "bufferutil", "utf-8-validate"],
    banner: {
      js: 'import { createRequire as __agentOsCreateRequire } from "node:module"; const require = __agentOsCreateRequire(import.meta.url);'
    }
  });

  await cp(distDir, path.join(outDir, "web"), { recursive: true });

  // The small script that prints a saved OpenRouter key to Claude Code and
  // Codex (server/runtime/secrets/keystore.js looks for it next to the bundle).
  await cp(path.join(root, "server", "runtime", "secrets", "print-key.mjs"), path.join(outDir, "print-key.mjs"));

  // node-pty for the target computer, where Node looks for it from server.mjs:
  // ./node_modules/node-pty. Stops the build if the target has no prebuilt binary.
  const pty = await copyNodePty({
    from: path.join(root, "node_modules", "node-pty"),
    to: path.join(outDir, "node_modules", "node-pty"),
    platform: target.platform,
    arch: target.arch
  });
  console.log(`node-pty ${pty.prebuild} copied to ${path.relative(root, outDir)}/node_modules/node-pty (${pty.files.length} files)`);

  const pkg = require(path.join(root, "package.json"));
  await writeFile(
    path.join(outDir, "bundle.json"),
    JSON.stringify({ version: pkg.version, builtAt: new Date().toISOString(), node: ">=24", target: pty.prebuild }, null, 2)
  );

  console.log(`Server bundle written to ${path.relative(root, outDir)}/`);
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Build for the target in `prepare-desktop.mjs`.** Replace the whole of `scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs` with:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Gets desktop/src-tauri/resources/ ready for `tauri build`:
//   resources/server  <- the esbuild server bundle + built UI (build/server), with
//                        node-pty's prebuilt binary for the target computer
//   resources/node    <- the app's own Node 24 runtime (scripts/fetch-node.mjs)
// Both folders are git-ignored; they are build output, not source.
// Called by the `desktop:prepare` / `desktop:build` scripts in package.json.
//
//   node scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs
//   node scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs --skip-node --platform darwin --arch x64
//
// --platform / --arch name the TARGET computer (default: this one), with the
// same names as scripts/fetch-node.mjs. They pick node-pty's prebuilt binary
// for the server bundle, and the Node to fetch when --skip-node is not given.
// --skip-node never fetches Node. The release workflow fetches the TARGET's
// Node first (the Intel Mac app is built on an Apple-silicon runner), and
// this script must not swap the host's Node in over it.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { cp, mkdir, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { parseTargetArgs } from "./node-pty-bundle.mjs";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const resources = path.join(root, "desktop", "src-tauri", "resources");

function run(command, args) {
  // shell:true so `npm` resolves to npm.cmd on Windows.
  const result = spawnSync(command, args, { cwd: root, stdio: "inherit", shell: process.platform === "win32" });
  if (result.status !== 0) {
    console.error(`\n\`${command} ${args.join(" ")}\` failed. Fix that first, then run this again.`);
    process.exit(result.status ?? 1);
  }
}

async function main() {
  const target = parseTargetArgs(process.argv.slice(2));

  // Always rebuild the UI and server so the app never ships a stale bundle.
  run("npm", ["run", "build"]);
  run("npm", ["run", "build:server-bundle", "--", "--platform", target.platform, "--arch", target.arch]);

  // Before the --skip-node check below: the release workflow always passes
  // --skip-node, and the server bundle (with node-pty for the target) must
  // reach resources/ in every build.
  const server = path.join(resources, "server");
  await rm(server, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await mkdir(resources, { recursive: true });
  await cp(path.join(root, "build", "server"), server, { recursive: true });
  console.log(`Copied build/server -> desktop/src-tauri/resources/server (node-pty for ${target.platform}-${target.arch})`);

  if (process.argv.includes("--skip-node")) {
    console.log("--skip-node: leaving resources/node exactly as it is.");
    return;
  }
  const nodeBinary = path.join(resources, "node", target.platform === "win32" ? "node.exe" : path.join("bin", "node"));
  if (!existsSync(nodeBinary)) {
    run("node", ["scripts/fetch-node.mjs", "--platform", target.platform, "--arch", target.arch]);
  } else {
    console.log("Bundled Node already present (run `npm run desktop:fetch-node` to refresh it).");
  }
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```markdown
### Terminals (node-pty)

Sessions run each agent in a real terminal through `node-pty`, a native
module. esbuild cannot put it inside `server.mjs`, so
`scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs` copies node-pty's `lib/`, `package.json` and
the one prebuilt folder for the target (`prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>`, without
debug symbols) to `build/server/node_modules/node-pty/`, where Node finds it
from `server.mjs`. The build stops if that prebuilt folder is missing. Every
copied binary's CPU is checked from its file header (never by running it), and
macOS's `spawn-helper` gets mode 755. A server without node-pty still starts;
it only says that sessions cannot start. A future Developer ID notarization
must sign `node`, `pty.node` and `spawn-helper` under `Contents/Resources`.
```

```markdown
  `desktop`).
```

#### Notes

1. **The packaged app itself is proven only on the owner's Mac (owner item, Task E2).** CI builds the shell and runs its unit tests but makes no installer, and nothing here starts `spawn-helper` from inside a signed, quarantined `.app`. One packaged-app check (`npm run desktop:build`, open the app, start a session) belongs with spike S7 in Task E2. A future Developer ID notarization must also sign `pty.node` and `spawn-helper` under `Contents/Resources` (the README says so).
2. **Windows is covered by CI only.** No Windows machine ran these steps. The real-terminal test is skipped there (it runs `/bin/sh`); on the Windows `test` leg the boot test's `pty: { ok: true, reason: null }` still proves the copied node-pty works, because `pty-host.js`'s probe starts `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a ConPTY through the copy (`conpty.node`, `conpty_console_list.node`, `conpty/` and `lib/worker/`). The `desktop (windows-latest)` job runs the same copy through `prepare-desktop.mjs`.
3. **The release workflow is otherwise unchanged.** The Intel Mac leg runs `npm ci` on the Apple-silicon runner, which installs node-pty with all six prebuilt folders (the npm package carries them all), so `--platform darwin --arch x64` finds `prebuilds/darwin-x64` there. No `tauri.conf.json` build hook runs `prepare-desktop.mjs` again, so nothing overwrites the target's copy with the runner's.
4. **The bundle tests start the server the way the desktop app does, and follow the session test rules although they start no session:** `AGENT_OS_PORT=0` and no `PORT` (decision Q11a; the boot test checks the port is not the default 8090), the stand-in login shell and the six fakes first on `PATH` (decision Q1c).
5. **Checked while drafting.**
   - The published node-pty 1.2.0-beta.14 was read, nothing installed: every prebuilt binary for the five shipped targets carries the CPU its folder names in its header (`win32-x64/conpty/conpty.dll` and `OpenConsole.exe` included); a copy without `.pdb` files is about 1.6 MB for win32-x64 and under 0.2 MB for the others, inside the test's 3 MB bound; the package has no `engines` field and uses N-API; its install script only checks that `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>` exists.
   - With node-pty not external, esbuild still bundles a dynamic `import("node-pty")` without errors, so between Task S8 and this task the old bundle script still builds and the bundled server only reports `pty: { ok: false }`.

The release-config block gave `# fail 2` before Step 9 and `# fail 0` after it, and both workflow files still parse as YAML. ### Task U1: Client foundations (sessionsApi, sessionsShared, socket client, nav keys, Shell palette keys, sessions count, quit question)

This task lays down everything the three Sessions UI tasks (U2, U3, U4) consume, before any of them draws a page. It adds the session types; one file with every sessions request (each with a time limit) and the WebSocket client for one terminal; and one pure file with the shared words and rules (titles, status words, the side panel's line, the Stop and Resume words, which keys belong to Agent OS, the quit question, and the pure half of the WebSocket protocol), tested with `node --test`. It also changes four things people will notice: the palette key becomes ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere (never both) and is ignored inside a terminal; the menu's Sessions item shows how many agent sessions are running; in the desktop app, quitting while sessions run asks first; and the update banner's "Install & restart", which also ends every session, asks the same question first. Last, it prepares the UI audit harness for sessions (ruling R17): the throwaway server gets the fake login shell, a real-path temp HOME that probes receive, and the six TUI-like fake agents in `fake-bin/`, which Tasks U3 and U4 reuse. All of this follows the spec's "Browser terminal", "WebSocket protocol" and "Persistence, quit and Stop" sections, planning decisions Q1c, Q2, Q5b, Q6, Q18, Q27, Q30, Q31 and Q40, and rulings R12, R17, R19, R21 and R26.

Depends on: S8 and S9 (the routes and frames this client speaks; the test and the probe here stub them, so U1 is checked without starting a session) and D1 (the shell side of the quit events, and the two page packages `@tauri-apps/api` 2.12.1 and `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` 2.8.3, which D1's Step 1 installs; this task installs nothing, and Step 0 only checks they are there, ruling R3). It also uses two things from earlier tasks: W1's `test/helpers/fake-agents.js` (the harness's fake agents and fake login shell) and S10's `sessionStopTitle` (one test keeps its words the same as `sessionTitle`).

**Decisions taken while drafting (the owner can overturn any of them; rows that now quote a ruling or decision follow it):**

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-U1-1 | Which kit state carries "Starting" and "Ended"? | `starting` → `idle` (dashed circle) labelled "Starting"; `exited` → `stopped` (stop icon) labelled "Ended" (decision Q18, ruling R26). | The only icons that do not claim "working", "ready" or "failed". E1 shows them to the owner. |
| D-U1-2 | What does the menu count? | Running agent sessions: every status but `exited`, `kind: "agent"` only. Shown as the number, spoken "Sessions, 2 running"; hidden at 0 and whenever the last read failed (never a stale number). | Spec Session kinds (an update session is never counted); Q31 (no stale numbers where no warn note fits). |
| D-U1-3 | The shell's 2 s limit (Q6) against a slow quit check | Wait up to 700 ms for the list before drawing anything (usually a few ms). Nothing running: answer quit at once. Slower: show "Checking which sessions are still running…" and tell the shell `quit-shown`, then wait up to 6 s more; still no answer: say so plainly and let the person choose. | The shell quits on its own after 2 s without `quit-shown`, so the question must be on screen well before that. |
| D-U1-4 | Where the update's name in the quit question comes from | The decisions' quit question sentences (ruling R21) are used word for word. "The <agent> update" and "Quitting also stops the <agent> update." are built from the quit check's title for that session ("Hermes update", decision Q27), so no second label map is needed. | One source for the words (S6 builds the title). |
| D-U1-5 | How does the palette key inside a terminal reach the Shell? | The terminal dispatches the `aos-palette` window event (`togglePalette()`); the Shell's own key handler ignores keys from inside `.xterm`. | Spec App shortcuts: the Shell skips `.xterm`, yet ⌘K in a terminal must still open the palette. |
| D-U1-6 | `isAppShortcut` return value | The shortcut (`{ action }`) or `null` (truthy, as U3 reads it), so a caller can also tell which one. Browser mode keeps only the palette key. ⌘\ (split) is not taken in SP3. No Ctrl+Shift+C/V (ruling R25). | Spec: browser mode offers only the palette key; split arrives with SP4, and a swallowed key would do nothing. |
| D-U1-7 | How "processed" is measured for acks | `onOut` may return a promise (U2 resolves it in xterm's write callback); the bytes count when it settles. | Spec: ack the seq this client has processed. Keeps the contract's socket shape. |
| D-U1-8 | The idle line when the time cannot be read | "Idle. Nothing is running." (S6 always sends `stateSince`; this covers a value that cannot be read). | Never make up a duration (Q31). |
| D-U1-9 | The update banner's "Install & restart" while sessions run | It asks first with the quit question: the same title ("Quit Agent OS?") and body, "Keep running", and "Install & restart" in place of "Quit" (decision Q5b, ruling R19). It checks first (the button reads "Checking…", at most the 8 s quit-check limit); no answer shows the "couldn't check" body; nothing running installs at once. | The approved restart leaves with `RESTART_EXIT_CODE`, which the shell's `prevent_exit()` ignores, so only the page can ask before every session ends (spec, Persistence, quit and Stop). |
| D-U1-10 | What a window does after the server closes its socket | `sessionCloseAdvice` reads the reason word: `too_far_behind` → "reattach", `session_ended` → "ended", `attach_failed` or ws's 1009 → "wait" (do not retry at once); anything else (a dropped connection, a refused upgrade, Agent OS restarting) → "reattach". `onClose` gets it as `advice`; U2 still attaches again after a refused upgrade or a 1006 close only while the session list says the session is live (ruling R12). | Clients decide by the word (decision Q40), so a changed number cannot make a window attach to an ended session. |
| D-U1-11 | An ended session whose recording is gone (the 1 GB cap or a delete) | The panel line ends "Its recording was removed." instead of "The recording is in Runs." (`recordingBytes` is 0; decision Q38). | The Runs row is gone then, so "is in Runs" would be false (Q31). |
| D-U1-12 | How the harness's `fake-bin/` gets the TUI-like fakes (ruling R17) | `audit.mjs` calls W1's `makeFakeAgentBin` on every start, so the six shims always run this Node and the repo's `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`; the old `fake-agent` file is left in place, unused. | A shim written once by hand would break silently after a Node upgrade. W1's fake keeps the two old answers SP2's probes rely on (a headless run keeps going until stopped; Hermes's approvals read `manual`). |
| D-U1-13 | The harness's end, once probes run real sessions | The `finally` block waits for the server to exit (its sessions stop within the server's 8 s hard exit; at most 10 s) before it removes the temp HOME. | Otherwise a session still writing its meta.json or recording could make the removal fail, and the server could still hold :8791 when the next run starts. |

```js
// Sessions (SP3) client logic (src/ui/sessionsShared.ts): titles, status words, the side panel's line,
// the Stop and Resume words, which keys belong to Agent OS, the quit question, and the pure half of the
// terminal's WebSocket protocol. Node strips the TypeScript types itself (decision P14), so the .ts files
// are imported directly. Nothing here talks to a server or starts anything.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { test } from "node:test";
import * as ss from "../src/ui/sessionsShared.ts";
import * as stopAll from "../src/ui/stopAllShared.ts";

// 3 pm local time, so durations read the same in every time zone.
const NOW = new Date(2026, 9, 14, 15, 0, 0).getTime();
const iso = (msAgo) => new Date(NOW - msAgo).toISOString();
const session = (over = {}) => ({
  id: "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", kind: "agent", agentId: "claude", agentLabel: "Claude Code",
  folder: "/Users/you/my-app", folderName: "my-app", folderShown: true, branch: null, status: "live",
  stateSince: iso(1000), startedAt: iso(60_000), endedAt: null, exitCode: null, signal: null, endedBy: null,
  dismissed: false, brain: null, resume: { available: true, reason: null, fallback: false }, alerts: "basic",
  recordingBytes: 0, ...over
});
const source = (file) => readFileSync(new URL(`../src/${file}`, import.meta.url), "utf8");
const key = (over) => ({ key: "", code: "", metaKey: false, ctrlKey: false, altKey: false, shiftKey: false, ...over });
const MAC = { isMac: true, desktop: true };
const MAC_BROWSER = { isMac: true, desktop: false };
const PC = { isMac: false, desktop: true };
const PC_BROWSER = { isMac: false, desktop: false };

test("an ended session says how it ended, then where its recording is (or that it was removed)", () => {
  // An ended session's recording holds at least its header line, so recordingBytes is above 0 until the
  // 1 GB cap (Q38) or a delete removes it.
  const ended = (over) => ss.sessionPanelLine(session({ status: "exited", endedAt: iso(1000), recordingBytes: 10, ...over }), NOW);
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: 0 }), "Ended normally. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: 3 }), "Ended with exit code 3. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }), "Ended by signal SIGKILL. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: 0, signal: "SIGHUP" }), "Ended by signal SIGHUP. The recording is in Runs.", "a signal says more than a 0 that comes with it");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: null, signal: "SIGTERM", endedBy: "stop" }), "Stopped by you. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: null, signal: "SIGTERM", endedBy: "quit" }), "Ended when Agent OS quit. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: null, signal: null }), "Ended. The recording is in Runs.");
  assert.equal(ended({ exitCode: 0, recordingBytes: 10 }), "Ended normally. The recording is in Runs.", "a recording that is there is in Runs");
  assert.equal(
    ended({ exitCode: 0, recordingBytes: 0 }),
    "Ended normally. Its recording was removed.",
    "after the 1 GB cap or a delete, Runs no longer has it, so the line does not send you there"
  );
});

test("the quit question's words (ruling R21): one session or many, an update named apart, checking, failed check", () => {
  assert.equal(ss.joinNames([]), "");
  assert.equal(ss.joinNames(["A"]), "A");
  assert.equal(ss.joinNames(["A", "B"]), "A and B");
  assert.equal(ss.joinNames(["A", "B", "C"]), "A, B and C");
  assert.equal(ss.joinNames(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]), "A, B, C, D and 2 more");
  // The quit check sends each item's kind (decision Q27); an agent session unless the test says otherwise.
  // An update session's title is "<agent> update" (S6).
  const item = (title, kind = "agent") => ({ id: title, title, kind });
  const CLAUDE_ITEM = item("Claude Code · my-app");
  const CODEX_ITEM = item("Codex · api");
  const UPDATE_ITEM = item("Hermes update", "update");
  const body = (...live) => ss.quitQuestionCopy({ phase: "asking", live }).body;
  assert.deepEqual(ss.quitQuestionCopy({ phase: "asking", live: [CLAUDE_ITEM, CODEX_ITEM] }), {
    title: "Quit Agent OS?",
    body: "These sessions are still running: Claude Code · my-app and Codex · api. Quitting ends them. Their recordings stay in Runs, and you can resume them later.",
    keep: "Keep running",
    quit: "Quit"
  });
  assert.equal(
    body(CLAUDE_ITEM),
    "Claude Code · my-app is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later."
  );
  assert.equal(
    body(CLAUDE_ITEM, UPDATE_ITEM),
    "Claude Code · my-app is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later. Quitting also stops the Hermes update.",
    "an update is never resumed: it gets its own sentence, and the resume promise covers only the agent session"
  );
  assert.equal(
    body(UPDATE_ITEM, CLAUDE_ITEM, CODEX_ITEM),
    "These sessions are still running: Claude Code · my-app and Codex · api. Quitting ends them. Their recordings stay in Runs, and you can resume them later. Quitting also stops the Hermes update.",
    "the update is never counted among the sessions that can be resumed, wherever it is in the list"
  );
  assert.equal(body(UPDATE_ITEM), "The Hermes update is still running. Quitting stops it.", "only an update running");
  assert.equal(ss.quitQuestionCopy({ phase: "checking" }).body, "Checking which sessions are still running…");
  assert.equal(
    ss.quitQuestionCopy({ phase: "unknown" }).body,
    "Agent OS couldn't check which sessions are running. Quitting ends any that are. Their recordings stay in Runs."
  );
  for (const view of [
    { phase: "checking" },
    { phase: "unknown" },
    { phase: "asking", live: [item("A")] },
    { phase: "asking", live: [item("A"), item("B"), UPDATE_ITEM] },
    { phase: "asking", live: [UPDATE_ITEM] }
  ]) {
    assert.doesNotMatch(Object.values(ss.quitQuestionCopy(view)).join(" "), /—/, "no em dash in visible text");
  }
});

// Time limits of 700 ms and 6 s become 7 ms and 60 ms: the same code path, no real waiting.
async function withFastClock(fn) {
  const realSetTimeout = globalThis.setTimeout;
  globalThis.setTimeout = (callback, ms, ...rest) => realSetTimeout(callback, typeof ms === "number" ? ms / 100 : ms, ...rest);
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    globalThis.setTimeout = realSetTimeout;
  }
}
const after = (ms, value) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(value), ms));
function quitFlow(check) {
  const calls = [];
  let open = true;
  return {
    calls,
    flow: {
      check,
      show: (view) => calls.push(["show", view.phase, view.phase === "asking" ? view.live.map((x) => x.title).join("|") : ""]),
      shown: () => calls.push(["shown"]),
      answer: (quit) => {
        open = false;
        calls.push(["answer", quit]);
      },
      isOpen: () => open
    }
  };
}
const CLAUDE = { id: "a", title: "Claude Code · my-app", kind: "agent" };

test("the quit flow: nothing running quits at once; running sessions are named; a slow answer shows Checking… first", async () => {
  await withFastClock(async () => {
    let q = quitFlow(async () => ({ live: [] }));
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["answer", true]], "nothing would be lost: quit without a question");

    q = quitFlow(async () => ({ live: [CLAUDE] }));
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "asking", "Claude Code · my-app"], ["shown"]]);

    q = quitFlow(async () => {
      throw new Error("Agent OS did not answer in time.");
    });
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "unknown", ""], ["shown"]], "a failed check still asks, and says it could not check");

    q = quitFlow(() => {
      throw new Error("thrown before any promise");
    });
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "unknown", ""], ["shown"]]);

    q = quitFlow(() => after(2000, { live: [CLAUDE] }));
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "checking", ""], ["shown"], ["show", "asking", "Claude Code · my-app"]], "slow: on screen first, names later");

    q = quitFlow(() => after(2000, { live: [] }));
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "checking", ""], ["shown"], ["answer", true]]);

    q = quitFlow(() => new Promise(() => {}));
    await ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "checking", ""], ["shown"], ["show", "unknown", ""]], "no answer at all: say so");

    q = quitFlow(() => after(2000, { live: [CLAUDE] }));
    const done = ss.runQuitFlow(q.flow);
    await after(1000);
    q.flow.answer(false); // the person pressed Keep running while it was checking
    await done;
    assert.deepEqual(q.calls, [["show", "checking", ""], ["shown"], ["answer", false]], "a late answer changes nothing after the person chose");
  });
  assert.ok(ss.QUIT_FAST_MS < 2000, "the question is on screen well inside the shell's 2 s");
});

test("WebSocket input is split into frames of at most 64 KB, never inside a character", () => {
  const frameBytes = (d) => Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify({ t: "in", d }));
  assert.deepEqual(ss.chunkInput(""), []);
  assert.deepEqual(ss.chunkInput("hi\r"), ["hi\r"]);
  assert.equal(ss.chunkInput("x".repeat(200_000)).length, 4, "frames are filled, not cut early");
  for (const text of ["x".repeat(200_000), "\u001b[A".repeat(30_000), "é🙂中".repeat(20_000), '"\\'.repeat(40_000)]) {
    const chunks = ss.chunkInput(text);
    assert.equal(chunks.join(""), text, "nothing is lost or reordered");
    assert.ok(chunks.length > 1);
    for (const chunk of chunks) {
      assert.ok(frameBytes(chunk) <= ss.MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES, `a frame of ${frameBytes(chunk)} bytes`);
      assert.doesNotMatch(chunk, /[\ud800-\udbff]$/, "a chunk never ends half way through an emoji");
    }
  }
  assert.equal(ss.utf8ByteLength("aé🙂中"), 1 + 2 + 4 + 3);
  assert.equal(ss.MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES, 65_536);
});

test("sizes outside 2-500 columns and 1-200 rows are never sent", () => {
  assert.equal(ss.validSize(2, 1), true);
  assert.equal(ss.validSize(500, 200), true);
  assert.equal(ss.validSize(120, 32), true);
  for (const [cols, rows] of [[1, 24], [501, 24], [80, 0], [80, 201], [80.5, 24], [80, Number.NaN], ["80", 24], [null, 24]]) {
    assert.equal(ss.validSize(cols, rows), false, `${cols} × ${rows}`);
  }
  assert.equal(ss.RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS, 50);
});

test("acks: one once 64 KB are on screen, carrying the seq reached; a new snapshot starts again at 0", () => {
  const acks = ss.createAckCounter();
  assert.equal(acks.processed(10_000), null);
  assert.equal(acks.processed(65_535), null);
  assert.equal(acks.processed(65_536), 65_536);
  assert.equal(acks.processed(70_000), null);
  assert.equal(acks.processed(60_000), null, "an older seq changes nothing");
  assert.equal(acks.processed(131_072), 131_072);
  acks.reset();
  assert.equal(acks.processed(65_536), 65_536, "after a new snapshot the count starts at 0 again");
  assert.equal(ss.ACK_EVERY_BYTES, 65_536);
});

test("server frames are read defensively", () => {
  const modes = { altScreen: true, bracketedPaste: true, mouseTracking: "any", mouseEncoding: "sgr", focusReporting: true, cursorKeysApp: true, kittyFlags: 1 };
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "snapshot", data: "x", cols: 80, rows: 24, modes })), { t: "snapshot", data: "x", cols: 80, rows: 24, modes });
  const off = { altScreen: false, bracketedPaste: false, mouseTracking: "none", mouseEncoding: "default", focusReporting: false, cursorKeysApp: false, kittyFlags: 0 };
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "snapshot", data: "", cols: 80, rows: 24 })).modes, off, "missing modes are all off");
  assert.deepEqual(ss.readModes({ altScreen: "yes", mouseTracking: "weird", mouseEncoding: "utf8", kittyFlags: 99 }), off, "values that are not allowed are off");
  assert.equal(ss.readModes({ mouseEncoding: "sgr-pixels" }).mouseEncoding, "sgr-pixels");
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "snapshot", data: "x", cols: 1, rows: 24 })), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "snapshot", cols: 80, rows: 24 })), null);
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: 12, d: "hi" })), { t: "out", seq: 12, d: "hi" });
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: -1, d: "hi" })), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: "12", d: "hi" })), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: 12 })), null);
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "state", status: "exited", exitCode: 3, signal: null, endedBy: "stop" })), {
    t: "state", status: "exited", exitCode: 3, signal: null, endedBy: "stop", resetAt: null
  });
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "state", status: "live" })), {
    t: "state", status: "live", exitCode: null, signal: null, endedBy: null, resetAt: null
  }, "the manager's first state frame carries only the status");
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "state", status: "live", endedBy: "other" })).endedBy, null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "state", status: "nope" })), null);
  assert.deepEqual(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "alert", raw: "bel" })), { t: "alert", raw: "bel" });
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "alert" })), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame(JSON.stringify({ t: "hello" })), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame("[]"), null);
  assert.equal(ss.parseServerFrame("not json"), null);
});

test("after the server closes a socket, the reason word decides (S9: 4000 too_far_behind, 4001 session_ended, 4004 attach_failed), not the number", () => {
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 4000, reason: "too_far_behind" }), "reattach", "too far behind: attach again for a fresh snapshot");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 4001, reason: "session_ended" }), "ended", "the session ended: never attach again");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 4004, reason: "attach_failed" }), "wait", "this window could not attach: not again at once");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 1009, reason: "" }), "wait", "a message over 1 MB (ws's own close): not again at once");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 4001, reason: "too_far_behind" }), "reattach", "the word decides, not the number");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 4000, reason: "session_ended" }), "ended", "the word decides, not the number");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 1006, reason: "" }), "reattach", "a dropped connection attaches again");
  assert.equal(ss.sessionCloseAdvice({ code: 1001, reason: "" }), "reattach", "Agent OS going away (a restart) attaches again");
});

test("wiring: every sessions request has a time limit, the Shell skips keys typed in a terminal, the new query keys are kept, and the update banner asks first", () => {
  const api = source("sessionsApi.ts");
```

```ts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sessions (SP3): an agent's own terminal, kept by server/runtime/sessions/. These mirror manager.js's
// SessionSummary, routes.js's answers and ws.js's frames (spec "SP3 Sessions engine and page"; the SP3
// contract). Frames are read defensively by src/ui/sessionsShared.ts (parseServerFrame).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type SessionKind = "agent" | "update";

// "waiting" and "held" are never produced in SP3; they arrive with SP4's signals.
export type SessionStatus = "starting" | "live" | "waiting" | "idle" | "held" | "exited";

// "stop" or "quit" when Agent OS ended the session, otherwise null.
export type SessionEndedBy = "stop" | "quit" | null;

export interface SessionSummary {
  id: string;
  kind: SessionKind;
  agentId: string;
  // The short name: "Claude Code", "Codex", "Cursor", "Hermes", "OpenClaw".
  agentLabel: string;
  folder: string;
  folderName: string;
  // false for OpenClaw until spike S5: it picks its own folder, so none is shown or claimed.
  folderShown: boolean;
  branch: string | null;
  status: SessionStatus;
  // When the current status began (ISO time), for "Idle for <time>".
  stateSince: string;
  startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string | null;
  // null when a signal ended the process.
  exitCode: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  endedBy: SessionEndedBy;
  dismissed: boolean;
  brain: { kind: "plan" | "openrouter" | "local"; label: string } | null;
  resume: { available: boolean; reason: string | null; fallback: boolean };
  // Every session's alerts are "basic" in SP3 (the 20 s rule).
  alerts: "basic";
  recordingBytes: number;
}

export interface SessionListResponse {
  sessions: SessionSummary[];
  // The quiet one-line notice when the login-shell environment could not be read (H2), else null.
  environmentNotice: string | null;
  pty: { ok: boolean; reason: string | null };
  maxLive: number;
}

// POST /api/sessions/:id/stop: the session (unchanged when it had already ended), plus Stop's note: OpenClaw's
// honest "Stopped the terminal. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step." when only its terminal could be
// stopped, otherwise null.
export interface StopSessionResult extends SessionSummary {
  note: string | null;
}

export interface SessionSettings {
  claudeFullscreen: boolean;
}

export interface SessionFolder {
  path: string;
  name: string;
  lastUsedAt: string;
}

export interface SessionFolderList {
  folders: SessionFolder[];
}

export interface QuitCheckItem {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  // An update session is never resumed, so the quit question promises a resume only when none is listed.
  kind: SessionKind;
}

export interface QuitCheckResponse {
  live: QuitCheckItem[];
}

export interface RecordingSummary {
  sessionId: string;
  // Update rows read "<agent> update" (spec, Session kinds).
  kind: SessionKind;
  agentId: string;
  agentLabel: string;
  folder: string;
  folderName: string;
  // false for OpenClaw until spike S5: its row reads "OpenClaw · Set by OpenClaw", never a folder it may not use.
  folderShown: boolean;
  startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string | null;
  bytes: number;
  live: boolean;
}

export interface RecordingListResponse {
  recordings: RecordingSummary[];
  // How many recordings were removed to stay under 1 GB since the server started (Q38).
  removedByCap: number;
}

// The terminal modes a snapshot carries (mirror.js), put back on reattach (spec, Browser terminal).
export type MouseTrackingMode = "none" | "x10" | "vt200" | "drag" | "any";
export type MouseEncodingMode = "default" | "sgr" | "sgr-pixels";

export interface SessionModes {
  altScreen: boolean;
  bracketedPaste: boolean;
  mouseTracking: MouseTrackingMode;
  mouseEncoding: MouseEncodingMode;
  focusReporting: boolean;
  cursorKeysApp: boolean;
  kittyFlags: number;
}

export interface SessionSnapshot {
  data: string;
  cols: number;
  rows: number;
  modes: SessionModes;
}

export interface SessionStateFrame {
  status: SessionStatus;
  exitCode: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  endedBy: SessionEndedBy;
  resetAt: string | null;
}

// Server to client, one JSON message per frame (ws.js).
export type SessionServerFrame =
  | ({ t: "snapshot" } & SessionSnapshot)
  | { t: "out"; seq: number; d: string }
  | ({ t: "state" } & SessionStateFrame)
  | { t: "alert"; raw: string };

// Client to server.
export type SessionClientFrame =
  | { t: "focus" }
  | { t: "in"; d: string }
  | { t: "resize"; cols: number; rows: number }
  | { t: "ack"; seq: number };
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the shared rules.** Create `src/ui/sessionsShared.ts`:

```ts
// Sessions (SP3): the words and small rules shared by the Sessions page, Home, Runs, the menu and the quit
// question, plus the pure half of the terminal's WebSocket protocol (frame sizes, acks, reading a frame).
// `import type` only (decision P14): test/sessions-shared.test.js loads this file straight from src/ and
// Node strips the types.
import type {
  MouseEncodingMode,
  MouseTrackingMode,
  QuitCheckItem,
  SessionModes,
  SessionServerFrame,
  SessionStatus,
  SessionSummary
} from "../types";
import type { StatusState } from "./components/StatusWord";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Titles, status words and the side panel's line
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// What every tab, dialog and recording calls a session: "Claude Code · my-app". OpenClaw picks its own
// folder until spike S5, so its sessions read "OpenClaw · Set by OpenClaw". An update session is
// "<agent> update" (spec, Session kinds). "—" stands in for a folder name that is not known.
export function sessionTitle(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "agentLabel" | "folderName" | "folderShown">): string {
  if (s.kind === "update") return `${s.agentLabel} update`;
  if (s.folderShown === false) return `${s.agentLabel} · Set by OpenClaw`;
  return `${s.agentLabel} · ${s.folderName || "—"}`;
}

// The kit's status words (planning decision Q18): "Starting" and "Ended" are new labels on existing
// states, not new colours. An unknown status from the server shows "—".
const STATE_WORDS: Record<SessionStatus, { state: StatusState; label: string }> = {
  starting: { state: "idle", label: "Starting" },
  live: { state: "live", label: "Live" },
  waiting: { state: "waiting", label: "Waiting for you" },
  idle: { state: "idle", label: "Idle" },
  held: { state: "held", label: "Held" },
  exited: { state: "stopped", label: "Ended" }
};

function knownStatus(status: unknown): status is SessionStatus {
  return typeof status === "string" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(STATE_WORDS, status);
}

export function sessionStateWord(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status">): { state: StatusState; label: string } {
  return knownStatus(s.status) ? STATE_WORDS[s.status] : { state: "unknown", label: "" };
}

// A session whose program is still running: every status but "exited" (an unknown status is not counted).
export function isSessionRunning(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status">): boolean {
  return knownStatus(s.status) && s.status !== "exited";
}

// The menu's count: running AGENT sessions only; an update session is never shown there (spec, Session kinds).
export function runningSessionCount(sessions: ReadonlyArray<Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "status">>): number {
  return sessions.filter((s) => s.kind === "agent" && isSessionRunning(s)).length;
}

// "under 1 m", "26 m", "1 h 05 m" (the same words as Home's elapsedLabel); "—" when not known.
export function sessionDuration(fromIso: string | null | undefined, now: number): string {
  const from = fromIso ? Date.parse(fromIso) : NaN;
  if (!Number.isFinite(from) || now < from) return "—";
  const minutes = Math.floor((now - from) / 60_000);
  if (minutes < 1) return "under 1 m";
  if (minutes < 60) return `${minutes} m`;
  return `${Math.floor(minutes / 60)} h ${String(minutes % 60).padStart(2, "0")} m`;
}

type EndFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "exitCode" | "signal" | "endedBy">;

// How a session ended, in words (spec, the side panel's exited lines). Agent OS's own Stop and quit come
// first, because both end the program with a signal; then a signal, which says more than an exit code
// that comes with it.
export function endedLine(s: EndFields): string {
  if (s.endedBy === "stop") return "Stopped by you.";
  if (s.endedBy === "quit") return "Ended when Agent OS quit.";
  if (typeof s.signal === "string" && s.signal.trim()) return `Ended by signal ${s.signal.trim()}.`;
  if (s.exitCode === 0) return "Ended normally.";
  if (typeof s.exitCode === "number" && Number.isFinite(s.exitCode)) return `Ended with exit code ${s.exitCode}.`;
  return "Ended.";
}

// The side panel's one line for the state, SP3 versions (spec, Session activity states). Before alerts
// exist, live says only "Working."; waiting and held never happen in SP3 but get true words anyway. An
// ended session's recording holds at least its header line, so 0 bytes means the 1 GB cap (Q38) or a
// delete removed it: then Runs has no row for it, and the line does not send the person there.
export function sessionPanelLine(
  s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status" | "agentLabel" | "recordingBytes"> & { stateSince?: string | null } & EndFields,
  now: number
): string {
  switch (s.status) {
    case "starting":
      return `Starting ${s.agentLabel}…`;
    case "live":
      return "Working.";
    case "waiting":
      return "The question is in the terminal. Agent OS never answers for you.";
    case "idle": {
      const time = sessionDuration(s.stateSince, now);
      return time === "—" ? "Idle. Nothing is running." : `Idle for ${time}. Nothing is running.`;
    }
    case "held":
      return "Plan limit reached.";
    case "exited":
      return s.recordingBytes > 0 ? `${endedLine(s)} The recording is in Runs.` : `${endedLine(s)} Its recording was removed.`;
    default:
      return "";
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The Stop dialog and the Resume confirm
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

type DialogFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "agentId" | "agentLabel" | "folderName" | "folderShown">;

export interface StopDialogCopy {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  note: string | null;
  cancel: string;
  confirm: string;
}

// The Stop dialog (spec, the prototype's stopDialog()). OpenClaw adds what Stop cannot promise for it
// until spike S5.
export function stopDialogCopy(s: DialogFields): StopDialogCopy {
  return {
    title: `Stop ${sessionTitle(s)}?`,
    body: `This ends ${s.agentLabel} in this tab. The recording stays in Runs.`,
    note: s.agentId === "openclaw" ? "OpenClaw may still finish its last step after the terminal closes." : null,
    cancel: "Keep it running",
    confirm: "Stop session"
  };
}

export interface ResumeConfirmCopy {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  warning: string | null;
  blocked: string | null;
  cancel: string;
  confirm: string;
}

// Resume conversation's confirm (spec, Resume per agent; planning decision Q36). `blocked` is the written
// reason when the rules say no (the button is disabled and shows it); `warning` is a fallback resume's
// honest limit.
export function resumeConfirmCopy(s: DialogFields & Pick<SessionSummary, "resume">): ResumeConfirmCopy {
  const resume = s.resume || { available: false, reason: null, fallback: false };
  return {
    title: `Resume ${sessionTitle(s)}?`,
    body: `This starts ${s.agentLabel} again in the same tab and continues the conversation. The recording continues after a marker.`,
    warning: resume.fallback
      ? `This resumes the most recent ${s.agentLabel} conversation in this folder, which may be one you started outside Agent OS.`
      : null,
    blocked: resume.available ? null : resume.reason || "This session can't be resumed.",
    cancel: "Cancel",
    confirm: "Resume conversation"
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Keys (spec, App shortcuts (precedence))
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function isMacPlatform(platform: string): boolean {
  return /mac/i.test(platform || "");
}

// The parts of a KeyboardEvent these rules read (a real KeyboardEvent fits).
export interface KeyLike {
  key: string;
  code?: string;
  metaKey: boolean;
  ctrlKey: boolean;
  altKey: boolean;
  shiftKey: boolean;
}

export type AppShortcut = { action: "palette" } | { action: "new-session" } | { action: "switch"; index: number };

// The letter pressed, also on a keyboard layout that types another letter in that place (for example
// Cyrillic): then the key's place (event.code) decides.
function isLetter(event: KeyLike, letter: string): boolean {
  const pressed = (event.key || "").toLowerCase();
  if (pressed === letter) return true;
  return !/^[a-z]$/.test(pressed) && event.code === `Key${letter.toUpperCase()}`;
}

// 1 to 9 on the number row: by the key's place first, because Shift changes the character (Ctrl+Shift+1 types "!").
function rowDigit(event: KeyLike): number | null {
  const byPlace = /^Digit([1-9])$/.exec(event.code || "");
  if (byPlace) return Number(byPlace[1]);
  return /^[1-9]$/.test(event.key || "") ? Number(event.key) : null;
}

// The palette key OUTSIDE a terminal: ⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl+K elsewhere, never both on one computer.
export function isPaletteKey(event: KeyLike, { isMac }: { isMac: boolean }): boolean {
  if (event.altKey || event.shiftKey) return false;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey : event.ctrlKey && !event.metaKey;
  return held && isLetter(event, "k");
}

// The only keys a terminal leaves to Agent OS: ⌘K, ⌘T and ⌘1-9 on a Mac; Ctrl+Shift+K/T/1-9 elsewhere.
// Everything else goes to the agent, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+R included. A browser keeps ⌘T and ⌘1-9 (Ctrl+T,
// Ctrl+1-9, Ctrl+Shift+T) for itself, so in browser mode only the palette key is Agent OS's. ⌘\ (split)
// arrives with SP4 and is not taken yet.
export function isAppShortcut(event: KeyLike, { isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): AppShortcut | null {
  if (event.altKey) return null;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.shiftKey : event.ctrlKey && event.shiftKey && !event.metaKey;
  if (!held) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "k")) return { action: "palette" };
  if (!desktop) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "t")) return { action: "new-session" };
  const digit = rowDigit(event);
  return digit === null ? null : { action: "switch", index: digit - 1 };
}

// The side panel footer's hints: desktop app only, nothing in browser mode (spec, Browser mode).
export function shortcutHints({ isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): Array<{ keys: string; word: string }> {
  if (!desktop) return [];
  return isMac
    ? [{ keys: "⌘T", word: "new" }, { keys: "⌘1-9", word: "switch" }]
    : [{ keys: "Ctrl+Shift+T", word: "new" }, { keys: "Ctrl+Shift+1-9", word: "switch" }];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The quit question (desktop app; planning decision Q6)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT = "agentos://quit-requested";
export const QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT = "agentos://quit-shown";
export const QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT = "agentos://quit-answer";
// The shell quits on its own when no window says "quit-shown" within 2 s. A local answer normally takes a
// few milliseconds; when it takes longer than this, the question shows "Checking…" first.
export const QUIT_FAST_MS = 700;
// How much longer the question waits for the list before it says it could not check.
export const QUIT_CHECK_MS = 6000;

export type QuitView = { phase: "checking" } | { phase: "asking"; live: QuitCheckItem[] } | { phase: "unknown" };

// "A", "A and B", "A, B and C", "A, B, C, D and 2 more".
export function joinNames(names: string[], max = 4): string {
  const shown = names.slice(0, max);
  const rest = names.length - shown.length;
  const parts = rest > 0 ? [...shown, `${rest} more`] : shown;
  if (parts.length <= 1) return parts[0] ?? "";
  return `${parts.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} and ${parts[parts.length - 1]}`;
}

// The quit question's words (planning decisions, "Quit question"; ruling R21). An update session is never
// resumed (spec, Session kinds), so the agent sentence, with its resume promise, covers only agent sessions,
// and a running update gets its own sentence. Its title is already "<agent> update" (S6, decision Q27).
export function quitQuestionCopy(view: QuitView): { title: string; body: string; keep: string; quit: string } {
  const base = { title: "Quit Agent OS?", keep: "Keep running", quit: "Quit" };
  if (view.phase === "checking") return { ...base, body: "Checking which sessions are still running…" };
  if (view.phase === "unknown") {
    return { ...base, body: "Agent OS couldn't check which sessions are running. Quitting ends any that are. Their recordings stay in Runs." };
  }
  const agents = view.live.filter((item) => item.kind !== "update").map((item) => item.title);
  const updates = view.live.filter((item) => item.kind === "update").map((item) => `the ${item.title}`);
  const sentences: string[] = [];
  if (agents.length === 1) {
    sentences.push(`${agents[0]} is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later.`);
  } else if (agents.length > 1) {
    sentences.push(
      `These sessions are still running: ${joinNames(agents)}. Quitting ends them. Their recordings stay in Runs, and you can resume them later.`
    );
  }
  if (updates.length > 0) {
    // At most one update runs at a time (S6), so this is nearly always "the Hermes update".
    const names = joinNames(updates);
    sentences.push(
      agents.length > 0
        ? `Quitting also stops ${names}.`
        : `${names.charAt(0).toUpperCase()}${names.slice(1)} ${updates.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} still running. Quitting stops ${updates.length === 1 ? "it" : "them"}.`
    );
  }
  return { ...base, body: sentences.join(" ") };
}

export interface QuitFlow {
  // POST /api/sessions/quit-check.
  check: () => Promise<{ live: QuitCheckItem[] }>;
  // Draw (or redraw) the question.
  show: (view: QuitView) => void;
  // Tell the shell the question is on screen ("agentos://quit-shown"). Called at most once.
  shown: () => void;
  // Answer without asking (nothing would be lost).
  answer: (quit: boolean) => void;
  // false once the person has answered, so a late check changes nothing.
  isOpen: () => boolean;
}

type Checked = { live: QuitCheckItem[] } | null;

function within<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, late: T): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(late), ms);
    void promise.then((value) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(value);
    });
  });
}

// What the window does when the shell asks to quit: quit at once when nothing runs; otherwise put the
// question on screen inside the shell's 2 s, naming the running sessions as soon as they are known.
export async function runQuitFlow(flow: QuitFlow): Promise<void> {
  const checked: Promise<Checked> = Promise.resolve()
    .then(() => flow.check())
    .then(
      (answer) => (answer && Array.isArray(answer.live) ? { live: answer.live } : null),
      () => null
    );
  const first = await within<Checked | "slow">(checked, QUIT_FAST_MS, "slow");
  if (!flow.isOpen()) return;
  if (first !== "slow") {
    if (first && first.live.length === 0) {
      flow.answer(true);
      return;
    }
    flow.show(first ? { phase: "asking", live: first.live } : { phase: "unknown" });
    flow.shown();
    return;
  }
  flow.show({ phase: "checking" });
  flow.shown();
  const later = await within<Checked>(checked, QUIT_CHECK_MS, null);
  if (!flow.isOpen()) return;
  if (later && later.live.length === 0) {
    flow.answer(true);
    return;
  }
  flow.show(later ? { phase: "asking", live: later.live } : { phase: "unknown" });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The terminal's WebSocket protocol, pure half (spec, WebSocket protocol)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Acknowledge at least every 64 KB received (and processed).
export const ACK_EVERY_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
// An {t:"in"} frame over 64 KB is refused, so every frame (JSON and all) stays at or under it.
export const MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
export const RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 50;
export const MIN_COLS = 2;
export const MAX_COLS = 500;
export const MIN_ROWS = 1;
export const MAX_ROWS = 200;

export function validSize(cols: unknown, rows: unknown): boolean {
  return (
    typeof cols === "number" &&
    typeof rows === "number" &&
    Number.isInteger(cols) &&
    Number.isInteger(rows) &&
    cols >= MIN_COLS &&
    cols <= MAX_COLS &&
    rows >= MIN_ROWS &&
    rows <= MAX_ROWS
  );
}

// Bytes the text takes as UTF-8 (a lone surrogate counts 3, as TextEncoder writes U+FFFD).
export function utf8ByteLength(text: string): number {
  let bytes = 0;
  for (const ch of text) {
    const cp = ch.codePointAt(0) as number;
    bytes += cp < 0x80 ? 1 : cp < 0x800 ? 2 : cp < 0x10000 ? 3 : 4;
  }
  return bytes;
}

// Bytes one character takes inside a JSON string, as UTF-8.
function jsonBytes(cp: number): number {
  if (cp === 0x22 || cp === 0x5c) return 2; // \" and \\
  if (cp === 0x08 || cp === 0x09 || cp === 0x0a || cp === 0x0c || cp === 0x0d) return 2; // \b \t \n \f \r
  if (cp < 0x20) return 6; // \u001b and the other control characters
  if (cp >= 0xd800 && cp <= 0xdfff) return 6; // a lone surrogate is written as \udxxx
  return cp < 0x80 ? 1 : cp < 0x800 ? 2 : cp < 0x10000 ? 3 : 4;
}

const IN_FRAME_OVERHEAD = utf8ByteLength(JSON.stringify({ t: "in", d: "" }));

// Splits typed or pasted text into {t:"in"} frames of at most `maxFrameBytes` each, never inside a
// character (an emoji stays whole).
export function chunkInput(data: string, maxFrameBytes = MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES): string[] {
  if (!data) return [];
  const budget = maxFrameBytes - IN_FRAME_OVERHEAD;
  const chunks: string[] = [];
  let current = "";
  let used = 0;
  for (const ch of data) {
    const size = jsonBytes(ch.codePointAt(0) as number);
    if (used + size > budget && current) {
      chunks.push(current);
      current = "";
      used = 0;
    }
    current += ch;
    used += size;
  }
  if (current) chunks.push(current);
  return chunks;
}

// Counts output that is on screen and says when to acknowledge it: once 64 KB more than the last ack.
export function createAckCounter(every = ACK_EVERY_BYTES) {
  let processed = 0;
  let acked = 0;
  return {
    // Output up to `seq` (cumulative UTF-8 bytes since the snapshot) is on screen. Returns the seq to
    // acknowledge now, or null.
    processed(seq: number): number | null {
      if (!Number.isFinite(seq) || seq <= processed) return null;
      processed = seq;
      if (processed - acked < every) return null;
      acked = processed;
      return processed;
    },
    // A fresh snapshot starts the count again at 0 (seq counts from 0 after each snapshot).
    reset() {
      processed = 0;
      acked = 0;
    }
  };
}

const MOUSE_TRACKING: readonly MouseTrackingMode[] = ["none", "x10", "vt200", "drag", "any"];
const MOUSE_ENCODING: readonly MouseEncodingMode[] = ["default", "sgr", "sgr-pixels"];

function oneOf<T extends string>(value: unknown, allowed: readonly T[], fallback: T): T {
  return (allowed as readonly unknown[]).includes(value) ? (value as T) : fallback;
}

// The snapshot's modes, every value checked; anything not allowed is off.
export function readModes(raw: unknown): SessionModes {
  const m = raw && typeof raw === "object" ? (raw as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
  const flags = m.kittyFlags;
  return {
    altScreen: m.altScreen === true,
    bracketedPaste: m.bracketedPaste === true,
    mouseTracking: oneOf(m.mouseTracking, MOUSE_TRACKING, "none"),
    mouseEncoding: oneOf(m.mouseEncoding, MOUSE_ENCODING, "default"),
    focusReporting: m.focusReporting === true,
    cursorKeysApp: m.cursorKeysApp === true,
    kittyFlags: typeof flags === "number" && Number.isInteger(flags) && flags >= 0 && flags <= 31 ? flags : 0
  };
}

const numberOrNull = (value: unknown): number | null => (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null);
const textOrNull = (value: unknown): string | null => (typeof value === "string" && value ? value : null);

// One server frame, or null for anything that is not a well-formed frame (it is then ignored).
export function parseServerFrame(text: string): SessionServerFrame | null {
  let raw: unknown;
  try {
    raw = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return null;
  const f = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (f.t === "snapshot") {
    if (typeof f.data !== "string" || !validSize(f.cols, f.rows)) return null;
    return { t: "snapshot", data: f.data, cols: f.cols as number, rows: f.rows as number, modes: readModes(f.modes) };
  }
  if (f.t === "out") {
    if (typeof f.d !== "string" || typeof f.seq !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(f.seq) || f.seq < 0) return null;
    return { t: "out", seq: f.seq, d: f.d };
  }
  if (f.t === "state") {
    if (!knownStatus(f.status)) return null;
    const endedBy = f.endedBy === "stop" || f.endedBy === "quit" ? f.endedBy : null;
    return { t: "state", status: f.status, exitCode: numberOrNull(f.exitCode), signal: textOrNull(f.signal), endedBy, resetAt: textOrNull(f.resetAt) };
  }
  if (f.t === "alert") return typeof f.raw === "string" ? { t: "alert", raw: f.raw } : null;
  return null;
}

// What a window does after the server closed its socket. S9's CLOSE_CODES give each reason word a number
// (too_far_behind 4000, session_ended 4001, attach_failed 4004), and the close reason text is that word.
// The word decides, never the number, so a changed number cannot make a window attach to an ended session.
// 1009 is ws's own close for a message over 1 MB and carries no word of Agent OS's: the one number read.
//   "reattach": attach again for a fresh snapshot (too far behind, a dropped connection, Agent OS restarting);
//   "ended":    the session ended; keep the last screen and never attach again;
//   "wait":     this window could not attach, or sent too much; do not try again at once.
export type SessionCloseAdvice = "reattach" | "ended" | "wait";

export function sessionCloseAdvice({ code, reason }: { code: number; reason: string }): SessionCloseAdvice {
  if (reason === "session_ended") return "ended";
  if (reason === "too_far_behind") return "reattach";
  if (reason === "attach_failed" || code === 1009) return "wait";
  return "reattach";
}
```
