```ts
// Sessions (SP3): every request the shell and the pages make about sessions, each one with a time limit
// (withTimeout, planning decision Q31), and the WebSocket client for one session's terminal (spec,
// WebSocket protocol). The pure rules (frame sizes, acks, reading a frame) live in
// src/ui/sessionsShared.ts, where test/sessions-shared.test.js checks them.
import { ApiError, request } from "./api";
import type {
  QuitCheckResponse,
  RecordingListResponse,
  SessionClientFrame,
  SessionFolderList,
  SessionListResponse,
  SessionSettings,
  SessionSnapshot,
  SessionStateFrame,
  SessionSummary,
  StopSessionResult
} from "./types";
import { withTimeout } from "./ui/homeShared";
import { chunkInput, createAckCounter, parseServerFrame, RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS, sessionCloseAdvice, validSize } from "./ui/sessionsShared";
import type { SessionCloseAdvice } from "./ui/sessionsShared";

// How long each request may take before the page says Agent OS did not answer.
export const SESSION_LIMITS_MS = {
  list: 8000,
  // The server waits for the login-shell environment (up to 10 s, H2) before it starts the agent.
  create: 30000,
  // The soft stop (2 s) and the kill grace (3 s), with room to spare.
  stop: 15000,
  resume: 30000,
  dismiss: 10000,
  settings: 10000,
  folders: 10000,
  quitCheck: 8000,
  recordings: 10000,
  signedIn: 5000
} as const;

const TIMEOUT_WORDS = "Agent OS did not answer in time.";
const UNREADABLE = "Agent OS gave an answer that could not be read.";

const sessionPath = (sessionId: string, tail = "") => `/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(sessionId)}${tail}`;
const postJson = (body: unknown = {}): RequestInit => ({ method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) });

export async function listSessions(): Promise<SessionListResponse> {
  const body = await withTimeout(request<SessionListResponse>("/api/sessions"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.list);
  if (!body || !Array.isArray(body.sessions)) throw new Error(UNREADABLE);
  return body;
}

// `folder` is null for OpenClaw, which picks its own folder until spike S5. The server checks the folder
// (planning decision Q14) and answers 400 folder_refused with a sentence when it is not allowed.
export function createSession({ agentId, folder }: { agentId: string; folder: string | null }): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>("/api/sessions", postJson({ agentId, folder })), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.create);
}

export function stopSession(sessionId: string): Promise<StopSessionResult> {
  return withTimeout(request<StopSessionResult>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/stop"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.stop);
}

export function resumeSession(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/resume"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.resume);
}

export function dismissSession(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/dismiss"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.dismiss);
}

export function getSessionSettings(): Promise<SessionSettings> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSettings>("/api/sessions/settings"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.settings);
}

export function putSessionSettings(patch: Partial<SessionSettings>): Promise<SessionSettings> {
  return withTimeout(
    request<SessionSettings>("/api/sessions/settings", { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify(patch) }),
    SESSION_LIMITS_MS.settings
  );
}

export function listSessionFolders(): Promise<SessionFolderList> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionFolderList>("/api/sessions/folders"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.folders);
}

// Every live session of both kinds, with its title, for the quit question (planning decision Q27).
export function quitCheck(): Promise<QuitCheckResponse> {
  return withTimeout(request<QuitCheckResponse>("/api/sessions/quit-check", postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.quitCheck);
}

export function listRecordings(): Promise<RecordingListResponse> {
  return withTimeout(request<RecordingListResponse>("/api/recordings"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.recordings);
}

export function deleteRecording(sessionId: string): Promise<{ ok: true }> {
  return withTimeout(request<{ ok: true }>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/recording"), { method: "DELETE" }), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.recordings);
}

// Words for a refused or failed request: the server's own sentence when it sent one (Q14, Q15, Q25),
// otherwise a plain fallback.
export function sessionProblem(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) return error.detail || "Agent OS couldn't do that. Try again.";
  if (error instanceof Error && error.message === TIMEOUT_WORDS) return TIMEOUT_WORDS;
  return "Couldn't reach Agent OS.";
}

// True when a request got no answer at all (time limit or network): it may still have happened, so a page
// never says "nothing was changed" then, and reads the list again instead (Q31).
export function sessionGotNoAnswer(error: unknown): boolean {
  return !(error instanceof ApiError);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The WebSocket client for one session's terminal
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface SessionSocketClose {
  // 4000 too_far_behind, 4001 session_ended, 4004 attach_failed (S9's CLOSE_CODES), ws's 1009, or the
  // browser's own (1006 for a dropped connection). For logs; `advice` is what to act on.
  code: number;
  // The server's reason word: "too_far_behind", "session_ended" or "attach_failed" (empty when none came).
  reason: string;
  // false when the socket closed before its snapshot arrived (refused, or the server went away).
  hadSnapshot: boolean;
  // Decided by the reason word (sessionCloseAdvice): "reattach" (attach again for a fresh snapshot),
  // "ended" (never attach again) or "wait" (attach_failed or 1009: do not try again at once). A refused
  // upgrade (an ended or unknown session gets a bare 403) arrives as 1006 with no word, so "reattach" here
  // is only advice: the terminal (U2) attaches again only while the session list still says the session is
  // live (ruling R12).
  advice: SessionCloseAdvice;
}

export interface SessionSocketHandlers {
  // The first frame. A returned promise holds every later frame until it settles, so output never lands
  // before the restored screen.
  onSnapshot: (snapshot: SessionSnapshot) => void | Promise<void>;
  // A returned promise means "not on screen yet": the bytes count as processed (for acks) when it settles.
  onOut: (data: string) => void | Promise<void>;
  onState: (state: SessionStateFrame) => void;
  // SP3: the raw OSC 9 / 99 / 777 payload, or "bel".
  onAlert: (raw: string) => void;
  // Not called after close() from this side.
  onClose: (info: SessionSocketClose) => void;
}

export interface SessionSocket {
  // This terminal has the keys: it becomes the writer, and its size follows at once.
  focus(): void;
  // Keystrokes, paste and the terminal's own replies to terminal queries.
  input(data: string): void;
  resize(cols: number, rows: number): void;
  close(): void;
}

// Same host as the page; no query string and no token in the address (the session cookie goes with the
// upgrade; Security 1, planning decision Q40).
export function sessionSocketUrl(sessionId: string): string {
  const scheme = window.location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:";
  return `${scheme}//${window.location.host}${sessionPath(sessionId, "/attach")}`;
}

// A socket that closes before its snapshot may mean the person is signed out: check, the way useRunStream does.
async function checkStillSignedIn(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const session = await withTimeout(request<{ authenticated?: boolean }>("/api/session"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.signedIn);
    if (session && session.authenticated === false) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("agentos:locked"));
  } catch {
    // A network hiccup here is not a sign-out.
  }
}

export function openSessionSocket(sessionId: string, handlers: SessionSocketHandlers): SessionSocket {
  const ws = new WebSocket(sessionSocketUrl(sessionId));
  const acks = createAckCounter();
  let closedHere = false;
  let hadSnapshot = false;
  // Settles once the snapshot is on screen; every later frame waits for it, in arrival order.
  let ready: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
  let size: { cols: number; rows: number } | null = null;
  let sent: { cols: number; rows: number } | null = null;
  let resizeTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  let focusWhenOpen = false;

  const send = (frame: SessionClientFrame): boolean => {
    if (ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return false;
    ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame));
    return true;
  };
  const cancelResize = () => {
    if (resizeTimer !== null) clearTimeout(resizeTimer);
    resizeTimer = null;
  };
  const sendSize = () => {
    cancelResize();
    if (size && send({ t: "resize", cols: size.cols, rows: size.rows })) sent = { ...size };
  };
  // {t:"focus"} makes this window the writer; its size follows right after it (spec).
  const takeKeys = () => {
    send({ t: "focus" });
    sendSize();
  };

  ws.onopen = () => {
    if (focusWhenOpen) {
      focusWhenOpen = false;
      takeKeys();
    }
  };

  ws.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    if (closedHere || typeof event.data !== "string") return;
    const frame = parseServerFrame(event.data);
    if (!frame) return;
    if (frame.t === "snapshot") {
      // One snapshot per socket; a fresh one comes with a new socket.
      if (hadSnapshot) return;
      hadSnapshot = true;
      acks.reset();
      const snapshot: SessionSnapshot = { data: frame.data, cols: frame.cols, rows: frame.rows, modes: frame.modes };
      ready = Promise.resolve()
        .then(() => handlers.onSnapshot(snapshot))
        .then(
          () => undefined,
          () => undefined
        );
      return;
    }
    // The snapshot always comes first; anything earlier has no screen to land on.
    if (!hadSnapshot) return;
    if (frame.t === "out") {
      const seq = frame.seq;
      const data = frame.d;
      void ready
        .then(() => (closedHere ? undefined : handlers.onOut(data)))
        .then(() => {
          const ack = acks.processed(seq);
          if (ack !== null) send({ t: "ack", seq: ack });
        })
        .catch(() => undefined);
      return;
    }
    if (frame.t === "state") {
      const state: SessionStateFrame = { status: frame.status, exitCode: frame.exitCode, signal: frame.signal, endedBy: frame.endedBy, resetAt: frame.resetAt };
      void ready.then(() => {
        if (!closedHere) handlers.onState(state);
      });
      return;
    }
    const raw = frame.raw;
    void ready.then(() => {
      if (!closedHere) handlers.onAlert(raw);
    });
  };

  ws.onclose = (event: CloseEvent) => {
    cancelResize();
    if (closedHere) return;
    if (!hadSnapshot) void checkStillSignedIn();
    const reason = event.reason || "";
    handlers.onClose({ code: event.code, reason, hadSnapshot, advice: sessionCloseAdvice({ code: event.code, reason }) });
  };

  return {
    focus() {
      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) takeKeys();
      else if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.CONNECTING) focusWhenOpen = true;
    },
    input(data: string) {
      for (const d of chunkInput(data)) send({ t: "in", d });
    },
    resize(cols: number, rows: number) {
      if (!validSize(cols, rows)) return;
      size = { cols, rows };
      cancelResize();
      if (sent && sent.cols === cols && sent.rows === rows) return;
      resizeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        resizeTimer = null;
        sendSize();
      }, RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    },
    close() {
      closedHere = true;
      cancelResize();
      try {
        ws.close(1000, "closed");
      } catch {
        // Already closed.
      }
    }
  };
}
```

```ts
export function queryParam(name: string) {
  return new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get(name) || "";
}

export function navigateTo(page: string, extra: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const next = new URL(window.location.href);
  next.searchParams.set("page", page);
  // `step` picks a Setup step (check, plan, install, brain, signin, ready) and
  // `example` asks the Runs page to open the New run dialog with the safe example typed in.
  // `session` picks a Sessions tab, `tab` a page's own tab (Runs: "recordings") and `highlight` the row
  // to mark there ("Open recording" lands on its session's row).
  for (const key of ["file", "folder", "filter", "agent", "run", "room", "step", "example", "session", "tab", "highlight"]) {
    if (extra[key]) next.searchParams.set(key, extra[key]);
    else next.searchParams.delete(key);
  }
  window.history.replaceState({}, "", next);
  window.dispatchEvent(new Event("aos-navigate"));
```

- [ ] **Step 8: One shared sessions poll (Q30).** Create `src/ui/useSessionsList.ts` (a `.ts` file, so the provider uses `createElement` rather than JSX; the path and the `{ source, available, refresh }` shape are what Task U3 consumes):

```ts
// One shared read of GET /api/sessions for the whole shell (planning decision Q30): the menu's sessions
// count, Home and the Sessions page all read this one list, so they never disagree for longer than a poll.
// It asks every 5 s (paused while the window is hidden, useInterval), one read at a time with the newest
// answer winning (latestRead.ts), and every read has a time limit (sessionsApi.ts). After a good read, a
// failed one keeps the last good list marked stale (homeShared.ts Source), so a page can show it under a
// warn note instead of wiping it. Where sessions do not exist (the public demo, the public mode), the server
// answers 404 not_available and `available` turns false, so a page says so instead of "Can't reach Agent OS".
import { createContext, createElement, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { ApiError } from "../api";
import { listSessions, sessionProblem } from "../sessionsApi";
import type { SessionListResponse } from "../types";
import { useInterval } from "./components/useInterval";
import { failedLoad, loaded } from "./homeShared";
import type { Source } from "./homeShared";
import { createLatestRead } from "./latestRead";
import { runningSessionCount } from "./sessionsShared";

export const SESSIONS_POLL_MS = 5000;
const NOT_AVAILABLE = "Sessions are not available here.";

export interface SessionsList {
  source: Source<SessionListResponse>;
  // false where sessions do not exist (the server answered 404 not_available, or the public demo).
  available: boolean;
  // Read again now (after Start, Stop, Resume or Dismiss). The same function on every render; a read still
  // waiting no longer counts.
  refresh: () => void;
}

const OFF: SessionsList = { source: { state: "error", message: NOT_AVAILABLE }, available: false, refresh: () => undefined };

const SessionsListContext = createContext<SessionsList>(OFF);

export function useSessionsList(): SessionsList {
  return useContext(SessionsListContext);
}

// How many agent sessions are running, for the menu. null while that is not known: still loading, or the
// last read failed (a stale number is never shown).
export function useLiveSessionCount(): number | null {
  const { source } = useSessionsList();
  if (source.state !== "ok" || source.stale) return null;
  return runningSessionCount(source.data.sessions);
}

function isNotAvailable(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 404 && error.message === "not_available";
}

export function SessionsListProvider({ enabled, children }: { enabled: boolean; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [source, setSource] = useState<Source<SessionListResponse>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [available, setAvailable] = useState(true);
  const [reads] = useState(createLatestRead);

  const load = useCallback(
    (fresh: boolean) => {
      if (!enabled) return;
      if (fresh) reads.cancel();
      void reads.run(
        () => listSessions(),
        (outcome) => {
          if (outcome.ok) {
            setAvailable(true);
            setSource(loaded(outcome.value));
            return;
          }
          if (isNotAvailable(outcome.error)) {
            setAvailable(false);
            setSource({ state: "error", message: NOT_AVAILABLE });
            return;
          }
          setSource((prev) => failedLoad(prev, sessionProblem(outcome.error)));
        }
      );
    },
    [enabled, reads]
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    load(true);
    // A read still waiting when the shell goes away must not update it.
    return () => reads.cancel();
  }, [load, reads]);
  useInterval(() => load(false), enabled ? SESSIONS_POLL_MS : null);

  const refresh = useCallback(() => load(true), [load]);
  const value = useMemo<SessionsList>(() => (enabled ? { source, available, refresh } : OFF), [enabled, source, available, refresh]);
  return createElement(SessionsListContext.Provider, { value }, children);
}
```

Create `src/ui/components/QuitQuestion.tsx`:

```tsx
// The quit question (desktop app only; spec "Quitting Agent OS", planning decision Q6). Instead of quitting
// at once, the Rust shell tells this window "agentos://quit-requested". The window asks Agent OS which
// sessions are running (both kinds) and either answers "quit" straight away, when nothing would be lost, or
// shows this question, tells the shell "agentos://quit-shown", and then sends the person's answer as
// "agentos://quit-answer" { quit }. If no window says quit-shown within 2 s, the shell quits on its own.
// The Tauri event module is imported lazily, so a browser tab never loads it.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { quitCheck } from "../../sessionsApi";
import { isDesktopApp } from "../desktop";
import { QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT, QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT, quitQuestionCopy, runQuitFlow } from "../sessionsShared";
import type { QuitView } from "../sessionsShared";
import AgentConfirmModal from "./AgentConfirmModal";

async function tellShell(event: string, payload?: unknown): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const { emit } = await import("@tauri-apps/api/event");
    await emit(event, payload);
  } catch {
    // Not inside the desktop shell after all (a browser tab with ?desktop=1): there is nobody to tell.
  }
}

export interface DesktopQuit {
  view: QuitView | null;
  keepRunning: () => void;
  quit: () => void;
}

export function useDesktopQuit(): DesktopQuit {
  const [view, setView] = useState<QuitView | null>(null);
  // True from the shell's request until an answer is sent; a second request in between changes nothing.
  const open = useRef(false);

  const answer = useCallback((quit: boolean) => {
    open.current = false;
    setView(null);
    void tellShell(QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, { quit });
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isDesktopApp()) return undefined;
    let unlisten: (() => void) | null = null;
    let gone = false;
    function onQuitRequested() {
      if (open.current) return;
      open.current = true;
      void runQuitFlow({
        check: () => quitCheck(),
        show: (next) => {
          if (open.current) setView(next);
        },
        shown: () => void tellShell(QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT),
        answer,
        isOpen: () => open.current
      });
    }
    import("@tauri-apps/api/event")
      .then(({ listen }) => listen(QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT, onQuitRequested))
      .then((stop) => {
        if (gone) stop();
        else unlisten = stop;
      })
      .catch(() => {
        // Not inside the desktop shell after all: nothing will ask.
      });
    return () => {
      gone = true;
      unlisten?.();
    };
  }, [answer]);

  return { view, keepRunning: () => answer(false), quit: () => answer(true) };
}

// `quitLabel` names the button that ends the sessions: "Quit" by default, "Install & restart" from the update
// banner (its restart quits Agent OS too, and the shell cannot ask on that path; see UpdateBanner.tsx).
export default function QuitQuestion({
  view,
  onKeepRunning,
  onQuit,
  quitLabel
}: {
  view: QuitView;
  onKeepRunning: () => void;
  onQuit: () => void;
  quitLabel?: string;
}) {
  const copy = quitQuestionCopy(view);
  // Focus starts on Keep running (the first button), so Enter never quits by accident; Escape keeps running.
  return (
    <AgentConfirmModal
      title={copy.title}
      cancelLabel={copy.keep}
      confirmLabel={quitLabel ?? copy.quit}
      onConfirm={onQuit}
      onClose={onKeepRunning}
      danger
      closeOnBackdrop={false}
    >
      <p aria-live="polite">{copy.body}</p>
    </AgentConfirmModal>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Ask before an update restarts Agent OS.** The banner's "Install & restart" calls `downloadAndInstall()` and then `relaunch()`. That restart quits Agent OS and ends every running session, and the shell cannot ask on that path: it leaves with `RESTART_EXIT_CODE`, which `prevent_exit()` ignores (decision Q5b). So the banner asks first, with the quit question (ruling R19, decision D-U1-9). Replace the whole of `src/ui/components/UpdateBanner.tsx` with:

```tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { ArrowUpCircle } from "lucide-react";
import type { Update } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-updater";
import { quitCheck } from "../../sessionsApi";
import type { QuitView } from "../sessionsShared";
import QuitQuestion from "./QuitQuestion";
import "../updateBanner.css";

// Only the desktop app has an updater. The Rust shell opens the window with
// ?desktop=1; window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ is the fallback marker.
function isDesktopApp(): boolean {
  if (typeof window === "undefined") return false;
  if (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("desktop") === "1") return true;
  return "__TAURI_INTERNALS__" in window;
}

const CHECK_EVERY_MS = 4 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const LOG_PREFIX = "[agent-os updater]";

// "checking": asking Agent OS which sessions run, before anything is downloaded.
type Phase = "ready" | "checking" | "installing" | "failed";

// A slim notice that appears only when a newer desktop build exists. It never
// installs or restarts on its own: running agents may be mid-task, so the
// user has to click "Install & restart". That restart quits Agent OS and ends
// every session, and the shell cannot ask first on this path (an approved
// restart leaves with RESTART_EXIT_CODE, which the shell's quit question cannot
// hold; see desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs). So the banner asks first, with the
// same quit question, whenever a session runs or Agent OS does not answer.
export default function UpdateBanner() {
  const desktop = isDesktopApp();
  const [update, setUpdate] = useState<Update | null>(null);
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<Phase>("ready");
  const [notesOpen, setNotesOpen] = useState(false);
  // The quit question while it asks before the restart, otherwise null.
  const [ask, setAsk] = useState<QuitView | null>(null);
  const installingRef = useRef(false);

  const checkForUpdate = useCallback(async () => {
    if (installingRef.current) return;
    try {
      // Lazy import: the plain browser build never loads the Tauri packages.
      const { check } = await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-updater");
      const found = await check();
      if (found) setUpdate(found);
    } catch (error) {
      // Expected until the app has a signing key and an update feed; kept
      // out of the UI so it never nags, but visible in the console.
      console.warn(`${LOG_PREFIX} update check failed:`, error);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!desktop) return undefined;
    void checkForUpdate();
    const timer = window.setInterval(() => void checkForUpdate(), CHECK_EVERY_MS);
    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
  }, [desktop, checkForUpdate]);

  // Downloads, installs and relaunches. Reached only when nothing runs, or from the question's "Install & restart".
  async function installNow() {
    if (!update) return;
    setAsk(null);
    setPhase("installing");
    try {
      await update.downloadAndInstall();
      const { relaunch } = await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-process");
      await relaunch();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`${LOG_PREFIX} install failed:`, error);
      installingRef.current = false;
      setPhase("failed");
    }
  }

  async function install() {
    if (!update || installingRef.current) return;
    installingRef.current = true;
    setPhase("checking");
    // Every live session of both kinds, with its title (POST /api/sessions/quit-check, with its time limit).
    const check = await quitCheck().catch(() => null);
    if (!check || !Array.isArray(check.live)) {
      // No answer: say so plainly and let the person choose.
      setPhase("ready");
      setAsk({ phase: "unknown" });
      return;
    }
    if (check.live.length > 0) {
      setPhase("ready");
      setAsk({ phase: "asking", live: check.live });
      return;
    }
    // Nothing running, so nothing would be lost: install at once, as before.
    await installNow();
  }

  // Keep running: nothing was downloaded or restarted, and the banner is back as it was.
  function keepRunning() {
    setAsk(null);
    installingRef.current = false;
    setPhase("ready");
  }

  if (!desktop || !update) return null;
  const notes = (update.body || "").trim();

  return (
    <>
      <div className="os-update" role="status" aria-live="polite">
        <div className="os-update__bar">
          <ArrowUpCircle size={16} className="os-update__icon" aria-hidden="true" />
          <span className="os-update__text">
            {phase === "failed"
              ? "The update didn't install. Nothing was changed; you can try again."
              : `Agent OS ${update.version} is ready to install`}
          </span>
          {notes ? (
            <button className="os-update__link" onClick={() => setNotesOpen((open) => !open)} aria-expanded={notesOpen}>
              What&apos;s new
            </button>
          ) : null}
          <button
            className="os-btn os-btn--primary os-update__action"
            onClick={() => void install()}
            disabled={phase === "checking" || phase === "installing" || ask !== null}
          >
            {phase === "checking" ? "Checking…" : phase === "installing" ? "Installing…" : phase === "failed" ? "Try again" : "Install & restart"}
          </button>
        </div>
        {notesOpen && notes ? <pre className="os-update__notes">{notes}</pre> : null}
      </div>
      {/* Outside .os-update: that wrapper ignores the pointer and is its own layer (updateBanner.css), so a
          dialog inside it could not be clicked or sit above the page. */}
      {ask ? <QuitQuestion view={ask} quitLabel="Install & restart" onKeepRunning={keepRunning} onQuit={() => void installNow()} /> : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

What changes for the person: with no session running, "Install & restart" works exactly as before (after a check that usually takes a few milliseconds). With sessions running, the quit question names them first, and only its "Install & restart" downloads and restarts; "Keep running" (or Escape) leaves everything as it was. If Agent OS does not answer the check, the question says it couldn't check, and the person chooses.

```bash
grep -cE "(^|[^A-Z_])SHELL[\"']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\"']?/bin/(ba|z)?sh" .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs
```

Expected: `SYNTAX-OK`, then `1`, `0` (S10's `SHELL` line is gone, so `SHELL` is set once), `1`, `1` and `0` (the harness names no real shell; Task E1 checks the same). The shims themselves are written by the first harness run in Step 15, which also checks them.

- [ ] **Step 14: Create the probe `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/sessions-foundation.mjs`** (git-ignored, never committed):

```js
// Task U1: the sessions client foundations. Run from the worktree root, after `npm run build`:
//   node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/sessions-foundation.mjs
// H. The harness later session probes stand on: the real-path HOME, the six fake agents in fake-bin/, terminals.
// A. The menu's sessions count: running agent sessions only, hidden at 0 and when unknown.
// B. The palette key: ⌘K on a Mac (Ctrl+K elsewhere), never from inside .xterm; the "aos-palette" event.
// C. The quit question, with a stand-in for the desktop shell's event bridge (window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__).
// D. openSessionSocket (src/sessionsApi.ts) against a mock WebSocket.
// E. The update banner's Install & restart asks first while a session runs (the stand-in also offers an update).
// Every sessions answer is stubbed (context.route / context.routeWebSocket): no session or agent is started,
// nothing is downloaded and nothing restarts. H runs one fake agent's --version, nothing more.
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { lstatSync, readFileSync, realpathSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import path from "node:path";

const W = 1470, H = 956;
const LIST = /\/api\/sessions(\?[^/]*)?$/;
const QUIT_CHECK = /\/api\/sessions\/quit-check$/;
const ATTACH = /\/api\/sessions\/[^/]+\/attach$/;
const SIGNED_IN = /\/api\/session$/;
const SID = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111";
const iso = (msAgo) => new Date(Date.now() - msAgo).toISOString();
const session = (over) => ({
  id: SID, kind: "agent", agentId: "claude", agentLabel: "Claude Code", folder: "/Users/you/my-app", folderName: "my-app",
  folderShown: true, branch: null, status: "live", stateSince: iso(1000), startedAt: iso(60000), endedAt: null, exitCode: null,
  signal: null, endedBy: null, dismissed: false, brain: null, resume: { available: false, reason: null, fallback: false },
  alerts: "basic", recordingBytes: 0, ...over
});
const listBody = (sessions) => JSON.stringify({ sessions, environmentNotice: null, pty: { ok: true, reason: null }, maxLive: 8 });

// The desktop shell's event bridge, faked, and (when `update` is true) an updater with an update ready. It
// runs in the page before the app, so isDesktopApp() is true. Every command is recorded in __fake.invoked.
function fakeDesktopBridge({ update = false } = {}) {
  const callbacks = new Map();
  let next = 1;
  window.__fake = { listeners: [], emitted: [], invoked: [] };
  window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ = {
    transformCallback(callback) {
      const id = next++;
      callbacks.set(id, callback);
      return id;
    },
    async invoke(cmd, args) {
      window.__fake.invoked.push(cmd);
      if (cmd === "plugin:updater|check") {
        return update ? { rid: 7, currentVersion: "0.4.0", version: "0.5.0", date: null, body: "", rawJson: {} } : null;
      }
      // Recorded above, and nothing else: nothing is downloaded and nothing restarts.
      if (cmd === "plugin:updater|download_and_install" || cmd === "plugin:process|restart") return null;
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|listen") {
        window.__fake.listeners.push({ event: args.event, handler: args.handler });
        return args.handler;
      }
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|unlisten") {
        window.__fake.listeners = window.__fake.listeners.filter((l) => l.handler !== args.eventId);
        return null;
      }
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|emit") {
        window.__fake.emitted.push({ event: args.event, payload: args.payload ?? null });
        return null;
      }
      throw new Error(`fake desktop bridge: ${cmd} is not available here`);
    }
  };
  window.__TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ = { unregisterListener() {} };
  window.__fireShell = (event) => {
    for (const l of window.__fake.listeners) if (l.event === event) callbacks.get(l.handler)?.({ event, id: l.handler, payload: null });
  };
}

const HARNESS = String.raw`
import { openSessionSocket } from "./src/sessionsApi";
import type { SessionSocket } from "./src/sessionsApi";

const log: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];
const sockets: Record<string, SessionSocket> = {};
window.addEventListener("agentos:locked", () => log.push({ key: "-", k: "locked" }));
(window as unknown as { __sock: unknown }).__sock = {
  log,
  open(key: string, id: string, slow: boolean) {
    sockets[key] = openSessionSocket(id, {
      onSnapshot: (snap) =>
        new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
          log.push({ key, k: "snapshot", data: snap.data, cols: snap.cols, mouse: snap.modes.mouseEncoding });
          setTimeout(resolve, slow ? 300 : 0);
        }),
      onOut: (d) => {
        log.push({ key, k: "out", d: d.length > 40 ? "len:" + d.length : d });
      },
      onState: (s) => {
        log.push({ key, k: "state", status: s.status });
      },
      onAlert: (raw) => {
        log.push({ key, k: "alert", raw });
      },
      onClose: (info) => {
        log.push({ key, k: "close", code: info.code, reason: info.reason, hadSnapshot: info.hadSnapshot, advice: info.advice });
      }
    });
  },
  focus(key: string) { sockets[key].focus(); },
  resize(key: string, cols: number, rows: number) { sockets[key].resize(cols, rows); },
  input(key: string, data: string) { sockets[key].input(data); },
  inputBig(key: string, n: number) { sockets[key].input("x".repeat(n)); },
  close(key: string) { sockets[key].close(); }
};
`;

export default async function ({ browser, shot, pass, fail, api, BASE, TOKEN, HERE, HOME }) {
  const check = (ok, name, why = "") => (ok ? pass(name) : fail(name, String(why)));
  const REPO = path.resolve(HERE, "..", "..");
  // A request this probe aborts on purpose shows as a failed load in the console; only other errors count.
  const realErrors = (errors) => errors.filter((e) => !/Failed to load resource/.test(e));
  async function open(page, setup) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: W, height: H } });
    if (setup) await setup(context);
    const tab = await context.newPage();
    const errors = [];
    tab.on("console", (m) => { if (m.type() === "error") errors.push(m.text()); });
    tab.on("pageerror", (e) => errors.push(String(e)));
    await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?launch=${TOKEN}`);
    await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?page=${page}`);
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1200);
    return { context, tab, errors };
  }

  // ---- H. The harness (Step 13): what the session probes of Tasks U3 and U4 stand on ----
  {
    let realHome = "";
    try {
      realHome = realpathSync(String(HOME));
    } catch {
      realHome = "";
    }
    check(typeof HOME === "string" && HOME !== "" && realHome === HOME, "harness: probes get the server's HOME, as a real path", String(HOME));
    const names = ["claude", "codex", "agent", "cursor-agent", "hermes", "openclaw"];
    const wrong = names.filter((name) => {
      const file = path.join(HERE, "fake-bin", name);
      try {
        const text = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
        return lstatSync(file).isSymbolicLink() || !text.includes(`FAKE_AGENT_NAME='${name}'`) || !text.includes("/test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs");
      } catch {
        return true;
      }
    });
    check(wrong.length === 0, "harness: fake-bin holds the six TUI-like fake agents (shims, not links)", wrong.join(", "));
    let version = "";
    try {
      version = execFileSync(path.join(HERE, "fake-bin", "claude"), ["--version"], { encoding: "utf8", timeout: 5000, env: { PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" } }).trim();
    } catch (error) {
      version = String(error.message || error);
    }
    check(version === "claude 9.9.9-fake", "harness: a fake agent runs with this Node and answers like the test fake", version);
    const list = await api("GET", "/api/sessions");
    check(
      list.status === 200 && Array.isArray(list.json.sessions) && list.json.pty?.ok === true,
      "harness: the throwaway server answers GET /api/sessions and can open terminals",
      `${list.status} ${JSON.stringify(list.json.pty ?? list.json)}`
    );
  }

  // ---- A. The menu's sessions count ----
  {
    let sessionsNow = [];
    let listFails = false;
    const { context, tab, errors } = await open("fleet", async (ctx) => {
      await ctx.route(LIST, (route) => {
        if (route.request().method() !== "GET") return route.fallback();
        if (listFails) return route.abort();
        return route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "application/json", body: listBody(sessionsNow) });
      });
    });
    const menu = () =>
      tab.evaluate(() => {
        const item = [...document.querySelectorAll(".os-nav__item")].find((b) => b.querySelector(".os-nav__label")?.textContent?.trim() === "Sessions");
        return { meta: item?.querySelector(".os-nav__meta")?.textContent?.trim() ?? null, aria: item?.getAttribute("aria-label") ?? null };
      });
    let m = await menu();
    check(m.meta === null && m.aria === null, "menu: no count while no session runs", JSON.stringify(m));
    sessionsNow = [
      session({ id: "a1", status: "live" }),
      session({ id: "a2", status: "idle", agentId: "codex", agentLabel: "Codex" }),
      session({ id: "a3", status: "exited", endedAt: iso(500), exitCode: 0 }),
      session({ id: "u1", kind: "update", status: "live", agentId: "hermes", agentLabel: "Hermes" })
    ];
    await tab.waitForTimeout(6000);
    m = await menu();
    check(m.meta === "2" && m.aria === "Sessions, 2 running", "menu: counts running agent sessions only (not ended, not an update)", JSON.stringify(m));
    await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, "menu-count");
    listFails = true;
    await tab.waitForTimeout(6000);
    m = await menu();
    check(m.meta === null, "menu: a failed read hides the count (never a stale number)", JSON.stringify(m));
    listFails = false;
    sessionsNow = [session({ id: "a3", status: "exited", endedAt: iso(500), exitCode: 0 })];
    await tab.waitForTimeout(6000);
    m = await menu();
    check(m.meta === null && m.aria === null, "menu: only ended sessions means no count", JSON.stringify(m));
    check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "menu: console clean", realErrors(errors).join(" | "));
    await context.close();
  }

  // ---- B. The palette key ----
  {
    const { context, tab, errors } = await open("fleet");
    const isMac = await tab.evaluate(() => /mac/i.test(navigator.platform || navigator.userAgent || ""));
    const wrong = isMac ? "Control+KeyK" : "Meta+KeyK";
    const right = isMac ? "Meta+KeyK" : "Control+KeyK";
    const paletteOpen = async () => (await tab.locator(".os-palette").count()) > 0;
    await tab.evaluate(() => document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement && document.activeElement.blur());
    await tab.keyboard.press(wrong);
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(!(await paletteOpen()), `palette: ${wrong} does not open it on this computer`);
    await tab.keyboard.press(right);
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(await paletteOpen(), `palette: ${right} opens it`);
    await tab.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(!(await paletteOpen()), "palette: Escape closes it");
    await tab.evaluate(() => {
      const box = document.createElement("div");
      box.className = "xterm";
      box.id = "probe-xterm";
      box.innerHTML = '<textarea aria-label="probe terminal input"></textarea>';
      document.body.appendChild(box);
    });
    await tab.focus("#probe-xterm textarea");
    await tab.keyboard.press(right);
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(!(await paletteOpen()), "palette: the key typed inside a terminal (.xterm) is left to the terminal");
    await tab.evaluate(() => document.getElementById("probe-xterm")?.remove());
    await tab.evaluate(() => window.dispatchEvent(new Event("aos-palette")));
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(await paletteOpen(), 'palette: the "aos-palette" event opens it');
    await tab.evaluate(() => window.dispatchEvent(new Event("aos-palette")));
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    check(!(await paletteOpen()), 'palette: the "aos-palette" event again closes it');
    const label = await tab.locator(".os-palette-trigger").getAttribute("aria-label");
    check(label === `Search pages and actions (${isMac ? "⌘K" : "Ctrl K"})`, "palette: the search button names this computer's key", label);
    check(errors.length === 0, "palette: console clean", errors.join(" | "));
    await context.close();
  }

  // ---- C. The quit question ----
  {
    let quitMode = "live";
    const CLAUDE_LIVE = { id: "a", title: "Claude Code · my-app", kind: "agent" };
    const UPDATE_LIVE = { id: "u", title: "Hermes update", kind: "update" };
    let quitLive = [CLAUDE_LIVE, { id: "b", title: "Codex · api", kind: "agent" }];
    const { context, tab, errors } = await open("fleet", async (ctx) => {
      await ctx.addInitScript(fakeDesktopBridge, { update: false });
      await ctx.route(QUIT_CHECK, (route) => {
        if (quitMode === "hang") return; // never answers
        const live = quitMode === "live" ? quitLive : [];
        return route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "application/json", body: JSON.stringify({ live }) });
      });
    });
    const listening = await tab
      .waitForFunction(() => window.__fake.listeners.some((l) => l.event === "agentos://quit-requested"), null, { timeout: 5000 })
      .then(() => true, () => false);
    check(listening, "quit: the window listens for agentos://quit-requested");
    const emitted = () => tab.evaluate(() => window.__fake.emitted.map((e) => ({ event: e.event, payload: e.payload })));
    const fire = () => tab.evaluate(() => window.__fireShell("agentos://quit-requested"));
    const dialog = tab.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Quit Agent OS?" });
    const body = async () => ((await dialog.locator(".os-modal__body").textContent().catch(() => "")) || "").trim();

    // 1. Two sessions running: the question names them; Keep running answers { quit: false }.
    await fire();
    await dialog.waitFor({ timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
    check(
      (await body()) === "These sessions are still running: Claude Code · my-app and Codex · api. Quitting ends them. Their recordings stay in Runs, and you can resume them later.",
      "quit: the question names the running sessions",
      await body()
    );
    let e = await emitted();
    check(e.filter((x) => x.event === "agentos://quit-shown").length === 1 && !e.some((x) => x.event === "agentos://quit-answer"), "quit: the shell is told the question is on screen", JSON.stringify(e));
    const focused = await tab.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    check(focused === "Keep running", "quit: focus starts on Keep running", focused);
    await fire(); // a second ⌘Q while the question is open
    await tab.waitForTimeout(500);
    e = await emitted();
    check(e.filter((x) => x.event === "agentos://quit-shown").length === 1 && (await dialog.count()) === 1, "quit: a second request while asking changes nothing", JSON.stringify(e));
    await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, "quit-question");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Keep running", exact: true }).click();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    e = await emitted();
    let last = e[e.length - 1];
    check(last?.event === "agentos://quit-answer" && last.payload?.quit === false && (await dialog.count()) === 0, "quit: Keep running answers { quit: false } and closes", JSON.stringify(last));

    // 1b. The question's other forms (ruling R21), each checked and kept for the owner's copy review (Task E1).
    const FORMS = [
      ["one", [CLAUDE_LIVE], "Claude Code · my-app is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later."],
      [
        "with-update",
        [CLAUDE_LIVE, UPDATE_LIVE],
        "Claude Code · my-app is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later. Quitting also stops the Hermes update."
      ],
      ["update-only", [UPDATE_LIVE], "The Hermes update is still running. Quitting stops it."]
    ];
    for (const [name, live, words] of FORMS) {
      quitLive = live;
      await fire();
      await dialog.waitFor({ timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
      check((await body()) === words, `quit: the ${name} form reads as decided`, await body());
      await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, `quit-${name}`);
      await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Keep running", exact: true }).click().catch(() => {});
      await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    }

    // 2. Nothing running: quit at once, without a question.
    quitMode = "none";
    await tab.evaluate(() => { window.__fake.emitted = []; });
    await fire();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1200);
    e = await emitted();
    check(e.length === 1 && e[0].event === "agentos://quit-answer" && e[0].payload?.quit === true && (await dialog.count()) === 0, "quit: with nothing running it answers quit at once, no question", JSON.stringify(e));

    // 3. No answer from Agent OS: "Checking…" first (the shell hears quit-shown inside its 2 s), then "couldn't check".
    quitMode = "hang";
    await tab.evaluate(() => { window.__fake.emitted = []; });
    await fire();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1300);
    e = await emitted();
    check((await body()) === "Checking which sessions are still running…" && e.some((x) => x.event === "agentos://quit-shown"), "quit: a slow answer shows Checking… and still tells the shell within 2 s", `${await body()} ${JSON.stringify(e)}`);
    await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, "quit-checking");
    await tab.waitForTimeout(6500);
    check((await body()) === "Agent OS couldn't check which sessions are running. Quitting ends any that are. Their recordings stay in Runs.", "quit: no answer at all is said plainly", await body());
    await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, "quit-unknown");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Quit", exact: true }).click();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
    e = await emitted();
    last = e[e.length - 1];
    check(last?.event === "agentos://quit-answer" && last.payload?.quit === true, "quit: Quit answers { quit: true }", JSON.stringify(last));
    check(errors.length === 0, "quit: console clean", errors.join(" | "));
    await context.close();
  }

  // ---- D. openSessionSocket against a mock WebSocket ----
  {
    let bundle = null;
    try {
      const { build } = createRequire(path.join(REPO, "package.json"))("esbuild");
      const result = await build({
        stdin: { contents: HARNESS, resolveDir: REPO, loader: "ts", sourcefile: "socket-harness.ts" },
        bundle: true, write: false, format: "iife", platform: "browser", logLevel: "silent",
        define: { "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"' }
      });
      bundle = result.outputFiles[0].text;
      pass("socket: the harness bundles from src/sessionsApi.ts");
    } catch (error) {
      fail("socket harness bundle", String(error.errors?.[0]?.text || error.message).slice(0, 200));
    }
    if (bundle) {
      const conns = [];
      const { context, tab, errors } = await open("fleet", async (ctx) => {
        await ctx.routeWebSocket(ATTACH, (ws) => {
          const conn = { ws, url: ws.url(), msgs: [], closed: null };
          conns.push(conn);
          ws.onMessage((m) => {
            try { conn.msgs.push(JSON.parse(String(m))); } catch { conn.msgs.push({ bad: String(m) }); }
          });
          ws.onClose((code) => { conn.closed = code ?? 0; });
        });
      });
      await tab.evaluate(bundle);
      const log = () => tab.evaluate(() => window.__sock.log);
      const until = async (fn, ms = 3000) => {
        const end = Date.now() + ms;
        while (Date.now() < end) {
          if (await fn()) return true;
          await tab.waitForTimeout(50);
        }
        return false;
      };

      await tab.evaluate((id) => window.__sock.open("a", id, true), SID);
      await until(() => conns.length === 1);
      const a = conns[0];
      check(a?.url.endsWith(`/api/sessions/${SID}/attach`) && !a.url.includes("?"), "socket: the address is /api/sessions/:id/attach, with no query string", a?.url);
      await tab.waitForTimeout(200);
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: 5, d: "early" }));
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "snapshot", data: "screen", cols: 80, rows: 24, modes: { mouseEncoding: "sgr" } }));
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq: 5, d: "after" }));
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "state", status: "live" }));
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "alert", raw: "bel" }));
      a.ws.send("not json");
      await tab.waitForTimeout(700);
      const order = (await log()).filter((x) => x.key === "a").map((x) => x.k + (x.d ? `:${x.d}` : ""));
      check(order.join(",") === "snapshot,out:after,state,alert", "socket: the snapshot comes first and holds later frames; earlier output and bad frames are dropped", order.join(","));

      await tab.evaluate(() => { window.__sock.resize("a", 100, 30); window.__sock.focus("a"); });
      await tab.waitForTimeout(150);
      check(a.msgs.length === 2 && a.msgs[0].t === "focus" && a.msgs[1].t === "resize" && a.msgs[1].cols === 100 && a.msgs[1].rows === 30, "socket: focus is sent, then the size right after it, once", JSON.stringify(a.msgs));
      a.msgs.length = 0;
      await tab.evaluate(() => {
        window.__sock.resize("a", 101, 30);
        window.__sock.resize("a", 102, 31);
        window.__sock.resize("a", 1, 31);
        window.__sock.resize("a", 102, 999);
      });
      await tab.waitForTimeout(200);
      check(a.msgs.length === 1 && a.msgs[0].t === "resize" && a.msgs[0].cols === 102 && a.msgs[0].rows === 31, "socket: resizes wait 50 ms for the last one, and sizes out of range are never sent", JSON.stringify(a.msgs));
      a.msgs.length = 0;
      await tab.evaluate(() => window.__sock.resize("a", 102, 31));
      await tab.waitForTimeout(150);
      check(a.msgs.length === 0, "socket: the same size is not sent twice", JSON.stringify(a.msgs));

      await tab.evaluate(() => window.__sock.input("a", "hi\r"));
      await tab.evaluate(() => window.__sock.inputBig("a", 200000));
      await tab.waitForTimeout(400);
      const ins = a.msgs.filter((x) => x.t === "in");
      const sizes = ins.map((x) => Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(x)));
      check(ins[0]?.d === "hi\r", 'socket: keys go out as {t:"in"}', JSON.stringify(ins[0]));
      check(ins.length === 5 && sizes.every((n) => n <= 65536) && ins.slice(1).map((x) => x.d).join("").length === 200000, "socket: a big paste is split into frames of at most 64 KB", sizes.join(","));

      a.msgs.length = 0;
      let seq = 5;
      for (let i = 0; i < 6; i += 1) {
        seq += 10000;
        a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq, d: "y".repeat(10000) }));
      }
      await tab.waitForTimeout(400);
      check(!a.msgs.some((x) => x.t === "ack"), "socket: no ack before 64 KB", JSON.stringify(a.msgs));
      seq += 10000;
      a.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "out", seq, d: "y".repeat(10000) }));
      await tab.waitForTimeout(400);
      const acks = a.msgs.filter((x) => x.t === "ack");
      check(acks.length === 1 && acks[0].seq === seq, "socket: an ack once 64 KB are processed, with the seq reached", JSON.stringify(acks));

      // S9's CLOSE_CODES: too_far_behind 4000, session_ended 4001, attach_failed 4004 (the reason text is the word).
      await a.ws.close({ code: 4000, reason: "too_far_behind" });
      await tab.waitForTimeout(400);
      const closeA = (await log()).find((x) => x.key === "a" && x.k === "close");
      check(
        closeA?.code === 4000 && closeA.reason === "too_far_behind" && closeA.hadSnapshot === true && closeA.advice === "reattach",
        "socket: too_far_behind (4000) reaches onClose with its code and reason, advising to attach again",
        JSON.stringify(closeA)
      );

      await tab.evaluate((id) => window.__sock.open("b", id, false), SID);
      await until(() => conns.length === 2);
      await tab.waitForTimeout(200);
      await tab.evaluate(() => window.__sock.close("b"));
      await tab.waitForTimeout(400);
      const closeB = (await log()).some((x) => x.key === "b" && x.k === "close");
      check(!closeB && conns[1].closed !== null, "socket: close() from this side closes it without calling onClose", `${closeB} ${conns[1].closed}`);

      // The window could not attach (S9 closes with 4004 attach_failed, before any snapshot): do not retry at
      // once. The person is still signed in here (the real /api/session answers), so the page is not locked.
      await tab.evaluate((id) => window.__sock.open("f", id, false), SID);
      await until(() => conns.length === 3);
      await conns[2].ws.close({ code: 4004, reason: "attach_failed" });
      await tab.waitForTimeout(600);
      const closeF = (await log()).find((x) => x.key === "f" && x.k === "close");
      check(
        closeF?.code === 4004 && closeF.reason === "attach_failed" && closeF.hadSnapshot === false && closeF.advice === "wait" &&
          !(await log()).some((x) => x.k === "locked"),
        "socket: attach_failed (4004) reaches onClose advising not to retry at once, and a signed-in page is not locked",
        JSON.stringify(closeF)
      );

      // Closed before any snapshot while the person is signed out: the page is told (agentos:locked).
      await context.route(SIGNED_IN, (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "application/json", body: JSON.stringify({ authenticated: false, required: true, mode: "local" }) }));
      await tab.evaluate((id) => window.__sock.open("c", id, false), SID);
      await until(() => conns.length === 4);
      await conns[3].ws.close({ code: 1008, reason: "refused" });
      await until(async () => (await log()).some((x) => x.k === "locked"), 3000);
      const closeC = (await log()).find((x) => x.key === "c" && x.k === "close");
      check(closeC?.hadSnapshot === false && (await log()).some((x) => x.k === "locked"), "socket: refused before a snapshot while signed out locks the page", JSON.stringify(closeC));
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "socket: console clean", realErrors(errors).join(" | "));
      await context.close();
    }
  }

  // ---- E. The update banner's Install & restart asks first while a session runs ----
  {
    const { context, tab, errors } = await open("fleet", async (ctx) => {
      await ctx.addInitScript(fakeDesktopBridge, { update: true });
      await ctx.route(QUIT_CHECK, (route) =>
        route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "application/json", body: JSON.stringify({ live: [{ id: "a", title: "Claude Code · my-app", kind: "agent" }] }) })
      );
    });
    const invoked = () => tab.evaluate(() => window.__fake.invoked.slice());
    const installCalls = (list) => list.filter((cmd) => cmd === "plugin:updater|download_and_install" || cmd === "plugin:process|restart");
    const button = tab.locator(".os-update__action");
    const dialog = tab.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Quit Agent OS?" });
    const shown = await button.waitFor({ timeout: 5000 }).then(() => true, () => false);
    check(shown && ((await button.textContent()) || "").trim() === "Install & restart", "update: the banner offers Install & restart", shown ? await button.textContent() : "no banner");

    await button.click();
    await dialog.waitFor({ timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
    const body = ((await dialog.locator(".os-modal__body").textContent().catch(() => "")) || "").trim();
    check(
      body === "Claude Code · my-app is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later.",
      "update: Install & restart first asks, naming the running session",
      body
    );
    check(
      (await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Keep running", exact: true }).count()) === 1 &&
        (await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Install & restart", exact: true }).count()) === 1,
      "update: the question's buttons are Keep running and Install & restart"
    );
    check(installCalls(await invoked()).length === 0, "update: nothing is downloaded or restarted while it asks", JSON.stringify(await invoked()));
    await shot(tab, "sessions-foundation", W, H, "update-question");

    await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Keep running", exact: true }).click();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(500);
    check(
      (await dialog.count()) === 0 && installCalls(await invoked()).length === 0,
      "update: Keep running calls neither downloadAndInstall nor relaunch",
      JSON.stringify(await invoked())
    );
    check(
      ((await button.textContent()) || "").trim() === "Install & restart" && (await button.isEnabled()),
      "update: Keep running puts the banner back as it was",
      await button.textContent()
    );

    await button.click();
    await dialog.waitFor({ timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
    await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Install & restart", exact: true }).click();
    await tab.waitForTimeout(500);
    check(
      installCalls(await invoked()).join(",") === "plugin:updater|download_and_install,plugin:process|restart",
      "update: only the question's Install & restart downloads, then restarts",
      JSON.stringify(await invoked())
    );
    const quitEvents = await tab.evaluate(() => window.__fake.emitted.filter((e) => String(e.event).startsWith("agentos://quit")).length);
    check(quitEvents === 0, "update: the shell's quit events are not used on this path", String(quitEvents));
    check(errors.length === 0, "update: console clean", errors.join(" | "));
    await context.close();
  }
}
```

### Task U2: SessionTerminal component (xterm 6.1, addons, theme, renderer, keys, clipboard, links, attach and reconnect)

This task builds the one piece every Sessions screen shows: the real terminal of one session, drawn by xterm.js `6.1.0-beta.304` in the Cobalt terminal theme. It attaches to the session over U1's socket client, puts back the screen and the terminal modes from the snapshot (so a closed window comes back exactly as it was), sends every key to the agent except Agent OS's own shortcuts, lets programs copy to the clipboard but never read it, opens only web links (http and https), draws with whichever renderer the page asks for (WebGL falls back to the DOM renderer if its context is lost), and attaches again by itself when the connection drops: at once when it fell too far behind, otherwise at a slowing pace while the page's session list still says the session is live, five tries, then "Lost the connection to this session." with a "Reconnect" button. It follows the spec's "Browser terminal", "WebSocket protocol" and "Persistence" sections, planning decisions Q17, Q40 and Q45, and rulings R12 and R25. No page uses the component until U3, so this task checks it with Node tests for its pure rules and with a probe that mounts it for real in the running app against a mock WebSocket (the way SP2's `kit2.mjs` mounted the page kit).

Depends on: W0 (the xterm set of decision Q42) and U1 (`openSessionSocket` and the `advice` its `onClose` carries, the session types, `isAppShortcut`, `isMacPlatform`, `togglePalette`). It is shaped for U3's page: the page draws the frame (`.os-sess-term`), owns the two browser-only settings and their defaults (`agentos.terminalPrefs`, `defaultTerminalPrefs`), passes `ended` from its session list, shows the `onNotice` sentence as a toast, and reads ⌘T / ⌘1-9 with its own `window` handler.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/ui/terminalShared.ts` (pure logic, `import type` only, decision P14)
- Create: `test/terminal-shared.test.js` (written first)
- Create: `src/ui/terminal.css`
- Create: `src/ui/components/SessionTerminal.tsx`
- Create (git-ignored, never committed): `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/terminal.mjs`

- Behaviour the page relies on (U3's Interfaces, ruling R12):

  - after an `exited` state frame, a `session_ended` close, or once `ended` is true (read at every close, before every try and whenever the prop changes), it keeps the last screen and never attaches again; mounted with `ended` already true, it never attaches;
  - a `too_far_behind` close attaches again at once for a fresh snapshot; any other close (a refused upgrade, 1006, Agent OS restarting, `attach_failed`, 1009) tries again after `reconnectDelay(attempts, advice)` while `ended` is false, at most `RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` tries in a row without a snapshot, then shows "Lost the connection to this session." with a "Reconnect" button that starts a fresh round and gives the keys back to this terminal;

**Decisions taken while drafting (the owner can overturn any of them):**

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-U2-1 | Line height, scrollback, cursor | `lineHeight: 1.2`, `scrollback: 5000`, xterm's own cursor (block, no blink). | Close to the prototype's 13/20 terminal; enough history for a long agent turn; a still cursor needs no reduced-motion rule. E1 compares by eye. |
| D-U2-2 | "OSC 52 read refused": answer empty, or not at all? | Not at all: a guard registered after the clipboard addon swallows every read request, so nothing is sent back. Writes go to `navigator.clipboard.writeText`; if the window refuses, nothing is copied. | The addon's own read path always answers (with whatever `readText` returns); no answer is the plainest refusal. |
| D-U2-3 | Links | Plain-text http/https links through the web-links addon's own pattern (it needs "//" after the scheme, so `mailto:` text is never a link); OSC 8 links through `linkHandler` with `allowNonHttpProtocols: false`; every open checks http/https again (`linkAllowed`). Browser mode: a new tab. Desktop app: the opener; when it refuses (an address outside the owner-approved allow list), the address is copied and `onNotice("Link copied. Open it in your browser.")`; if the window refuses the copy too, `onNotice("Agent OS couldn't open or copy that link.")`. | Ruling R25 and Q45. The opener's own refusal is the allow-list check, so the page keeps no second copy of the list (as `OpenAddress.tsx` does). |
| D-U2-4 | Renderer | The `webgl` prop decides. Its default is U3's `defaultTerminalPrefs` (Q45: DOM on macOS and in the Linux desktop app, WebGL in the Windows desktop app and in a browser tab on Windows or Linux). A lost WebGL context goes back to the DOM renderer and stays there until the setting is switched off and on. | Spec: "WebGL as a setting, with a context-loss fallback to DOM"; ruling R25. |
| D-U2-5 | Size of a window that does not have the keys (a viewer) | Every window fits its own box; only the writer's size reaches the agent (the server ignores a viewer's resize). | The protocol has no "size changed" frame from the server (see Notes). |
| D-U2-6 | Reattach | `too_far_behind`: at once. Any other close: after 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 5 s (the `"wait"` advice starts at 5 s), only while `ended` is false, at most 5 tries in a row without a snapshot; then "Lost the connection to this session." with "Reconnect". Never after an `exited` frame, a `session_ended` close or once `ended` is true. | Ruling R12 and Q40. S9 refuses an ended session's upgrade with a bare 403 (close 1006, no reason), so only the page's list can say why a try was refused. |
| D-U2-7 | Order of the reattach | `ESC c` (full reset) through the write queue, the snapshot at the size it was taken, then the modes the snapshot does not carry, then this window's own size. The alternate screen is switched on only if the snapshot did not already do it. Each step waits until its write is parsed (a promise around `t.write`'s callback) and then acts outside the callback: `resize()` and fit never run inside an xterm write callback. | Anything still queued from an earlier socket cannot land on the new screen; switching to the alternate screen a second time would wipe it. xterm 6.1's `resize()` flushes the write queue synchronously from the start of its buffer, which runs already-parsed chunks and their callbacks again; the outer resize then lands last, so the terminal would keep the snapshot's size while the agent was told the fitted one. |
| D-U2-8 | X10 mouse reports (bytes above 127, `onBinary`) | Sent only when every byte is plain ASCII; otherwise dropped. | The `in` frame is UTF-8 text, so those bytes would arrive changed. Agents use the SGR mouse form, which is plain ASCII. |
| D-U2-9 | Theme changes | Read the tokens at mount and again when `<html>`'s `data-theme`, `class` or `style` changes. | Q17. Only one theme exists today; this keeps a later one working. |
| D-U2-10 | Notices | "Connecting…" and "Reconnecting…" in a small pill in the terminal's corner (`role="status"`); "Lost the connection to this session." in the same place, in the brighter ink, with a "Reconnect" button (the kit's secondary button); nothing once open. The link sentence goes to `onNotice` only. | "…" means loading (Q31); the person must see why typing does nothing. The Sessions page shows `onNotice` as a toast (U3), and the sentence must not appear twice. |
| D-U2-11 | Who draws the frame | The page (U3's `.os-sess-term`: hairline, 10 px corners, cobalt edge while it has the keys). The component only fills it, with the terminal ground and the prototype's inner padding. | U3 draws it; one frame, not two. |
| D-U2-12 | "Reconnect" and the keys | Pressing "Reconnect" focuses the terminal, so it takes the keys again once its snapshot is back. | The button disappears as the tries start; focus must not fall to the page (Q31). |

```js
  const out = [];
  const clean = css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "");
  for (const match of clean.matchAll(/([^{}]*)\{([^{}]*)\}/g)) {
    const vars = {};

  const [r, g, b] = rgb(hex).map((v) => {
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the terminal's pure rules.** Create `src/ui/terminalShared.ts`:

```ts
// The browser terminal's pure rules (spec "Browser terminal"): the Cobalt colours read from the tokens, the
// modes a reattach puts back, which links may open, the OSC 52 rule and the reconnect pace. `import type`
// only, so test/terminal-shared.test.js loads this file straight from src/ (decision P14).
import type { ITheme } from "@xterm/xterm";
import type { SessionModes } from "../types";
import type { SessionCloseAdvice } from "./sessionsShared";

// JetBrains Mono at 13 px (spec), rows a little apart like the prototype's 13/20 terminal.
export const TERMINAL_FONT_SIZE = 13;
export const TERMINAL_LINE_HEIGHT = 1.2;
export const TERMINAL_SCROLLBACK = 5000;

type ThemeKey = Exclude<keyof ITheme, "extendedAnsi">;

// Which token gives which part of the xterm theme (tokens.css, "Terminal ground and the 16 ANSI colours").
export const THEME_TOKENS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [ThemeKey, string]> = [
  ["background", "--os-term-bg"],
  ["foreground", "--os-term-fg"],
  ["cursor", "--os-term-cursor"],
  ["cursorAccent", "--os-term-bg"],
  ["selectionBackground", "--os-term-select"],
  ["black", "--os-ansi-0"],
  ["red", "--os-ansi-1"],
  ["green", "--os-ansi-2"],
  ["yellow", "--os-ansi-3"],
  ["blue", "--os-ansi-4"],
  ["magenta", "--os-ansi-5"],
  ["cyan", "--os-ansi-6"],
  ["white", "--os-ansi-7"],
  ["brightBlack", "--os-ansi-8"],
  ["brightRed", "--os-ansi-9"],
  ["brightGreen", "--os-ansi-10"],
  ["brightYellow", "--os-ansi-11"],
  ["brightBlue", "--os-ansi-12"],
  ["brightMagenta", "--os-ansi-13"],
  ["brightCyan", "--os-ansi-14"],
  ["brightWhite", "--os-ansi-15"]
];

// The Cobalt terminal theme (Q17). `read` returns a token's value (getComputedStyle in the page). A token
// that reads empty is left out, so xterm keeps its own colour rather than an empty one.
export function terminalTheme(read: (token: string) => string): ITheme {
  const theme: ITheme = {};
  for (const [key, token] of THEME_TOKENS) {
    const value = (read(token) || "").trim();
    if (value) theme[key] = value;
  }
  return theme;
}

export function sameTheme(a: ITheme, b: ITheme): boolean {
  return THEME_TOKENS.every(([key]) => a[key] === b[key]);
}

const TRACKING: Record<SessionModes["mouseTracking"], string> = {
  none: "",
  x10: "\x1b[?9h",
  vt200: "\x1b[?1000h",
  drag: "\x1b[?1002h",
  any: "\x1b[?1003h"
};
const ENCODING: Record<SessionModes["mouseEncoding"], string> = {
  default: "",
  sgr: "\x1b[?1006h",
  "sgr-pixels": "\x1b[?1016h"
};

// The modes a reattach writes into this window's terminal after the snapshot (spec: the mirror "tracks the
// modes the serializer omits … and re-sends them on reattach"). Setting a mode the snapshot already set does
// nothing, except the alternate screen: switching to it again would clear it, so that one is written only
// when the snapshot left the normal screen active. Kitty flags (CSI = flags ; 1 u, "set all") only while the
// kitty keyboard setting is on.
export function modeRestoreSequence(modes: SessionModes, { altActive, kitty }: { altActive: boolean; kitty: boolean }): string {
  let out = "";
  if (modes.altScreen && !altActive) out += "\x1b[?1049h";
  if (modes.cursorKeysApp) out += "\x1b[?1h";
  if (modes.bracketedPaste) out += "\x1b[?2004h";
  if (modes.focusReporting) out += "\x1b[?1004h";
  out += TRACKING[modes.mouseTracking] ?? "";
  out += ENCODING[modes.mouseEncoding] ?? "";
  if (kitty && Number.isInteger(modes.kittyFlags) && modes.kittyFlags > 0) out += `\x1b[=${modes.kittyFlags};1u`;
  return out;
}

const LINK_SCHEMES = new Set(["http:", "https:"]);

// Only web links ever open from a terminal (decision Q45: `mailto:` text is not made a link).
export function linkAllowed(uri: string): boolean {
  try {
    return LINK_SCHEMES.has(new URL(uri).protocol);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

// OSC 52 "<selection>;?" asks the terminal for the clipboard. Reading is refused (spec); writing is allowed.
export function isOsc52Read(data: string): boolean {
  const parts = data.split(";");
  return parts.length >= 2 && parts[1] === "?";
}

export function isAsciiOnly(data: string): boolean {
  return /^[\x00-\x7f]*$/.test(data);
}

// How many tries in a row a window makes before it says the connection is lost and offers Reconnect (Q40).
export const RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 5;

const RECONNECT_STEPS_MS = [500, 1000, 2000, 5000];
const WAIT_ADVICE_MS = 5000;

// How long to wait before the next try, after `attempt` failed tries in a row (0 before the first one):
// 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 5 s (Q40). After the "wait" advice (attach_failed, or a message over 1 MB) the pace starts
// at 5 s instead.
export function reconnectDelay(attempt: number, advice?: SessionCloseAdvice): number {
  const step = Math.min(Math.max(0, Math.floor(attempt) || 0), RECONNECT_STEPS_MS.length - 1);
  const delay = RECONNECT_STEPS_MS[step];
  return advice === "wait" ? Math.max(delay, WAIT_ADVICE_MS) : delay;
}
```

```css
/* The browser terminal (SP3, SessionTerminal.tsx). It fills its nearest positioned parent, which draws the
   frame (the Sessions page's .os-sess-term: hairline, 10 px corners, cobalt edge while it has the keys). Inside,
   the terminal ground and the prototype's padding (.term-body: 20 px by 24 px). xterm draws the text itself with

.os-term {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;

}

.os-term__screen {
  flex: 1 1 auto;

  min-height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
}

/* "Connecting…" and "Reconnecting…": a quiet pill in the corner. "Lost the connection to this session." with

.os-term__notice {
  position: absolute;
  right: var(--os-sp-3);
  bottom: var(--os-sp-3);
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--os-sp-3);
  box-sizing: border-box;
  max-width: calc(100% - 2 * var(--os-sp-3));
  padding: var(--os-sp-1) var(--os-sp-3);
  font-family: var(--os-font-ui);
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  line-height: 1.4;
  color: var(--os-text-2);
  background: var(--os-surface-2);
  border: 1px solid var(--os-line-2);
  border-radius: var(--os-r-pill);
}

.os-term__notice-text {

  min-width: 0;

}

.os-term__notice--lost {
  padding: var(--os-sp-2) var(--os-sp-2) var(--os-sp-2) var(--os-sp-4);

}

.os-term__notice .os-btn {

  min-height: 28px;
  padding: 0 var(--os-sp-3);
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
}

@media (max-width: 1320px) {
  .os-term {
    padding: var(--os-sp-4);
  }
}
```
