- [ ] **Step 6: Write the plan rules.** Create `server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plan-rules.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// The rules of OpenClaw's plan brains (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-plan-brains-design.md,
// sections 2, 3 and 5): which plan a model runs on, how the model lists and the
// sign-in lists are read, and every sentence the server says about plans.
//
// Pure: no imports and no I/O. The parsers take values that parseJsonOutput
// (models.js) has already parsed. The readers (openclaw-plans.js), the model
// answer (readAgentModel in models.js), the job runner (jobs.js) and the tests
// all use this one copy, so models.js and openclaw-plans.js never import each other.

export const OPENCLAW_PLANS = Object.freeze(["claude", "chatgpt"]);
export const PLAN_PROVIDER = Object.freeze({ claude: "anthropic", chatgpt: "openai" });
export const PLAN_MODE = Object.freeze({ claude: "claude-plan", chatgpt: "chatgpt-plan" });
export const PLAN_MODELS_AS_OF = "2026-10-15";
// `models list`, `models auth list` and `models status` may each take this long;
// `config get` keeps its own 10 s limit (CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS).
export const PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000;

// Shown when the account's own list can't be read (dated: plans change).
export const PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS = Object.freeze({
  claude: Object.freeze(["claude-opus-5-5", "claude-sonnet-5-5", "claude-haiku-5-5", "claude-fable-5-1"]),
  chatgpt: Object.freeze(["gpt-6.1-sol", "gpt-6-sol", "gpt-6-luna"])
});
export const PLAN_MODEL_NAMES = Object.freeze({
  "claude-opus-5-5": "Opus 5.5",
  "claude-sonnet-5-5": "Sonnet 5.5",
  "claude-haiku-5-5": "Haiku 5.5",
  "claude-fable-5-1": "Fable 5.1",
  "gpt-6.1-sol": "GPT-6.1 Sol",
  "gpt-6-sol": "GPT-6 Sol",
  "gpt-6-luna": "GPT-6 Luna"
});

// A model name the person typed, after the provider prefix: no slash (the
// server adds anthropic/ or openai/), and it can never start with "-".
export const TYPED_MODEL_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._:-]{0,99}$/;

export const FABLE_NOTE = "Uses usage credits: on Pro from the first request, on Max after half your weekly limit.";
export function isFableModel(id) {
  return /^claude-fable-/i.test(String(id ?? ""));
}

// `claude auth status`'s authMethod words: Claude Code's own sign-in, and the
// ways that bill an API key or a cloud account instead of the plan.
export const CLAUDE_PLAN_METHODS = Object.freeze(["claude.ai", "oauth_token"]);
export const CLAUDE_API_METHODS = Object.freeze(["api_key", "api_key_helper", "third_party"]);

// An id from OpenClaw's own list, as it may go into `models set <provider>/<id>`:
// plain characters only, never a leading "-", a space, a slash or an "@" (in
// OpenClaw "@..." names an auth profile, which could pick another sign-in than
// the plan, and planOfPrimary never labels such a primary a plan).
const LISTED_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119}$/;
const MAX_NAME_CHARS = 120;

function plainObject(value) {
  return value !== null && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function knownPlan(plan) {
  return typeof plan === "string" && Object.hasOwn(PLAN_PROVIDER, plan);
}

// `models list --provider <p> --json` -> [{ id, name }] with no provider
// prefix, or null when it can't be read (any other shape, or nothing usable).
export function planModelRows(value, plan) {
  if (!knownPlan(plan)) return null;
  const list = Array.isArray(value) ? value : plainObject(value) && Array.isArray(value.models) ? value.models : null;
  if (!list) return null;
  const prefix = `${PLAN_PROVIDER[plan]}/`;
  const seen = new Set();
  const rows = [];
  for (const row of list) {
    if (!plainObject(row)) continue;
    const raw = typeof row.key === "string" ? row.key : typeof row.id === "string" ? row.id : null;
    if (raw === null) continue;
    let id = raw.trim();
    if (id.startsWith(prefix)) id = id.slice(prefix.length);
    // Another provider's model (or an id that isn't plain) is never offered.
    if (!LISTED_ID_RE.test(id)) continue;
    const key = id.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(key)) continue;
    seen.add(key);
    const own = typeof row.name === "string" ? row.name.trim().slice(0, MAX_NAME_CHARS) : "";
    rows.push({ id, name: own || (Object.hasOwn(PLAN_MODEL_NAMES, id) ? PLAN_MODEL_NAMES[id] : id) });
  }
  return rows.length ? rows : null;
}

function runtimeIdOf(entry) {
  return plainObject(entry) && plainObject(entry.agentRuntime) && typeof entry.agentRuntime.id === "string"
    ? entry.agentRuntime.id
    : null;
}

// `config get agents.defaults.models --json`: does any model run through
// Claude Code (the claude-cli runtime) yet?
export function hasClaudeCliPin(modelsConfig) {
  if (!plainObject(modelsConfig)) return false;
  return Object.values(modelsConfig).some((entry) => runtimeIdOf(entry) === "claude-cli");
}

// Would OpenClaw run anthropic/<id> through Claude Code (so on the Claude plan)?
// The model's own entry decides when it names a runtime; otherwise the
// "anthropic/*" entry does (spec section 2, step 3).
export function claudeCliPinned(modelsConfig, id) {
  if (!plainObject(modelsConfig) || typeof id !== "string" || !id) return false;
  const ownKey = `anthropic/${id}`;
  const own = Object.hasOwn(modelsConfig, ownKey) ? runtimeIdOf(modelsConfig[ownKey]) : null;
  if (own !== null) return own === "claude-cli";
  return Object.hasOwn(modelsConfig, "anthropic/*") && runtimeIdOf(modelsConfig["anthropic/*"]) === "claude-cli";
}

// signInStatus("claude") -> whether the Claude plan can be applied, and if not, why.
export function claudePlanReadiness({ installed, status, method } = {}) {
  if (!installed) return "not_installed";
  if (status === "not_signed_in") return "not_signed_in";
  if (CLAUDE_API_METHODS.includes(method)) return "api_billing";
  if (status !== "signed_in" || !CLAUDE_PLAN_METHODS.includes(method)) return "unknown_method";
  return "ready";
}

// `models auth list --provider openai --json` -> [{ method, sharing }], or null
// when it can't be read. Only each row's method and token sharing are kept:
// e-mail, names and everything else are dropped here. The field names are
// provisional until live check S-B3 (2026.9.6 rows carry only `type`).
export function parseAuthRows(value) {
  const list = Array.isArray(value) ? value : plainObject(value) && Array.isArray(value.profiles) ? value.profiles : null;
  if (!list) return null;
  const rows = [];
  for (const row of list) {
    if (!plainObject(row)) continue;
    if (row.provider !== undefined && row.provider !== "openai") continue;
    const method = typeof row.method === "string" ? row.method : typeof row.type === "string" ? row.type : null;
    rows.push({ method, sharing: typeof row.tokenSharing === "boolean" ? row.tokenSharing : null });
  }
  return rows;
}

// Signed in with ChatGPT (method "siwc"), and whether token sharing was allowed.
export function chatgptSignIn(rows) {
  if (!Array.isArray(rows)) return { signedIn: null, sharing: null };
  const siwc = rows.filter((row) => row?.method === "siwc");
  if (!siwc.length) return { signedIn: false, sharing: null };
  const sharing = siwc.some((row) => row.sharing === true) ? true : siwc.some((row) => row.sharing === false) ? false : null;
  return { signedIn: true, sharing };
}

// `models status --check --plain`, from runCommand's answer: the exit code only.
// A timeout is { ok: false, code: 0, signal: "SIGTERM" }, so it is not ready.
export function readinessOf(result) {
  if (result?.ok === true) return "ready";
  if (result && result.ok === false && result.code === 2 && !result.signal) return "expiring";
  return "not_ready";
}

// Which plan OpenClaw's primary model runs on (spec section 5), or null.
export function planOfPrimary(primary, modelsConfig, signedInWithChatgpt) {
  if (typeof primary !== "string" || primary.includes("@")) return null;
  const slash = primary.indexOf("/");
  if (slash <= 0 || slash === primary.length - 1) return null;
  const provider = primary.slice(0, slash);
  const id = primary.slice(slash + 1);
  if (provider === "anthropic" && claudeCliPinned(modelsConfig, id)) return "claude";
  if (provider === "openai" && signedInWithChatgpt === true) return "chatgpt";
  return null;
}

// The provider label of OpenClaw's model answer; null for every other provider,
// which keeps today's label.
export function openclawProviderLabel(provider, plan) {
  if (provider === "anthropic") return plan === "claude" ? "Claude plan" : "Anthropic API key";
  if (provider === "openai") return plan === "chatgpt" ? "ChatGPT plan" : "OpenAI";
  return null;
}

// ---- what the server says (spec sections 2, 3 and 5; contract "User-visible sentences") ----

export const PLAN_NOT_READY_MESSAGE = Object.freeze({
  openclaw_missing: "Install OpenClaw first.",
  not_installed: "Install Claude Code first.",
  not_signed_in: "Sign in to Claude Code first, then try again.",
  api_billing: "Claude Code uses an API key or a cloud account, not your Claude plan, so OpenClaw would bill that instead.",
  unknown_method: "Agent OS couldn't tell how Claude Code is signed in. Update Claude Code, then check again.",
  chatgpt_signed_out: "Sign in with ChatGPT first, then try again."
});
export const RUNTIME_CHECK_FAILED = "OpenClaw would use an Anthropic API key for this model, not your Claude plan.";
export const CHATGPT_EXPIRING = "Your ChatGPT sign-in expires soon. Sign in again.";
export const CHATGPT_NOT_READY = "OpenClaw can't use your ChatGPT plan yet. Sign in again, and allow token sharing when ChatGPT asks.";
export const INVALID_PLAN_MODEL = "That doesn't look like a model name.";
export const PLAN_JOB_INTERRUPTED = "Agent OS quit before this finished. Apply the plan again.";
export function noEarlierPrimary(ref) {
  return `OpenClaw had no model set before, so it keeps ${ref}.`;
}
// The say-hello fix lines for a plan brain (healthFixLine in jobs.js).
export const PLAN_HEALTH_LINES = Object.freeze({
  usageLimit: "Your plan's usage limit is used up. Try again after it resets.",
  signedOut: "OpenClaw isn't signed in to your plan anymore. Sign in again.",
  unreachable: Object.freeze({ "claude-plan": "Couldn't reach Anthropic.", "chatgpt-plan": "Couldn't reach OpenAI." }),
  timedOut: "The agent didn't answer within a minute. Try again."
});
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the readers.** Create `server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plans.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// OpenClaw's plan brains, read from the programs themselves (spec
// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-plan-brains-design.md, sections 2, 3 and 7):
// the plan status for the brain card, the plan model lists, and the model a
// request asks for, matched against the list read again here.
//
// Everything is read through OpenClaw's and Claude Code's own commands
// (`config get`, `models list`, `models auth list`, `models status`, `auth
// status`), never their files, and through runCommand only (output kept in
// memory, never written to a run log). `models auth list` leaves this module
// as each row's method and token sharing only; `models status --check` as its
// exit code only. Nothing here changes OpenClaw: jobs.js does that.
import { ADAPTERS } from "../agents/index.js";
import { runCommand } from "../safety.js";
import { OPENCLAW_MODEL_PATH, parseConfigText, parseJsonOutput } from "./models.js";
import { openclawVersionInfo } from "./openclaw-version.js";
import {
  FABLE_NOTE,
  INVALID_PLAN_MODEL,
  OPENCLAW_PLANS,
  PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS,
  PLAN_MODELS_AS_OF,
  PLAN_MODEL_NAMES,
  PLAN_PROVIDER,
  PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS,
  TYPED_MODEL_RE,
  chatgptSignIn,
  claudeCliPinned,
  hasClaudeCliPin,
  isFableModel,
  parseAuthRows,
  planModelRows,
  planOfPrimary,
  readinessOf
} from "./openclaw-plan-rules.js";
import { signInStatus } from "./signin.js";

const CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 * 1000;

function planError(code, message) {
  const error = new Error(message);
  error.code = code;
  return error;
}

function assertPlan(plan) {
  if (!OPENCLAW_PLANS.includes(plan)) throw new TypeError('plan must be "claude" or "chatgpt"');
}

// A fresh detection every time (never the 30 s detect cache or the 60 s system
// check), so an OpenClaw updated a moment ago is seen at once.
async function openclawNow(detected) {
  return detected ?? ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true });
}

// `config get agents.defaults.models --json`: the per-model settings, where the
// claude-cli runtime pins live. A plain object, or null.
export async function readOpenclawModelsConfig(detected) {
  if (!detected?.installed) return null;
  const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "agents.defaults.models", "--json"], CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS);
  if (!result.ok) return null;
  const value = parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
  return value !== null && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value) ? value : null;
}

// Signed in with ChatGPT? Only each saved sign-in's method and token sharing
// are kept; the command's output goes no further than this function.
export async function readChatgptAuth(detected) {
  if (!detected?.installed) return { signedIn: null, sharing: null };
  const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "auth", "list", "--provider", "openai", "--json"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return chatgptSignIn(result.ok ? parseAuthRows(parseJsonOutput(result.stdout)) : null);
}

// Can OpenClaw use the ChatGPT plan right now? `models status --check --plain`
// makes no model call (it never gets the probe option); only its exit code is
// read, and its output is dropped here.
export async function readChatgptReadiness(detected) {
  if (!detected?.installed) return "not_ready";
  const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "status", "--check", "--plain"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return readinessOf({ ok: result.ok, code: result.code, signal: result.signal });
}

async function readPrimary(detected) {
  const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", OPENCLAW_MODEL_PATH], CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return result.ok ? parseConfigText(result.stdout) : null;
}

// GET /api/setup/openclaw/plans: { version, claude, chatgpt } (spec section 7).
export async function readOpenclawPlans() {
  const [claude, detected] = await Promise.all([signInStatus("claude"), ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true })]);
  const answer = {
    version: openclawVersionInfo(detected),
    claude: { installed: Boolean(claude.installed), status: claude.status, method: claude.method ?? null, note: claude.note },
    chatgpt: { signedIn: null, sharing: null, readiness: null }
  };
  if (!detected?.installed) return answer;
  const [auth, primary] = await Promise.all([readChatgptAuth(detected), readPrimary(detected)]);
  // The readiness check runs only while OpenClaw is on the ChatGPT plan, so the
  // card can say "expires soon" later.
  const readiness = planOfPrimary(primary, null, auth.signedIn) === "chatgpt" ? await readChatgptReadiness(detected) : null;
  answer.chatgpt = { signedIn: auth.signedIn, sharing: auth.sharing, readiness };
  return answer;
}

// GET /api/setup/openclaw/plan-models?plan=claude|chatgpt (spec sections 2, 3, 5, 7).
export async function readPlanModels(plan, { detected } = {}) {
  assertPlan(plan);
  const found = await openclawNow(detected);
  let rows = null;
  let modelsConfig = null;
  if (found?.installed) {
    const [list, config] = await Promise.all([
      runCommand(found.path, ["models", "list", "--provider", PLAN_PROVIDER[plan], "--json"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS),
      plan === "claude" ? readOpenclawModelsConfig(found) : Promise.resolve(null)
    ]);
    rows = list.ok ? planModelRows(parseJsonOutput(list.stdout), plan) : null;
    modelsConfig = config;
  }
  const source = rows ? "account" : "fallback";
  const listed = rows ?? PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS[plan].map((id) => ({ id, name: PLAN_MODEL_NAMES[id] }));
  // Before a first Claude plan onboard has written any claude-cli pin, every
  // model is offered (the Apply's runtime check still stops one that isn't pinned).
  const pinsExist = plan === "claude" && hasClaudeCliPin(modelsConfig);
  return {
    models: listed.map(({ id, name }) => ({
      id,
      name,
      note: isFableModel(id) ? FABLE_NOTE : null,
      available: pinsExist ? claudeCliPinned(modelsConfig, id) : true
    })),
    source,
    asOf: source === "fallback" ? PLAN_MODELS_AS_OF : null
  };
}

// The model id an Apply uses (spec section 5, "Model names from the person").
// The list is read again here, with the same code as plan-models: a name in it
// is accepted whatever its letter case, and the list's own spelling is used; any
// other name counts as typed and is accepted only while the list is the
// fallback (the only time the card offers "Type a model name").
export async function resolvePlanModel(plan, model, { detected } = {}) {
  assertPlan(plan);
  const text = typeof model === "string" ? model.trim() : "";
  if (text) {
    const { models, source } = await readPlanModels(plan, { detected });
    const lower = text.toLowerCase();
    const listed = models.find((entry) => entry.id.toLowerCase() === lower);
    if (listed) return listed.id;
    const prefix = `${PLAN_PROVIDER[plan]}/`;
    const typed = text.startsWith(prefix) ? text.slice(prefix.length) : text;
    if (source === "fallback" && TYPED_MODEL_RE.test(typed)) return typed;
  }
  throw planError("invalid_model_id", INVALID_PLAN_MODEL);
}
```

export async function signInStatus(agentId) {

  const base = { agentId, label: def.label, cost: def.cost, installed: Boolean(detected.installed) };

  }

  return { ...base, ...interpretStatus(agentId, result), checkedAt: new Date().toISOString() };

with:

```js
// How Claude Code is signed in: the `authMethod` word `claude auth status`
// printed, only when it is one this module knows (a key of CLAUDE_METHOD_NOTE),
// else null. The plan brains need it (spec 2026-10-15, section 2); the account,
// e-mail and organisation printed next to it are never kept.
function signInMethod(agentId, result) {
  if (agentId !== "claude" || result.signal || typeof result.code === "string") return null;
  const parsed = parseJson(result.stdout);
  const method = parsed && typeof parsed === "object" ? parsed.authMethod : null;
  return typeof method === "string" && Object.hasOwn(CLAUDE_METHOD_NOTE, method) ? method : null;
}

// Asks the agent itself (never its files). One of signed_in | not_signed_in |
// unknown, plus a plain note and `method` (Claude Code only; null otherwise).
// Reused by the AI brain step for these agents and by the plan brains.
export async function signInStatus(agentId) {
  const def = definition(agentId);
  const detected = await ADAPTERS[agentId].detect({ refresh: true });
  const base = { agentId, label: def.label, cost: def.cost, installed: Boolean(detected.installed) };
  if (!detected.installed) {
    return { ...base, status: "unknown", note: `${def.label} isn't installed yet. Install it first, then sign in.`, method: null };
  }
  // The same limited environment Agent OS gives the agents it runs, so the
  // answer matches what a run started from here would see.
  const result = await runCommand(detected.path, def.statusArgs, STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS, { env: childEnv(process.env) });
  return { ...base, ...interpretStatus(agentId, result), method: signInMethod(agentId, result), checkedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
}

```

with:

```js
// Which plan OpenClaw's model runs on (spec 2026-10-15, section 5), checked the
// way OpenClaw itself decides, through its own commands (never its files): an
// anthropic/ model pinned to the claude-cli runtime is the Claude plan, an
// openai/ model with a Sign in with ChatGPT profile is the ChatGPT plan. Only
// each sign-in's method is kept from `models auth list`; its output is never
// logged or returned.
async function openclawPlanOf(detected, primary) {
  if (typeof primary !== "string" || primary.includes("@")) return null;
  if (primary.startsWith("anthropic/")) {
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "agents.defaults.models", "--json"], CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS);
    return planOfPrimary(primary, result.ok ? parseJsonOutput(result.stdout) : null, false);
  }
  if (primary.startsWith("openai/")) {
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "auth", "list", "--provider", "openai", "--json"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const { signedIn } = chatgptSignIn(result.ok ? parseAuthRows(parseJsonOutput(result.stdout)) : null);
    return planOfPrimary(primary, null, signedIn);
  }
  return null;
}

// Hermes and OpenClaw's current model, read through their own `config get`
// (never from their config files). `detected` is the agent's detection result.
// OpenClaw's answer also says which plan it runs on (`plan`), and labels an
// anthropic/ or openai/ model by it; Hermes's answer keeps its shape.
export async function readAgentModel(agentId, detected) {
  if (!detected?.installed) {
    const missing = { agentId, installed: false, provider: null, providerLabel: null, model: null, isPreset: false, presetSlug: null };
    return agentId === "openclaw" ? { ...missing, plan: null } : missing;
  }

with:

```js
export async function getSetupJob(id) {
  const active = activeJobs.get(id);
  if (active) return active.job;
  const stored = await loadJob(id);
  // A plan job saved as "running" that this process isn't running: Agent OS
  // quit while it ran (a plan job is in activeJobs before its first save).
  if (stored?.plan && stored.status === "running") return markPlanJobInterrupted(stored);
  return stored;
}

// Answered, and saved, as failed with a plain sentence, so the card stops
// waiting and offers Apply again (Review Focus 5). Plan jobs only: every other
// job keeps today's answer. The sentence goes on the step that never finished:
// the one saved as running, else the first one not succeeded. currentStepIndex
// can still point at a step that succeeded (runConfigureJobSteps saves step i
// as succeeded before step i + 1 as running), so it is only the fallback for a
// job whose every step succeeded (Agent OS quit while writing the receipt).
async function markPlanJobInterrupted(job) {
  const steps = Array.isArray(job.steps) ? job.steps : [];
  let current = steps.findIndex((step) => step.status === "running");
  if (current < 0) current = steps.findIndex((step) => step.status !== "succeeded");
  if (current < 0) {
    current = Number.isInteger(job.currentStepIndex) && steps[job.currentStepIndex] ? job.currentStepIndex : steps.length - 1;
  }
  const step = steps[current];
  if (step) {
    step.status = "failed";
    step.error = PLAN_JOB_INTERRUPTED;
  }
  job.status = "failed";
  job.endedAt = job.endedAt || new Date().toISOString();
  await persistJob(job).catch(() => {});
  return job;
}
```

with:

```js
// `openclaw onboard`'s arguments, each flag checked against this OpenClaw's own
// `onboard --help` first: the three it can't work without stop the step, and
// the optional ones are added only when listed (a log line names any skipped).
// `authArgs` is --auth-choice and what that choice needs. One copy for the
// OpenRouter and Local brains and the Claude plan.
async function onboardArgs(step, detected, authArgs) {
  const help = await runCommand(detected.path, ["onboard", "--help"], HELP_TIMEOUT_MS);
  const helpText = `${help.stdout}\n${help.stderr}`;
  for (const flag of ["--non-interactive", "--accept-risk", "--auth-choice"]) {
    if (!helpText.includes(flag)) {
      throw jobError("configure_failed", `This OpenClaw version's "onboard" command has no ${flag} flag.`);
    }
  }
  const args = ["onboard", "--non-interactive", "--accept-risk", ...authArgs];
  for (const flag of ["--skip-health", "--skip-channels", "--skip-skills", "--skip-ui", "--install-daemon"]) {
    if (helpText.includes(flag)) {
      args.push(flag);
    } else {
      timestampedLog(step, `openclaw onboard --help does not list ${flag}; skipped.`);
    }
  }
  return args;
}

async function configureOpenclawBrain(step, check, ctx, manager) {
  const detected = check.agents.openclaw.detected;
  const target = ctx.targets.openclaw;

  // KNOWN LIMITATION: `openclaw onboard --help` (2026.9.6) offers the key
  // only as `--openrouter-api-key <key>`, so it is a command-line argument,
  // visible to other programs on this computer for the second or two the
  // command runs. There is no env-variable or stdin option, and
  // `--secret-input-mode ref` only stores a pointer to an env variable that
  // OpenClaw's background gateway would not have, so it can't be used here.
  // Ollama is reached at its native API (no /v1); OpenClaw's docs note that
  // the OpenAI-compatible /v1 path makes tool calling unreliable.
  const args = await onboardArgs(
    step,
    detected,
    target.mode === "ollama"
      ? ["--auth-choice", "ollama", "--custom-base-url", ollamaBaseUrl()]
      : ["--auth-choice", "openrouter-api-key", "--openrouter-api-key", ctx.apiKey]
  );
```

function healthFixLine(output, target, timedOut) {
  const text = String(output || "");
  if (/\b429\b|rate.?limit|too many requests|free-models-per-day|quota/i.test(text)) {
    return "OpenRouter's free limit was reached (50 requests a day until you add $10 of credit). Try again tomorrow, add credit, or use Local.";
  }
  if (/\b40[13]\b|unauthori[sz]ed|invalid.{0,12}(api )?key|no auth|authentication|credential/i.test(text)) {

      : "Couldn't reach OpenRouter. Check your internet connection and try again.";

  if (timedOut) {

with:

```js
// Today's network pattern and last sentence, shared by every brain.
const HEALTH_NETWORK_RE = /econnrefused|enotfound|fetch failed|network|could not resolve|connection (refused|error)/i;
const HEALTH_LAST_LINE = "The agent didn't reply as expected. Open its run on the Runs page for details, or pick another model.";

// A short, plain next step for a failed "say hello" check. `target` is the
// brain we just gave that agent. A plan brain (claude-plan, chatgpt-plan) has
// its own lines and never gets an OpenRouter or Ollama sentence (spec
// 2026-10-15, section 5); openrouter and ollama keep today's order and words.
export function healthFixLine(output, target, timedOut) {
  const text = String(output || "");
  const mode = target?.mode;
  if (mode === "claude-plan" || mode === "chatgpt-plan") {
    if (/usage limit|limit reached|rate.?limit|\b429\b|quota/i.test(text)) return PLAN_HEALTH_LINES.usageLimit;
    if (/not (logged|signed) in|\/login|\b401\b|unauthori[sz]ed|expired/i.test(text)) return PLAN_HEALTH_LINES.signedOut;
    if (HEALTH_NETWORK_RE.test(text)) return PLAN_HEALTH_LINES.unreachable[mode];
    if (timedOut) return PLAN_HEALTH_LINES.timedOut;
    return HEALTH_LAST_LINE;
  }
  if (/\b429\b|rate.?limit|too many requests|free-models-per-day|quota/i.test(text)) {
    return "OpenRouter's free limit was reached (50 requests a day until you add $10 of credit). Try again tomorrow, add credit, or use Local.";
  }
  if (/\b40[13]\b|unauthori[sz]ed|invalid.{0,12}(api )?key|no auth|authentication|credential/i.test(text)) {
    return "The agent didn't accept the key. Connect OpenRouter again and press the button again.";
  }
  if (HEALTH_NETWORK_RE.test(text)) {
    return mode === "ollama"
      ? "Couldn't reach Ollama. Open the Ollama app and try again."
      : "Couldn't reach OpenRouter. Check your internet connection and try again.";
  }
  if (timedOut) {
    return "The agent didn't answer within a minute. Free models are sometimes busy; try again, or pick another model.";
  }
  if (mode === "ollama") {
    return "This local model didn't answer properly. Try a bigger model, or use OpenRouter.";
  }
  return HEALTH_LAST_LINE;
}

(i) The plan section. Replace the banner before the Ollama download section:

// =========================================================================

```

with:

```js
// =========================================================================
// OpenClaw's plan brains (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-plan-brains-design.md,
// sections 2 and 3). The Claude plan points OpenClaw at the person's own
// signed-in Claude Code (OpenClaw's claude-cli runtime runs the unmodified
// `claude` program); the ChatGPT plan uses the Sign in with ChatGPT the person
// already did in the card. No key or token is ever passed. Started only by
// POST /api/setup/openclaw/plan: POST /api/setup/configure and normalizeTarget
// keep refusing these modes. Same machinery as the other jobs: one at a time,
// saved to disk, cancelable, a hello check at the end.
// =========================================================================

export const PLAN_JOB_STEPS = Object.freeze({
  claude: Object.freeze([
    "openclaw-plan-onboard",
    "openclaw-safe-defaults",
    "openclaw-plan-runtime-check",
    "openclaw-plan-model",
    "services",
    "health"
  ]),
  chatgpt: Object.freeze(["openclaw-plan-model", "openclaw-safe-defaults", "openclaw-plan-readiness", "health"])
});

function planNotReady(reason) {
  return jobError("plan_not_ready", PLAN_NOT_READY_MESSAGE[reason]);
}

// The OpenClaw a plan step works on (installed when the job started).
function planOpenclaw(check) {
  const detected = check.agents.openclaw.detected;
  if (!detected?.installed) throw jobError("configure_failed", PLAN_NOT_READY_MESSAGE.openclaw_missing);
  return detected;
}

export async function startOpenclawPlanJob({ plan, model, acceptOpenClawRisk } = {}) {
  // The risk tick comes first: without it nothing runs and nothing is read.
  if (acceptOpenClawRisk !== true) {
    throw jobError("openclaw_risk_not_accepted", "OpenClaw brain configuration requires acceptOpenClawRisk:true.");
  }
  if (!OPENCLAW_PLANS.includes(plan)) throw new TypeError('plan must be "claude" or "chatgpt"');
  return withJobLock(() => startOpenclawPlanJobLocked({ plan, model }));
}

async function startOpenclawPlanJobLocked({ plan, model }) {
  const detected = await ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true });
  if (!detected?.installed) throw planNotReady("openclaw_missing");
  // Read again here, never trusted from the card: Claude Code may have been
  // signed out, or switched to an API key, since the card last looked.
  if (plan === "claude") {
    const readiness = claudePlanReadiness(await signInStatus("claude"));
    if (readiness !== "ready") throw planNotReady(readiness);
  } else if ((await readChatgptAuth(detected)).signedIn !== true) {
    throw planNotReady("chatgpt_signed_out");
  }
  const modelId = await resolvePlanModel(plan, model, { detected });
  const mode = PLAN_MODE[plan];
  const id = generateJobId();
  const now = new Date().toISOString();
  const job = {
    id,
    kind: "configure",
    status: "running",
    plan,
    mode,
    model: modelId,
    targets: { hermes: null, openclaw: { mode, model: modelId } },
    scope: ["openclaw"],
    steps: PLAN_JOB_STEPS[plan].map((stepId) =>
      makeConfigureStep(stepId, stepId === "services" || stepId === "health" ? null : "openclaw", "run")
    ),
    currentStepIndex: 0,
    startedAt: now,
    endedAt: null,
    acceptOpenClawRisk: true,
    acceptOpenClawRiskAt: now,
    previousPrimary: null,
    readiness: null
  };
  // In activeJobs before its first save, so a read in between never takes it
  // for a job that Agent OS quit during (getSetupJob).
  activeJobs.set(id, { job, controller: null });
  try {
    await persistJob(job);
  } catch (error) {
    activeJobs.delete(id);
    throw error;
  }
  runningJobId = id;
  runConfigureJobSteps(job, "").catch(() => {});
  return job;
}

// Claude plan, step 1: `openclaw onboard ... --auth-choice anthropic-cli`, which
// points OpenClaw at the signed-in Claude Code on this computer, with today's
// flag checks.
async function onboardOpenclawForClaudePlan(step, check, manager) {
  const detected = planOpenclaw(check);
  const args = await onboardArgs(step, detected, ["--auth-choice", "anthropic-cli"]);
  await runConfigureCommand(
    manager,
    { agentId: "openclaw", kind: "configure", title: "openclaw onboard", command: detected.path, args, cwd: os.tmpdir(), timeoutMs: CONFIGURE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS },
    step
  );
}

// Claude plan, step 3, before `models set`: OpenClaw must run this model
// through Claude Code (claude-cli on anthropic/<model>, or on anthropic/* when
// the model has no runtime of its own). Otherwise it would bill an Anthropic
// API key, so the job stops here and OpenClaw keeps its old model.
async function checkClaudePlanRuntime(job, check) {
  const config = await readOpenclawModelsConfig(planOpenclaw(check));
  if (!claudeCliPinned(config, job.model)) throw jobError("configure_failed", RUNTIME_CHECK_FAILED);
}

// `openclaw models set <provider>/<model>`. For the ChatGPT plan the current
// model is read first, so a failed readiness check can put it back.
async function setOpenclawPlanModel(job, step, check, manager) {
  const detected = planOpenclaw(check);
  if (job.plan === "chatgpt") {
    const current = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", OPENCLAW_MODEL_PATH], CONFIG_GET_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const primary = current.ok ? parseConfigText(current.stdout) : null;
    // Only a plain model reference ever goes back onto a command line.
    job.previousPrimary = primary && MODEL_ID_PATTERN.test(primary) ? primary : null;
    await persistJob(job);
  }
  await runConfigureCommand(
    manager,
    {
      agentId: "openclaw",
      kind: "configure",
      title: "openclaw models set",
      command: detected.path,
      args: ["models", "set", `${PLAN_PROVIDER[job.plan]}/${job.model}`],
      cwd: os.tmpdir(),
      timeoutMs: CONFIGURE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS
    },
    step
  );
}

// ChatGPT plan, step 3: can OpenClaw use the plan? Exit code only
// (readChatgptReadiness). Expiring soon: a warning, and the job goes on. Not
// ready: the earlier model is put back (or, when there was none, the job's last
// line says OpenClaw keeps the new one) and the job stops.
async function checkChatgptPlanReadiness(job, step, check, manager) {
  const detected = planOpenclaw(check);
  const readiness = await readChatgptReadiness(detected);
  job.readiness = readiness;
  if (readiness === "ready") return;
  if (readiness === "expiring") {
    step.warnings.push(CHATGPT_EXPIRING);
    return;
  }
  if (job.previousPrimary) {
    const back = await runConfigureCommand(
      manager,
      {
        agentId: "openclaw",
        kind: "configure",
        title: "openclaw models set",
        command: detected.path,
        args: ["models", "set", job.previousPrimary],
        cwd: os.tmpdir(),
        timeoutMs: CONFIGURE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS
      },
      step,
      { optional: true }
    );
    if (back.run.status !== "succeeded") step.warnings.push("openclaw models set failed; see the run log.");
  } else {
    step.warnings.push(noEarlierPrimary(`openai/${job.model}`));
  }
  throw jobError("configure_failed", CHATGPT_NOT_READY);
}

// Downloading a local model (Ollama). Same machinery as the other jobs --

#### Notes

1. **Decisions this task makes** (the contract leaves them open; the owner can overturn any):
   - **One onboard check.** The `onboard --help` flag check moves into a small `onboardArgs` helper that today's OpenRouter and Local brains and the Claude plan share, so "as today" stays true if the check ever changes. The argv of today's brains is the same item for item, and `test/setup-brain.test.js` (Step 13) checks it.
   - **Ids from OpenClaw's list must be plain.** Beyond the contract's "another provider's prefix is dropped", a listed id that still holds a slash, a space, a leading `-`, any character outside `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`, or more than 120 characters is dropped too, because the id goes into `models set <provider>/<id>`. An `@` is refused on purpose: in OpenClaw an `@` suffix names an auth profile, so `models set anthropic/<x@y>` could pick another sign-in than the plan, and spec section 5 never labels such a primary a plan (`planOfPrimary` and `openclawPlanOf` answer `null`), so a model Agent OS had just applied as the Claude plan would show "Anthropic API key". A listed name longer than 120 characters is cut. Private constants `LISTED_ID_RE` and `MAX_NAME_CHARS` in the rules module.
   - **The earlier model** is read with `config get agents.defaults.model.primary` and kept only when it passes `MODEL_ID_PATTERN` (no leading `-`, no space), because it may go back onto a command line. A read that fails counts as "no earlier model".
   - **A put-back that fails** keeps the readiness step's error (`CHATGPT_NOT_READY`) and adds today's run sentence for that command as a warning, "openclaw models set failed; see the run log.", rather than a new sentence.
   - **`readiness` is saved on the job** for every outcome of the readiness step, and stays `null` for the Claude plan.
   - **`retrySetupJob` marks a stale plan job failed first**, so a plan job left "running" by a quit is refused like every other configure job (`key_required_for_retry`), not handed back as "running".
   - **Which step a quit marks failed.** The step saved as `"running"`, else the first step not `"succeeded"`; `currentStepIndex` only when every step had succeeded (Agent OS quit after the last step, while writing the receipt or before saving `"succeeded"`), else the last step. `runConfigureJobSteps` saves step i as succeeded before it saves step i + 1 as running, so `currentStepIndex` alone could put "Agent OS quit before this finished" on a step that succeeded. When every step had succeeded, the last step carries the sentence, because the receipt may be missing; Apply again writes it.
   - **A plan job's hello** runs through the same `afterModelChange` branch as a model change (a fresh OpenClaw conversation and the 90 s cap), so it never holds the job lock for 30 minutes.
   - **`PLAN_HEALTH_LINES`** (beyond the contract) keeps the five plan hello sentences with the other plan sentences in the rules module; `healthFixLine` uses them and keeps today's OpenRouter and Ollama branches word for word (it now shares `HEALTH_NETWORK_RE` and `HEALTH_LAST_LINE` with them).
   - **Private names beyond the contract:** `onboardArgs`, `markPlanJobInterrupted`, `planNotReady`, `planOpenclaw`, `onboardOpenclawForClaudePlan`, `checkClaudePlanRuntime`, `setOpenclawPlanModel`, `checkChatgptPlanReadiness`, `HEALTH_NETWORK_RE`, `HEALTH_LAST_LINE` (jobs.js); `signInMethod` (signin.js); `openclawPlanOf` (models.js); `LISTED_ID_RE`, `MAX_NAME_CHARS` (rules); `PLAN_VALUE_ERROR`, `planValue` (inside `createSetupRouter`).
   - **The plan tests' environment** (`test/helpers/openclaw-plan-env.js`, beyond the contract) installs W1's fakes for `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent` and `hermes` and the two Setup fakes for `claude` and `openclaw`, so the PATH holds all six names as fakes; it starts a 127.0.0.1 mirror so the system check never reaches a real host; it removes `H1_ENV_NAMES` and every `OPENCLAW_*` and `FAKE_*` variable from its own environment first, so Safety 4 is meaningful; and it never starts `server/index.js` or a session, so it needs no `SHELL` of its own (the runner's `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` applies anyway).
   - **No real agent behind a missing fake.** `which()` (`executableSearchDirs` in `server/runtime/safety.js`) always searches `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, whatever PATH says, and Claude Code's and OpenClaw's own fallback folders are inside the temp HOME. So `withPlanEnv` calls `refuseSystemAgent("claude")` when `claude: "missing"` and `refuseSystemAgent("openclaw")` when `openclaw: false`, and every test that removes the fake Claude Code calls `refuseSystemAgent("claude")` right after the `rm`. Such a test fails with a plain sentence instead of running a real program. The existing `test/setup-models.test.js` tests share the same weakness; this task leaves them alone.
   - **B1b's safety flows run once** and three tests read the result, because each Apply takes a second or two.
   - **One source scan.** B1b's block pushes its two modules onto B1a's `NEW_SERVER_MODULES`, so B1a's Safety 3 test scans them (B1a's comment says the later tasks add theirs there); B1b's own Safety 3 test only checks that the push reached the list. Before Step 7 that makes B1a's Safety 3 test fail too (Step 5 expects it).
   - **`node:test` as a namespace in the safety block** (`import * as planNodeTest from "node:test"; const planTest = planNodeTest.test;`), so the file keeps exactly one line that Task B1c's Step 0 grep counts. Test-only names beyond the contract in that block: `planNodeTest`, `planTest`, `planModules` (with the earlier `planAssert`, `planPath`, `planSafety`, `planPosixSkip`, `planFlowsRun`, `planFlows`, `planRunFlows`, `planApply` and the five renamed helper imports).
   - **Look only** is tested for both plans in one test: the plan is still applied (Setup's configuration steps are not gated, as today), the hello is skipped with `HELLO_SKIPPED_AT_LOOK_ONLY`, and no `kind: "agent"` run reaches the run manager.
2. **Copy for the owner's review at E1.** New server sentences this task brings (all listed in the contract): "Install OpenClaw first."; "Sign in to Claude Code first, then try again."; "Sign in with ChatGPT first, then try again."; "OpenClaw had no model set before, so it keeps openai/<id>."; "Agent OS quit before this finished. Apply the plan again." Spec sentences it uses verbatim: the `plan_not_ready` sentences for an API key and for an unknown sign-in method, "Install Claude Code first.", the runtime check, readiness and model-name sentences, the Fable note, the five plan hello lines and the four labels. Reused unchanged: "openclaw models set failed; see the run log." (today's run failure sentence) and the developer-facing refusal `plan must be "claude" or "chatgpt"` (the contract's body).
3. **Risks.**
   - The field names of `models auth list` (`method`, else `type`; `tokenSharing`) and the shapes of `models list --json` and `config get agents.defaults.models --json` are provisional until live check S-B3 (Task E3); the fakes and `parseAuthRows`/`planModelRows` change together if they differ. S-B3 should also record how `config get agents.defaults.model.primary` answers when nothing is set (exit code), because a failed read counts as "no earlier model".
   - The "fresh conversation" half of the plan hello is not visible in these tests: the Setup OpenClaw fake's `agent --help` lists no `--session-id`, so the adapter uses its older transport. The 90 s cap is tested; the fresh conversation is the model job's existing branch.
   - `getSetupJob` marks a stored "running" plan job failed when this process isn't running it. Two Agent OS servers sharing one `AGENT_OS_HOME` (already a parked E2 question) could then mark each other's plan job failed.
   - `signInStatus` runs Claude Code through `childEnv`, which drops `FAKE_*` variables, so every test writes its knobs as files; a test that set a knob only in `process.env` would silently test the marker files instead.
   - This task depends on B1a's helper names and shapes exactly as the contract states them (Step 0 checks them); if B1a lands with a different shape, the B1b worker stops at Step 0 rather than adapting.
   - On a Mac with a real `claude` or `openclaw` in `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin`, the tests that need that program missing fail with `refuseSystemAgent`'s sentence (by design: never run a real agent). The owner's Mac has neither there today. If that changes, the orchestrator decides between a skip with that reason and a different test HOME setup; the worker never moves the program.

### Task B1c: openCommandInTerminal and the Hermes model picker Terminal.app launch

The Hermes brain card on the Agents page gets one new button in Task B2, "Choose in Hermes". It opens Hermes's own model picker (`hermes model`) in its own Terminal.app window (spec §4, owner decision 3). This task builds the server half. Setup already has a helper that does almost exactly this for signing in to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor: `openSignInInTerminal` (`server/runtime/setup/signin.js`) writes a tiny `.command` file holding one fixed command line and asks macOS to open it with `open -a Terminal <file>`, or hands the command back to copy on Windows and Linux. This task splits the general part out as `openCommandInTerminal(binPath, args, { name, platform, spawnFn })`, so both callers share one tested path. Every sign-in answer, the sign-in file name (`<agentId>-login-<8 hex>.command`) and the sign-in source-scan rule stay as they are.

On top of that helper, a new module `server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js` finds Hermes with its adapter's own fresh detection and opens `<detected hermes> model`. A new route, `POST /api/setup/hermes/model-terminal`, sits behind `requireLocalMode` and answers `{ opened, command, reason? }`, the same shape as the sign-in terminal route. Nothing from the request reaches the command or the file. Agent OS never starts a session or a PTY for it, and never reads or changes Hermes's config: the person picks in Hermes's own window, with their own shell and settings (H1, H2), and the card reads what Hermes saved afterwards (Task B2). Hermes not installed answers 400 `agent_not_installed`, written by the route itself, because `mapJobError` would turn that code into 409 and spec §7 says 400.

It owns the server half of spec §4, §7's Hermes route, Safety 2's Hermes part (the exact `open` argv, the file holding only `<hermes path> model`, no PTY session), and the Hermes launch's share of Safety 1 (no agent file touched) and Safety 3 (no forbidden flag in the argv or the code). It also adds the launch's share of Safety 4 (no environment of its own), because the shared safety file covers Safety 4 for every command the feature runs. Its tests never open a real Terminal window and never run a real agent: the launch functions get an injected spawn function, and the one route test that reaches the real spawn (macOS only) finds a fake `open` first on PATH, after asserting that it does.

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// A spawn function that starts nothing: it records the call, then says the
// program started ("spawn") or could not start ("error").
function fakeSpawn(outcome, calls) {
  return (command, args, options) => {
    calls.push({ command, args, options });
    const child = new EventEmitter();
    child.unref = () => {};
    setImmediate(() => (outcome === "spawn" ? child.emit("spawn") : child.emit("error", new Error("could not start"))));
    return child;
  };
}

async function exists(file) {
  return stat(file).then(
    () => true,
    () => false
  );
}

async function jsonLines(file) {
  const text = await readFile(file, "utf8").catch(() => "");
  return text
    .split("\n")
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
}

async function startedFakes(agentLog) {
  return (await jsonLines(agentLog)).filter((entry) => entry.event === "start");
}

  await makeFakeAgentBin(fakeBin, { names: FAKE_AGENT_NAMES.filter((name) => hermes || name !== "hermes") });

  await chmod(path.join(fakeBin, "open"), 0o755);
  try {

        ...LOCAL_MODE,
        HOME: home,

        PATH: [fakeBin, ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter),
        SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
        FAKE_AGENT_LOG: agentLog
      },
      async () => {
        assert.equal(os.homedir(), home, "tests must never see the real home folder");
        clearDetectCaches();
        try {
          await fn({
            home,
            agentOsHome,
            fakeBin,
            agentLog,
            terminalDir: path.join(agentOsHome, "setup", "terminal"),
            openLog: path.join(home, ".fake-open-calls.log")
          });
        } finally {
          clearDetectCaches();
        }
      }
    );
  } finally {
    await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

// The real Setup router on a real port, with a session manager that records
// every property the router reads from it. The Hermes route must read none,
// so it can never start a session.
async function withSetupApp(fn) {
  const touched = [];
  const sessionManager = new Proxy(
    {},
    {
      get(_target, property) {
        touched.push(String(property));
        return () => {
          throw new Error(`the session manager was used (${String(property)})`);
        };
      }
    }
  );
  const app = express();
  app.use(express.json());
  app.use("/api/setup", createSetupRouter({ sessionManager }));
  app.use((error, _req, res, _next) => {
    res.status(error?.status || 500).json({ ok: false, error: error?.message || "Internal server error" });
  });
  touched.length = 0;
  const server = app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1");
  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once("listening", resolve));
  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/api/setup/hermes/model-terminal`;
  const post = async (body) => {
    const response = await fetch(url, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      ...(body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(body) })
    });
    return { status: response.status, json: await response.json() };
  };
  try {
    await fn({ post, touched });
  } finally {
    await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(resolve));
  }
}

// The fake `open` runs detached, so its log line can land a moment after the answer.
async function waitForOpenLine(openLog, timeoutMs = 5000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const lines = (await readFile(openLog, "utf8").catch(() => "")).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
    if (lines.length) {
      assert.equal(lines.length, 1, "exactly one open call");
      return lines[0];
    }
    if (Date.now() > deadline) assert.fail("the fake open was never called");
    await delay(50);
  }
}

// Code with its comments taken out, the way the sign-in source scan in
// test/setup-builders.test.js reads it.
async function codeOf(...parts) {
  const source = await readFile(path.join(root, ...parts), "utf8");
  return source.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "").replace(/\s\/\/ .*$/gm, "");
}

test("openCommandInTerminal(): on macOS, a <name>-<8 hex>.command file (0700) holding only the command line, opened with exactly `open -a Terminal <file>`", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withLaunchEnv(async ({ terminalDir }) => {
    const command = "'/opt/fake tools/bin/hermes' model";
    const calls = [];
    const result = await openCommandInTerminal("/opt/fake tools/bin/hermes", ["model"], {
      name: "hermes-model",
      platform: "darwin",
      spawnFn: fakeSpawn("spawn", calls)
    });
    assert.deepEqual(result, { opened: true, command });
    assert.equal(calls.length, 1);
    const file = calls[0].args[2];
    assert.deepEqual(calls[0], { command: "open", args: ["-a", "Terminal", file], options: OPEN_OPTIONS });
    assert.equal(path.dirname(file), terminalDir);
    assert.match(path.basename(file), PICKER_FILE);
    assert.equal(await readFile(file, "utf8"), `${command}\n`, "nothing but the one command line");
    assert.equal((await stat(file)).mode & 0o777, 0o700);
    assert.equal((await stat(terminalDir)).mode & 0o777, 0o700);

    // Every launch gets a file of its own.
    const again = [];
    await openCommandInTerminal("/opt/fake tools/bin/hermes", ["model"], {
      name: "hermes-model",
      platform: "darwin",
      spawnFn: fakeSpawn("spawn", again)
    });
    assert.notEqual(again[0].args[2], file);
    assert.deepEqual((await readdir(terminalDir)).sort(), [path.basename(file), path.basename(again[0].args[2])].sort());
  });
});

test("POST /api/setup/hermes/model-terminal: 200 { opened, command, reason? } with only the fixed command, whatever the request carries; no session", posixSkip, async () => {
  await withLaunchEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, fakeBin, agentLog, terminalDir, openLog }) => {
    const hermes = path.join(fakeBin, "hermes");
    await withSetupApp(async ({ post, touched }) => {
      if (process.platform === "darwin") {
        // The route uses the real spawn, so prove first that PATH finds the fake `open`.
        assert.equal(process.env.PATH.split(path.delimiter)[0], fakeBin);
        assert.ok((await stat(path.join(fakeBin, "open"))).mode & 0o100, "the fake open is executable");
      }
      const answer = await post({ confirm: true, command: "rm -rf ~", args: ["--yolo"], path: "/tmp/evil", name: "evil" });
      assert.equal(answer.status, 200);
      if (process.platform === "darwin") {
        assert.deepEqual(answer.json, { opened: true, command: `${hermes} model` });
        const line = await waitForOpenLine(openLog);
        assert.ok(line.startsWith("-a Terminal "), line);
        const file = line.slice("-a Terminal ".length);
        assert.equal(path.dirname(file), terminalDir);
        assert.match(path.basename(file), PICKER_FILE);
        assert.equal(await readFile(file, "utf8"), `${hermes} model\n`);
      } else {
        assert.deepEqual(answer.json, { opened: false, reason: "copy", command: `${hermes} model` });
        assert.equal(await exists(path.join(agentOsHome, "setup")), false);
      }
      assert.deepEqual(touched, [], "the route never reads the session manager");
    });
    assert.deepEqual(await startedFakes(agentLog), []);
    // (an agent session would write this folder; a setup session never does,
    // so the Proxy and the start log cover that kind)
    assert.equal(await exists(path.join(agentOsHome, "sessions")), false);
  });
});

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the Hermes launch to the safety tests.** Append this block to the very end of `test/plan-brains-safety.test.js` (after B1a's and B1b's tests; change nothing above it). It does two things: it pushes the Hermes module onto B1a's `NEW_SERVER_MODULES`, so B1a's existing Safety 3 test scans it (the way B1b's block pushes its two modules), and it adds one test for the launch:

```js

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Task B1c: "Choose in Hermes" opens Hermes's own model picker (`hermes model`)
// in its own Terminal.app window (spec §4). Its share of the Safety items:
//   1. the file-access spy over the launch sees no agent file at all, not even
//      OpenClaw's openclaw.json (the one touch allowed elsewhere);
//   3. the launch's argv (the one `open` call and the words in its .command
//      file) holds no forbidden flag, nothing ran `hermes model` inside Agent
//      OS, and the source scan finds nothing in hermes-model-terminal.js (a
//      new module: the push below puts it on NEW_SERVER_MODULES, so B1a's
//      Safety 3 test scans it) or in signin.js, where its Terminal helper
//      lives (an existing module, so not on that list; the test scans it);
//   4. the launch passes no environment of its own and changes none. For the
//      Hermes launch, the only program Agent OS starts is `open`; its
//      environment is the spawn options (no env, so the inherited one, with
//      HOME the temp home and no H1 name set), and the detection fakes answer
//      --version and --help without an env log. The spawn function below logs
//      that inherited environment at the moment of the spawn.
// Safety 2's Hermes part (the exact `open` argv, the file's content, no
// session) is in test/hermes-model-terminal.test.js. Two names come from the
// part above: `test`, and NEW_SERVER_MODULES (B1a's list of the feature's new
// server modules). This block declares no name of its own at the top level;
// everything else is imported inside the test, so no name here can clash with
// the imports above.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// B1a's Safety 3 test runs the source scan over every module in this list.
NEW_SERVER_MODULES.push("server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js");

test(
  "Safety 1, 3 and 4 (B1c): Choose in Hermes opens the picker without an agent file, a forbidden flag or an environment of its own",
  { skip: process.platform === "win32" ? "POSIX only: the fake agents are sh scripts" : false },
  async () => {
    const { default: assert } = await import("node:assert/strict");
    const { EventEmitter } = await import("node:events");
    const { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm } = await import("node:fs/promises");
    const { default: os } = await import("node:os");
    const { default: path } = await import("node:path");
    const { fileURLToPath } = await import("node:url");
    const { clearDetectCaches } = await import("../server/runtime/agents/detect.js");
    const { HERMES_MODEL_ARGS, openHermesModelTerminal } = await import("../server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js");
    const { FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } = await import("./helpers/fake-agents.js");
    const { FORBIDDEN_PATH, H1_ENV_NAMES, argvProblems, sourceProblems, spyOnFileAccess } = await import(
      "./helpers/plan-brains-safety.js"
    );

    const setupDir = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "server", "runtime", "setup");
    const base = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-b1c-safety-")));
    const home = path.join(base, "home");
    const agentOsHome = path.join(base, "agent-os");
    const fakeBin = path.join(base, "fake-bin");
    const agentLog = path.join(base, "fake-agents.jsonl");
    const vars = {
      HOME: home,
      USERPROFILE: home,
      AGENT_OS_HOME: agentOsHome,
      HERMES_AGENT_OS_HOME: undefined,
      HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS: undefined,
      PATH: [fakeBin, "/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"].join(path.delimiter),
      SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
      FAKE_AGENT_LOG: agentLog
    };
    // Safety 4 checks start without the H1 variables (HOME is the temp one).
    for (const name of H1_ENV_NAMES) if (name !== "HOME" && name !== "USERPROFILE") vars[name] = undefined;
    const previous = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(vars).map((key) => [key, process.env[key]]));
    const setEnv = (values) => {
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(values)) {
        if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
        else process.env[key] = value;
      }
    };
    setEnv(vars);
    try {
      await mkdir(home, { recursive: true });
      await mkdir(agentOsHome, { recursive: true });
      await makeFakeAgentBin(fakeBin);
      clearDetectCaches();
      const hermes = path.join(fakeBin, "hermes");
      const h1Before = Object.fromEntries(H1_ENV_NAMES.map((name) => [name, process.env[name]]));
      const calls = [];
      const spawnFn = (command, args, options) => {
        // Safety 4's environment log: what `open` would inherit, read at the moment of the spawn.
        const inherited = {
          HOME: process.env.HOME,
          h1Set: H1_ENV_NAMES.filter((name) => process.env[name] !== undefined)
        };
        calls.push({ command, args, options, inherited });
        const child = new EventEmitter();
        child.unref = () => {};
        setImmediate(() => child.emit("spawn"));
        return child;
      };

      // Safety 1: the spy runs over the whole launch, Hermes's detection included.
      const seen = [];
      const restore = spyOnFileAccess(seen);
      let result;
      try {
        result = await openHermesModelTerminal({ platform: "darwin", spawnFn });
      } finally {
        restore();
      }
      assert.deepEqual(result, { opened: true, command: `${hermes} model` });
      assert.ok(seen.includes(hermes), "the spy saw Hermes being looked up (a control)");
      assert.ok(
        seen.some((p) => p.startsWith(path.join(agentOsHome, "setup", "terminal"))),
        "the spy saw the .command file being written (a control)"
      );
      assert.deepEqual(seen.filter((p) => FORBIDDEN_PATH.test(p)), [], "no agent file, not even ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json");

      // Safety 3: the launch's argv and the words in its file; nothing started `hermes model`; the code.
      assert.equal(calls.length, 1);
      const fileText = await readFile(calls[0].args[2], "utf8");
      assert.equal(fileText, `${hermes} model\n`);
      const fileWords = fileText.trim().split(" ");
      assert.deepEqual(fileWords, [hermes, ...HERMES_MODEL_ARGS]);
      assert.deepEqual(argvProblems([[calls[0].command, ...calls[0].args], fileWords]), []);
      const logText = await readFile(agentLog, "utf8").catch(() => "");
      const started = logText
        .split("\n")
        .filter(Boolean)
        .map((line) => JSON.parse(line))
        .filter((entry) => entry.event === "start");
      assert.deepEqual(started, [], "nothing ran `hermes model` inside Agent OS");
      // The new module's scan is B1a's Safety 3 test; this only proves the push above reached its list.
      assert.ok(
        NEW_SERVER_MODULES.includes("server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js"),
        "hermes-model-terminal.js is in B1a's source scan"
      );
      // signin.js is an existing module, so it is not on that list; its Terminal helper is scanned here.
      assert.deepEqual(sourceProblems(await readFile(path.join(setupDir, "signin.js"), "utf8")), [], "signin.js");

      // Safety 4: `open` gets no env and no folder of its own (Terminal.app's own
      // shell decides), so it inherits this process's environment: HOME the temp
      // home and no H1 name set. And the launch changed none of them.
      assert.deepEqual(calls[0].options, { stdio: "ignore", detached: true, shell: false });
      assert.deepEqual(calls[0].inherited, { HOME: home, h1Set: [] }, "HOME unchanged and no H1 name set");
      assert.deepEqual(Object.fromEntries(H1_ENV_NAMES.map((name) => [name, process.env[name]])), h1Before);
      assert.equal(process.env.HOME, home);
    } finally {
      setEnv(previous);
      clearDetectCaches();
      await rm(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }

The push runs while the file loads, before B1a's Safety 3 test reads the list, so that test scans the Hermes module too (checked on the worktree's Node v22: a test defined earlier in a file sees an item pushed at the top level further down).

// macOS: opens Terminal.app on a tiny .command file holding ONLY the login
// command, so the person can sign in where a real terminal is available.
// Elsewhere there is no one way to open a terminal, so the command is handed
// back to be copied. `command` is always returned, for either path.
export async function openSignInInTerminal(agentId, { platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {}) {
  const def = definition(agentId);

    } catch {
      resolve(false);

    }

      resolve(true);
    });

with:

```js
// The name part of a .command file (`<name>-<8 hex>.command`): lower-case
// letters, digits and dashes only, so it can never hold a path piece.
const TERMINAL_NAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$/;

// macOS: opens Terminal.app on a tiny .command file holding ONLY one fixed
// command line (an agent's own program and fixed words, nothing from a
// request), so the person runs it in a real terminal with their own shell and
// settings. Elsewhere there is no one way to open a terminal, so the command
// is handed back to be copied. `command` is always returned, for either path.
// Used by the sign-in fallback below and by Hermes's model picker
// (hermes-model-terminal.js).
export async function openCommandInTerminal(binPath, args, { name, platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {}) {
  if (typeof name !== "string" || !TERMINAL_NAME_RE.test(name)) {
    throw new TypeError("openCommandInTerminal: name must be 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits or dashes.");
  }
  const command = loginCommandLine(binPath, args, platform);
  if (platform !== "darwin") return { opened: false, reason: "copy", command };

  const dir = path.join(runtimePaths().root, "setup", "terminal");
  await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  await sweepOldTerminalFiles(dir);
  const file = path.join(dir, `${name}-${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString("hex")}.command`);
  await fs.writeFile(file, `${command}\n`, { mode: 0o700 });

  const opened = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    let child;
    try {
      child = spawnFn("open", ["-a", "Terminal", file], { stdio: "ignore", detached: true, shell: false });
    } catch {
      resolve(false);
      return;
    }
    child.once("error", () => resolve(false));
    child.once("spawn", () => {
      child.unref?.();
      resolve(true);
    });
  });
  return opened ? { opened: true, command } : { opened: false, reason: "spawn_failed", command };
}

// The sign-in fallback: the agent's own login command, in Terminal.app on macOS.
export async function openSignInInTerminal(agentId, { platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {}) {
  const def = definition(agentId);
  const detected = await ADAPTERS[agentId].detect({ refresh: true });
  if (!detected.installed) throw signInError("agent_not_installed", `${def.label} isn't installed on this computer yet.`);
  return openCommandInTerminal(detected.path, def.loginArgs, { name: `${agentId}-login`, platform, spawnFn });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the Hermes launch.** Create `server/runtime/setup/hermes-model-terminal.js`:

```js
// "Choose in Hermes" (plan brains spec §4): opens Hermes's own model picker,
// `hermes model`, in its own Terminal.app window. Agent OS adds nothing of its
// own here. The window runs one fixed command line, `<detected hermes> model`,
// with the person's own shell and settings, so Hermes sees exactly what it sees
// in Terminal (H1, H2), and nothing typed or shown there passes through Agent
// OS. This never starts a session or a PTY and never changes Hermes's config;
// the Agents page reads what Hermes saved afterwards (readAgentModel).
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { ADAPTERS } from "../agents/index.js";
import { openCommandInTerminal } from "./signin.js";

export const HERMES_MODEL_ARGS = Object.freeze(["model"]);
export const HERMES_TERMINAL_NAME = "hermes-model";

const HERMES_NOT_INSTALLED_MESSAGE = "Hermes isn't installed on this computer yet.";

// Answers what openCommandInTerminal answers: { opened: true, command } on
// macOS, { opened: false, reason: "spawn_failed", command } when Terminal could
// not start, and { opened: false, reason: "copy", command } on Windows and
// Linux. Throws code "agent_not_installed" when Hermes can't be found. Only
// `platform` and `spawnFn` are read from the options; nothing a caller passes
// reaches the command, the file or the argv.
export async function openHermesModelTerminal({ platform = process.platform, spawnFn = spawn } = {}) {
  // A fresh look, never the 30 s detect cache, so a Hermes installed a moment ago is found.
  const detected = await ADAPTERS.hermes.detect({ refresh: true });
  if (!detected.installed || !detected.path) {
    const error = new Error(HERMES_NOT_INSTALLED_MESSAGE);
    error.code = "agent_not_installed";
    throw error;
  }
  return openCommandInTerminal(detected.path, HERMES_MODEL_ARGS, { name: HERMES_TERMINAL_NAME, platform, spawnFn });
}
```

1. **Decisions this task makes** (the owner or the orchestrator can overturn any of them):

They check the file's folder and `.command` suffix, and only the macOS-only HTTP test checks the `claude-login-<hex>` name, so the new file's `openSignInInTerminal()` test pins the exact file name, content and answers on macOS and Linux alike.

### Task B2: UI: BrainPlanCard, Choose in Hermes, Setup's third card, BrainResult labels, client API and probe

This task builds what the person sees of the plan brains. On OpenClaw's Brain card (Agents page) a new "Your plan" panel, `BrainPlanCard`, offers two ways to give OpenClaw a brain from a plan the person already pays for: **Claude plan** (OpenClaw runs their own signed-in Claude Code) and **ChatGPT plan** (OpenClaw signs in with OpenAI's official "Sign in with ChatGPT", in a small terminal right inside the card). Each plan shows the models the account offers, or a dated fallback list with a "Type a model name" field, the Fable usage-credits note, the models OpenClaw can't use on the plan yet, one security notice with one risk tick, and an Apply button that runs the plan's job on the server and shows its steps and its result. On Hermes's Brain card a "Choose in Hermes" button, with the two honest warning lines next to it, opens Hermes's own model picker in its own Terminal.app window (or hands back the command on Windows and Linux) and then shows what Hermes saved, on Refresh and whenever the window gets focus. Setup's AI brain step shows the same plan card as an OpenClaw-only third card, and the job result (`BrainResult`) names the new modes "Claude plan" and "ChatGPT plan", never "Local".

Why it is built this way, in plain words: everything the card says comes from the server's answers (Tasks B1a, B1b and B1c), which ask the agents through their own commands, so the card never guesses and never holds a sign-in. The sign-in terminal is the same browser terminal and WebSocket as the Sessions page (Task U2), so nothing new talks to the PTY. Every sentence on screen is the spec's, word for word, kept in one pure file (`src/ui/planBrainsShared.ts`) that a Node test checks against the spec text and against the server's own constants, so the card and the server can't drift apart. The parts a test can't reach (the cards in a real browser, every state, and the real sign-in session against Task W1's fake) are covered by a new audit probe with screenshots for the owner.

This task owns the UI side of spec sections 1 to 6 (the in-card sign-in terminal, its reattach, Close and end, and its keyboard way out: Close before the terminal, Ctrl+C inside it; the Claude plan and ChatGPT plan states, lists, notes and Apply; Choose in Hermes; the labels; where the controls go), the client part of section 7 (`src/setupApi.ts`, `src/sessionsApi.ts`), and the spec's Testing "UI probes". Of the Safety items it owns the UI's share: the risk tick (Apply only with it, cleared after each job, spec section 2); Safety 2's "the Hermes launch never creates a PTY session" on the client; and Safety 5's "keeps nothing" as the page sees it (the card stores only a job id, logs nothing, and the probe checks no recording is left after a sign-in). It also covers the UI half of the plan-brains Review Focus items 1 to 5 (contract "Review Focus (plan brains)").

**Depends on:** B1a, B1b, B1c, U2, U3, U4 (all committed before this task starts; Step 1 checks), and this task's four contract amendments written into `00-contract-brains.md` by the orchestrator before dispatch (Step 0; Step 1 checks).

- **Contract amendments (this task's new names and shapes).** The contract wins where a task differs (its first paragraph), and the contract does not yet say these four things, so B2 is not dispatched until they are in it: the orchestrator writes them into `00-contract-brains.md` in Step 0 (the exact text is there), and the worker's Step 1 stops when they are missing. The code below already does all four.
  - A. **Apply waits 55 s, not 20 s.** `PLAN_LIMITS_MS.apply = 55_000` (the brain read's `BRAIN_READ_LIMIT_MS`). Before the job exists, `startOpenclawPlanJob` reads everything again inside the job lock (Task B1b): a fresh OpenClaw detection (`--version`, 5 s, and on a cache miss the two feature `--help` reads, 8 s), then `signInStatus("claude")` (a fresh Claude Code detection, up to 10 s on a cache miss, then `claude auth status`, 10 s) or `models auth list` (15 s), then `resolvePlanModel`'s `models list` (15 s, beside `config get`, 10 s). That is up to about 48 s (13 + 20 + 15), so with 20 s a slow OpenClaw would get "It may or may not have been applied" while the job starts and runs with no remembered id, and the card would never show its steps or its result. No route lists jobs, so the card cannot look for the job afterwards; waiting as long as the server can take is the fix. Starting the sign-in, Cancel, the job reads and the Hermes launch keep 20 s (`PLAN_LIMITS_MS.action`).
  - B. **Setup's class list.** In Setup the root is `className="os-panel os-brain-card os-plan-card"`, where the contract says "Setup adds `os-brain-card`": `.os-brain-card` is only a column layout (`src/ui/brain.css`), and Setup's other two cards get their panel look from `.os-panel` (`BrainOpenRouterCard` and `BrainLocalCard` are `className="os-panel os-brain-card"`). The Agents page keeps `os-plan-card` alone.
  - C. **`PlanSignInTerminal`'s `autoFocus`, Close first, and Ctrl+C.** `PlanSignInTerminal({ sessionId, onEnded, onClose, autoFocus = false }: { sessionId: string; onEnded(): void; onClose(): void; autoFocus?: boolean })`. The card passes `autoFocus` only right after the person pressed "Sign in with ChatGPT", so a page load that finds a waiting sign-in again never takes the keys (P26 focus rule; `SessionTerminal`'s own `autoFocus`). Task U2's `SessionTerminal` keeps Tab and Shift+Tab while it is connected (`tabLeavesTerminal` in `src/ui/terminalShared.ts` frees them only when the terminal is not open), so the panel's Close row comes before the terminal (Tab reaches Close first), and inside the terminal Ctrl+C is the keyboard's way out: it reaches the sign-in program as in any terminal (no app shortcut uses it, U2 Notes 1), the program ends, and the panel closes by itself with the keyboard on the ChatGPT plan heading (Notes 3).
  - D. **Where the plan card and Choose in Hermes show.** `BrainPlanCard` (Agents page and Setup) and `ChooseInHermes` show only where `useSessionsList().available` is true (local mode, where their routes exist; elsewhere the routes answer 404 `not_available`, which has no sentence), and Setup's third card only when `showPlanCard` is true, `available` is true and the OpenClaw line is installed. On the Agents page both show once the last good brain answer said the agent is installed (`installed !== false`, so Hermes not installed gets no "Choose in Hermes"), and they sit after the Brain section's states, not inside them, so a failed brain read or Retry never unmounts them (P26: a typed model name, a job's result or an open sign-in is never thrown away). When the read failed they show under its banner.

// Plan brains, the UI's side (Task B2; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-plan-brains-design.md): the words and
// pure rules of src/ui/planBrainsShared.ts, the plan mode and step labels of src/ui/brainShared.ts, the new client
// calls of src/setupApi.ts (driven with a fake fetch and a fake sessionStorage), and the client words that mirror the
// server's own: server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plan-rules.js is pure and is imported; the two version sentences of
// server/runtime/setup/openclaw-version.js are read as text, so this file loads nothing that touches the disk. The
// sign-in terminal's name is the setup session's own title (sessionTitle in src/ui/sessionsShared.ts, Task B1a).
// Nothing here talks to a server or starts anything; the cards themselves are checked by the plan-brains probe of
// the UI audit. setupApi.ts imports its neighbours without a file extension (the Vite way), which Node does not
// follow by itself, so this file first teaches Node that one rule (a resolve hook that adds .ts), as
// test/sessions-api.test.js does.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { registerHooks } from "node:module";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

registerHooks({
  resolve(specifier, context, nextResolve) {
    if (/^\.\.?\//.test(specifier) && !/\.[a-z]+$/.test(specifier) && context.parentURL) {
      for (const extension of [".ts", ".tsx"]) {
        const url = new URL(specifier + extension, context.parentURL);
        if (existsSync(fileURLToPath(url))) return { url: url.href, shortCircuit: true };
      }
    }
    return nextResolve(specifier, context);
  }
});

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const read = (relative) => readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, relative), "utf8");

});
const listOf = (source, models) => ({ source, asOf: source === "fallback" ? "2026-10-15" : null, models });
const model = (id, available = true) => ({ id, name: id, note: null, available });

test("every sentence the cards show is the spec's, word for word, in straight quotes and with no em dash", () => {
  const sentences = [
    shared.OPENCLAW_SECURITY_NOTICE,
    shared.PLAN_LABEL.claude,
    shared.PLAN_LABEL.chatgpt,
    shared.PLAN_NOTE.claude,
    shared.PLAN_NOTE.chatgpt,
    ...Object.values(shared.CLAUDE_PLAN_WORDS),
    ...Object.values(shared.CHATGPT_PLAN_WORDS),
    shared.FALLBACK_LIST_NOTE,
    shared.NOT_ON_PLAN_NOTE,
    shared.TYPED_MODEL_LABEL,
    shared.INVALID_PLAN_MODEL,
    ...shared.HERMES_PICKER_LINES,
    ...Object.values(shared.HERMES_TERMINAL_WORDS)
  ];
  assert.equal(sentences.length, 22);
  for (const sentence of sentences) {
    assert.ok(SPEC.includes(sentence), `the spec says this, word for word: ${sentence}`);
    assert.doesNotMatch(sentence, /\u2014/, "no em dash");
    assert.doesNotMatch(sentence, /[\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]/, "straight quotes, as in the spec");
  }
  assert.equal(shared.HERMES_PICKER_LINES.length, 2, "two quiet lines next to Choose in Hermes");
  assert.ok(SPEC.indexOf(shared.HERMES_PICKER_LINES[0]) < SPEC.indexOf(shared.HERMES_PICKER_LINES[1]), "in the spec's order");
  assert.deepEqual(shared.PLAN_LABEL, { claude: "Claude plan", chatgpt: "ChatGPT plan" });
  assert.equal(shared.TYPED_MODEL_LABEL, "Type a model name");
  assert.equal(shared.NOT_ON_PLAN_NOTE, "Not available on your plan in this OpenClaw yet");
  // The terminal's accessible name adds no words: it is the setup session's own title (contract copy, Task B1a).
  const setupSession = { kind: "setup", agentId: "openclaw", agentLabel: "OpenClaw", folderName: "someone", folderShown: false };
  assert.equal(shared.SIGNIN_TERMINAL_LABEL, sessions.sessionTitle(setupSession));
  assert.equal(shared.SIGNIN_TERMINAL_LABEL, "OpenClaw · ChatGPT sign-in");
});
