### Task E3: Plan brains live checks S-B1 to S-B4 on the owner's Mac (orchestrator, ask first each time)

Every test of Tasks B1a, B1b, B1c and B2 runs against fakes, and those fakes were written from OpenClaw's docs and its 2026.9.6 help text. Nobody has yet run the ChatGPT sign-in, `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice anthropic-cli` or the new `models` reads on a real account. This task runs them once on the owner's Mac with his real OpenClaw, Hermes and Claude Code, writes down what the real programs print, and turns every place where a fake differs into a small follow-up task that fixes B1b's fakes (and its parsers, where Agent OS reads that part) before the plan brains work is called done. It builds no product code.

These checks change agent settings and run an installer (an OpenClaw update, a ChatGPT sign-in, OpenClaw's first onboard, two model changes, Hermes's own picker), which Task E2's rule forbids. So they run as their own task with their own rule. The orchestrator runs it, never a worker. Each check is asked first in chat, saying what it changes, what it may cost and what cannot be undone. Before each check the current model is recorded with `readAgentModel`, and afterwards the orchestrator offers to put that model back with the same command the check used. Nothing reads a credential file, and no raw output of an agent's sign-in, auth or status command is ever shown, logged or kept.

What keeps that true is a set of small git-ignored tools in `.superpowers/plan-brains-live/`:
- they run each fixed read through Agent OS's own `runCommand` and keep its output in memory;
- they print only its shape (field names, types, safe words such as `siwc`, a sharing word or a model ref), counts, and Agent OS's own parsed answer;
- a self-test first proves that a token, an e-mail address, a person's name (also inside a profile id or as a key) and a file path never get through;
- a dry run against B1b's fake OpenClaw and fake Claude Code proves it again before the first real command, and refuses to run if detection would find a real agent;
- B1a's file-access spy runs around every read mode of `live-read.mjs`.

**Owns:** spec "Live checks on the owner's Mac" (S-B1, S-B2, S-B3, S-B4, in the spec's order, with one optional change of order only on the owner's explicit OK, Step 8) and its last "Done when" item ("The live checks S-B1 to S-B4 have run on the owner's Mac in Task E3 (or the owner deferred them).").
- **Safety items:** none as a test, since each has its test in B1a, B1b or B1c. Against the real programs, the checks re-confirm only what they can see: Safety 1 for the read modes (the spy runs inside `live-read.mjs`), Safety 2 and 3 for the sign-in session's argv (a `ps` look while it runs, Step 9) and for the recorded runs (Step 15), and Safety 5 (the sign-in session kept nothing, Step 9). The spike server's own flows (the sign-in session, both Applies, the readiness reads and the Hermes launch) run without a spy; their Safety 1 tests are B1a's, B1b's and B1c's (Notes, item 10).
- **Main-spec harness rules:** H1 (the owner's own binaries, HOME and config), H2 (the spike server gets the desktop app's environment, not this terminal's) and H7 (an update is never undone by Agent OS: no downgrade).

**What the owner does himself**, beyond answering each question in chat (about 45 minutes in all, mostly waiting for the update, the sign-in and two hello checks). Three windows are involved: **the pane** (Claude's browser pane, where the orchestrator drives the throwaway Agent OS: it presses every button there except the risk tick, unless he asks it to), **his own browser** (the same throwaway Agent OS, opened with its Open link) and **his own Terminal.app**.
- Step 6: leaves his installed Agent OS app's Setup alone until Step 15 (it works on the same agents).
- Step 7: answers in chat when the orchestrator reads him Setup's own confirm question for the OpenClaw update; the orchestrator presses its confirm button in the pane only after his yes.
- Step 8 (optional): in his own browser, opens the Open link and signs in to ChatGPT through the card with token sharing left off. If ChatGPT shows no sharing choice, he cancels there, presses "Close" on the card's terminal panel and says so. If he also says yes to the extra Apply (it changes the approved order), he picks the model in chat and ticks the risk box as below.
- Step 9: in his own browser, opens the Open link (if that tab is not still open), goes to Agents, OpenClaw, "Your plan", presses "Sign in with ChatGPT", opens the link the small terminal shows, approves in ChatGPT and allows token sharing, finishes in that terminal if it asks, and says no if it offers to change OpenClaw's default model. Then he tells the orchestrator when the panel closed, and describes in his own words (never the code) what the terminal did, whether the link wrapped over several lines and whether clicking it still opened it.
- Steps 8, 11 and 12: picks the model for each Apply from the options in chat (Fable is not offered: it uses usage credits). Before each Apply he ticks OpenClaw's risk box in the Agent OS page **in the pane**, or tells the orchestrator to tick it there after reading it. A tick in his own browser does not count: the tick belongs to one page, and the Apply is pressed in the pane.
- Step 12: optionally copies `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` himself as a backup before OpenClaw's first onboard (the orchestrator never opens that folder). Only if Step 12 finds Claude Code signed out or on an API key: signs in himself with `claude auth login` in his own Terminal, then says so.
- Step 13: answers which model OpenClaw keeps. Optionally, later, removes the ChatGPT sign-in himself with `openclaw models auth logout` in his own Terminal.
- Step 14: confirms that a Terminal window opened with Hermes's picker and says whether Terminal.app or macOS asked anything first; before he picks, opens Agents, then Hermes in his own browser's Agent OS tab; picks a model in Hermes's picker himself; then clicks back into his own browser's Agent OS tab and says whether it already shows the new model. If the card does not change, he may be asked to run `echo ${HERMES_HOME:+set}` in his Terminal and say what it printed. Later, if he wants his old Hermes model back, he picks it again the same way. Last, he closes Hermes's Terminal window(s) before Step 15.
- Step 17: reads the results block before it goes into the spec, says whether any fake may stay as it is (Step 16), and decides any finding that would change what the spec promises (Notes, item 7).

Depends on: E2 (its closing ledger line, Interfaces), and through it E1, B1a, B1b, B1c and B2, all committed.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes, at HEAD (checked in the code at `a6c9f4a`):
  - `server/runtime/safety.js`: `runCommand(command, args = [], timeout = 5000, options = {})` resolves to `{ ok, stdout, stderr, code, signal, aborted }`. It uses `execFile` (no shell), keeps the output in memory and, without `options.cwd`, runs in the caller's working folder. `withSiblingNodePath` puts a managed-Node binary's own folder first on `PATH`. A timeout is `{ ok: false, code: 0, signal: "SIGTERM" }`; exit 2 is `{ ok: false, code: 2, signal: null }`.
  - `which()` searches, in this order: `HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS`; `PATH`; the HOME folders (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`, `~/.volta/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/share/pnpm`, `~/.agent-os/node/bin`); the newest nvm bin; then always `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/bin`.
  - `server/runtime/agents/detect.js`: `resolveBinary(command, fallbackPaths = [])` (`which()`, then the first existing fallback; it runs nothing), `openclawFallbackPaths()` and `claudeFallbackPaths()`.
  - `server/runtime/agents/index.js`: `ADAPTERS`. `ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true })`, `ADAPTERS.claude.detect({ refresh: true })` and `ADAPTERS.hermes.detect({ refresh: true })` find the binary with `resolveBinary`, then run its `--version` and `--help` checks, and answer `{ installed, path, version, versionFull, features }`, where `version` is the first line of `--version`.
  - `server/runtime/setup/models.js`:
    - `MODEL_ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._:/@~][A-Za-z0-9._:/@~-]{0,119}$/`, what Agent OS lets into a command line. OpenClaw primaries that Agent OS itself writes, such as `openrouter/@preset/<slug>` (`openclawModelRef` plus the preset path in `jobs.js`'s `setOpenclawModel`), match it. `OPENCLAW_MODEL_PATTERN` in `server/runtime/agents/openclaw.js` (line 243) allows neither `@` nor `~`, so this task never uses it;
    - `readAgentModel(agentId, detected)` (OpenClaw's primary splits at the first `/` into `provider` and `model`, so `openrouter/@preset/x` reads back whole), `parseJsonOutput(stdout)` and `parseConfigText(stdout)`.
  - Setup's OpenClaw update (`server/runtime/setup/recipes.js` and `plan.js`, `src/ui/setupGroupShared.ts`):
    - it is the plan step `openclaw-update` (action `update`, not chosen by default), which runs `<detected openclaw> update --json` through the run manager;
    - in Setup's plan step ("Keep, update or install each agent"), the "Always-on agents" group's button reads "Update OpenClaw" when only that update is chosen (`groupAction`), and Setup confirms in its own dialog before anything runs;
    - an update needs no risk tick (only an install does), and Setup never updates Hermes (`NO_UPDATE_STEP`).
  - `server/runtime/local-session.js`: `loginLine` prints `Agent OS is running. Open: http://<host>:<port>/?launch=<token>` once at start in local mode (the token stays valid for the server's whole life), and `server/index.js` prints `AGENT_OS_READY:<port>`. The server finds `dist` and its `.env` from its own file's folder, not from its working folder.
  - `GET /api/runs?limit=<n>` answers `{ runs }` (at most 1000). Each run's meta carries `commandPreview`: the command path, then the arguments, each JSON-quoted when it holds a space (`quoteArg`), with HOME shown as `~`.
  - `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`: the packaged server starts with `working_dir: home_dir()` (`resolve_launch`, line 119), `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` set to the PATH the app was started with, and `PATH` from `server_path_env()`: `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.agent-os/node/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`, `~/.volta/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` and `~/.bun/bin` (those that exist), ahead of the PATH the app was started with.

  - The log `.superpowers/sp3-plan-brains-checks.md`; the follow-up briefs `task-E3-F<n>-brief.md`; the spec's `### Results (Task E3, <date>)` block.
  - The ledger lines `Task E3-F<n>: ...` and one closing line `Task E3: complete (run: <checks>; deferred by the owner: <checks or none>; follow-ups <E3-F1 to E3-F<n> | none>, commits <hashes>)`.

```js
check("free text gives back only a line count and a secret count", () => {

check("model list: keys, names and flags show; numbers are types only", () => {

check("models config: refs and runtime ids show, and the refs collapse for a structural diff", () => {
  const config = {
    "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } },
    "anthropic/*": { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } },
    "openai/gpt-6-sol": { agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }, alias: PERSON }
  };

check("an object key that is an e-mail address or a token is hidden too", () => {
  const shape = shapeOf({ [EMAIL]: { [TOKEN]: true } }, { shown: CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS });
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(shape).sort(), ["(top)", "<hidden key>", "<hidden key> > <hidden key>"]);
  assert.equal(JSON.stringify(shape).includes("someone"), false);
});

check("the diff names fields only one side has, type changes and different method words", () => {
  const live = shapeOf([{ provider: "openai", authMethod: "siwc", sharing: "full" }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS });
  const fake = shapeOf([{ provider: "openai", method: "siwc", tokenSharing: true }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS });
  const diff = diffShapes(live, fake, { enumKeys: ["provider", "method"] });
  assert.deepEqual(diff.onlyLive, ["[] > authMethod", "[] > sharing"]);
  assert.deepEqual(diff.onlyFake, ["[] > method", "[] > tokenSharing"]);
  assert.deepEqual(diff.typeMismatch, []);
  assert.equal(diff.same, false);
  assert.equal(diffShapes(fake, fake, { enumKeys: ["method"] }).same, true);
  const words = diffShapes(shapeOf([{ method: "oauth" }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }), shapeOf([{ method: "siwc" }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }), { enumKeys: ["method"] });
  assert.deepEqual(words.valueMismatch, [{ path: "[] > method", live: ["oauth"], fake: ["siwc"] }]);
  const types = diffShapes(shapeOf([{ tokenSharing: "yes" }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }), shapeOf([{ tokenSharing: true }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }));
  assert.deepEqual(types.typeMismatch, [{ path: "[] > tokenSharing", live: ["string"], fake: ["boolean"] }]);
});

check("with exactValues, two sign-ins that differ only in a list's words are told apart", () => {
  const noSharing = shapeOf([{ provider: "openai", method: "siwc", scopes: ["openid"] }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS });
  const sharing = shapeOf([{ provider: "openai", method: "siwc", scopes: ["openid", "model.request"] }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS });
  assert.equal(diffShapes(noSharing, sharing, { enumKeys: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }).same, true);
  const exact = diffShapes(noSharing, sharing, { enumKeys: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS, exactValues: true });
  assert.equal(exact.same, false);
  assert.deepEqual(exact.valueMismatch, [{ path: "[] > scopes > []", live: ["openid"], fake: ["openid", "model.request"] }]);
  const flags = diffShapes(shapeOf([{ tokenSharing: false }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }), shapeOf([{ tokenSharing: true }], { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }), { enumKeys: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS, exactValues: true });
  assert.deepEqual(flags.valueMismatch, [{ path: "[] > tokenSharing", live: [false], fake: [true] }]);
});

check("a model ref read back from OpenClaw round-trips, even one that looks like a token", () => {

    assert.equal(restorableRef(bad, MODEL_ID_PATTERN_COPY), null, String(bad).slice(0, 12));
  }
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the shape module.** Create `.superpowers/plan-brains-live/shape.mjs`:

```js
// Task E3 (git-ignored, never committed): shape-only views of agent CLI output for the plan
// brains live checks. Pure: no imports, no I/O. A string value is shown only when its key is on
// the read's list AND it does not look like a token, an e-mail address or a file path; everything
// else is reduced to its type and a reason, so nothing private reaches the terminal, the log or
// the chat. A profile id shows only its provider part, and an object key with a space is hidden,
// because people choose both and may put their name there.

export const AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS = Object.freeze([
  "method",
  "type",
  "provider",
  "mode",
  "status",
  "kind",
  "profileId",
  "source",
  "state",
  "tokenSharing",
  "sharing",
  "scope",
  "scopes",
  "permissions",
  "capabilities",
  "access",
  "plan",
  "planType"
]);
export const MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS = Object.freeze(["key", "id", "name", "provider", "api", "input", "runtime", "status", "tags", "available", "auth", "reason"]);
export const CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS = Object.freeze(["id", "agentRuntime", "runtime", "primary", "model"]);
export const ROOT_SHOWN = Object.freeze([""]);
export const HIDDEN_KEY = "<hidden key>";

const SECRET_PREFIX = /^(sk-|sk_|rk_|pk_|eyJ|ghp_|gho_|ghs_|ghu_|xox[abprs]-|AKIA|AIza|ya29\.)/;
const SECRET_MARK = /oat01|-ant-api|-ant-oat/i;
const EMAIL = /[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/;
const PATH_LIKE = /^(\/|~|[A-Za-z]:\\)|\/(Users|home|private|var|tmp)\//;
const SAFE_TEXT = /^[A-Za-z0-9 ._:/()+,*#@=-]{1,80}$/;
const SAFE_KEY = /^[A-Za-z0-9._:/()+*@=-]{1,100}$/;
const PROFILE_KEY = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}:[^/]+$/;
const PROFILE_ID_WORDS = new Set(["default", "manual", "claude-cli"]);
const byCodePoint = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);

export function looksSecret(text) {
  const value = String(text ?? "");
  if (SECRET_PREFIX.test(value) || SECRET_MARK.test(value)) return true;
  if (/^[A-Fa-f0-9]{32,}$/.test(value)) return true;
  return value.length >= 32 && /^[A-Za-z0-9_\-+/=.]+$/.test(value) && /[A-Z]/.test(value) && /[a-z]/.test(value) && /\d/.test(value);
}

// "openai:default" stays; "openai:work" or "openai:<a name>" becomes "openai:<id>"; anything
// without a plain provider part becomes "<id>".
export function profileIdShown(text) {
  const value = String(text ?? "");
  const colon = value.indexOf(":");
  const provider = colon > 0 ? value.slice(0, colon) : "";
  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$/.test(provider)) return "<id>";
  return PROFILE_ID_WORDS.has(value.slice(colon + 1)) ? value : `${provider}:<id>`;
}

// A model ref read back through `config get` (OpenClaw's primary), printed as it is so it can be
// passed to restore-openclaw: it must contain a slash, match `pattern` (models.js's
// MODEL_ID_PATTERN, what Agent OS lets into a command line) and carry no token marker. Else null.
export function restorableRef(value, pattern) {
  if (typeof value !== "string") return null;
  if (!value.includes("/") || !pattern.test(value) || SECRET_PREFIX.test(value) || SECRET_MARK.test(value)) return null;
  return value;
}

function safeKey(key) {
  const text = String(key);
  if (looksSecret(text) || EMAIL.test(text) || !SAFE_KEY.test(text)) return HIDDEN_KEY;
  return PROFILE_KEY.test(text) ? profileIdShown(text) : text;
}

function hiddenReason(key, value, shown) {
  if (looksSecret(value)) return "secret-like";
  if (EMAIL.test(value)) return "email-like";
  if (PATH_LIKE.test(value)) return "path";
  if (!shown.has(key)) return "not-shown";
  if (!SAFE_TEXT.test(value)) return "unusual";
  return null;
}

// Every path in the value ("models > [] > key"), with its types, how often it was seen, array
// lengths, up to six shown examples and, for strings that are not shown, why not.
export function shapeOf(value, { shown = [] } = {}) {
  const shownKeys = new Set(shown);
  const paths = new Map();
  const visit = (node, segments, key) => {
    const where = segments.length ? segments.join(" > ") : "(top)";
    let entry = paths.get(where);
    if (!entry) {
      entry = { types: new Set(), count: 0, lengths: new Set(), examples: [], hidden: {} };
      paths.set(where, entry);
    }
    entry.count += 1;
    if (node === null || node === undefined) {
      entry.types.add("null");
    } else if (Array.isArray(node)) {
      entry.types.add("array");
      entry.lengths.add(node.length);
      for (const item of node) visit(item, [...segments, "[]"], key);
    } else if (typeof node === "object") {
      entry.types.add("object");
      for (const [childKey, child] of Object.entries(node)) visit(child, [...segments, safeKey(childKey)], childKey);
    } else if (typeof node === "boolean") {
      entry.types.add("boolean");
      if (!entry.examples.includes(node)) entry.examples.push(node);
    } else if (typeof node === "string") {
      entry.types.add("string");
      const reason = hiddenReason(key, node, shownKeys);
      const example = key === "profileId" ? profileIdShown(node) : node;
      if (reason) entry.hidden[reason] = (entry.hidden[reason] ?? 0) + 1;
      else if (entry.examples.length < 6 && !entry.examples.includes(example)) entry.examples.push(example);
    } else {
      entry.types.add(typeof node);
    }
  };
  visit(value, [], "");
  const out = {};
  for (const where of [...paths.keys()].sort(byCodePoint)) {
    const entry = paths.get(where);
    out[where] = {
      types: [...entry.types].sort(byCodePoint),
      count: entry.count,
      ...(entry.lengths.size ? { lengths: [...entry.lengths].sort((a, b) => a - b) } : {}),
      ...(entry.examples.length ? { examples: entry.examples } : {}),
      ...(Object.keys(entry.hidden).length ? { hidden: entry.hidden } : {})
    };
  }
  return out;
}

// Where in the value a string (or an object key) looks like a token, with a count. Never the value.
export function secretPaths(value) {
  const found = {};
  const note = (where) => {
    found[where] = (found[where] ?? 0) + 1;
  };
  const visit = (node, segments) => {
    if (typeof node === "string") {
      if (looksSecret(node)) note(segments.join(" > ") || "(top)");
    } else if (Array.isArray(node)) {
      for (const item of node) visit(item, [...segments, "[]"]);
    } else if (node && typeof node === "object") {
      for (const [key, child] of Object.entries(node)) {
        if (looksSecret(key)) note([...segments, HIDDEN_KEY].join(" > "));
        visit(child, [...segments, safeKey(key)]);
      }
    }
  };
  visit(value, []);
  return found;
}

// Free text (stdout, stderr, a file) comes back as two numbers only.
export function textStats(text) {
  const value = String(text ?? "");
  return {
    lines: value === "" ? 0 : value.split(/\r?\n/).length,
    secretLike: value.split(/[^A-Za-z0-9_\-+/=.]+/).filter((piece) => piece && looksSecret(piece)).length
  };
}

function mergeEntry(into, entry) {
  const types = [...new Set([...(into?.types ?? []), ...entry.types])].sort(byCodePoint);
  const lengths = [...new Set([...(into?.lengths ?? []), ...(entry.lengths ?? [])])].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const examples = [...new Set([...(into?.examples ?? []), ...(entry.examples ?? [])])].slice(0, 6);
  const hidden = { ...(into?.hidden ?? {}) };
  for (const [reason, n] of Object.entries(entry.hidden ?? {})) hidden[reason] = (hidden[reason] ?? 0) + n;
  return {
    types,
    count: (into?.count ?? 0) + entry.count,
    ...(lengths.length ? { lengths } : {}),
    ...(examples.length ? { examples } : {}),
    ...(Object.keys(hidden).length ? { hidden } : {})
  };
}

// The models config is keyed by model refs, which differ between the owner's OpenClaw and the
// fake; this folds every first-level key into "<ref>" so only the structure is compared.
export function collapseFirstSegment(shape, label = "<ref>") {
  const merged = {};
  for (const [where, entry] of Object.entries(shape)) {
    const key = where === "(top)" ? where : [label, ...where.split(" > ").slice(1)].join(" > ");
    merged[key] = mergeEntry(merged[key], entry);
  }
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(merged).sort(([a], [b]) => byCodePoint(a, b)));
}

// The field a path ends in, skipping list steps ("[] > scopes > []" is "scopes").
const fieldOf = (where) => where.split(" > ").filter((segment) => segment !== "[]").pop();
const sameValues = (a, b) => a.length === b.length && a.every((value) => b.includes(value));

// First against second (live against fake, or two live reads): paths only one side has, paths
// whose types differ, and, for the fields named in enumKeys (method words, runtime ids, sharing
// words), shown values with nothing in common, or, with exactValues, shown values that differ at all.
export function diffShapes(live, fake, { enumKeys = [], exactValues = false } = {}) {
  const enums = new Set(enumKeys);
  const livePaths = Object.keys(live);
  const onlyLive = livePaths.filter((where) => !Object.hasOwn(fake, where));
  const onlyFake = Object.keys(fake).filter((where) => !Object.hasOwn(live, where));
  const both = livePaths.filter((where) => Object.hasOwn(fake, where));
  const typeMismatch = both
    .filter((where) => live[where].types.join("|") !== fake[where].types.join("|"))
    .map((where) => ({ path: where, live: live[where].types, fake: fake[where].types }));
  const valueMismatch = both
    .filter((where) => enums.has(fieldOf(where)))
    .filter((where) => {
      const a = live[where].examples ?? [];
      const b = fake[where].examples ?? [];
      if (exactValues) return !sameValues(a, b);
      return a.length > 0 && b.length > 0 && !a.some((value) => b.includes(value));
    })
    .map((where) => ({ path: where, live: live[where].examples ?? [], fake: fake[where].examples ?? [] }));
  return {
    same: !onlyLive.length && !onlyFake.length && !typeMismatch.length && !valueMismatch.length,
    onlyLive,
    onlyFake,
    typeMismatch,
    valueMismatch
  };
}

// One value built from a shape: the live field names with fake values only (shown words stay,
// a hidden e-mail becomes someone@example.com, a hidden token becomes `secret`, anything else
// hidden becomes "fake"; a list of shown words keeps all of them). A follow-up task uses it as a
// fake's default answer or knob value.
export function synthFrom(shape, base = "(top)", { secret = "SECRET-fake-0000" } = {}) {
  const entry = shape[base];
  if (!entry) return null;
  const type = entry.types.find((t) => t !== "null") ?? "null";
  const childPrefix = base === "(top)" ? "" : `${base} > `;
  if (type === "object") {
    const out = {};
    for (const where of Object.keys(shape)) {
      if (where === "(top)" || where === base || !where.startsWith(childPrefix)) continue;
      const rest = where.slice(childPrefix.length);
      if (rest.includes(" > ")) continue;
      out[rest] = synthFrom(shape, where, { secret });
    }
    return out;
  }
  if (type === "array") {
    const item = `${childPrefix}[]`;
    if (!Object.hasOwn(shape, item)) return [];
    const words = shape[item];
    if (words.examples?.length && words.types.every((t) => t === "string" || t === "boolean")) return [...words.examples];
    return [synthFrom(shape, item, { secret })];
  }
  if (type === "boolean") return entry.examples?.[0] ?? true;
  if (type === "number") return 0;
  if (type === "string") {
    if (entry.examples?.length) return entry.examples[0];
    if (entry.hidden?.["email-like"]) return "someone@example.com";
    if (entry.hidden?.["secret-like"]) return secret;
    return "fake";
  }
  return null;
}
```

```js
// Task E3 (git-ignored, never committed): live reads of the owner's real OpenClaw, Hermes and
// Claude Code for the plan brains live checks (spec "Live checks on the owner's Mac"). Run it only
// through run.sh, and only after the owner said yes in chat to the check it serves.
// Each mode runs fixed commands through Agent OS's own runCommand (output kept in memory) and
// prints only shapes, counts and Agent OS's own parsed answers. `restore-openclaw` is the one mode
// that changes anything (`openclaw models set <ref>`). A file-access spy runs around every mode:
// if Agent OS code touched ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, ~/.openclaw or ~/.hermes (other than
// brain.js's existence check of ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json), the run fails. Files inside this
// worktree are Agent OS's own: the worktree sits under the main checkout's .claude/worktrees/, so
// FORBIDDEN_PATH would match them too.
import { promises as fsp } from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { claudeFallbackPaths, openclawFallbackPaths, resolveBinary } from "../../server/runtime/agents/detect.js";
import { ADAPTERS } from "../../server/runtime/agents/index.js";
import { runCommand } from "../../server/runtime/safety.js";
import { MODEL_ID_PATTERN, parseConfigText, parseJsonOutput, readAgentModel } from "../../server/runtime/setup/models.js";
import { openclawVersionInfo } from "../../server/runtime/setup/openclaw-version.js";
import {
  PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS,
  PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS,
  chatgptSignIn,
  claudeCliPinned,
  claudePlanReadiness,
  hasClaudeCliPin,
  parseAuthRows,
  planModelRows,
  readinessOf
} from "../../server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plan-rules.js";
import { readOpenclawModelsConfig, readOpenclawPlans, readPlanModels } from "../../server/runtime/setup/openclaw-plans.js";
import { signInStatus } from "../../server/runtime/setup/signin.js";
import { FORBIDDEN_PATH, allowedAgentFile, spyOnFileAccess } from "../../test/helpers/plan-brains-safety.js";
import { AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS, CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS, MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS, ROOT_SHOWN, looksSecret, restorableRef, secretPaths, shapeOf, textStats } from "./shape.mjs";

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(HERE, "..", "..");
const SHAPES_FILE = path.join(HERE, "live-shapes.json");
const LIVE_ROOT = "/private/tmp/sp3-brains-live";
const CONFIG_READ_MS = 10 * 1000; // models.js's limit for `config get`
const SET_MODEL_MS = 60 * 1000; // jobs.js's limit for a configure run
const HOME = os.homedir();
const PROVIDER_PLAN = Object.freeze({ anthropic: "claude", openai: "chatgpt" });
const SAVED_MODES = new Set(["models", "auth", "status", "models-config", "primary"]);
// Where detection looks for each agent, without running it (detect() runs --version and --help).
const FIND = Object.freeze({
  openclaw: () => resolveBinary("openclaw", openclawFallbackPaths()),
  claude: () => resolveBinary("claude", claudeFallbackPaths())
});

const tidy = (text) => String(text ?? "").split(HOME).join("~");
const exitOf = (result) => ({ ok: result.ok, code: result.code, signal: result.signal });
const jsonKind = (value) => (value === null ? "unreadable" : Array.isArray(value) ? "array" : typeof value);
const isPlainObject = (value) => Boolean(value) && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value);
const runtimeOf = (entry) => (isPlainObject(entry?.agentRuntime) ? entry.agentRuntime.id ?? null : entry?.agentRuntime ?? null);

// A single value that is safe to print (a method word, a version line), else a placeholder that
// says only how long it was.
function word(value) {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
  const text = String(value);
  if (looksSecret(text) || /[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/.test(text) || !/^[A-Za-z0-9 ._:/()+*@=-]{1,120}$/.test(text)) {
    return `<hidden, ${text.length} characters>`;
  }
  return text;
}

// A model ref read back from OpenClaw is printed as it is (so restore-openclaw can take it back),
// anything else goes through word().
const refOrWord = (value) => restorableRef(value, MODEL_ID_PATTERN) ?? word(value);

// With --expect-root (the dry run), every agent a mode may run must be the fake inside that
// folder. This looks only at where detection would find it, and runs nothing.
async function refuseOutside(ctx, agentIds) {
  if (!ctx.expectRoot) return;
  for (const agentId of agentIds) {
    const found = await FIND[agentId]();
    if (found && !found.startsWith(`${ctx.expectRoot}${path.sep}`)) {
      throw new Error(`Refused: ${agentId} would be found at ${tidy(found)}, outside ${tidy(ctx.expectRoot)}.`);
    }
  }
}

async function findOpenclaw(ctx) {
  await refuseOutside(ctx, ["openclaw"]);
  const detected = await ADAPTERS.openclaw.detect({ refresh: true });
  if (!detected.installed) throw new Error("OpenClaw isn't installed, or Agent OS can't find it.");
  if (ctx.expectRoot && !detected.path.startsWith(`${ctx.expectRoot}${path.sep}`)) {
    throw new Error(`Refused: OpenClaw was found at ${tidy(detected.path)}, outside ${tidy(ctx.expectRoot)}.`);
  }
  return detected;
}

function throwawayAgentOsHome() {
  const home = path.resolve(process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME || "");
  if (!home.startsWith(`${LIVE_ROOT}${path.sep}`)) throw new Error(`This mode reads only a throwaway Agent OS folder inside ${LIVE_ROOT}.`);
  return home;
}

const MODES = {
  async version(ctx) {
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    return { path: tidy(detected.path), versionLine: word(detected.version), gate: openclawVersionInfo(detected) };
  },

  async model(ctx, agentId) {
    if (agentId !== "openclaw" && agentId !== "hermes") throw new Error("model takes openclaw or hermes.");
    const detected = agentId === "openclaw" ? await findOpenclaw(ctx) : await ADAPTERS.hermes.detect({ refresh: true });
    const info = await readAgentModel(agentId, detected);
    const answer = {
      agentId,
      installed: info.installed,
      provider: word(info.provider),
      providerLabel: word(info.providerLabel),
      model: word(info.model),
      known: info.known !== false,
      ...(Object.hasOwn(info, "plan") ? { plan: info.plan } : {}),
      restoreRef: info.model ? refOrWord(info.provider ? `${info.provider}/${info.model}` : info.model) : null
    };
    if (agentId === "openclaw") {
      const exec = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "tools.exec.mode"], CONFIG_READ_MS);
      answer.execMode = exec.ok ? word(parseConfigText(exec.stdout)) : { failed: exitOf(exec) };
    }
    return answer;
  },

  async models(ctx, provider) {
    const plan = Object.hasOwn(PROVIDER_PLAN, provider ?? "") ? PROVIDER_PLAN[provider] : null;
    if (!plan) throw new Error("models takes anthropic or openai.");
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "list", "--provider", provider, "--json"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const value = parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
    const rows = planModelRows(value, plan);
    const served = await readPlanModels(plan, { detected });
    return {
      command: `openclaw models list --provider ${provider} --json`,
      exit: exitOf(result),
      stdout: textStats(result.stdout),
      stderr: textStats(result.stderr),
      json: jsonKind(value),
      shape: shapeOf(value, { shown: MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS }),
      secretPaths: secretPaths(value),
      parsed: rows === null ? null : { count: rows.length, ids: rows.slice(0, 40).map((row) => word(row.id)) },
      served: {
        source: served.source,
        asOf: served.asOf,
        count: served.models.length,
        notAvailable: served.models.filter((model) => !model.available).map((model) => word(model.id)),
        withNote: served.models.filter((model) => model.note).map((model) => word(model.id))
      }
    };
  },

  async auth(ctx) {
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "auth", "list", "--provider", "openai", "--json"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const value = parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
    const rows = parseAuthRows(value);
    return {
      command: "openclaw models auth list --provider openai --json",
      exit: exitOf(result),
      stdout: textStats(result.stdout),
      stderr: textStats(result.stderr),
      json: jsonKind(value),
      shape: shapeOf(value, { shown: AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS }),
      secretPaths: secretPaths(value),
      parsed: rows === null ? null : rows.map((row) => ({ method: word(row.method), sharing: row.sharing })),
      signIn: chatgptSignIn(rows)
    };
  },

  async status(ctx) {
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "status", "--check", "--plain"], PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS);
    return {
      command: "openclaw models status --check --plain",
      exit: exitOf(result),
      readiness: readinessOf(result),
      stdout: textStats(result.stdout),
      stderr: textStats(result.stderr)
    };
  },

  async "models-config"(ctx) {
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "agents.defaults.models", "--json"], CONFIG_READ_MS);
    const value = parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
    const config = isPlainObject(value) ? value : null;
    const entries = config ? Object.entries(config) : [];
    const reader = await readOpenclawModelsConfig(detected);
    return {
      command: "openclaw config get agents.defaults.models --json",
      exit: exitOf(result),
      stdout: textStats(result.stdout),
      json: jsonKind(value),
      shape: shapeOf(value, { shown: CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS }),
      secretPaths: secretPaths(value),
      hasClaudeCliPin: config ? hasClaudeCliPin(config) : false,
      pinnedToClaudeCli: entries.filter(([, entry]) => runtimeOf(entry) === "claude-cli").map(([ref]) => word(ref)),
      wildcard: config && Object.hasOwn(config, "anthropic/*") ? word(runtimeOf(config["anthropic/*"]) ?? "an entry with no runtime") : null,
      otherRuntimes: entries
        .filter(([, entry]) => runtimeOf(entry) && runtimeOf(entry) !== "claude-cli")
        .map(([ref, entry]) => `${word(ref)} -> ${word(runtimeOf(entry))}`),
      fallbackIdsPinned: config ? PLAN_FALLBACK_MODELS.claude.filter((id) => claudeCliPinned(config, id)) : [],
      readerAgrees: (reader === null) === (config === null)
    };
  },

  async primary(ctx) {
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const plain = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "agents.defaults.model.primary"], CONFIG_READ_MS);
    const asJson = await runCommand(detected.path, ["config", "get", "agents.defaults.model.primary", "--json"], CONFIG_READ_MS);
    const value = parseJsonOutput(asJson.stdout);
    return {
      command: "openclaw config get agents.defaults.model.primary (plain, then --json)",
      plain: { exit: exitOf(plain), stdout: textStats(plain.stdout), value: refOrWord(parseConfigText(plain.stdout)) },
      exit: exitOf(asJson),
      json: jsonKind(value),
      shape: shapeOf(value, { shown: ROOT_SHOWN })
    };
  },

  async "claude-status"(ctx) {
    await refuseOutside(ctx, ["claude"]);
    const status = await signInStatus("claude");
    return { installed: status.installed, status: status.status, method: word(status.method), note: status.note, readiness: claudePlanReadiness(status) };
  },

  async plans(ctx) {
    await refuseOutside(ctx, ["openclaw", "claude"]);
    return readOpenclawPlans();
  },

  async "last-job"() {
    const dir = path.join(throwawayAgentOsHome(), "setup", "jobs");
    const names = (await fsp.readdir(dir)).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".json"));
    if (!names.length) throw new Error("No setup job yet.");
    const stamped = await Promise.all(names.map(async (name) => ({ name, at: (await fsp.stat(path.join(dir, name))).mtimeMs })));
    const newest = stamped.sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at)[0].name;
    const job = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(path.join(dir, newest), "utf8"));
    return {
      kind: job.kind,
      status: job.status,
      plan: job.plan ?? null,
      mode: job.mode ?? null,
      model: word(job.model),
      readiness: job.readiness ?? null,
      previousPrimary: job.previousPrimary ? refOrWord(job.previousPrimary) : null,
      execModeChanged: job.execModeChanged ?? null,
      steps: (job.steps ?? []).map((step) => ({
        id: step.id,
        action: step.action,
        status: step.status,
        error: step.error ? tidy(step.error) : null,
        warnings: (step.warnings ?? []).map(tidy)
      })),
      health: Object.fromEntries(
        Object.entries(job.health ?? {}).map(([agentId, entry]) => [agentId, { promptOk: entry.promptOk, skipped: entry.skipped === true, hint: entry.hint ?? null }])
      )
    };
  },

  async "restore-openclaw"(ctx, ref) {
    const valid = restorableRef(ref, MODEL_ID_PATTERN);
    if (!valid) throw new Error("restore-openclaw takes one model reference, for example openrouter/vendor/model.");
    const detected = await findOpenclaw(ctx);
    const result = await runCommand(detected.path, ["models", "set", valid], SET_MODEL_MS);
    const after = await readAgentModel("openclaw", detected);
    return {
      command: `openclaw models set ${valid}`,
      exit: exitOf(result),
      stdout: textStats(result.stdout),
      now: after.model ? refOrWord(after.provider ? `${after.provider}/${after.model}` : after.model) : null,
      plan: after.plan ?? null
    };
  },

  async scan(_ctx, folder) {
    const root = path.resolve(String(folder ?? ""));
    if (root !== LIVE_ROOT && !root.startsWith(`${LIVE_ROOT}${path.sep}`)) throw new Error(`scan reads only inside ${LIVE_ROOT}.`);
    const where = {};
    let files = 0;
    let skipped = 0;
    const walk = async (dir) => {
      for (const entry of await fsp.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
        const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
        if (entry.isDirectory()) {
          await walk(full);
        } else if (entry.isFile()) {
          if ((await fsp.stat(full)).size > 20 * 1024 * 1024) {
            skipped += 1;
            continue;
          }
          files += 1;
          const { secretLike } = textStats(await fsp.readFile(full, "utf8"));
          if (secretLike) where[path.relative(root, full)] = secretLike;
        }
      }
    };
    await walk(root);
    return { root: tidy(root), files, skipped, secretLike: Object.values(where).reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0), where };
  }
};

function parseArgs(argv) {
  const options = { expectRoot: null, label: null, save: true };
  const rest = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    if (argv[i] === "--expect-root") options.expectRoot = path.resolve(argv[++i] ?? "");
    else if (argv[i] === "--label") options.label = String(argv[++i] ?? "");
    else if (argv[i] === "--no-save") options.save = false;
    else rest.push(argv[i]);
  }
  return { options, mode: rest[0], argument: rest[1] ?? null };
}

async function saveAnswer(label, mode, answer) {
  let store = {};
  try {
    store = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(SHAPES_FILE, "utf8"));
  } catch {
    store = {};
  }
  const at = new Date().toISOString();
  if (mode === "status") store.statusExits = [...(store.statusExits ?? []), { label, at, ...answer.exit, readiness: answer.readiness }];
  else store[label] = { at, ...answer };
  await fsp.writeFile(SHAPES_FILE, `${JSON.stringify(store, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
}

const { options, mode, argument } = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
if (!Object.hasOwn(MODES, mode ?? "")) {
  console.error(`Usage: sh .superpowers/plan-brains-live/run.sh <${Object.keys(MODES).join(" | ")}> [argument] [--label <name>] [--no-save] [--expect-root <dir>]`);
  process.exit(2);
}
const seen = [];
const restoreFs = spyOnFileAccess(seen);
let answer = null;
let failed = null;
try {
  answer = await MODES[mode]({ expectRoot: options.expectRoot }, argument);
} catch (error) {
  failed = tidy(error?.message || String(error));
} finally {
  restoreFs();
}
const allowed = path.resolve(allowedAgentFile(HOME));
const ownFile = (full) => full.startsWith(`${REPO_ROOT}${path.sep}`) && !/(^|[\\/])\.env($|\.)/.test(full);
const forbidden = [...new Set(seen.filter((p) => FORBIDDEN_PATH.test(p) && path.resolve(p) !== allowed && !ownFile(path.resolve(p))).map(tidy))];
const label = options.label || [mode, argument].filter(Boolean).join(" ");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ mode, argument, label, ...(failed ? { failed } : { answer }), forbiddenFileAccess: forbidden }, null, 2));
if (!failed && options.save && SAVED_MODES.has(mode)) await saveAnswer(label, mode, answer);
process.exitCode = failed || forbidden.length ? 1 : 0;
```

Create `.superpowers/plan-brains-live/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Task E3 (git-ignored, never committed): runs live-read.mjs the way the desktop app's server runs
# agent commands: a clean environment (nothing from this terminal: no CLAUDECODE markers, no keys,
# no HERMES_HOME), the PATH the desktop shell gives its server (server_path_env in
# desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs) and HOME as the working folder (the packaged server's
# working_dir). LIVE_PATH and LIVE_AOS override the PATH and the throwaway Agent OS folder
# (dry-run.sh uses them); nothing else from the caller reaches live-read.mjs.
set -eu
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
NODE_BIN="${NODE_BIN:-$(command -v node)}"
cd "$HOME"
exec env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="${USER:-}" LOGNAME="${LOGNAME:-}" SHELL="${SHELL:-/bin/zsh}" TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
  PATH="${LIVE_PATH:-/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.agent-os/node/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$HOME/.volta/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin}" \
  AGENT_OS_HOME="${LIVE_AOS:-/private/tmp/sp3-brains-live/aos}" \
  "$NODE_BIN" "$ROOT/.superpowers/plan-brains-live/live-read.mjs" "$@"
```

Create `.superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs`:

```js
// Task E3 (git-ignored, never committed): runs B1b's FAKE OpenClaw (never a real agent) for the
// same reads as live-read.mjs and compares the shapes with the live ones.
//   node .superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs make-fake-home <dir>   a fake HOME for dry-run.sh
//   node .superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs fakes                  fake-shapes.json and its paths
//   node .superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs diff                   live against fake, plus fake rows with the live field names
import { mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { runCommand } from "../../server/runtime/safety.js";
import { parseConfigText, parseJsonOutput } from "../../server/runtime/setup/models.js";
import { installFakeAgent, writeFakeAgentCli } from "../../test/helpers/fake-builder-clis.js";
import { writeFakeAgentState } from "../../test/helpers/fake-knobs.js";
import { FAKE_CLAUDE_CLI_PINS, FAKE_SECRET, installFakeOpenclawShim } from "../../test/helpers/fake-openclaw.js";
import { AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS, CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS, MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS, ROOT_SHOWN, collapseFirstSegment, diffShapes, shapeOf, synthFrom } from "./shape.mjs";

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const LIVE_FILE = path.join(HERE, "live-shapes.json");
const FAKE_FILE = path.join(HERE, "fake-shapes.json");
// The row W1's fake sign-in program saves (contract, "Fakes and knobs"). When a follow-up changes
// that row in test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs, this constant changes with it (Step 16).
const SIGNED_IN_ROW = Object.freeze({ provider: "openai", method: "siwc", tokenSharing: true, email: "someone@example.com" });
const exitOf = (result) => ({ ok: result.ok, code: result.code, signal: result.signal });

// A fake `openclaw` (~/.npm-global/bin) and a fake `claude` (~/.local/bin): detection searches
// both folders before /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin, so no real agent is ever found.
async function makeFakeHome(dir) {
  await installFakeOpenclawShim(dir);
  await installFakeAgent(dir, "claude", await writeFakeAgentCli(dir));
  await writeFakeAgentState(dir, { primary: null, models: null, authRows: [SIGNED_IN_ROW] });
  return path.join(dir, ".npm-global", "bin", "openclaw");
}

async function fakeReads() {
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "e3-fake-openclaw-")));
  try {
    const shim = await makeFakeHome(home);
    const env = { HOME: home, USER: "fake", LOGNAME: "fake", TMPDIR: os.tmpdir(), PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" };
    const run = (args) => runCommand(shim, args, 15000, { env, cwd: home });
    const read = async (args, shown) => {
      const result = await run(args);
      return { exit: exitOf(result), shape: shapeOf(parseJsonOutput(result.stdout), { shown }) };
    };
    const primaryRead = async () => {
      const plain = await run(["config", "get", "agents.defaults.model.primary"]);
      return {
        ...(await read(["config", "get", "agents.defaults.model.primary", "--json"], ROOT_SHOWN)),
        plain: { exit: exitOf(plain), value: parseConfigText(plain.stdout) }
      };
    };
    const out = {};
    out["models anthropic"] = await read(["models", "list", "--provider", "anthropic", "--json"], MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS);
    out["models openai"] = await read(["models", "list", "--provider", "openai", "--json"], MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS);
    out.auth = await read(["models", "auth", "list", "--provider", "openai", "--json"], AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS);
    out["models-config before onboard"] = await read(["config", "get", "agents.defaults.models", "--json"], CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS);
    out["primary unset"] = await primaryRead();
    const onboard = await run(["onboard", "--non-interactive", "--accept-risk", "--auth-choice", "anthropic-cli"]);
    if (!onboard.ok) throw new Error("The fake onboard failed.");
    out["models-config after onboard"] = await read(["config", "get", "agents.defaults.models", "--json"], CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS);
    const set = await run(["models", "set", "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"]);
    if (!set.ok) throw new Error("The fake models set failed.");
    out["primary after onboard"] = await primaryRead();
    const status = await run(["models", "status", "--check", "--plain"]);
    out.statusExits = [{ label: "fake default", ...exitOf(status) }];
    out.pins = FAKE_CLAUDE_CLI_PINS.map((id) => `anthropic/${id}`);
    return out;
  } finally {
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

async function fakesMode() {
  const fake = await fakeReads();
  await writeFile(FAKE_FILE, `${JSON.stringify(fake, null, 2)}\n`);
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(fake).map(([key, value]) => [key, value?.shape ? Object.keys(value.shape) : value]));
}

async function diffMode() {
  const live = JSON.parse(await readFile(LIVE_FILE, "utf8"));
  const fake = await fakeReads();
  await writeFile(FAKE_FILE, `${JSON.stringify(fake, null, 2)}\n`);
  const report = {};
  const compare = (key, enumKeys, collapse = false) => {
    if (!live[key]?.shape) {
      report[key] = "not read live";
      return;
    }
    const a = collapse ? collapseFirstSegment(live[key].shape) : live[key].shape;
    const b = collapse ? collapseFirstSegment(fake[key].shape) : fake[key].shape;
    report[key] = { liveExit: live[key].exit, fakeExit: fake[key].exit, ...diffShapes(a, b, { enumKeys }) };
  };
  compare("models anthropic", ["provider"]);
  compare("models openai", ["provider"]);
  compare("auth", ["method", "type", "provider"]);
  compare("models-config after onboard", ["id"], true);
  // Two live reads, not a fake difference: how a sign-in without token sharing shows next to one
  // with it ("live" below is the no-sharing read, "fake" the sharing one).
  if (live["auth no-sharing"]?.shape && live.auth?.shape) {
    report["auth no-sharing vs auth"] = diffShapes(live["auth no-sharing"].shape, live.auth.shape, { enumKeys: [...AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS], exactValues: true });
  }
  const primaryOf = (entry) => (entry ? { plainExit: entry.plain.exit, jsonExit: entry.exit, value: entry.plain.value } : "not read live");
  report.primary = { live: primaryOf(live["primary after onboard"]), fake: primaryOf(fake["primary after onboard"]) };
  report["primary unset"] = { live: primaryOf(live["primary unset"]), fake: primaryOf(fake["primary unset"]) };
  report.pins = {
    live: live["models-config after onboard"]?.pinnedToClaudeCli ?? "not read live",
    wildcardLive: live["models-config after onboard"]?.wildcard ?? null,
    fake: fake.pins,
    wildcardFake: null
  };
  report.statusExits = {
    live: (live.statusExits ?? []).map(({ label, ok, code, signal, readiness }) => ({ label, ok, code, signal, readiness })),
    fakeDefault: fake.statusExits[0]
  };
  report.synth = Object.fromEntries(
    ["auth", "auth no-sharing", "models anthropic", "models openai", "models-config after onboard"]
      .filter((key) => live[key]?.shape)
      .map((key) => [key, synthFrom(live[key].shape, "(top)", { secret: FAKE_SECRET })])
  );
  return report;
}

const [mode, argument] = process.argv.slice(2);
let output;
if (mode === "make-fake-home" && argument) {
  output = { shim: await makeFakeHome(path.resolve(argument)) };
} else if (mode === "fakes") {
  output = await fakesMode();
} else if (mode === "diff") {
  output = await diffMode();
} else {
  console.error("Usage: node .superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs <make-fake-home <dir> | fakes | diff>");
  process.exit(2);
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(output, null, 2));
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Task E3 (git-ignored, never committed): every read-only live-read mode against B1b's FAKE
# OpenClaw and fake Claude Code in a throwaway HOME, before anything touches the owner's real
# agents. The PATH holds only the system folders; --expect-root refuses, before anything runs, any

mkdir -p "$FH" "$LV/fake-aos" "$LV/dry"
node "$ROOT/.superpowers/plan-brains-live/compare-shapes.mjs" make-fake-home "$FH" > "$LV/dry/fake-home.json" || exit 1
dry() {

  HOME="$FH" LIVE_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin LIVE_AOS="$LV/fake-aos" \
    sh "$ROOT/.superpowers/plan-brains-live/run.sh" "$@" --expect-root "$FH" --no-save > "$LV/dry/$name.json"
  status=$?

  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
}

dry plans plans
echo "leaks: $(cat "$LV"/dry/[a-z]*.json | grep -c -E 'SECRET-fake-0000|someone@example\.com')"
echo "forbidden: $(cat "$LV"/dry/*.json | grep -c -E '"forbiddenFileAccess": \[$')"
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Ask once for the live setup, start the spike server and record the baseline.** Use AskUserQuestion: "To check the plan brains with your real agents, I'd start a second, separate Agent OS server on port 8794. It uses your real OpenClaw, Hermes and Claude Code and your real home folder, but a throwaway Agent OS data folder (/private/tmp/sp3-brains-live). Starting it changes nothing in your agents. Like your installed Agent OS, it checks which agents are installed (each one's `--version` and `--help`). Then I'd read, without changing anything, OpenClaw's version and model, Hermes's model, and whether Claude Code is signed in. That runs `openclaw --version`, a few `openclaw config get` reads, `openclaw models auth list`, OpenClaw's model lists (`openclaw models list`), `hermes config get` and `claude auth status`, each a few times; opening OpenClaw's card in Agent OS runs some of them too. I only see field names and model names, never your e-mail or a token. If your installed Agent OS app is open, please leave its Setup alone until we finish. OK?" Options: "Yes, set it up (Recommended)" / "Not now". On "Not now", record "deferred by the owner" for all four checks and go to Step 17.

On yes, build first (foreground), from the worktree root:

```bash
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -2
```

Then start the server in the background, from the worktree root:

```bash
ROOT="$PWD"; LV=/private/tmp/sp3-brains-live; mkdir -p $LV/aos; NODE="$(command -v node)"
cd "$HOME" && env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" LOGNAME="$LOGNAME" SHELL="$SHELL" TMPDIR="$TMPDIR" PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.agent-os/node/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$HOME/.volta/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin AGENT_OS_HOME=$LV/aos AGENT_OS_PORT=8794 "$NODE" "$ROOT/server/index.js"
```

How this environment is built:
- `env -i` starts the server with only what a Dock launch gives an app, as in Task E2 Step 1, so the sign-in session gets the owner's own login-shell environment (H2) and nothing from this terminal.
- `PATH` is what the desktop shell's `server_path_env()` gives its server (folders that do not exist do no harm), and `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` is the PATH the app itself was started with. This differs from E2's short PATH on purpose: the Claude plan's hello check makes OpenClaw run the owner's `claude`, and the desktop app would find it.
- The working folder is HOME, as `working_dir: home_dir()` gives the packaged server. The server finds `dist` and its `.env` from its own file, so this changes nothing for it, but every command it runs without its own folder (`claude auth status` among them) runs in HOME, as in the installed app. Claude Code reads project settings from its working folder, so the worktree would be the wrong place.
- `AGENT_OS_PORT` keeps the port out of the sessions' environment (decision Q11a).
- Known differences from the installed app, recorded in the log: it is the worktree's `server/index.js` run by the worktree's Node (not the bundled Node), it serves the worktree's `dist`, `AGENT_OS_PACKAGED` and `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN` are unset (it is stopped with SIGTERM), and the port is fixed.

The output shows `AGENT_OS_READY:8794` and the line `Agent OS is running. Open: http://127.0.0.1:8794/?launch=<token>`. Open that link in the pane. The token belongs to this throwaway server only (it is not one of the owner's credentials) and stays valid while the server runs; Steps 8, 9 and 14 give the same link to the owner for his own browser. - [ ] **Step 15: What Agent OS ran and kept, then stop and clean up.** No ask: these read only Agent OS's own throwaway data and stop the server this task started. In the pane, read-only:

```js
const { runs } = await fetch("/api/runs?limit=1000").then((r) => r.json());
const NEVER = ["setup-token", "paste-token", "--token", "--method oauth", "--device-code", "--dangerously-skip-permissions", "--yolo", "--probe"];
const ONBOARD = /^onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice anthropic-cli( --(skip-health|skip-channels|skip-skills|skip-ui|install-daemon))*$/;
// Drop the command path (JSON-quoted when it holds a space), keep the arguments.
const lines = runs.map((run) => String(run.commandPreview || "").replace(/^("[^"]*"|\S+)\s*/, ""));
const onboards = lines.filter((line) => line.startsWith("onboard "));
({
  runs: lines.length,
  forbidden: lines.filter((line) => NEVER.some((flag) => line.includes(flag))).length,
  acceptRiskOutsideOnboard: lines.filter((line) => line.includes("--accept-risk") && !line.startsWith("onboard ")).length,
  outputKeptFor: lines.filter((line) => /^models (status|auth)/.test(line)).length,
  onboards: onboards.length,
  onboardsWithOtherFlags: onboards.filter((line) => !ONBOARD.test(line))
});
```

Expected:
- `forbidden: 0`, `acceptRiskOutsideOnboard: 0` and `outputKeptFor: 0`. The sign-in status and readiness reads run in memory, never as a recorded run;
- `onboards` equals the number of Claude plan Applies the owner said yes to in Step 12 (0, 1, or 2 when he applied again with a pinned model), and `onboardsWithOtherFlags` is `[]`: each onboard carries `--non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice anthropic-cli` plus only flags from today's optional list (Safety 3, live).

Reading the report:
- `models anthropic`, `models openai`, `auth` and `models-config after onboard`: `same: true` means the fake matches. Otherwise `onlyLive`, `onlyFake`, `typeMismatch` and `valueMismatch` name the fields.
- `auth no-sharing vs auth`: two live reads, not a fake difference. It names the field and words that tell a sign-in without token sharing from one with it (`valueMismatch` with `exactValues`: "live" is the no-sharing read, "fake" the sharing one). `parseAuthRows` must read `sharing: false` from that field for the no-sharing row and `true` for the other.
- `primary`: the live plain value and exits against the fake's, after onboard. `primary unset`: how an unset primary answers live (exits and value) against the fake's (B1b's open question).
- `pins`: the live list against `FAKE_CLAUDE_CLI_PINS`, and whether OpenClaw wrote `anthropic/*`.
- `statusExits`: the exit codes seen live, by label.
- `synth`: fake values in the live shape, for "auth", "auth no-sharing", "models anthropic", "models openai" and "models-config after onboard".
- E1's ledger line: compare what it says the fakes assume with what `fake-shapes.json` shows and with the live report. Note any mismatch in the log ("E1's line said <x>; the fakes print <y>; live is <z>"). A mismatch between E1's line and the fakes needs no code: it only shows that E1's summary was off.

What counts as a difference (the spec's S-B3: "Any field that differs from the fakes is fixed in B1's parsers and fakes before the work is called done"):
- any `same: false` in the four reads above: a path only one side has (a field only live, even one Agent OS never reads, such as a context-window number), a type that differs, or a method, runtime or provider word with nothing in common;
- the no-sharing row, when `auth no-sharing`'s `parsed` gave `sharing: null` (B1b's parser does not read the real sharing field);
- the primary, when its live form or exit codes differ from the fake's (after onboard, or unset);
- the pins: per-model entries against a wildcard, the entry's shape, or which ids were pinned;
- the status exits: a live code that the fake's `FAKE_OPENCLAW_STATUS_EXIT` cannot give (anything but 0, 1 or 2). A code whose meaning differs from `readinessOf`'s goes to the owner first (Notes, item 7).

Every difference gets a follow-up. A follow-up always changes the fake's default answer for that read to the live shape (from `synth`), and also changes the B1b parser or reader when Agent OS reads that part of the answer. If the real sign-in program saved a row whose names differ from W1's fake row, that fake row changes in the same follow-up as `parseAuthRows`. The only way to leave a difference without a follow-up is the owner's explicit OK: the orchestrator may propose it (for example keeping the fake's pinned ids, so tests still see one unpinned model), lists it under "Fakes left as they are" in the Results block, and asks him in Step 17 before the ledger's closing line is written.

A difference that changes what the spec promises is not a parser fix. It goes to the owner first, with the finding and a proposed spec sentence (Notes, item 7).

#### Notes

1. **Why the tools exist.** The reads E3 needs (`models auth list`, `models status`, the model lists, `config get`) print account data. Printed in a terminal, that data would land in this conversation's transcript. So each read goes through `live-read.mjs`, which keeps the output in memory and prints only what the self-test proves safe:
   - the fields' names and types, and shown words only for a short list of keys (method, type, provider, the sharing, scope and plan words, model key and name, runtime id);
   - a profile id's provider part only (`openai:<id>`, unless the rest is `default`, `manual` or `claude-cli`), because people choose profile ids (`--profile-id openai:work`); an object key with a space is hidden for the same reason;
   - booleans, and counts;
   - Agent OS's own parsed answer, and a model ref read back from OpenClaw as it is, so it can be put back.
   The dry run proves it again on B1b's fakes, whose rows carry `someone@example.com` and `SECRET-fake-0000` on purpose. The tools are git-ignored orchestrator probes, like the UI audit probes, so E3 adds no file under `test/`. Each difference becomes a worker follow-up with a real failing test in `test/openclaw-plans.test.js`, built from the synthesized rows (with plan words and anything of the owner's replaced, Step 16).
2. **The environment.** `run.sh` and the spike server use `env -i`, the desktop shell's server PATH (`server_path_env`, including `~/.volta/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` and `~/.bun/bin`) and HOME as their working folder (the packaged server's `working_dir: home_dir()`), so reads and jobs see what the installed app sees: no `CLAUDECODE` markers, no keys from this terminal, no `HERMES_HOME`, and no project settings from the worktree. E2's server used only the system folders. E3 adds the desktop folders because the Claude plan's hello makes OpenClaw run the owner's `claude`. The known differences that remain (worktree server and Node, worktree `dist`, not packaged, fixed port) are in the log. The test rules (fake login shell, fake bin PATH) apply to the dry run, which uses only fakes, and not to the live server, which exists to use the real agents (as in E2).
3. **Which window does what.** The orchestrator drives the throwaway Agent OS in Claude's browser pane: navigation, model picks, both Applies, Setup's update and its confirm button (after the owner's yes), "Choose in Hermes" and "Refresh". The owner's own browser holds the same throwaway Agent OS, opened with its `Open:` link: he does both ChatGPT sign-ins there (where he is already signed in to ChatGPT), and Step 14's window-focus check happens there, because a real window focus is what the card listens for. The risk tick belongs to one page, so it is ticked in the pane, by the owner or by the orchestrator at his word after the two sentences were quoted. Before each sign-in the orchestrator moves the pane off the Agents page, so the pane never attaches to the sign-in terminal and the one-time code never reaches a screenshot or page read. The owner says what the terminal did, in words.
4. **Step 8 is optional, and its Apply changes the spec's order only with the owner's explicit OK.** The no-sharing sign-in and its two reads are inside the approved order (they come before S-B3's reads, and change no model). The extra Apply is not: the spec says S-B1 applies no model and S-B3's reads come "right after that sign-in and before any apply". It is the only live way to test the claim that the readiness check still catches a sign-in without token sharing (spec §3, "Until S-B3"), so it gets its own question that names the change of order; his answer is logged and goes into the Results block. That Apply is put back by the job itself (or by `restore-openclaw`), Safety stays on Look only so a readiness that wrongly passes spends no plan usage on a hello, and Step 10's reads still come right after the real sign-in (labelled "primary after sign-in").
5. **What is restored and what is not.**
   - Restored on request: OpenClaw's model, with `openclaw models set <ref>`, the same command the checks used (any ref Agent OS itself writes, OpenRouter presets included, can be passed back). Hermes's model is restored by the owner himself, in Hermes's own picker (Agent OS never changes Hermes's settings).
   - Not undone:
     - the OpenClaw update (H7: no downgrades), and any settings migration OpenClaw's own updater makes;
     - the ChatGPT sign-in (the owner can remove it with OpenClaw's own `models auth logout`);
     - onboarding's pins, its record that the owner saw the security notice, and any default model it set (put back on request with `models set`, when there was an earlier model);
     - a gateway service that onboarding installed;
     - `tools.exec.mode` at `ask` (never loosened).
   Each question says so before the owner answers.
6. **Copy.** This task adds no product sentence. The chat questions are the orchestrator's own words, not product copy. The spec's Results block and any rewritten "Until S-B3" bullet go to the owner for his OK before they are committed.
7. **Findings that go to the owner, not to a worker** (they change what the spec promises, so the spec changes first):
   - `models status --check --plain` exits 0 for a sign-in without token sharing, so readiness can't catch it;
   - an exit code whose meaning differs from `readinessOf`'s (for example 2 while nothing expires);
   - onboard pins nothing, or pins in a shape the runtime check can't recognise;
   - neither model list has a usable id;
   - the sign-in program refuses Agent OS's fixed argv, or needs another flag, or sets a default model by itself;
   - a second sign-in is refused or makes a duplicate profile;
   - Hermes's picker doesn't save where `readAgentModel("hermes")` reads (`model.provider`, `model.default`), or `HERMES_HOME` differs between Terminal and Agent OS.
8. **Risks.**
   - Onboarding is a first run on the owner's real OpenClaw settings. The `--skip-*` flags keep it small, but it may still change gateway or workspace settings or set a default model; the backup suggestion is in the question, and Step 12 reads the model after any failure.
   - The Claude plan hello runs through OpenClaw's gateway service, a launchd service whose own PATH may not find `claude`. A failing hello with a "not signed in" or "claude not found" hint is recorded for the owner; Agent OS can only say so.
   - Anthropic may enforce its rules without notice (spec "Terms basis"); the research rates the account risk low to moderate.
   - The hello checks use a little of each plan. Fable is never offered (usage credits).
   - The scan's secret test can flag Agent OS's own key files; the step says which hits matter.
   - If the owner's OpenClaw updates again later, its output may change again. The fallback list and "cannot be read" handling cover an unreadable list, and a new E3-style read can be run with the same tools.
9. **Port 8794.** 8791 is the UI audit harness, 8792 E1's smoke server, 8793 E2's spike server.
10. **What the checks prove live, and what they do not.**
    - Safety 1 live covers only the read modes: B1a's spy runs inside `live-read.mjs`. It ignores files inside this worktree, because the worktree sits under the main checkout's `.claude/worktrees/` and `FORBIDDEN_PATH` would match every one of Agent OS's own files (a worktree `.env` would still count). The spike server's own flows (the sign-in session, both Applies, the readiness reads and the Hermes launch) run without a spy; their Safety 1 tests are B1a's, B1b's and B1c's.
    - Safety 2 and 3 live: the sign-in session's argv, seen with `ps` while it runs (Step 9); the recorded runs, from `commandPreview` (Step 15); the Hermes `.command` file (Step 14). The `runCommand` reads (`models status`, `models auth list`, `config get`) are not recorded runs, so Step 15 cannot see them; their argv is fixed in B1b's code and tested there.
    - Safety 5 live: Step 9's checks after the sign-in.
    - The dry-run guard uses `resolveBinary` (where detection would look) instead of `detect()`, because `detect()` runs `--version` and `--help` on whatever it finds, which is exactly what must not happen to a real agent during the dry run.
11. **Names this task adds beyond the contract** (all git-ignored, orchestrator-only):
    - the folder `.superpowers/plan-brains-live/` with `selftest.mjs`, `shape.mjs` (`AUTH_SHOWN_KEYS`, `MODEL_SHOWN_KEYS`, `CONFIG_SHOWN_KEYS`, `ROOT_SHOWN`, `HIDDEN_KEY`, `looksSecret`, `profileIdShown`, `restorableRef`, `shapeOf`, `secretPaths`, `textStats`, `collapseFirstSegment`, `diffShapes` with its `exactValues` option, `synthFrom`), `live-read.mjs` (its modes, `refuseOutside`, `refOrWord`, `REPO_ROOT`), `run.sh` (`LIVE_PATH`, `LIVE_AOS`, `NODE_BIN`), `compare-shapes.mjs` (`SIGNED_IN_ROW`) and `dry-run.sh`;
